So I'll attempt to articulate this clearly in one sentence: While a person is not condemned 'presently' by Jesus if they are 'presently' holding faith in Him, and while Jesus did not 'judge' those who heard but did not do what He said, the same word that they rejected will judge later and there is still a day of wrath coming for those who are not sanctified into loving their neighbour the way God has commanded them to. Continuing on in the faith soundly involves abiding in the sound doctrine of Jesus Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20John%201%3A1-11&version=ESV][II John 1:1-11]]*) which includes walking according to Jesus' commandments (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A23-24&version=ESV][I John 3:23-24]]*). Though God will have mercy on those He has mercy. But we want to have confidence for the day of judgement so we should be walking in godliness holding our faith in Jesus so that the deeds that we do, coming from faith, are good deeds (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A12&version=ESV][John 14:12]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A17-21&version=ESV][John 3:17-21]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A3-6&version=ESV][I John 2:3-6]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%203%3A1-10&version=ESV][Colossians 3:1-10]]* - If then you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God. Set your minds on things that are above, not on things that are on earth. For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God. When Christ who is your life appears, then you also will appear with him in glory. Put to death therefore what is earthly in you: sexual immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry. *On account of these the wrath of God is coming.* In these you too once walked, when you were living in them. But now you must put them all away: anger, wrath, malice, slander, and obscene talk from your mouth. Do not lie to one another, seeing that you have put off the old self with its practices and have put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge after the image of its creator. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A17-21&version=ESV][John 3:17-21]]* - *For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but in order that the world might be saved through him.* Whoever believes in him is not condemned, but whoever does not believe is condemned already, because he has not believed in the name of the only Son of God. And this is the judgment: the light has come into the world, and people loved the darkness rather than the light *because their deeds were evil.* For everyone who does wicked things hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his deeds should be exposed. But whoever does [[strongs:G4160][(G4160 poiōn; doing)]] what is true comes to the light, so that it may be clearly seen that his deeds have been carried out in God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

The one who rejects me and does not receive my words has a judge; the word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A19-21&version=ESV][I John 4:19-21]]* - We love because he first loved us. If anyone says, I love God, and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen cannot love God whom he has not seen. And this commandment we have from him: *whoever loves God must also love his brother*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I think that to have the love of God completed in us (the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us: *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A3-4&version=ESV][Romans 8:3-4]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A13-14&version=ESV][Galatians 5:13-14]]*) is something that is necessary for the Christian to avoid the wrath of God on the day of wrath (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%203%3A7-8&version=ESV][Luke 3:7-8]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2013%3A24-30&version=ESV][Matthew 13:24-30]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A17-21&version=ESV][John 3:17-21]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2013%3A3&version=ESV][Luke 13:3]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A36&version=ESV][John 3:36]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%201%3A17-18&version=ESV][Romans 1:17-18]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A5&version=ESV][Romans 2:5]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Peter%203%3A7&version=ESV][II Peter 3:7]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A16-18&version=ESV][Romans 6:16-18]],7:25,8:1-4*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A46-49&version=ESV][Luke 6:46-49]]* - Why do you call me Lord, Lord, and not do what I tell you? _Everyone who comes to me and hears my words and does them, I will show you *what he is like: he is like* a man building a house, who dug deep and laid the foundation on the rock_. And when a flood arose, the stream broke against that house and could not shake it, because it had been well built. But the one who hears and does not do them is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation. When the stream broke against it, immediately it fell, and the ruin of that house was great. (ESV)

Whoever says I know him but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, but whoever keeps his word, in him truly the love of God is perfected. By this we may be sure that we are in him: whoever says he abides in him ought to walk in the same way in which he walked. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2010%3A4-6&version=ESV][II Corinthians 10:4-6]]* - For the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh but have divine power to destroy strongholds. We destroy arguments and every lofty opinion raised against the knowledge of God, and take every thought captive to obey Christ, being ready to punish every disobedience, when your obedience is complete. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A14&version=ESV][I John 3:14]]* - We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. Whoever does not love abides in death. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We have faith in Jesus Christ into loving as God *requires* from us, and that means loving God and the children of God and our neighbour as God has commanded (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2013%3A9-10&version=ESV][Romans 13:9-10]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1-5&version=ESV][I John 5:1-5]]*). Keep in mind that if Jesus has said that "even sinners" do the same, as in love those who love them, and how Paul has said that what does not proceed from faith is sin, then what proceeds from a /genuine/ faith in Jesus Christ will be that the requirement to love God and our neighbour, loving even those neighbours who hate us, will be met, and in the /way/ that God requires us to love our neighbour:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A32-36&version=ESV][Luke 6:32-36]]* - If you love those who love you, what benefit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them. And if you do good to those who do good to you, what benefit is that to you? For even sinners do the same. And if you lend to those from whom you expect to receive, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, to get back the same amount. But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, expecting nothing in return, and your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, for he is kind to the ungrateful and the evil. Be merciful, even as your Father is merciful. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

(ESV)

(ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

"Sinless perfection" means "without even 'having' sin". The Apostle Paul describes having "indwelling sin" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A22-23&version=ESV][Romans 7:22-23]]*). John says that if we say we /have/ no sin we deceive ourselves. Having "indwelling sin" does not mean "committing sin", which is making more sin by transgression. Now Jesus Christ is sinless. Jesus has no sin at all. Neither does Jesus commit sin. When a person uses a dirty towel on a clean plate, they dirty the plate. When a person uses a clean towel on a dirty plate, they clean the plate. Jesus is clean and cleans us. Jesus sanctifies us. 'Having sin' (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A6-10&version=ESV][I John 1:6-10]]*) is actually different from "committing sin". We can confess sin that we have (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A9&version=ESV][1 John 1:9]]*) and should to be cleaned from it.

Someone who is born-again has had their old self crucified, and has been set free from sin (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A6-8&version=ESV][Romans 6:6-8]]*) in the sense that they now have the power to rule over sin and to put sinful desires to death.
If a born-again person loves Jesus more than some evil desire, then they have the power through faith in Jesus to put that evil desire to death completely and to stop doing the evil deeds that arise from that bad desire, and to put a stop to those evil deeds. We are instructed to, from a love of the truth, practice righteousness with our members instead (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A16-18&version=ESV][Galatians 5:16-18]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A10-13&version=ESV][Romans 6:10-13]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A29-30&version=ESV][Matthew 5:29-30]]*).

Someone who used to do evil with their hands should then from the love of the truth instead do good with their hands. But I think this really extends even to what people do with their resources genreally such as computer or their money, etc.

The mind of the old self must be "shaken off" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A11&version=ESV][Romans 6:11]]*) and we do that by taking every thought captive for obedience to Jesus Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2010%3A5-6&version=ESV][II Corinthians 10:5-6]]*).
We must set our minds on the things of the Spirit, rather than the things of the flesh; We must walk by the spirit, and this will help us to "put to death the deeds of the body [of sin]" (i.e. stop obeying the flesh):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A16-18&version=ESV][Galatians 5:16-18]]* - But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh. For the desires of the flesh are against the Spirit, and the desires of the Spirit are against the flesh, for these are opposed to each other, to keep you from doing the things you want to do. But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must "continue" in obedience to God, obeying Jesus Christ to be overcome by walking by the spirit practicing righteousness, rather than obeying sin.
The mind of the repentant person must continue on in the love for the truth practicing righteousness. At the end of sanctification is eternal life and receiving the inheritance.

But from what I've seen, shaking off this mindset of the former self can be challenging while one's company is still clinging to the ways of the flesh resisting the new creation, but I think the way forward most importantly is to continue practicing the truth for oneself regardless of physical circumstances, as responding to such resistance with faith and obedience to Jesus is, I believe, sanctifying.
There has been a struggle against the flesh, for me: Persecutions, isolation, hardship, restrictions on freedom, people ghosting, getting put out of 'churches' etc.

Though, we will fall short of God's glory, we still need to be conformed to love and holiness to inherit in the Kingdom of God as we behold the glory of the Lord Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%206%3A17-18&version=ESV][II Corinthians 6:17-18]],7:1* - Therefore go out from their midst, and be separate from them, says the Lord, and touch no unclean thing; then I will welcome you, and I will be a father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty. Since we have these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of body and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience. Therefore do not associate with them; for at one time you were darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Walk as children of light (for the fruit of light is found in all that is good and right and true), and try to discern what is pleasing to the Lord. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

For this comes from the Lord who is the Spirit. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

This was to show God's righteousness, because in his divine forbearance he had passed over former sins. It was to show his righteousness at the present time, so that he might be just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The "body of sin being brought to nothing" I think involves, for example, using one's members to practice righteousness, shaking off sinful behaviour that the former person used to practice.
Bringing the "body of sin to nothing" involves denying ungodliness, and walking in the truth in reality from the heart with a desire to please God, rather than having evil deeds that come from trusting in what is false.
While a person is given a brand new heart and a brand new spirit, I think God then circumcises that new heart to walk in His ways, and that heart circumcision involves walking in the commandments of God that are given for the Christian to walk in so it involves a Christian receiving correction by God after getting born-again, and this circumcision happens as we are obedient to the standard of teaching that the Apostles speak of (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A16-18&version=ESV][Romans 6:16-18]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A3-11&version=ESV][I John 3:3-11]]*) that is in agreement with Jesus' teaching (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A9-14&version=ESV][John 15:9-14]]*). The circumcision results in loving God with our *whole* heart and soul (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy%2030%3A6&version=ESV][Deuteronomy 30:6]]*) which means also loving the children of God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A2&version=ESV][I John 5:2]]*), not only just the fact that God has loved us first:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A11&version=ESV][Romans 6:11]]* - So you also must consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

And you, who were dead in your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, God made alive together with him, having forgiven us all our trespasses, by canceling the record of debt that stood against us with its legal demands. #+END_QUOTE

Real faith loves God rather than evil.
Real faith in Jesus prefers Him to evil.
Real faith in Jesus prefers Him to other things.
And God cleans us as we hold our faith in Jesus Christ preferring Him.

There is no rest for the unrepentant. Whether a person has a disease/illness or not, they need to come to faith in Jesus with the love of God. A sick person finds no cure in being unrepentant. Real love and compassion encourages people to turn from the error of their ways. It's not right to say, "The ill/diseased are excused from needing to repent and have faith." We don't just /take/ the rest from Jesus without coming to Jesus (learning from Him). Jesus gives the rest to those who come to Him. We need to come to have a genuine faith in Jesus which loves the truth. Whoever is presently having faith in Jesus is not committing sin. God justifies the ungodly who have faith in Jesus and in having faith in Jesus they have repented and in having faith in Jesus are not committing sin (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A18&version=ESV][I John 5:18]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1-6&version=ESV][I John 5:1-6]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]*).

Those who love the darkness rather than love God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A14-19&version=ESV][John 3:14-19]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%203%3A1-5&version=ESV][II Timothy 3:1-5]]*) are unrepentant people (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%203%3A6-8&version=ESV][II Timothy 3:6-8]]*) who are disqualified in their faith and who do not come to the knowledge of the truth which God desires all people to come to know (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%202%3A4&version=ESV][I Timothy 2:4]]*). So having the love of God in us is important for being saved. And unless someone is keeping God's commandments, for them, then they surely cannot have come to the knowledge of the truth (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A3-6&version=ESV][I John 2:3-6]]*). We have to have the love of God in us to have genuine faith in Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2048%3A22&version=ESV][Isaiah 48:22]]* - There is no peace, says the LORD, for the wicked. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]* - But whoever has doubts is condemned if he eats, because the eating is not from faith. For _whatever does not proceed from faith is sin._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

Jesus said to him, Get up, take up your bed, and walk. And at once the man was healed, and he took up his bed and walked. Now that day was the Sabbath. #+END_QUOTE

When a person gets born-again of the spirit, they do need to not then double-down on the passions of the flesh. They do need to not "walk by the corpse/flesh" letting the corpse dictate one's actions, but rather "walk by the spirit" doing the will of God. New spirit in old flesh needs to not be carnal and walk by the flesh, but should rather try to use the old flesh to practice righteousness from an inward desire to do the will of God. The flesh does seem to resist the will of the spirit though (consider, for example, if a born-again person's flesh was craving nicotine or pornography while this person knows in their heart that to act on indulging themself with it is against their faith in Jesus, and I'm not saying that having a cigarette is sin in all circumstances) for what is not done in faith is sin. It's right for a person who has been born-again of the spirit to strive to then walk by the spirit, as in not just be driven by the cravings of the flesh, of the old nature, but to actually by faith practice righteousness, resisting carnality, the way that we have been instructed to do, using ones' body for practicing righteousnessness, putting to death the "passions of the flesh". Being born-again of the spirit, a person has "woken up" and is in the light where all things are visible and the right thing to do is to put off the old self and to walk like Christ, as He has instructed:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A24&version=ESV][Galatians 5:24]]* - And those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I believe that additionally to the need of "receiving a heart transplant" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2018%3A31&version=ESV][Ezekiel 18:31]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2036%3A25-28&version=ESV][Ezekiel 36:25-28]]*), we should "divorce ourselves" from our "sinning members". And what I mean by that is, for example, if a person were, for example, practicing something sinful with their hands, such as stealing, then instead of making time to practice that, use one's hands for doing good works instead. And this is metaphorically, "cutting off the 'sinful flesh'".

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%209%3A45&version=ESV][Mark 9:45]]* - And if your foot causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than with two feet to be thrown into hell. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Not only does this point to the fact that we need a new heart. But if you are using your members for doing evil, then instead of doing evil with them, do good with them, effectively "cutting off the sinful flesh" from the heart (i.e. nipping it at the bud happens with a change of heart):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A29-30&version=ESV][Matthew 5:29-30]]* - If your right eye causes you to sin, tear it out and throw it away. For it is better that you lose one of your members than that your whole body be thrown into hell ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/1067.htm][1067. geenna]]). And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. For it is better that you lose one of your members than that your whole body go into hell. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

For just as you once presented your members as slaves to impurity and to lawlessness leading to more lawlessness, so now present your members as slaves to righteousness leading to sanctification. When you were slaves of sin, you were free in regard to righteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

And you, who were dead in your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, God made alive together with him, having forgiven us all our trespasses, by canceling the record of debt that stood against us with its legal demands. (ESV)

And Jesus answered them, Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick. *I have not come to call the righteous but sinners to repentance.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%203%3A17-22&version=ESV][I Peter 3:17-22]]* - For it is better to suffer for doing good, if that should be God's will, than for doing evil. For Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh but made alive in the spirit, in which he went and proclaimed to the spirits in prison, because they formerly did not obey, when God's patience waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was being prepared, in which a few, that is, eight persons, were brought safely through water. Baptism, which corresponds to this, now saves you, not as a removal of dirt from the body but as an appeal to God for a good conscience, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, with angels, authorities, and powers having been subjected to him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Paul really makes it clear that Father God is not in subjection to Jesus Christ the Son of God, but that Christ is reigning supremely at the right hand of Father God, Father God having given all judgement to Christ the Son, until all things are subjected to Christ. And then Christ Himself will be subjected to Father God. Christ has already defeated the last enemy, death, from His perspective:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A22-28&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:22-28]]* - For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ shall all be made alive. But each in his own order: Christ the firstfruits, then at his coming those who belong to Christ. Then comes the end, when he delivers the kingdom to God the Father after destroying every rule and every authority and power. For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet. The last enemy to be destroyed is death. For God has put all things in subjection under his feet. But when it says, all things are put in subjection, it is plain that he is excepted who put all things in subjection under him. When all things are subjected to him, then the Son himself will also be subjected to him who put all things in subjection under him, that God may be all in all. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A21-24&version=ESV][John 5:21-24]]* - For as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom he will. The Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son, that *all may honor the Son, just as they honor the Father.* _Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him_. Truly, truly, I say to you, whoever _hears my word and believes [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g4100/kjv/tr/0-1/][(G4100 pisteuo)]] him who sent me has eternal life_. He does not come (*[[https://biblehub.com/greek/2064.htm][2064. erchomai]]*) into judgment, but has passed from death to life.
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%203%3A17-22&version=ESV][I Peter 3:17-22]]* - For it is better to suffer for doing good, if that should be God's will, than for doing evil. For Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh but made alive in the spirit, in which he went and proclaimed to the spirits in prison, because they formerly did not obey, when God's patience waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was being prepared, in which a few, that is, eight persons, were brought safely through water. Baptism, which corresponds to this, now saves you, not as a removal of dirt from the body but as an appeal to God for a good conscience, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, with angels, authorities, and powers having been subjected to him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%201%3A18&version=ESV][Revelation of John 1:18]]* - and the living one. I died, and behold I am alive forevermore, and I have the keys of Death and Hades. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

A believer at some point dies (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2011%3A25-27&version=ESV][John 11:25-27]]*), and it happens when they are baptised into Christ's death (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A3-8&version=ESV][Romans 6:3-8]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%202%3A19-21&version=ESV][Galatians 2:19-21]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A1-6&version=ESV][Romans 7:1-6]]*) and is born of the spirit in order to be able to keep God's commandments (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2011%3A19-20&version=ESV][Ezekiel 11:19-20]]*). We don't have to be a slave of sin (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A34-35&version=ESV][John 8:34-35]],36,42,51*). But when does a person get born-again of the spirit? It's mysterious (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A6-8&version=ESV][John 3:6-8]]*) but it's partly not a mystery because a person who turns away from sin and has faith in Jesus will get born-again (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2018%3A31&version=ESV][Ezekiel 18:31]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2011%3A25-27&version=ESV][John 11:25-27]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2011%3A25-27&version=ESV][John 11:25-27]]* - Jesus said to her, I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live, and everyone who lives and believes in me shall never [[strongs:G3756][(G3756 οὐ)]] [[strongs:G3361][(G3361 μή)]] die. Do you believe this? She said to him, Yes, Lord; I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who is coming into the world. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A34-35&version=ESV][John 8:34-35]],36,42,51* - Jesus answered them, Truly, truly, I say to you, everyone who commits sin is a slave to sin. The slave does not remain in the house forever; the son remains forever. So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed. Jesus said to them, If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came from God and I am here. I came not of my own accord, but he sent me. Truly, truly, I say to you, if anyone keeps my word, he will never see death. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

When a person is "born-again", they are baptized into Jesus Christ's death, and so have died and been set free (aquitted) from sin, cleansed from former sin, and they are reborn, born of the Spirit. So all things have become new for them. But being born-again, we need to continue to do the will of God for us. We must continue abiding in Jesus Christ's commandments, in love for God and one's neighbour and practicing righteousness, not wickedness:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%203%3A16&version=ESV][Luke 3:16]]* - John answered them all, saying, I baptize you with water, but he who is mightier than I is coming, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie. He will baptize you with *the Holy Spirit* and with fire.
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A3-8&version=ESV][Romans 6:3-8]]* - Do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? We were buried therefore with him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life. For if we have been united with him in a death like his, we shall certainly be united with him in a resurrection like his. We know that our old self was crucified with him in order that the body of sin might be brought to nothing, so that we would no longer be enslaved to sin. For one who has died has been set free from sin. Now if we have died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://www.earlychristianwritings.com/text/polycarp-lightfoot.html][Polycarp 2:2]] :: 
    Now He that raised Him from the dead will raise us also; if we
    do His will and walk in His commandments and love the things which He
    loved, abstaining from all unrighteousness, covetousness, love of
    money, evil speaking, false witness; not rendering evil for evil or
    railing for railing or blow for blow or cursing for cursing;

Going forward we need to continue in love and holiness:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Peter%201%3A3-9&version=ESV][II Peter 1:3-9]]* - His divine power has granted to us all things that pertain to life and godliness, through the knowledge of him who called us to his own glory and excellence, by which he has granted to us his precious and very great promises, so that through them you may become partakers of the divine nature, having escaped from the corruption that is in the world because of sinful desire. For this very reason, make every effort to supplement your faith with virtue, and virtue with knowledge, and knowledge with self-control, and self-control with steadfastness, and steadfastness with godliness, and godliness with brotherly affection, and brotherly affection with love. For if these qualities are yours and are increasing, they keep you from being ineffective or unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ. For whoever lacks these qualities is so nearsighted that he is blind, having forgotten that he was cleansed from his former sins. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%202%3A11-12&version=ESV][II Timothy 2:11-12]]* - The saying is trustworthy, for: If we have died with him, we will also live with him; if we endure, we will also reign with him; if we deny him, he also will deny us; (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Titus%201%3A16&version=ESV][Titus 1:16]]* - They profess to know God, but they _deny him by their works_. They are detestable, *disobedient, unfit for any good work*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The person who is born of God has stopped "committing sin" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A4&version=ESV][I John 3:4]],8,9*) in the sense that this new beginning of repentance and faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%206%3A1&version=ESV][Hebrews 6:1]]*) has been obedience to God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A14-21&version=ESV][Romans 10:14-21]]*) rather than sin and going on they must continue on in faith, in the love of the truth, obeying righteousness (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A4&version=ESV][I John 3:4]],8,9*). The person born of God doesn't commit sin (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A18&version=ESV][I John 5:18]]*).
The person born of God is also not the sin in their flesh (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A17-23&version=ESV][Romans 7:17-23]]*).

For the person with a genuine faith in Jesus Christ, sin no longer has dominion over them because Jesus has defeated death:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%201%3A6&version=ESV][Philippians 1:6]]* - And I am sure of this, that he who began a good work in you will bring it to completion at the day of Jesus Christ. (ESV)

That Jesus Christ is the Son of God entails the truth that Jesus Christ "takes after" God ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%201%3A15&version=ESV][Colossians 1:15]]).
Believing that Jesus is the Son of God entails believing that Jesus' works were good, that Jesus practiced righteousness (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A31&version=ESV][John 14:31]]*). A son of God practices righteousness. A child of the devil practices wickedness:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

The good deeds done in faith are not contrived as God provides (sets up) the deeds to do and works through the person who has faith in Jesus Christ. God would supply such deeds as in *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2025%3A31-40&version=ESV][Matthew 25:31-40]]*, but we should be obedient (with love for God; [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2081%3A15&version=ESV][Psalms 81:15]]), giving thought to do what pleases God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2012%3A17-21&version=ESV][Romans 12:17-21]]*) ready to do those deeds (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Titus%201%3A16&version=ESV][Titus 1:16]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%202%3A21&version=ESV][II Timothy 2:21]]*). So we would recall, observe (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2028%3A18-20&version=ESV][Matthew 28:18-20]]*), delight in (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A17-23&version=ESV][Romans 7:17-23]]*) Jesus' commandments and apply them by faith in Jesus when the opportunity to do so presents itself (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%204%3A17&version=ESV][James 4:17]]*), which could be right now as for many of Jesus' commandments, they can be applied from the heart immediately. Given Jesus' instructions in *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A38-48&version=ESV][Matthew 5:38-48]]*, we should apply them generally to bear with others in love and to not return evil for evil, turning the other cheek, loving those who hate us. God works through those who are having faith in Jesus:

God at some point in His Sovereign and wise plan, makes a person born again. This new birth I believe is being baptised into Jesus' death, and this purifies the heart, regenerating the spirit, killing the sin that was there, and empowers the person to practice righteousness from a position of being dead to sin:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A3&version=ESV][I Peter 1:3]]* - Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! According to his great mercy, he has caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Jude%201%3A20-21&version=ESV][Jude 1:20-21]]* - But you, beloved, build yourselves up in your most holy faith; pray in the Holy Spirit; keep yourselves in the love of God, waiting for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ that leads to eternal life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A22-25&version=ESV][I Peter 1:22-25]]* - Having purified your souls by your obedience to the truth for a sincere brotherly love, love one another earnestly from a pure heart, since you have been born again, not of perishable seed but of imperishable, through the living and abiding word of God; for All flesh is like grass and all its glory like the flower of grass. The grass withers, and the flower falls, but the word of the Lord remains forever. And this word is the good news that was preached to you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Water baptism is an appeal to God for a good conscience through the death and resurrection of Christ. So water baptism is an appeal to God to die and be reborn, born-again of the spirit, made new:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%203%3A21&version=ESV][I Peter 3:21]]* - Baptism, which corresponds to this, now saves you, not as a removal of dirt from the body but as an appeal to God for a good conscience, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2011%3A25-27&version=ESV][John 11:25-27]]* - Jesus said to her, I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live, and everyone who lives and believes in me shall never [[strongs:G3756][(G3756 οὐ)]] [[strongs:G3361][(G3361 μή)]] die. Do you believe this? She said to him, Yes, Lord; I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who is coming into the world. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

This person is freed from compulsively committing evil deeds by the power that comes from having faith in Jesus Christ who is victorious over evil, Jesus Christ having condemned sin in the flesh.
When someone is born-again / baptised into Christ's death it is especially necessary to consider oneself dead to sin.

If a person is from the love of the truth (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A2&version=ESV][I John 5:2]]*) obeying God's commandment to have faith in Jesus Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A23-24&version=ESV][I John 3:23-24]]*), obedient now to Christ, then by the grace of God they no longer compulsively sin:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A6-8&version=ESV][Romans 6:6-8]]* - We know that our old self was crucified with him in order that the body of sin might be brought to nothing, so that we would no longer be enslaved to sin. For one who has died has been set free from sin. Now if we have died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A2&version=ESV][I John 5:2]]* - By this we know that we love the children of God, _when we *love God* and obey his commandments._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Getting born-again does result in sin's power to enslave a person into doing evil deeds being taken away.
Born-again people have the power to put to death the deeds of the flesh, and the power to abstain from sin, but they need to maintain their faith in Jesus as they do so, because they must walk by the spirit and not by the flesh.
Sanctification does result in putting a total stop to the deeds of the flesh: whatever causes people to commit sin, to do evil deeds.
Sometimes a born-again person might "sin" from a lapse of faith, but that doesn't mean they are totally enslaved to sin. If a person has been baptised into Christ's death, Jesus has the power to get that person to the point where they no longer sin.
If they haven't totally turned their back on Jesus Christ then they still have Him as their advocate to Father God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A1-6&version=ESV][I John 2:1-6]]*).

If a person commits sin (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A34-35&version=ESV][John 8:34-35]],36,42,51*), then that means they're enslaved to sin in some way but it doesn't mean they always will be.
If a person abstains from committing a sin, then they just "stopped sinning" in a way.
If someone who has been born-again does sin, that doesn't mean that they can't ever stop sinning, because they can stop or be stopped as they continue to be cleaned as they confess sin (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A9&version=ESV][1 John 1:9]]*) and as they walk in the light (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A7&version=ESV][I John 1:7]]*), by faith and love for Jesus Christ.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15&version=ESV][John 14:15]]* - If you love me, you will keep my commandments. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A12&version=ESV][John 14:12]]* - Truly, truly, I say to you, whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do; and greater works than these will he do, because I am going to the Father. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A21-24&version=ESV][John 14:21-24]]* - Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves me. And he who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him. Judas (not Iscariot) said to him, Lord, how is it that you will manifest yourself to us, and not to the world? Jesus answered him, If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him. Whoever does not love me does not keep my words. And the word that you hear is not mine but the Father's who sent me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We've got to love Jesus rather than evil. Jesus cleans us so that we stop committing sin (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A5-13&version=ESV][Romans 8:5-13]]*). That's sanctification. For sanctification and to inherit the Kingdom of God we must actually stop committing from a love of evil and be those who love God instead. This is true. But if a person does sin after getting born-again that doesn't mean that there will not be a point at which they will have got it under control. Now I think that because we can say that a believer, even a "sanctified" believer may "have" sin, that does not mean that they "commit" sin and it also does not mean that in having that sin that person's future is death (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A16-17&version=ESV][I John 5:16-17]]*).

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Job%2015%3A15&version=ESV][Job 15:15]]* - Behold, God puts no trust in his holy ones, and the heavens are not pure in his sight; (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A34-35&version=ESV][John 8:34-35]],36,42,51* - Jesus answered them, Truly, truly, I say to you, everyone who commits sin is a slave to sin. The slave does not remain in the house forever; the son remains forever. So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed. Jesus said to them, If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came from God and I am here. I came not of my own accord, but he sent me. Truly, truly, I say to you, if anyone keeps my word, he will never see death. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

And Jesus looked around and said to his disciples, How difficult it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God! And the disciples were amazed at his words. Is this Pharisee correct here (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%207%3A39&version=ESV][Luke 7:39]]*) in saying the woman is a sinner? The woman is at that time worshiping Jesus Christ so in that sense I would say she is "not a sinner" because I believe she is "born of God" and from the love of Jesus Christ practicing righteousness (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A7&version=ESV][I John 4:7]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A4&version=ESV][I John 3:4]],8,9*) and is justified by faith in Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A4-6&version=ESV][Romans 4:4-6]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%207%3A50&version=ESV][Luke 7:50]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A29-30&version=ESV][Romans 3:29-30]]*) and God knows her and she is by the grace of God now 'law-abiding' (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%207%3A23&version=ESV][Matthew 7:23]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%208%3A3&version=ESV][I Corinthians 8:3]]*) to the law of faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15&version=ESV][John 14:15]]*) by faith in Christ Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%207%3A39&version=ESV][Luke 7:39]]* - Now when the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said to himself, If this man were a prophet, he would have known who and what sort of woman this is who is touching him, for she is a sinner. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A4&version=ESV][I John 3:4]],8,9* - Everyone who makes a practice of sinning also practices lawlessness; sin is lawlessness. Whoever makes a practice of sinning is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. The reason the Son of God appeared was to destroy the works of the devil. No one born of God makes a practice of sinning, for God's seed abides in him, and he cannot keep on sinning because he has been born of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A11&version=ESV][Romans 6:11]]* - So you also must consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A16-18&version=ESV][Romans 6:16-18]]* - Do you not know that if you present yourselves to anyone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin, which leads to death, or of obedience, which leads to righteousness? But thanks be to God, that you who were once slaves of sin have become obedient from the heart to the standard of teaching to which you were committed, and, having been set free from sin, have become slaves of righteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

However, in the sense that we all fall short of the glory of God, and are not without sin (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A8&version=ESV][I John 1:8]]*), and sometimes make mistakes (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A15&version=ESV][Romans 14:15]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A9&version=ESV][I John 1:9]]*), one might call the woman (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%207%3A39&version=ESV][Luke 7:39]]*) here a "sinner" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%201%3A15&version=ESV][I Timothy 1:15]]*) but certainly she is no longer a sinner by "default" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A4&version=ESV][I John 3:4]],8,9*).

We can say that _we *formerly* were practitioners of sinning while we were unbelievers_ but by the grace of God no longer:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%201%3A13&version=ESV][I Timothy 1:13]]* - though *formerly* I was a blasphemer, persecutor, and insolent opponent. But I received mercy because I had acted ignorantly in unbelief, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

 #+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2011%3A32&version=ESV][Romans 11:32]],35* - For God has consigned all to disobedience, that he may have mercy on all. Or who has given a gift to him that he might be repaid? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Humility bears with one-another in love:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%204%3A1-3&version=ESV][Ephesians 4:1-3]]* - I therefore, a prisoner for the Lord, urge you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling to which you have been called, with all *humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love*, eager to maintain the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Loving as God has commanded *is* humble:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Zephaniah%202%3A3&version=ESV][Zephaniah 2:3]]* - Seek the LORD, all you humble of the land, who do his just commands; seek righteousness; seek humility; perhaps you may be hidden on the day of the anger of the LORD. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ Journal <2026-06-26 Fri 10:23> :: Amongst harassing dreams I received this morning there was one interesting dream conversation in my sleep
    which was of a young person sitting outside a popular dairy (corner store) in Dunedin asking me about justification by faith.
    And I said "With humility", and he emoted, "Well there you go." / "Well that's your answer."

    While this is true, I certainly do not think that keeping God's word is against humility at all.
    Keeping Jesus' commandments for God to see, seeking praise from God, this is not against humility.
    If somebody is self-commending, then sure, that's not humble.
    But good teaching would instruct people to be doers of the word, that we should do what God says in reality,

Having received forgiveness through faith in Jesus, we need to go on walking in godliness as we continue walking by faith in Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A3-6&version=ESV][I John 2:3-6]]* - And by this we know that we have come to know him, if we keep his commandments. Whoever says I know him but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, but whoever keeps his word, in him truly the love of God is perfected. By this we may be sure that we are in him: whoever says he abides in him ought to walk in the same way in which he walked. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So the following is what I wanted to say about how a Christian ought to act when confronted with a situation where they are called to do good to/for/towards someone who is persecuting them.
It's important for a Christian to maintain the awareness that they should not be self-commending as being righteous themself, and so a Christian should, similarly to the Apostle James suggested, be a doer rather than a judge (*James 1:23*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%204%3A11&version=ESV][James 4:11]]*), and like Jesus taught, listen and do what hypocrites who judge from the law instruct to do from the law, but not do what they themselves do, which is to judge in hypocrisy. With regards to God's commandments for them, the Christian should endeavour to be a doer of God's word in reality and at all times, rather than claim to have "done better" than someone else ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2010%3A12&version=ESV][II Corinthians 10:12]]).

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A2-4&version=ESV][Matthew 23:2-4]]* - The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses' seat, so practice and observe whatever they tell you—but not what they do. For they preach, but do not practice. They tie up heavy burdens, hard to bear, and lay them on people's shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to move them with their finger. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

And, therefore, when a person is confronted with a situation where they are tempted to withhold doing good for their enemy from a belief that "they are in the right and their enemy is in the wrong" (say from the belief that because Jesus forgave them they are the righteous one in the situation and the other person is in the wrong) they should resist that temptation because to have faith in Jesus and have His righteousness in that situation involves keeping His commandments (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%20103%3A17-18&version=ESV][Psalms 103:17-18]]*) in that situation. And so, the righteousness that one has by faith in Jesus Christ is surely actively teaching us to do good generally rather than evil, as from a love of righteousness in their heart while not self-commending (i.e. not putting oneself in the position of being the righteous one with absolute certainty, because God is the one who sees the heart and commends faith), the person is entrusting themselves to God's judgement while endeavouring to do what would please God.
So now it's easy to see that the one who truly believes in Jesus Christ also practices righteousness ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A12&version=ESV][John 14:12]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A7&version=ESV][I John 3:7]]) as Jesus did and walks like Jesus Himself walked ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A4-6&version=ESV][I John 2:4-6]]), and so the fear of God is retained (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Malachi%201%3A6&version=ESV][Malachi 1:6]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%206%3A9&version=ESV][Ephesians 6:9]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A14-17&version=ESV][John 15:14-17]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2025%3A14&version=ESV][Psalms 25:14]]*) with a genuine faith in Jesus. They have a desire to do as God has commanded, a desire to do what pleases God, remembering to do what God commands for God to see (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%20103%3A17-18&version=ESV][Psalms 103:17-18]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A21&version=ESV][John 14:21]]*).

And when God sees, He remembers. The person may not know *when* they served Jesus' family in their hour of need. The Bible does teach to do good to all:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2025%3A31-40&version=ESV][Matthew 25:31-40]]* - When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, then he will sit on his glorious throne. Before him will be gathered all the nations, and he will separate people one from another as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats. And he will place the sheep on his right, but the goats on the left. Then the King will say to those on his right, Come, you who are blessed by my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry and you gave me food, I was thirsty and you gave me drink, I was a stranger and you welcomed me, _I was naked and you clothed me, I was sick and you visited me, I was in prison and you came to me._ Then the righteous will answer him, saying, Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you drink? And when did we see you a stranger and welcome you, or naked and clothe you? And when did we see you sick or in prison and visit you? And the King will answer them, Truly, I say to you, _as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me._
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2010%3A25-37&version=ESV][Luke 10:25-37]]* - And behold, a lawyer stood up to put him to the test, saying, Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life? He said to him, What is written in the Law? How do you read it? And he answered, You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind, and your neighbor as yourself. And he said to him, You have answered correctly; do this, and you will live. But he, desiring to justify himself, said to Jesus, And who is my neighbor? Jesus replied, A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who stripped him and beat him and departed, leaving him half dead. Now by chance a priest was going down that road, and when he saw him he passed by on the other side. So likewise a Levite, when he came to the place and saw him, passed by on the other side. But a Samaritan, as he journeyed, came to where he was, and when he saw him, he had compassion. He went to him and bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he set him on his own animal and brought him to an inn and took care of him. And the next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper, saying, Take care of him, and whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I come back. Which of these three, do you think, proved to be a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers? He said, The one who showed him mercy. And Jesus said to him, You go, and do likewise. (ESV)
