If someone has genuine faith in Jesus Christ that loves Him but still holding some evil desires, then they will receive discipline from God and they are "saved" at the end of that discipline. God cleans that person up, allowing for them to struggle against sin as they trust and obey Jesus Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A4-8&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:4-8]]* - In your struggle against sin you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood. And have you forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons? My son, do not regard lightly the discipline of the Lord, nor be weary when reproved by him. For the Lord disciplines the one he loves, and chastises every son whom he receives. It is for discipline that you have to endure. God is treating you as sons. For what son is there whom his father does not discipline? If you are left without discipline, in which all have participated, then you are illegitimate children and not sons. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2013%3A13&version=ESV][Mark 13:13]]* - And you will be hated by all for my name's sake. But the one who endures to the end will be saved. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2024%3A12-13&version=ESV][Matthew 24:12-13]]* - And because lawlessness will be increased, the love of many will grow cold. But the one who endures to the end will be saved. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So there is a promise for the person who loves Jesus, and that promise is that they will be sanctified (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A18&version=ESV][Acts 26:18]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15&version=ESV][John 14:15]]*) and to be sanctified means to be cleaned up.
A person who doesn't love Jesus can't receive sanctification because sanctification is by faith in Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A18&version=ESV][Acts 26:18]]*) and obedience to Jesus for a love of our family in Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A22&version=ESV][I Peter 1:22]]*).

Jesus Christ's blood is able to clean a person from moral sin, meaning that they can have their heart, mind and soul healed in order to stop lying, idolising, coveting, stealing, committing adultery, etc. in reality from the heart for God to see, so that they are able to in reality love the way that God wants us to love.
Though we can never exceed God in holiness which means that from God's perspective, He's always going to be able to point out to us some way in which we fall short of His glory. Even the heavens are not pure in His eyes (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Job%2015%3A15&version=ESV][Job 15:15]]*).

A person who was under law may die to the law to make Christ their Master (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A4&version=ESV][Romans 7:4]]*). A person can have only one Master and Christians have Christ as their Master and what this means is that we follow Jesus in preference to anyone else, and our love for Him has to surpass anything or anyone else (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%206%3A24&version=ESV][Matthew 6:24]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2010%3A32-38&version=ESV][Matthew 10:32-38]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2016%3A25&version=ESV][Matthew 16:25]]*). So He has got to be our first agape love (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%202%3A4&version=NASB][Revelation of John 2:4]]*).

When the Scripture says "by faith Abraham obeyed" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A8&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:8]]*), Abraham's obedience was done in faith. Everyone on the Earth who has breath does deeds whether good or evil. The question is, "With faith in what or with love for what are those deeds being done?" While Abraham was loving God's word, he was doing deeds which God finds commendable. Abraham treasured God's word spoken to him. Abraham treasured the promise of God and did deeds while actually believing God's word.

Abel's offering to God was done in faith. Cain was half-hearted (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A4&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:4]]*) with his offering to the LORD, as Ananias was (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%205%3A3&version=ESV][Acts 5:3]]*). Cain having evil deeds means that Cain was not walking by faith. As I understand it, then, Cain was not doing his deeds from the love of God, but rather doing them from the love of evil:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%204%3A3-5&version=ESV][Genesis 4:3-5]]* - In the course of time Cain brought to the Lord an offering of the fruit of the ground, and Abel also brought of the firstborn of his flock and of their fat portions. And the Lord had regard for Abel and his offering, but for Cain and his offering he had no regard. So Cain was very angry, and his face fell. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A12&version=ESV][1 John 3:12]]* - We should not be like Cain, who was of the evil one and murdered his brother. And why did he murder him? *Because his own deeds were evil and his brother's righteous.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A4&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:4]]* - *By faith* Abel offered to God a more acceptable sacrifice than Cain, through which he was commended as righteous, God commending him by accepting his gifts. And through his faith, though he died, he still speaks. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I do not believe that a Christians' faith is centered on the promise that God has given to Abraham and to his offspring, Christ. If someone were to make the promise given to Abraham the foundation of their own personal faith then that person would not be on solid ground. A Christian follows Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%207%3A24&version=ESV][Matthew 7:24]]*) so treasures Jesus Christ Himself:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A15-18&version=ESV][Galatians 3:15-18]]* - To give a human example, brothers: even with a man-made covenant, no one annuls it or adds to it once it has been ratified. Now the promises were made to Abraham and to his offspring. *It does not say, And to offsprings, referring to many, but referring to one, And to your offspring, who is Christ.* This is what I mean: the law, which came 430 years afterward, does not annul a covenant previously ratified by God, so as to make the promise void. For if the inheritance comes by the law, it no longer comes by promise; but God gave it to Abraham by a promise. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So rather, a Christian becomes a partaker of the promise by having faith in Jesus Christ Himself (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A20-25&version=ESV][Romans 4:20-25]]*), by being found "in Christ" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A23-24&version=ESV][I John 3:23-24]]*).
Now that faith is still modelled on Abraham's faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A16&version=ESV][Romans 4:16]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A39-42&version=ESV][John 8:39-42]]*), and bears the same "characteristics" such as "trust in the truth" and the "fear of God" and "continuing on trusting the truth", and being a "doer of God's word" and even "obedience" to God.
But the object of a Christian's faith is Christ Himself rather than the promise given to Abraham and his descendant, Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A16&version=ESV][Galatians 3:16]]*).

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A5&version=ESV][James 2:5]]* - Listen, my beloved brothers, has not God chosen those who are poor in the world to be *rich in faith* and heirs of the kingdom, which he has promised to *those who love him*? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%202%3A6-8&version=ESV][I Peter 2:6-8]]* - For it stands in Scripture: Behold, I am laying in Zion a stone, a cornerstone chosen and precious, and whoever believes in him will not be put to shame. So the honor is for you who believe, but for those who do not believe, The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone, and A stone of stumbling, and a rock of offense. They stumble because they disobey the word, as they were destined to do. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A19-25&version=ESV][Romans 4:19-25]]* - He did not weaken in faith when he considered his own body, which was as good as dead (since he was about a hundred years old), or when he considered the barrenness of Sarah's womb. No distrust made him waver concerning the promise of God, but he grew strong in his faith as he gave glory to God, fully convinced that God was able to do what he had promised. That is why his faith was counted to him as righteousness. But the words it was counted to him were not written for his sake alone, but for ours also. _It will be counted to us who *believe in him* who raised from the dead Jesus our Lord, who was delivered up for our trespasses and raised for our justification._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A16&version=ESV][Romans 4:16]]* - That is why it depends on faith, in order that the promise may rest on grace and be guaranteed to all his offspring—not only to the adherent of the law but also to the one who shares the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A39-42&version=ESV][John 8:39-42]]* - They answered him, Abraham is our father. Jesus said to them, If you were Abraham's children, you would be doing what Abraham did, but now you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. This is not what Abraham did. You are doing what your father did. They said to him, We were not born of sexual immorality. We have one Father—even God. Jesus said to them, If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came from God and I am here. I came not of my own accord, but he sent me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The inheritance comes by promise rather than the Law, but that doesn't mean it's not by love for God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A18&version=ESV][Galatians 3:18]]* - For if the inheritance comes by the law, it no longer comes by promise; but God gave it to Abraham by a promise. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A5&version=ESV][James 2:5]]* - Listen, my beloved brothers, has not God chosen those who are poor in the world to be *rich in faith* and heirs of the kingdom, which he has promised to *those who love him*? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%208%3A12-21&version=ESV][Proverbs 8:12-21]]* - I, wisdom, dwell with prudence, and I find knowledge and discretion. The fear of the LORD is hatred of evil. Pride and arrogance and the way of evil and perverted speech I hate. I have counsel and sound wisdom; I have insight; I have strength. By me kings reign, and rulers decree what is just; by me princes rule, and nobles, all who govern justly. _I love those who love me, and those who seek me diligently find me. Riches and honor are with me, enduring wealth and righteousness._ My fruit is better than gold, even fine gold, and my yield than choice silver. _I walk in the way of righteousness, in the paths of justice, granting an inheritance to those who love me, and filling their treasuries._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Abraham had faith in the promise that was given to Him and to Christ, but that promise was to them. Christians need to have Abraham's faith but with regards to the promises given to us:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A15-16&version=ESV][Galatians 3:15-16]]* - To give a human example, brothers: even with a man-made covenant, no one annuls it or adds to it once it has been ratified. Now the promises were made to Abraham and to his offspring. It does not say, And to offsprings, referring to many, but referring to one, And to your offspring, who is Christ. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So neither the Law, nor "obedience", nor love for God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A5&version=ESV][James 2:5]]*) are "against" justification by faith. But to seek justification by the Law rather than by faith is what is the problem:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%204%3A21&version=ESV][Galatians 4:21]]* - Tell me, you who desire to be under the law, do you not listen to the law? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A7&version=ESV][Galatians 5:7]]* - You were running well. Who hindered you from obeying the truth? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Biblical obedience issues from a heart that loves the Truth (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A45&version=ESV][Luke 6:45]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2081%3A15&version=ESV][Psalms 81:15]]*).

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A46-49&version=ESV][Luke 6:46-49]]* - Why do you call me Lord, Lord, and not do what I tell you? _Everyone who comes to me and hears my words and does them, I will show you *what he is like: he is like* a man building a house, who dug deep and laid the foundation on the rock_. And when a flood arose, the stream broke against that house and could not shake it, because it had been well built. But the one who hears and does not do them is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation. When the stream broke against it, immediately it fell, and the ruin of that house was great. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A3-6&version=ESV][I John 2:3-6]]* - And by this we know that we have come to know him, if we keep his commandments. Whoever says I know him but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, but whoever keeps his word, in him truly the love of God is perfected. By this we may be sure that we are in him: whoever says he abides in him ought to walk in the same way in which he walked. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2010%3A4-6&version=ESV][II Corinthians 10:4-6]]* - For the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh but have divine power to destroy strongholds. We destroy arguments and every lofty opinion raised against the knowledge of God, and take every thought captive to obey Christ, being ready to punish every disobedience, when your obedience is complete. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A14&version=ESV][I John 3:14]]* - We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. Whoever does not love abides in death. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Walking by the spirit involves obeying our Master Jesus Christ from a love of Jesus Christ. Even though we are not "under law", it's still necessary to _by *faith*_ obey Jesus Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A14-18&version=ESV][Romans 6:14-18]]* - For sin will have no dominion over you, since you are not under law but under grace. What then? Are we to sin because we are not under law but under grace? By no means! Do you not know that if you present yourselves to anyone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin, which leads to death, or of obedience, which leads to righteousness? But thanks be to God, that you who were once slaves of sin have become obedient from the heart to the standard of teaching to which you were committed, and, having been set free from sin, have become slaves of righteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Christians who did not have a background as a Jew under Mosaic law who come to (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%206%3A45&version=ESV][John 6:45]]*) Jesus Christ still make Him their Master (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%206%3A9&version=ESV][Ephesians 6:9]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A14-17&version=ESV][John 15:14-17]]*). We should use our freedom wisely, doing things that resemble the purpose, goal, fulfillment of the law, which is serving one-another. Jesus saying that He did not come to be served but to serve (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2020%3A25-28&version=ESV][Matthew 20:25-28]]*), and that "the older will serve the younger" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%209%3A12&version=ESV][Romans 9:12]]*), means that those who "outrank us" in God's Kingdom (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%203%3A16&version=ESV][Luke 3:16]]*) are serving us (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%204%3A6-12&version=ESV][II Corinthians 4:6-12]]*), and what to serve Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%206%3A6&version=ESV][Ephesians 6:6]]*) who didn't come to be served really means for those who seek to serve Him and to imitate Him is that they are obligated (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A6&version=ESV][I John 2:6]]*) to serve Jesus' family, especially those who are younger in God's Kingdom:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2025%3A40&version=ESV][Matthew 25:40]]* - And the King will answer them, Truly, I say to you, as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus is the ultimate servant and thus the greatest in the Kingdom, the one who we need forgiveness from ultimately.

Jesus didn't come to Earth to judge but, rather, to save, but He does judge (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2011%3A28-32&version=ESV][I Corinthians 11:28-32]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%2019%3A11&version=ESV][Revelation of John 19:11]]*) and will judge.
Jesus didn't come to Earth to be served but, rather, to serve (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2020%3A25-28&version=ESV][Matthew 20:25-28]]*), but He is served (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A18&version=ESV][Romans 14:18]]*) and will be served (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Daniel%207%3A13-14&version=ESV][Daniel 7:13-14]]*).
So when people say "Jesus didn't come to earth to judge, and that He didn't come to be served", it's still right to say we need to serve Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A15-23&version=ESV][Romans 6:15-23]]*) rather than evil, and it's still right to say that Jesus will judge the living and the dead (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2010%3A41-44&version=ESV][Acts 10:41-44]]*).

Even Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are served by Jesus Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%208%3A11&version=ESV][Matthew 8:11]]* - I tell you, many will come from east and west and recline at table with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2012%3A37&version=ESV][Luke 12:37]]* - Blessed are those servants whom the master finds awake when he comes. Truly, I say to you, he will dress himself for service and have them recline at table, and he will come and serve them. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2018%3A4&version=ESV][Matthew 18:4]]* - Whoever humbles himself like this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So understanding this passage, Jesus is in the full context implying that humbling oneself to serve others is what is considered to be great in the Kingdom of Heaven:

So in God's Kingdom lead by example, rather than enforce by 'lording' (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Nehemiah%205%3A15&version=ESV][Nehemiah 5:15]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%205%3A1-3&version=ESV][I Peter 5:1-3]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%203%3A9&version=ESV][II Thessalonians 3:9]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%203%3A17&version=ESV][Philippians 3:17]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%204%3A9&version=ESV][Philippians 4:9]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%201%3A5-6&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 1:5-6]]*).

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2022%3A25-26&version=ESV][Luke 22:25-26]]* - So Jesus declared, “The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those in authority over them call themselves benefactors. But you shall not be like them. Instead, the greatest among you should be like the youngest, and the one who leads like the one who serves. (engbsb2020eb)
#+END_QUOTE

I believe that the writing of God's commandments on our hearts comes with sanctification after being born-again (given a new heart of flesh). A heart of stone can't be circumcised (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2011%3A19-20&version=ESV][Ezekiel 11:19-20]]*). God gives us a new heart that fears Him and is responsive to correction (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2036%3A25-28&version=ESV][Ezekiel 36:25-28]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2018%3A31&version=ESV][Ezekiel 18:31]]*) then circumcises our hearts to love Him with *all* our heart (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy%2030%3A6&version=ESV][Deuteronomy 30:6]]*), and loving God with all our heart I do believe involves having the complete (rather than partial) love of God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A4-6&version=ESV][I John 2:4-6]]*) which means that we love others how God has loved us, not merely appreciating God ([[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cFGZ_eaj2LE][youtube.com:  John Piper on Why We Glorify God ' by ' Enjoying Him {@ universegroove }]]) but also loving one-another as we have been loved by God. With the new heart that fears God and is responsive to correction and from the love of Jesus Christ we then by faith love our neighbour the way that is actually loving our neighbour (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2013%3A9-10&version=ESV][Romans 13:9-10]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A3-4&version=ESV][Romans 8:3-4]]*).

God is also glorified by deeds done by His power by faith in Him and in love for others:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%201%3A9-12&version=ESV][II Thessalonians 1:9-12]]* - They will suffer the punishment of eternal destruction, away from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of his might, when he comes on that day to be glorified in his saints, and to be marveled at among all who have believed, because our testimony to you was believed. To this end we always pray for you, that our God may make you worthy of his calling and may fulfill every resolve for good and every work of faith by his power, so that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

(ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

God writing His laws for us on our hearts involves us learning them, and having the love of God completed in us involves putting it into practice in reality:

And they shall not teach, each one his neighbor and each one his brother, saying, Know the Lord, for they shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest. (ESV)

#+END_QUOTE

Love for Jesus:

In faith and love, keep Jesus' word:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%201%3A13&version=ESV][II Timothy 1:13]]* - Follow the pattern of the sound words that you have heard from me, in the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A21-24&version=ESV][John 14:21-24]]* - Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves me. Judas (not Iscariot) said to him, Lord, how is it that you will manifest yourself to us, and not to the world? Jesus answered him, If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him. Whoever does not love me does not keep my words. And the word that you hear is not mine but the Father's who sent me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I am speaking in human terms, because of your natural limitations. #+END_QUOTE

If we do what Jesus commands us then we will love one-another (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A14-17&version=ESV][John 15:14-17]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1-2&version=ESV][I John 5:1-2]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

Jesus instructed His disciples to call no man on earth "father". This instruction, therefore, is for the Christian. After all, Jesus' father was not Joseph and yet Jesus was able to keep the 5th commandment to honor father and mother, and Jesus said Himself that He honors His father, and says that His father is God. And Father God said that Jesus is His Son who He is well pleased with:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A1&version=ESV][Matthew 23:1]]* - Then Jesus said to the crowds and to his disciples, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A9&version=ESV][Matthew 23:9]]* - And call no man your father on earth, for you have one Father, who is in heaven. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%208%3A21-22&version=ESV][Matthew 8:21-22]]* - Another of the disciples said to him, Lord, let me first go and bury my father. And Jesus said to him, Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Disciples of Jesus Christ should not give the title of 'father' to anybody else other than to God because the title belongs to God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2022%3A21&version=ESV][Matthew 22:21]]* - They said, Caesar's. Then he said to them, Therefore render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and *to God the things that are God's.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Malachi%201%3A6&version=ESV][Malachi 1:6]]* - A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If then I am a father, where is my honor? And if I am a master, where is my fear? says the LORD of hosts to you, O priests, who despise my name. But you say, How have we despised your name? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

With regard to Jesus Christ's commandment to call no man on earth "father", the [Mark 4:17] "trouble or persecution on account of the word" might refer to
any difficulties as people oppose the fact that one practices this commandment in reality. The good soil would not fall away:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A18&version=ESV][John 5:18]]* - This was why the Jews were seeking all the more to kill him, because not only was he breaking the Sabbath, but he was even calling God his own Father, making himself equal with God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%204%3A17&version=ESV][Mark 4:17]]* - And they have no root in themselves, but endure for a while; then, when tribulation or persecution arises on account of the word, immediately they fall away. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

When the stream broke against it, immediately it fell, and the ruin of that house was great. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A46-49&version=ESV][Luke 6:46-49]]* - Why do you call me Lord, Lord, and not do what I tell you? _Everyone who comes to me and hears my words and does them, I will show you *what he is like: he is like* a man building a house, who dug deep and laid the foundation on the rock_. And when a flood arose, the stream broke against that house and could not shake it, because it had been well built. # The traditional interpretation of Mark 7:6-13 (I found this on the chaimbentorah website) is that Jesus was speaking to the priest and Pharisees about the fifth commandment which is to honor your father and mother. Jesus was saying that you neglect your duty to help your parents financially by saying that all your resources are a corban or a gift to God but you use that as an excuse not to help your parents as your parents would rather starve to death than steal from God. Then you keep those resources for your own benefit. 

The title of 'father' belongs to God for the person to keeps Jesus' commandment to call no man on earth father for they have one father who is in heaven.

#+END_QUOTE

But we must do so from the love of God ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2081%3A15&version=ESV][Psalms 81:15]]) and of Jesus Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A42&version=ESV][John 8:42]]*) and through faith in Jesus Christ's name (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A12&version=ESV][John 1:12]]*) and God will discipline every son He receives into loving Him and one-another in the way He has commanded (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A9&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:9]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A4-8&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:4-8]]*).

The title of 'father' belongs to God, as Jesus has commanded, and as Jesus has instructed we should give God what belongs to God. And so, to pressure someone into not keeping Jesus' commandment to call no man on earth 'father' is actually to pressure them into dishonoring God.
It's not dishonoring to one's previous parents to give the title of 'father' to God and no longer to one's previous father. So by saying it's dishonoring to not abide by this commandment from Jesus Christ is actually to make void the commandment of Jesus Christ who is God the Son, in order to establish a tradition that is against the teachings of Christ.

Now a Christian is instructed by the Apostle Peter to honor all people [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%202%3A17&version=ESV][1 Peter 2:17]], and so to keep Christ's commandment to call no man on earth father, is not against honoring one's previous parents because both Christ's commandment and the Apostle Peter's instruction are able to be kept at the same time.

Now since these people who appear as my previous parents, are truly no longer my parents,
then in understanding Jesus' teaching that anyone who comes to Him and does not hate their mother and father
cannot be His disciple, it's correct to say that there is no need for me to hate these people who are not my parents if I am to come to Jesus Christ some more.

The people they used to be were those who used to be my parents, and I hate my old life.
I simply can't affirm that these people I formerly regarded as being my parents, are my parents anymore if I am to love them in reality how I'm commanded to love.

The word of God given through Jesus is what we are born-again by.

So Jesus Christ and His brothers are all sons of God, Jesus being the first.
But as Paul made it clear, one person may father another through the gospel.

So Jesus can also be regarded as a spiritual father (in the new genaeology).
But Jesus instructs His distiples to call His father their father.

Paul clearly led people to be imitators of Christ for themself as he is an imitator of Christ, so Paul's followers should imitate him in imitating Christ:

+ [[https://www.earlychristianwritings.com/text/polycarp-lightfoot.html][Polycarp 5:3]] :: In like manner also the younger men must be blameless in all things,
    caring for purity before everything and curbing themselves from every
    evil. For it is a good thing to refrain from lusts in the world, for
    every lust warreth against the Spirit, and neither whoremongers
    nor effeminate persons nor defilers of themselves with men shall
    inherit the kingdom of God, neither they that do untoward things.
    Wherefore it is right to abstain from all these things, submitting
    yourselves to the presbyters and deacons as to God and Christ. The
    virgins must walk in a blameless and pure conscience.

If a person has come to have the love of Jesus Christ in them then praise God because it's happened by God's grace. Forgiveness is in Christ for those who by the grace of God have come around to having the love of God in their heart and they now practice righteousness rather than doing deeds done from a love of evil.

But we certainly have to continue walking by faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2010%3A37-39&version=ESV][Hebrews 10:37-39]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]*) and love (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A14-18&version=ESV][Romans 14:14-18]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A19-21&version=ESV][I John 4:19-21]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A14-18&version=ESV][Romans 14:14-18]]* - I know and am persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself, but it is unclean for anyone who thinks it unclean. For if your brother is grieved by what you eat, you are *no longer walking in love*. By what you eat, do not destroy the one for whom Christ died. So do not let what you regard as good be spoken of as evil. For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking but of righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit. Whoever thus serves Christ is acceptable to God and approved by men. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2010%3A37-39&version=ESV][Hebrews 10:37-39]]* - For, Yet a little while, and the coming one will come and will not delay; _but my righteous one shall live by faith, and if he shrinks back, my soul has no pleasure in him. *But we are not of those who shrink back and are destroyed, but of those who have faith and preserve their souls*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's clear that when a deed is done in faith it is good, and when a deed is not done in faith, it's evil.

Whatever does not proceed from faith sin (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]*), and sin is lawlessness (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A4&version=ESV][I John 3:4]]*), and any obedience that doesn't come from a love for the truth is feigned (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A45&version=ESV][Luke 6:45]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2081%3A15&version=ESV][Psalms 81:15]]*). We must be law of faith abiding (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15&version=ESV][John 14:15]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A27&version=ESV][Romans 3:27]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%209%3A21&version=ESV][I Corinthians 9:21]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2013%3A41&version=ESV][Matthew 13:41]]*).

If a person doubts, then they shouldn't eat, because to eat while doubting would be to commit sin:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]* - But whoever has doubts is condemned if he eats, because the eating is not from faith. For _whatever does not proceed from faith is sin._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A4&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:4]]* - *By faith* Abel offered to God a more acceptable sacrifice than Cain, through which he was commended as righteous, God commending him by accepting his gifts. And through his faith, though he died, he still speaks. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

If someone loves Jesus Christ then they have forgiveness from Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2010%3A41-44&version=ESV][Acts 10:41-44]]*).
If someone has forgiveness from Jesus then they must now love Jesus Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%207%3A40-50&version=ESV][Luke 7:40-50]]*) in their heart:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%202%3A8-9&version=ESV][Ephesians 2:8-9]]* - For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A18&version=ESV][Acts 26:18]]* - to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, *that they may receive* forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are sanctified by faith in me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Christians *must* be law-abiding by Jesus' commandments (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2013%3A38-43&version=ESV][Matthew 13:38-43]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A23-24&version=ESV][I John 3:23-24]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%209%3A21&version=ESV][I Corinthians 9:21]]*) but not under the Book of the Law (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A10&version=ESV][Galatians 3:10]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A23&version=ESV][Galatians 3:23]]*) and not reliant on the works of the law (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A20&version=ESV][Romans 3:20]]*), the works of the Law being inclusive of the external actions.

It's the _[[strongs:G458]['anomian']]_ (i.e. the wicked; those who hate righteousness, those who prefer evil to Jesus Christ) who don't abide in Jesus, and who not abiding are cast out, and wither and are eventually burned. God is longsuffering and merciful but we do need to become those who end up bearing good fruit. If a person loves Jesus Christ more than anyone or anything else, then they will bear good fruit:

Just as the weeds are gathered and burned with fire, so will it be at the close of the age. Christians are justified by the law of faith in Jesus Christ ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A26-28&version=ESV][Romans 3:26-28]]) apart from [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] the works of the law (Romans 3:20-22) and rather than by the Old Covenant Law. It's faith in heart which God sees (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A10&version=ESV][Romans 10:10]]*).

When God justifies an ungodly person for their faith in Jesus, it's as they are trusting in Jesus Christ and His words, and the person is forgiven of their former sin, just like it shows in (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2018%3A20-24&version=ESV][Ezekiel 18:20-24]]*), and going forward while holding their faith in Jesus is cleaned up and they will also be practicing righteousness, doing the deeds of Jesus. In other words, a person may be ungodly and have evil deeds, but when they put their faith in Jesus Christ, their former evil deeds are no longer taken into account. And holding faith in Jesus, they practice righteousness. They are obeying the gospel of God as they are holding their faith in Jesus Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A3-8&version=ESV][Romans 4:3-8]]* - For what does the Scripture say? Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness. Now to the one who works, his wages are not counted as a gift but as his due. And to the one who does not work but trusts him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted as righteousness, just as David also speaks of the blessing of the one to whom God counts righteousness apart from works: Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven, and whose sins are covered; blessed is the man against whom the Lord will not count his sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A12&version=ESV][John 14:12]]* - Truly, truly, I say to you, whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do; and greater works than these will he do, because I am going to the Father. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A person cannot have justification while they are presently committing willful sin. Because what is not done in faith is sin and we need faith in Jesus for justification. So if a person does commit sin, then they need to return to faith:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%201%3A17-18&version=ESV][Romans 1:17-18]]* - For the gospel reveals the righteousness of God that comes by faith from start to finish, just as it is written: “The righteous will live by faith.” The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness. (engbsb2020eb)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2010%3A37-39&version=ESV][Hebrews 10:37-39]]* - For, Yet a little while, and the coming one will come and will not delay; _but my righteous one shall live by faith, and if he shrinks back, my soul has no pleasure in him. *But we are not of those who shrink back and are destroyed, but of those who have faith and preserve their souls*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The person must not ultimately remain ungodly if they are to avoid the wrath of God. Someone who is overcome by and enslaved to ungodliness to the suppression of the truth, to the ruin of their faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%201%3A18-19&version=ESV][I Timothy 1:18-19]]*), will still receive the wrath of God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%201%3A18-25&version=ESV][Romans 1:18-25]]* - For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven *against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men*, who by their unrighteousness suppress the truth. For what can be known about God is plain to them, because God has shown it to them. For his invisible attributes, namely, his eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly perceived, ever since the creation of the world, in the things that have been made. So they are without excuse. For although they knew God, they did not honor him as God or give thanks to him, but they became futile in their thinking, and their foolish hearts were darkened. Claiming to be wise, they became fools, and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images resembling mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles. Therefore God gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to impurity, to the dishonoring of their bodies among themselves, because they exchanged the truth about God for a lie and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever! Amen. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We need to continue to hold fast to the truth of the Gospel. It's important to continue to hold fast to what is of first importance. Holding fast to these most important doctrines of faith, eventually the believer will "win out", because they're holding fast to the actual truth:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A1-8&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:1-8]]* - Now I would remind you, brothers, of the gospel I preached to you, which you received, in which you stand, and *by which you are being saved, if you hold fast to the word I preached to you—unless you believed in vain.* For I delivered to you as of _first importance what I also received: that Christ died for our sins in accordance with the Scriptures, that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day in accordance with the Scriptures,_ and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve. Then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers at one time, most of whom are still alive, though some have fallen asleep. Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles. Last of all, as to one untimely born, he appeared also to me. (ESV)

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2012%3A3&version=ESV][Proverbs 12:3]]* - No one is established by wickedness, but the root of the righteous will never be moved. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Brothers, I do not consider that I have made it my own. But one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus. Let those of us who are mature think this way, and if in anything you think otherwise, God will reveal that also to you. Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and they glory in their shame, with *minds set on earthly things*. But our citizenship is in heaven, and from it we await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ, who will transform our lowly body to be like his glorious body, by the power that enables him even to subject all things to himself. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2012%3A9&version=ESV][Romans 12:9]]* - *Let love be genuine.* /Abhor what is evil;/ _hold fast to what is good._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%207%3A9&version=ESV][Isaiah 7:9]]* - And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If *you are not firm in faith, you will not be firm at all.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

As we exercise faith in Jesus Christ, holding fast to the truth, we are saved through sanctification and that faith in Jesus Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%202%3A13&version=ESV][II Thessalonians 2:13]]* - But we ought always to give thanks to God for you, brothers beloved by the Lord, because God chose you as the firstfruits to be saved, through sanctification by the Spirit and belief in the truth. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A justified person is "being saved" / "being sanctified" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A24&version=ESV][John 5:24]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A18&version=ESV][Acts 26:18]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2017%3A19&version=ESV][John 17:19]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2010%3A12-17&version=ESV][Hebrews 10:12-17]]*), i.e. cleaned up (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%203%3A11-13&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 3:11-13]],5:23*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%203%3A11-13&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 3:11-13]],5:23* - Now may our God and Father himself, and our Lord Jesus, direct our way to you, and may the Lord make you increase and abound in love for one another and for all, as we do for you, so that he may establish your hearts blameless in holiness before our God and Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all his saints. Now may the God of peace himself sanctify you completely, and may your whole spirit and soul and body be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Confession of faith unto salvation:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A9-10&version=ESV][Romans 10:9-10]]* - because, if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. For with the heart one believes and is justified, and with the mouth one confesses and is saved. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A15&version=ESV][I John 4:15]]* - Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him, and he in God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

With the mouth one confesses and is saved. I confess that Jesus is the Son of God.

I do not want to be yoked with people who stubbornly refuse to provide from their mouth a confession that Jesus is the Son of God. God can see from His perspective if they are actually believers, but I can't see everything from God's perspective, and so I think I should separate from them, because I feel frequently opposed by them.

[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A21&version=ESV][Romans 3:21]] speaks of the righteousness [[strongs:G1343][(G1343 dikaiosynē)]] of God [[strongs:G2316][(G2316 Theou)]] apart from [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] law [[strongs:G3551][(G3551 nomou)]].
The righteousness of God through faith in Jesus *is* that righteousness. Simply put, God sees when someone has faith in Jesus Christ and someone who abides in Jesus Christ's commandments has it, not commending themselves and comparing themselves with others *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2010%3A11-12&version=ESV][II Corinthians 10:11-12]]* but, rather, seeking to please God who sees the heart.

We must make it our aim to please God without hypocrisy (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2012%3A1-9&version=ESV][Luke 12:1-9]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%202%3A5&version=ESV][II Timothy 2:5]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ecclesiastes%2012%3A13-14&version=ESV][Ecclesiastes 12:13-14]]* - The end of the matter; all has been heard. Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole duty of man. For God will bring every deed into judgment, with every secret thing, whether good or evil. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%205%3A9-12&version=ESV][II Corinthians 5:9-12]]* - So whether we are at home or away, we make it our aim to please him. For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each one may receive what is due for what he has done in the body, whether good or evil. Therefore, knowing the fear of the Lord, we persuade others. But what we are is known to God, and I hope it is known also to your conscience. We are not commending ourselves to you again but giving you cause to boast about us, so that you may be able to answer those who boast about outward appearance and not about what is in the heart. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2019%3A23&version=ESV][Proverbs 19:23]]* - The fear of the LORD leads to life, and whoever has it rests satisfied; he will not be visited by harm. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%202%3A5&version=ESV][II Timothy 2:5]]* - An athlete is not crowned unless he competes according to the rules. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

    If then we entreat the Lord that He would forgive us, we also ought

And it's apart from the [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] the works of the law that we are justified by:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A28&version=ESV][Romans 3:28]]* - For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from works [[strongs:G2041][(G2041 ergōn; works)]] of the law [[strongs:G3551][(G3551 nomou; of the Law)]]. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Now imagine if someone called God their father, but in a way that was displeasing to God because their heart wasn't right. So doing what Jesus says without hypocrisy is clearly also about a correct heart posture towards God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%209%3A23-27&version=ESV][Luke 9:23-27]]* - And he said to all, If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me. For whoever would save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake will save it. For what does it profit a man if he gains the whole world and loses or forfeits himself? For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words, of him will the Son of Man be ashamed when he comes in his glory and the glory of the Father and of the holy angels. But I tell you truly, there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A42&version=ESV][John 8:42]]* - Jesus said to them, If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came from God and I am here. I came not of my own accord, but he sent me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So the faith we need to be found by God having is a loving faith in Jesus Christ. That doesn't mean that there are not any works associated with that faith (but God looks at the heart), and it doesn't mean that there are not any commandments / law associated with that faith that the person who is commended was trying to abide by (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A8&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:8]]*). Walking by faith involves seeking to please God as opposed to committing sin (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A24-25&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:24-25]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A4&version=ESV][I John 3:4]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A4&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:4]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2010%3A26-29&version=ESV][Hebrews 10:26-29]]*).

The righteousness [[strongs:G1343][(G1343 dikaiosynē)]] of God [[strongs:G2316][(G2316 Theou)]] apart from [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] law [[strongs:G3551][(G3551 nomou)]] certainly means that there is an "alien" righteousness that a person can have *by faith in* the person who *is* righteous, Jesus Christ. I think of it a bit like a [[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pointer_(computer_programming)]["pointer"]] in computer programming.
That faith is not a hatred of Jesus Christ, but is a love for Jesus Christ.

We "pursue" Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%202%3A22&version=ESV][II Timothy 2:22]]* - So flee youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, along with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Why does a person decide to keep Jesus' commandments? It should be out of a loving faith in God, loving righteousness, and the only way to actually keep His commandments commendably is for them to be done out of faith and love for the truth (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15&version=ESV][John 14:15]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A31-47&version=ESV][John 8:31-47]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2011%3A22-32&version=ESV][I Corinthians 11:22-32]]* - What! Do you not have houses to eat and drink in? Or do you despise the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I commend you in this? No, I will not. For I received from the Lord what I also delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night when he was betrayed took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it, and said, This is my body which is for you. Do this in remembrance of me. In the same way also he took the cup, after supper, saying, This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me. For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes. Whoever, therefore, eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of profaning the body and blood of the Lord. Let a person examine himself, then, and so eat of the bread and drink of the cup. For anyone who eats and drinks without discerning (*[[https://biblehub.com/greek/1252.htm][G1252 diakrinó]]*) the body eats and drinks judgment on himself. That is why many of you are weak and ill, and some have died. But *if we judged ourselves truly, we would not be judged.* But when we are judged by the Lord, we are disciplined so that we may not be condemned along with the world. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

What faith choris law means is that it's the faith that is counted distinctly from any corresponding works or law, the way in which you could count a person's heart attitude as distinct from any external action or commandment.
God looks at the faith, the heart posture to Him, rather than His commendation resting solely on external actions (For example, "managing to confess sin verbally to another follower of Christ", or "managing to use exactly bread and wine when taking communion").

Salvation involves both justification /and/ sanctification, though, justification being God's righteousness given to the person who has a heart attitude of loving faith in Jesus Christ and sanctification which is a process of being cleaned up as we hold our faith in Jesus and love our family in Christ, and we must continue on in the faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20John%201%3A9-10&version=ESV][II John 1:9-10]]*) which means to continue in agreement with Jesus Christ (who He is and what He did and what He taught), rather than disagreeing with Him.
Salvation involves God *working* in us as we obey Jesus Christ. As we (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Exodus%2014%3A16&version=ESV][Exodus 14:16]]*) by faith obey Jesus Christ, God works (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Exodus%2014%3A13&version=ESV][Exodus 14:13]]*) His salvation in us:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%202%3A12-16&version=ESV][Philippians 2:12-16]]* - Therefore, my beloved, as you have always obeyed, so now, not only as in my presence but much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling, for it is God who works in you, both to will and to work for his good pleasure. Do all things without grumbling or questioning, that you may be blameless and innocent, children of God without blemish in the midst of a crooked and twisted generation, among whom you shine as lights in the world, holding fast to the word of life, so that in the day of Christ I may be proud that I did not run in vain or labor in vain. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Justification clearly does not mean the same thing as salvation as [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A10&version=ESV][Romans 10:10]] shows. But if a person is justified for having faith in Jesus Christ in their heart then they can be saved (they then may call out to God for deliverance saying, for example, "Please save me, LORD Jesus Christ, Yahweh, Son of God."):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A21&version=ESV][Romans 3:21]],9:31,10:4-10* - But now the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, although the Law and the Prophets bear witness to it— but that Israel who pursued a law that would lead to righteousness did not succeed in reaching that law. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes. For Moses writes about the righteousness that is based on the law, that the person who does the commandments shall live by them. But the righteousness based on faith says, Do not say in your heart, Who will ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down) or Who will descend into the abyss? (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead). But what does it say? The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart (that is, the word of faith that we proclaim); because, if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. For *with the heart one believes and is justified*, and with the mouth one confesses and is saved. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A14-21&version=ESV][Romans 10:14-21]]* - *But how are they to call on him in whom they have not believed?* And how are they to believe in him of whom they have never heard? And how are they to hear without someone preaching? And how are they to preach unless they are sent? As it is written, How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the good news! But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Isaiah says, Lord, who has believed what he has heard from us? So faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ. But I ask, have they not heard? Indeed they have, for Their voice has gone out to all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world. But I ask, did Israel not understand? First Moses says, I will make you jealous of those who are not a nation; with a foolish nation I will make you angry. Then Isaiah is so bold as to say, I have been found by those who did not seek me; I have shown myself to those who did not ask for me. But of Israel he says, All day long I have held out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A person is justified by faith in Jesus Christ in their heart, and they are saved as they hold that faith. As they hold that faith, they produce deeds done in faith. For example, a person may get water baptised while holding faith in Jesus Christ, or while holding faith in Jesus Christ they may confess to another that "Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, who came into the world from God and died for our sins on a tree and rose from the dead on the third day and has ascended into heaven":

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A14-17&version=ESV][James 2:14-17]]* - What good is it, my brothers, if someone says he has faith but does not have works? Can that faith save him? If a *brother or sister* is poorly clothed and lacking in daily food, and one of you says to them, Go in peace, be warmed and filled, without giving them the things needed for the body, what good is that? So also faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A9-10&version=ESV][Romans 10:9-10]]* - because, if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. For with the heart one believes and is justified, and with the mouth one confesses and is saved. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2016%3A16&version=ESV][Mark 16:16]]* - Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So faith is counted distinctly from [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] any corresponding external actions:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A20-25&version=ESV][Romans 3:20-25]]* - For by works of the law no human being will be justified in his sight, since through the law comes knowledge of sin. But now the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, although the Law and the Prophets bear witness to it— the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe. For there is no distinction: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, and are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God put forward as a propitiation by his blood, to be received by faith. This was to show God's righteousness, because in his divine forbearance he had passed over former sins. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So, for example, we should never 'rely' merely (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2016%3A15-16&version=ESV][Mark 16:15-16]]*) on "having been baptised" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%208%3A13-23&version=ESV][Acts 8:13-23]]*) or on merely, say, being physically circumcised (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A1-7&version=ESV][Galatians 5:1-7]]*).
But we must have a circumcised heart (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A29&version=ESV][Romans 2:29]]*).
Baptism, like confessing with one's mouth (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A9&version=ESV][Romans 10:9]]*), is a visible testimony of one's faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2012%3A8&version=ESV][Luke 12:8]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%206%3A12&version=ESV][I Timothy 6:12]]*).

"Putting on Christ" involves walking out our faith in Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2013%3A14&version=ESV][Rom 13:14]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%204%3A1&version=ESV][I Peter 4:1]]*), for example, calling no man on earth our father because we trust and obey His word.

In trusting Jesus Christ and His words, and obeying His commandments we are led by His Spirit. By faith we trust and obey Jesus Christ to call no man on earth our Father, for we have faith in Jesus that we have one Father who is in heaven (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A14-17&version=ESV][Romans 8:14-17]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A9&version=ESV][Matthew 23:9]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A20&version=ESV][I John 5:20]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A14-17&version=ESV][Romans 8:14-17]]* - For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God. For you did not receive the spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you have received the Spirit of adoption as sons, by whom we cry, Abba! Father! The Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God, and if children, then heirs—heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ, provided we suffer with him in order that we may also be glorified with him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A9&version=ESV][Matthew 23:9]]* - And call no man your father on earth, for you have one Father, who is in heaven. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A20&version=ESV][I John 5:20]]* - And we know that *the Son of God has come and has given us understanding, so that we may know him who is true*; and we are in him who is true, in his Son Jesus Christ. He is the true God and eternal life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Faith in Jesus involves believing who He is (Son of God, Messiah) and remaining faithful to Him and obeying out of faith, just as Abraham did. Our faith is modelled after Abraham's faith. If a person denies who Jesus is then they deny His name. A person who claims to have faith in Jesus because they "love their neighbour" but at the same time denies who Jesus actually is is not loving their neigbour at all:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%203%3A8&version=ESV][Revelation of John 3:8]]* - I know your works. Behold, I have set before you an open door, which no one is able to shut. I know that you have but little power, and yet you have kept my word and have not denied my name. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2016%3A8-9&version=ESV][John 16:8-9]]* - And when he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin and righteousness and judgment: concerning sin, because they do not believe in me; (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Undergoing baptism of water is something Christians do in walking out their faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A25-27&version=ESV][Galatians 3:25-27]]*). Christians must maintain faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%203%3A6&version=ESV][Hebrews 3:6]]*) and a good conscience (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%201%3A18-19&version=ESV][I Timothy 1:18-19]]*) and baptism is done in faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2016%3A16&version=ESV][Mark 16:16]]*) as an appeal to God for a good conscience (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%203%3A21&version=ESV][I Peter 3:21]]*) through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

The person "doing the will of Father God" is the same who "believes" and is the person who is the "doer in reality" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A21&version=ESV][John 3:21]]*), not merely by lipservice (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%207%3A6-8&version=ESV][Mark 7:6-8]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Samuel%2016%3A7&version=ESV][1 Samuel 16:7]]*) and is the person who regardless of performance in the vineyard (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%203%3A11-15&version=ESV][I Corinthians 3:11-15]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2025%3A24-30&version=ESV][Matthew 25:24-30]]*) does end up /"going"/ to work in the vineyard (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2021%3A24-32&version=ESV][Matthew 21:24-32]]*). And "going to work in the vineyard" is "embarking like Abraham" to "do the will of God". 

The one who truly believes in Jesus will walk like He walked, doing the things that Jesus did (things like calling no man on earth 'father', but rather naming God as their father as Jesus did):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A12&version=ESV][John 14:12]]* - Truly, truly, I say to you, whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do; and greater works than these will he do, because I am going to the Father. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A6&version=ESV][I John 2:6]]* - whoever says he abides in him ought to walk in the same way in which he walked. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Peter%202%3A19&version=ESV][II Peter 2:19]]* - They promise them freedom, but they themselves are slaves of corruption. For whatever overcomes a person, to that he is enslaved. (ESV)

Seek to please God who sees everything. The person who does the will of God in reality doesn't require other mere humans to commend them in order to have confidence. Rather, the person who does the will of God in reality knows God sees when they do as instructed of by Him, and so they just seek to do what God has instructed:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2010%3A11-12&version=ESV][II Corinthians 10:11-12]]* - Let such a person understand that what we say by letter when absent, we do when present. But when they measure themselves by one another and compare themselves with one another, they are without understanding. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

If we see others not doing the will of God, then we should in similar fashion to Jesus teach others what to do (i.e. what Jesus' instruction is) but not judge them if they do not appear do it after instructing them, but rather quote *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2012%3A44-50&version=ESV][John 12:44-50]]* to them. Let them know that Jesus' word will judge on the last day but that Jesus has come to save and we should imitate His patience. Let them know that you'll still endeavour to keep Jesus' commandment. Saying it once is enough. Staying silent is also an option if they insist that Jesus' commandment is wrong:

What I say, therefore, I say as the Father has told me.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Holding faith in Jesus while going through suffering is sanctifying. Obeying Jesus while going through suffering is sanctifying.
Suffering in and of itself is not sanctifying.

+ [[https://youtube.com/watch?v=gKOMCpe-rqM&t=207][youtube.com:  Jim Carrey Delivers Powerful Speech About Jesus , Suffering & Forgiveness { MUST WATCH } {@ aboveinspiration } @time: 3 min 27 sec]] :: Base your forgiveness on what God has done for you, rather than on what the person has done to you. ... When I realise how much I've been forgiven, how can I /not/ forgive you?

Sanctification is always salvific because sanctification is by faith in Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2016%3A31&version=ESV][Acts 16:31]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A16-18&version=ESV][Acts 26:16-18]]*) and by obedience to Jesus Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A22&version=ESV][I Peter 1:22]]*) and both faith and obedience to Jesus Christ is to do with salvation (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%205%3A9&version=ESV][Hebrews 5:9]]*).

If a person by faith in Jesus Christ keeps His instruction to "not worry about tomorrow", for example, while enduring suffering, that is sanctifying. If Jesus instructed it then to keep the instruction by faith in Jesus Christ while enduring suffering is sanctifying:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%206%3A30-34&version=ESV][Matthew 6:30-34]]* - But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today is alive and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, will he not much more clothe you, O you of little faith? Therefore do not be anxious, saying, What shall we eat? or What shall we drink? or What shall we wear? For the Gentiles seek after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all. But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you. Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus' sacrifice is propitiation for sin (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%202%3A24&version=ESV][I Peter 2:24]]*).

+ [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TNAikc8G1DU][youtube.com:  Why Most Christians Misunderstand Sin and Animal Blood Sacrifices - Michael Heiser {@ stefanlouw6395 }]] :: "Take this bird, take this animal, do this and that and you will be 'cleansed from your sin'"... The Hebrew word for sin and "sin offering" [[https://biblehub.com/hebrew/2402.htm][(H2402 chattaah; sin, sin offering)]] in many circumstances has nothing to do with moral violation. It actually refers to being decontaminated. And it's about doing something to the person to decontaminate them so that they don't contaminate sacred space. All these rituals weren't about curing moral violation. If you committed a moral offence, an abomination, there's no sacrifice for you. You're either put to death or exiled from the community. So the writer of Hebrews actually knows what he was talking about:

And thus we are actually able to love properly because we can be healed by Jesus from moral sin to not practice them anymore:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A19-21&version=ESV][I John 4:19-21]]* - We love because he first loved us. If anyone says, I love God, and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen cannot love God whom he has not seen. And this commandment we have from him: *whoever loves God must also love his brother*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%202%3A24&version=ESV][I Peter 2:24]]* - *He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree*, _that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. *By his wounds you have been healed*_. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A2&version=ESV][I John 5:2]]* - By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and obey his commandments. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus didn't sin at all and He suffered in the flesh. Disciples of Jesus suffer in the flesh too as they have "ceased from committing sin".

Because whoever abstains from sin subsequently suffers in the flesh (e.g. the Adamic flesh rebels against the will to do the will of God, and the world hates the person because they're a disciple of Jesus), then whoever suffers in the flesh has "ceased from sin". That's how to read this. As in, someone who now holds their faith in Jesus Christ abstains from sin (because they now obey Christ, from the love of God rather than the love of evil; they now obey Christ instead of sin), as consequence that person suffers in the flesh. And someone who has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%204%3A1-3&version=ESV][I Peter 4:1-3]]* - Since therefore Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves with the same way of thinking, for whoever has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin, so as to live for the rest of the time in the flesh no longer for human passions but for the will of God. The time that is past suffices for doing what the Gentiles want to do, living in sensuality, passions, drunkenness, orgies, drinking parties, and lawless idolatry. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Being under grace doesn't mean no longer needing to obey God!

Getting born-again, we are aquitted of sin, and are instructed to continue on in obedience to Jesus Christ.

But without being born-again, we can't enter the kingdom of God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2010%3A23-27&version=ESV][Mark 10:23-27]]* - And Jesus looked around and said to his disciples, How difficult it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God! Jesus looked at them and said, With man it is impossible, but not with God. For all things are *possible* with God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A5-7&version=ESV][John 3:5-7]]* - Jesus answered, Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.
