producing disciples of Jesus teaching them to keep everything that Jesus has commanded and thus producing other scribes trained in the Kingdom of God and other households for God inside of God's greater household [[strongs:G1577][(G1577 ekklēsiais; churches, [See: Revelation of John 2:7])]],
people calling God their Father and calling no man on earth their father.

+ Journal <2026-04-22 Wed 08:10> :: I have been listening recently to people's testimonies of how difficult is has been for them to afford food and find jobs and have hope (e.g. [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=netNh-AdVaM][youtube.com:  How TF are people getting jobs ? {@ Jett . franzen }]], [[https://youtube.com/watch?v=eDSaZveGttk&t=271][youtube.com:  The AI Backlash Has Reached a Tipping Point {@ VanessaWing % C3 % A5rdh } @time: 4 min 31 sec]], etc.).

    I've heard it [[https://youtu.be/8JzvzK4yMTU?t=862][said]] "You can't control what happens to you. All you can do is respond." That's not exactly true though. We're not powerless. We can turn the tables around by seeking refuge in God (See: *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2091%3A9-12&version=ESV][Psalms 91:9-12]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2018&version=ESV][Ezekiel 18]]*) and through faith in Jesus we can overcome the world ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A4-5&version=ESV][I John 5:4-5]]). The smartest thing we can do is simply do what Jesus Christ instructs in reality, knowing there is forgiveness in Christ, forgiveness for those who are abiding in His commandments, and in that sense the world then needs to respond to you (rather than you to the world). But Jesus said to His followers that the world will hate them (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A23-24&version=ESV][I John 3:23-24]]*, [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A4&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:4]], *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%201%3A3-14&version=ESV][Colossians 1:3-14]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2010%3A17-23&version=ESV][Mark 10:17-23]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2010%3A34&version=ESV][Hebrews 10:34]]*).

    I think we must stop walking in the ways of the world and start walking by the spirit of God instead.

    OK, so in an oppressive economy where the rich in earthly goods oppress the poor in earthly goods,
    doesn't it make sense to stop trusting in the "way of the world" of dishonest gain, and instead, speak and do what pleases God (He can see), and keep God's commandments for us and follow Jesus in reality?

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2010%3A17-23&version=ESV][Mark 10:17-23]]* - And as he was setting out on his journey, a man ran up and knelt before him and asked him, Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life? And Jesus said to him, Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone. You know the commandments: Do not murder, Do not commit adultery, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Do not defraud, Honor your father and mother. And he said to him, Teacher, all these I have kept from my youth. And Jesus, looking at him, loved him, and said to him, You lack one thing: go, sell all that you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me. Disheartened by the saying, he went away sorrowful, for he had great possessions. And Jesus looked around and said to his disciples, How difficult it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God! (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    The person walking "by the flesh" keeps deferring obedience to Christ's commandments, and in deferring making the flesh their strength rather than Christ, and believes they need material wealth *before" they can do what Jesus says.
    But the person walking by the spirit trusts and obeys Christ.

    Doesn't it make sense to stop making the flesh one's strength (it wasn't going to work out anyway), and to instead make God one's strength by trusting Jesus and His words?

    + [[https://www.earlychristianwritings.com/text/diognetus-roberts.html][Mathetes to Diognetus]] :: This was not that He at all delighted in our sins, but that He simply endured them; nor that He approved the time of working iniquity which then was, but that He sought to form a mind conscious of righteousness, so that being convinced in that time of our unworthiness of attaining life through our own works, it should now, through the kindness of God, be vouchsafed to us; and having made it manifest that _in ourselves we were unable to enter into the kingdom of God_, *we might through the power of God be made able.*

    Through faith and obedience to Jesus Christ, a person is empowered by God to enter into the Kingdom of God:

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2010%3A4-6&version=ESV][II Corinthians 10:4-6]]* - For the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh but have divine power to destroy strongholds. We destroy arguments and every lofty opinion raised against the knowledge of God, and take every thought captive to obey Christ, being ready to punish every disobedience, when your obedience is complete. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%202%3A11-14&version=ESV][Colossians 2:11-14]]* - In him also you were circumcised with a circumcision made without hands, by putting off the body of the flesh, by the circumcision of Christ, having been buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him through faith in the powerful working of God, who raised him from the dead. And you, who were dead in your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, God made alive together with him, having forgiven us all our trespasses, by canceling the record of debt that stood against us with its legal demands. This he set aside, nailing it to the cross. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    God makes it *possible* to enter by His power. But just because the propitiation for sin and power of God is available to us, doesn't mean people make use of it. The power is available for those who by faith obey Jesus Christ. If, trusting Jesus Christ, we walk the way He instructs, then we can enter the Kingdom of God like that:

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2010%3A23-27&version=ESV][Mark 10:23-27]]* - And Jesus looked around and said to his disciples, How difficult it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God! And the disciples were amazed at his words. But Jesus said to them again, Children, how difficult it is to enter the kingdom of God! It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God. And they were exceedingly astonished, and said to him, Then who can be saved? Jesus looked at them and said, With man it is impossible, but not with God. For all things are *possible* with God. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    If a person owns very little in worldly goods then isn't that a golden opportunity to lay up treasure in heaven and then go forward keeping Jesus' commandments in reality rather than in false-pretense or in bad conscience? You could move forward in knowledge that God owns everything (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy%2010%3A14&version=ESV][Deuteronomy 10:14]]*) and will take care of you as you are able to have peace with God in good conscience doing as Jesus instructs which is so much better, and is also like a wise man who builds his house on the rock. If you have only $10 worth of worldly goods but in good conscience gave "let's say "half" (though why not all?) of all the worldly goods you had" ($5? by a worldly estimate) to those in need of them and out of faith and obedience to Jesus' instruction to "give to the one who begs from you", you can still say "you gave half of all the worldly goods you have out of faith and obedience to Jesus to the instruction to give to the one who begs from you" and then go forward keeping Jesus' commandments in reality rather than in false-pretense. Now change $10 for $10 billion dollars, and that's just as true, but how many people do you hear about giving away their fortune?. Being poor in worldly goods, in my view, is a nice opportunity to fall out of agreement with the way of the world and instead store up some treasure in heaven and go forward following Jesus in reality.

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2019%3A8-9&version=ESV][Luke 19:8-9]]* - And Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor. And if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I restore it fourfold. And Jesus said to him, Today salvation has come to this house, since he also is a son of Abraham. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    All Christians need to go forward abiding in Jesus' commandments in reality, holding their faith with a good conscience. The Christian's walk begins with repentance (i.e. turning away from the love of evil and towards the love of God). You can't start your Abraham-like faith in Jesus with an act of committing sin such as theft because by faith Abraham obeyed. Robin-hood-style giving is not the way to start a relationship with Jesus. Rather we should put our faith in Jesus Christ as He commanded (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A1&version=ESV][John 14:1]]*) and continue to by faith obey Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A11-14&version=ESV][John 5:11-14]]*).

    Abiding in God's Law / God's commandments for us, even as Christians who abide by Jesus' commandments, is dependent on keeping genuine faith in God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%209%3A30-32&version=ESV][Romans 9:30-32]]*) and maintaining faith in God is dependent on maintaining love for God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A45&version=ESV][Luke 6:45]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A42-43&version=ESV][John 5:42-43]]*). The faith of Abraham which Christians must have (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A14-17&version=ESV][Romans 4:14-17]]*) includes the fear of God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A17&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:17]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%2022%3A9-14&version=ESV][Genesis 22:9-14]]*) and the fear of God is the hatred of evil (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%208%3A13&version=ESV][Proverbs 8:13]]*), and a genuine faith seeks God's commendation (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A6&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:6]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A28-29&version=ESV][John 5:28-29]],37-47*).
    
    + An analogy :: If someone were to instruct, "Stand up straight and you won't fall over." Then someone else protests and says, "That sounds like legalism." That's an absurd protest.

    God instructs us, "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind. This is the great and first commandment. And a second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself."

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2022%3A36-40&version=ESV][Matthew 22:36-40]]* - Teacher, which is the great commandment in the Law? And he said to him, You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind. This is the great and first commandment. And a second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments depend all the Law and the Prophets. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2010%3A25-28&version=ESV][Luke 10:25-28]]* - And behold, a lawyer stood up to put him to the test, saying, Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life? He said to him, What is written in the Law? How do you read it? And he answered, You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind, and your neighbor as yourself. And he said to him, You have answered correctly; do this, and you will live. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy%2030%3A6&version=ESV][Deuteronomy 30:6]]* - And the LORD your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your offspring, so that you will love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, that you may live. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%203%3A3-11&version=ESV][Philippians 3:3-11]]* - For we are the real circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God and glory in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh— though I myself have reason for confidence in the flesh also. If anyone else thinks he has reason for confidence in the flesh, I have more: circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; as to the law, a Pharisee; as to zeal, a persecutor of the church; as to righteousness, under the law blameless. But whatever gain I had, I counted as loss for the sake of Christ. Indeed, I count everything as loss because of the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. For his sake I have suffered the loss of all things and count them as rubbish, in order that I may gain Christ and be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own that comes from the law, but that which comes through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God that depends on faith— that I may know him and the power of his resurrection, and may share his sufferings, becoming like him in his death, that by any means possible I may attain the resurrection from the dead. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A3&version=ESV][I John 2:3]]* - And by this we know that we have come to know Him, if the commandments of Him [[https://biblehub.com/greek/te_ro_men_5083.htm][we keep]]. (Interlinear)
    #+END_QUOTE

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A10-13&version=ESV][I John 5:10-13]]* - Whoever believes ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/pisteuo_n_4100.htm][G4100 pisteuōn]] - /is believing (verb)/) in the Son of God has the testimony in himself. Whoever does not believe God has made him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony that God has borne concerning his Son. And this is the testimony, that God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life. I write these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God that you may know that you have eternal life. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A15-17&version=ESV][I John 4:15-17]]* - Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him, and he in God. So we have come to know and to believe the love that God has for us. God is love, and whoever abides in love abides in God, and God abides in him. By this is love perfected with us, so that we may have confidence for the day of judgment, because as he is so also are we in this world. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    To protest saying, "That sounds like legalism" is absurdity.

    Of course we need God's help in order to be sanctified and do this well.

The salvation of the believer necessitates them having a love for their family in Christ, and that happens through sanctification:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A22&version=ESV][I Peter 1:22]]* - Having purified your souls by your obedience to the truth for a sincere brotherly love, love one another earnestly from a pure heart, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

At the end of sanctification, obeying the truth for a sincere love of our family in Christ, there is eternal life:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A22-23&version=ESV][Romans 6:22-23]]* - But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of God, the fruit you get leads to sanctification and its end, eternal life. For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Because we must love God with our whole heart to live (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy%2030%3A6&version=ESV][Deuteronomy 30:6]]*), and we can't love God with our whole heart if we hate His children (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1-2&version=ESV][I John 5:1-2]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A19-21&version=ESV][I John 4:19-21]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A8&version=ESV][I John 4:8]],19-21* - Anyone who does not love does not know God, because God is love. We love because he first loved us. *If anyone says, I love God, and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen cannot love God whom he has not seen. And this commandment we have from him: whoever loves God must also love his brother.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A8-12&version=ESV][I John 2:8-12]]* - At the same time, it is a new commandment that I am writing to you, which is true in him and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining. Whoever says he is in the light and hates his brother is still in darkness. *Whoever loves his brother abides in the light, and in him there is no cause for stumbling. But whoever hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness, and does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes. *I am writing to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven for his name's sake. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%208%3A21&version=ESV][Luke 8:21]]* - But he answered them, My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1-2&version=ESV][I John 5:1-2]]* - Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the Father loves whoever has been born of him. _By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God *and* obey his commandments._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Getting us to this point of loving the children of God the way God wants us to is the circumcision of the heart of flesh (the new heart God gives us) and this circumcision involves God writing His laws on that new heart which happens as we are taught by God to walk in His ways after getting born-again.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%208%3A10-11&version=ESV][Hebrews 8:10-11]]* - For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the Lord: I will put my laws into their minds, and write them on their hearts, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. And they shall not teach, each one his neighbor and each one his brother, saying, Know the Lord, for they shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A15-23&version=ESV][Romans 6:15-23]]* - What then? Are we to sin because we are not under law but under grace? By no means! Do you not know that if you present yourselves to anyone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin, which leads to death, or of *obedience, which leads to righteousness*? But thanks be to God, that _you who were once slaves of sin have become *obedient from the heart* to the standard of teaching to which you were committed_, and, _having been set free from sin, have *become slaves of righteousness*_. I am speaking in human terms, because of your natural limitations. For just as you once presented your members as slaves to impurity and to lawlessness leading to more lawlessness, so now present your members as slaves to righteousness leading to sanctification. When you were slaves of sin, you were free in regard to righteousness. But what fruit were you getting at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? The *end of those things is death*. But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of God, the fruit you get leads to sanctification and its end, eternal life. For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's strange the way that people look at the commandments of Christ as a heavy burden or as against grace protesting for having to "do" something
as they misconstrue obedience as meaning depending on self rather than on Christ.
If Jesus advised a weary person to sit on a chair to rest on the chair, and then that person protested saying, "That sounds like I have to 'do' something. That sounds like I'm depending on myself..."
well that is plainly ridiculous. But many people view Jesus' commandments like that, as if it's no longer depending on Jesus when a person trusts and obeys Christ.
Jesus said that the person who hears His word and does is it is like a wise man who builds a house with a strong foundation on the rock.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%207%3A24&version=ESV][Matthew 7:24]]* - Everyone then who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house on the rock. (ESV)

And when a flood arose, the stream broke against that house and could not shake it, because it had been well built. But the one who hears and does not do them is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation. When the stream broke against it, immediately it fell, and the ruin of that house was great. (ESV)

God considers the intentions of our hearts even for the mistakes that we make:

Therefore I command you, You shall set apart three cities. (ESV)

Deeds are given to the person who has faith.

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A4-6&version=ESV][Romans 4:4-6]]* - Now to the one who works [[strongs:G2038][(G2038 ergazomenō; is working for payment)]], his wages are not counted as a gift but as his due. And to the one who does not work [[strongs:G2038][(G2038 ergazomenō; is working for payment)]] but trusts him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted as righteousness, just as David also speaks of the blessing of the one to whom God counts righteousness apart from [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] works [[strongs:G2041][(G2041 ergōn)]]: (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A person who has been forgiven much, loves much. So somebody who is forgiven by Jesus will love Jesus, and a person who loves Jesus will be "law of faith"-abiding (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15&version=ESV][John 14:15]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A27&version=ESV][Romans 3:27]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%209%3A21&version=ESV][I Corinthians 9:21]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2013%3A41&version=ESV][Matthew 13:41]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%207%3A40-50&version=ESV][Luke 7:40-50]]* - And Jesus answering said to him, Simon, I have something to say to you. And he answered, Say it, Teacher. A certain moneylender had two debtors. One owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty. When they could not pay, he cancelled the debt of both. Now which of them will love him more? Simon answered, The one, I suppose, for whom he cancelled the larger debt. And he said to him, You have judged rightly. Then turning toward the woman he said to Simon, Do you see this woman? I entered your house; you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair. You gave me no kiss, but from the time I came in she has not ceased to kiss my feet. You did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment. Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven—for she loved much. But he who is forgiven little, loves little. And he said to her, Your sins are forgiven. Then those who were at table with him began to say among themselves, Who is this, who even forgives sins? And he said to the woman, Your faith has saved you; go in peace. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15&version=ESV][John 14:15]]* - If you love me, you will keep my commandments. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A19-21&version=ESV][I John 4:19-21]]* - We love because he first loved us. If anyone says, I love God, and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen cannot love God whom he has not seen. And this commandment we have from him: *whoever loves God must also love his brother*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But love for God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2016%3A22&version=ESV][I Corinthians 16:22]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%202%3A10&version=ESV][II Thessalonians 2:10]]*), faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A18&version=ESV][Acts 26:18]]*) and obedience (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%205%3A7-10&version=ESV][Hebrews 5:7-10]]*) and trying (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2025%3A14-30&version=ESV][Matthew 25:14-30]]*) and making effort (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Peter%201%3A5&version=ESV][II Peter 1:5]]*) and self examination (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2013%3A5&version=ESV][II Corinthians 13:5]]*) and being corrected (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%203%3A16&version=ESV][II Timothy 3:16]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Jeremiah%205%3A3&version=ESV][Jeremiah 5:3]]*) by the truth, and endeavouring (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%202%3A17&version=ESV][Galatians 2:17]]*) to abide in sound teaching (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%204%3A3&version=ESV][II Timothy 4:3]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20John%201%3A9&version=ESV][II John 1:9]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%206%3A3&version=ESV][I Timothy 6:3]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%201%3A13&version=ESV][II Timothy 1:13]]*) and abiding in Jesus' commandments (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A24&version=ESV][I John 3:24]]*) are all good (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A45&version=ESV][Luke 6:45]]*).

It's *very sad* that people attack the gospel by waging war against effort and against obedience and against doing the truth ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A21&version=ESV][John 3:21]]) in reality.

The big reason I think it's *very sad* that people who attack the gospel by waging war agianst effort and against obedience, etc. is because they are effectively teaching against seeking to please God. God wants us walk by faith *out of love for Him*. God wants us to "do faith". And heart intentions such as trust, 'effort' and love are to do with faith.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%201%3A22-24&version=ESV][James 1:22-24]]* - But be doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves. For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man who looks intently at his natural face in a mirror. For he looks at himself and goes away and at once forgets what he was like. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ Journal <2026-06-25 Thu 13:03> :: Firstly, I've been born-again of the spirit. God has indeed done a work in me to give me a heart that fears Him and has been writing His laws on my heart, circumcising my heart, and has given me a new spirit. So thank God for His grace. However, from my angle my getting born-again happened in [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2018%3A31&version=ESV][Ezekiel 18:31]] style. It's still by God's grace. That being said... I have been reflecting on "doers of the Law by faith" being justified by faith as distinct from seeking justification by being a "doer of the law including the works", and so relying on the "external actions".

    "Doers of the Law" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A1-13&version=ESV][Romans 2:1-13]]*) are also "doers of faith" because whatever is not done in faith is sin which is lawlessness (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A4&version=ESV][I John 3:4]]*). So "doers of the Law" will be justified because they are also "doers of faith", and we are saved from being a "slave to sin" to being a "slave to righteousness" by faith in Jesus Christ.
    A person is surely justified by faith rather than being a "doer of the works of the Law" because the "works of the Law" talk about both heart attitude *and* external action, but when talking about being a "doer of the Law", someone *actually* doing it, then they must be doing it by faith, because obedience without love for the truth is feigned (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2081%3A15&version=ESV][Psalm 81:15]]*). So the question becomes, "How does a person get to this point of doing the will of God obediently from the heart in reality, to 'doing the Word' by faith obedient from the heart, to 'doing the Law, even', albeit as a follower of Jesus?" And the answer is by repenting (changing one's mind) and having faith in Jesus Christ, and God works His salvation in that person, salvation which is salvation from committing sin. The Law can surely be done if it is by faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%202%3A6-8&version=ESV][I Peter 2:6-8]]*) rather than works. Indeed we're supposed to do everything by faith (that is by a love for the truth). God fixes a person so that from all of their heart they "do" His word in reality for God to see walking by the spirit. God is our father and we must honor God and we must Honor the Son of God. A person can be an actual doer of the word while being sanctified towards doing God's will better and from all their heart to have the love of God perfected in them:
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A4-6&version=ESV][I John 2:4-6]]* - Whoever says I know him but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, but whoever keeps his word, in him truly the love of God is perfected. By this we may be sure that we are in him: whoever says he abides in him ought to walk in the same way in which he walked. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A28&version=ESV][Romans 3:28]]* - For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from works [[strongs:G2041][(G2041 ergōn; works)]] of the law [[strongs:G3551][(G3551 nomou; of the Law)]]. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%209%3A30-32&version=ESV][Romans 9:30-32]]* - What shall we say, then? That Gentiles who did not pursue righteousness have attained it, that is, a righteousness that is by faith; but that Israel who pursued a law that would lead to righteousness did not succeed in reaching that law. Why? Because they did not pursue it by faith, but as if it were based on works. They have stumbled over the stumbling stone, (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%202%3A6-8&version=ESV][I Peter 2:6-8]]* - For it stands in Scripture: Behold, I am laying in Zion a stone, a cornerstone chosen and precious, and whoever believes in him will not be put to shame. So the honor is for you who believe, but for those who do not believe, The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone, and A stone of stumbling, and a rock of offense. They stumble because they disobey the word, as they were destined to do. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE
    
    The believer is a "doer of the word" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A12&version=ESV][John 14:12]]*) who obeys the gospel and does good as opposed to evil (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%204%3A12-19&version=ESV][I Peter 4:12-19]]*), after all Jesus Christ didn't do evil and so someone who is walking by faith in Jesus does good (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A12&version=ESV][John 14:12]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A16-21&version=ESV][John 3:16-21]]*).
    
    God gives us a new heart so that we will love Him with *all* our heart, and *all* our soul:
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy%205%3A29&version=ESV][Deuteronomy 5:29]]* - Oh that they had such a mind as this *always*, to fear me and to keep all my commandments, that it might go well with them and with their descendants forever! (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy%2029%3A4&version=ESV][Deuteronomy 29:4]]* - But to this day the LORD has not given you a heart to understand or eyes to see or ears to hear. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy%2030%3A6&version=ESV][Deuteronomy 30:6]]* - And the LORD your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your offspring, so that you will love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, that you may live. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE
    
    When *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A9-16&version=ESV][Romans 2:9-16]]* says "all who have sinned under the law will be judged by the law", think about that for a moment.
    Have I personally sinned while having some knowledge of the Law (for example, the 10 commandments)? Yes, it's happened before. Before I was born-again, I was hopelessly enslaved to sin, but there is a difference now where I love Jesus and hope in Him and striving against sin while challenging, I believe is worth the fight. I do not feel enslaved to sin. I feel enslaved to righteousness from a love of rightetousness who is Jesus Christ, as God is teaching me His precepts and His will. The Apostle Paul had been judged by the Law in the past (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A9-13&version=ESV][Romans 7:9-13]]*). But do I *always* sin while having knowledge of the law? Certainly not (*Romans 6:15-23*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%201%3A21-25&version=ESV][James 1:21-25]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A6-18&version=ESV][I John 3:6-18]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A16-18&version=ESV][Romans 6:16-18]]*). I have personally found the Law of God to be a valuable resource in my fight against bad doctrine and to stand secure in beliefs that I have about what God loves and hates, as I endeavour to seek to please God. So God has given me a heart that fears Him and when I read His law I naturally concur with it. It seems to me that God is teaching me and helping me to walk in His precepts as I'm holding faith in Jesus. I'm certainly not being conformed to the full Mosaic Law! That would be like an actual artwork (God's workmanship) being conformed to a sketch (shadow), rather than the finished product (the image of Christ to some degree of glory). But Jesus' commandments depend on the Great 2 commandments, so I'm certainly being conformed to do those. Also, the 10 commandments I believe are still to be kept (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2010%3A17-23&version=ESV][Mark 10:17-23]]*), but in the Christian way (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Malachi%201%3A6&version=ESV][Malachi 1:6]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A9&version=ESV][Matthew 23:9]]*).
    
    A saved person who is walking by faith in Jesus Christ in love for Jesus Christ loving righteousness is under grace and does deeds out of a love of righteousness with Jesus Christ who is righteousness to them as their first love. Their heart becomes oriented in a particular way to be doing the will of God from the heart and in doing God's will for us which is our sanctification (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%204%3A3-8&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 4:3-8]]*) through faith in Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A16-18&version=ESV][Acts 26:16-18]]*) we are under grace being taught to renounce ungodliness (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Titus%202%3A11-15&version=ESV][Titus 2:11-15]]*). That makes sense because God wants us to be cleaned up (sanctified) through faith. That is His will for us:

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%204%3A3-8&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 4:3-8]]* - For this is the will of God, your sanctification: that you abstain from sexual immorality; that each one of you know how to control his own body in holiness and honor, not in the passion of lust like the Gentiles who do not know God; that no one transgress and wrong his brother in this matter, because the Lord is an avenger in all these things, as we told you beforehand and solemnly warned you. For God has not called us for impurity, but in holiness. Therefore whoever disregards this, disregards not man but God, who gives his Holy Spirit to you. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    So when a person is actually operating from that love of Jesus Christ as their first agape love, doing faith, the law isn't judging them. That person is being a doer in reality of Jesus Christ's commandments under grace and getting cleaned up, being sanctified to keep God's commandments better as they hold Jesus as their first love (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2010%3A32-38&version=ESV][Matthew 10:32-38]]*). That makes sense to me because Jesus said that whoever is believing (is doing faith) in Him is not judged. Through faith in Jesus Christ we become "doers in reality" of God's law, and we get better at it because God teaches us and sanctifies us as we trust and obey Jesus Christ from the heart. So we are justified by doing faith in Jesus and this doing of faith in Jesus is God's commandment for us being done and this brings us into keeping God's commandments in reality, and we get better at keeping God's commandments in reality as we continue doing this commandment of faith in Jesus. We get better at loving God and people (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%203%3A11-13&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 3:11-13]],5:23*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%201%3A3&version=ESV][II Thessalonians 1:3]]) the way God commands (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1-2&version=ESV][I John 5:1-2]]*) as we continue in faith in Jesus Christ. So being a doer in reality of the word, of Jesus Christ, of Jesus Christ's commandments, justifies because being commandments given by Christ Himself, to truly obey them implies that they are done out of a loving faith in Jesus Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2081%3A12-15&version=ESV][Psalms 81:12-15]]*). So a person is saved by obeying Jesus Christ and that salvation is inclusive of sanctification as we are saved by sanctification that happens as we hold faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%202%3A10-13&version=ESV][II Thessalonians 2:10-13]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%203%3A18&version=ESV][II Corinthians 3:18]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A16-18&version=ESV][Acts 26:16-18]]*) in Jesus Christ.
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A9-16&version=ESV][Romans 2:9-16]]* - There will be tribulation and distress for every human being who does evil, the Jew first and also the Greek, but glory and honor and peace for everyone who does good, the Jew first and also the Greek. For God shows no partiality. For all who have sinned without the law will also perish without the law, and all who have sinned under the law will be judged by the law. For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but the doers of the law who will be justified. For when Gentiles, who do not have the law, by nature do what the law requires, they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the law. They show that the work of the law is written on their hearts, while their conscience also bears witness, and their conflicting thoughts accuse or even excuse them on that day when, according to my gospel, God judges the secrets of men by Christ Jesus. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

Find a scripture which says effort is against faith. I guarantee you will find none. Yet the lie that effort is against faith is prevelant.

In fact, here is a verse which as clear as day shows that effort is not against faith:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Peter%201%3A5-10&version=ESV][II Peter 1:5-10]]* - For this very reason, make every effort to supplement your faith with _virtue, and virtue with knowledge, and knowledge with self-control, and self-control with steadfastness, and steadfastness with godliness, and godliness with brotherly affection, and brotherly affection with love._ For if these qualities are yours and are increasing, they keep you from being ineffective or unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ. For whoever lacks these qualities is so nearsighted that he is blind, having forgotten that he was *cleansed from his former sins*. Therefore, brothers, be all the more diligent to make your calling and election sure, for if you practice these qualities you will never fall. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Rather than link Romans 8:30 all together like a daisy chain where nothing could go wrong, I take each segment as conveying a truth, then take the wisdom from the Apostle Peter who says we should make every effort to supplement our faith with such things as he has mentioned to make election sure:

| *Romans 8:30* - And those whom he predestined he also called, and those whom he called he also justified, and those whom he justified he also glorified. (ESV) |                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Reality                                                         |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Someone who is predestined will be called.                                                                                                                     | Many are called, but few are chosen. (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2022%3A1-14&version=ESV][Matthew 22:1-14]]*)                                                                                                                                                        | Few made it past this step                                                |
| Those whom He called, He also justified                                                                                                                        | We must continue in the faith. (*Ezekiel 18:26-27*, *Colossians 1:21-23*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%206%3A20-21&version=ESV][I Timothy 6:20-21]]*)                                                                                                                  | Sadly, some people apostate and go back to loving evil rather than Jesus. |
| Those whom He justified, He also glorified                                                                                                                     | God will bring every deed into judgement, if we sow to the spirit the we will reap eternal life, but if we sow to the flesh, we will reap corruption. (*Ecclesiastes 12:14*, *Galatians 6:8*, *Romans 6:17-18*) | God is not mocked                                                         |

+ [[https://www.earlychristianwritings.com/text/polycarp-lightfoot.html][Polycarp 5:1]] :: Knowing then that God is not mocked, we ought to walk worthily of His commandment and His glory.

God does it like this, but we must unite faith in Jesus Christ with patience (continuing in faith in Jesus Christ, abiding in His teachings) to inherit the promise of an inheritance to those who are sanctified by faith in Him.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Peter%201%3A3-12&version=ESV][II Peter 1:3-12]]* - His divine power has granted to us all things that pertain to life and godliness, through the knowledge of him who called us to his own glory and excellence, by which he has granted to us his precious and very great promises, so that through them you may become partakers of the divine nature, having escaped from the corruption that is in the world because of sinful desire. For this very reason, make every effort to supplement your faith with virtue, and virtue with knowledge, and knowledge with self-control, and self-control with steadfastness, and steadfastness with godliness, and godliness with brotherly affection, and brotherly affection with love. For if these qualities are yours and are increasing, they keep you from being ineffective or unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ. For whoever lacks these qualities is so nearsighted that he is blind, having forgotten that he was cleansed from his former sins. Therefore, brothers, be all the more diligent to make your calling and election sure, for if you practice these qualities you will never fall. For in this way there will be richly provided for you an entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. Therefore I intend always to remind you of these qualities, though you know them and are established in the truth that you have. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So run that you may obtain it. Every athlete exercises self-control in all things. They do it to receive a perishable wreath, but we an imperishable. So I do not run aimlessly; I do not box as one beating the air. But I discipline my body and keep it under control, lest after preaching to others I myself should be disqualified. (ESV)

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2013%3A57&version=ESV][Matthew 13:57]]* - And they took offense at him. But Jesus said to them, A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown and in his own household. (ESV)

So we have to do Jesus' commandments lawfully ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%201%3A8-11&version=ESV][I Timothy 1:8-11]]) and that means as we follow Jesus' commandments, that shouldn't violate the 2 Great Commandments (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2022%3A36-40&version=ESV][Matthew 22:36-40]]*). That shouldn't be daunting or sound impossible that Jesus' commandments depend on the 2 Great Commandments because we are justified by faith. It should also sound correct that Jesus Christ's commandments depend on the 2 Great Commandments because Jesus is our God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2010%3A30&version=ESV][John 10:30]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A10-15&version=ESV][John 14:10-15]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2020%3A28&version=ESV][John 20:28]]*), and we must love one-another in Christ as ourself. Those in Christ are one in Spirit (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%206%3A16-20&version=ESV][I Corinthians 6:16-20]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%205%3A1-13&version=ESV][I Corinthians 5:1-13]]*):

Jesus is the Truth ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A6&version=ESV][John 14:6]]) and we must obey the Truth ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A8&version=ESV][Romans 2:8]]). Jesus is our Righteousness ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%201%3A30&version=ESV][I Corinthians 1:30]]) and we must obey Righteousness ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A13-23&version=ESV][Romans 6:13-23]]).

Biblical obedience issues from a heart that loves the Truth (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A45&version=ESV][Luke 6:45]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2081%3A15&version=ESV][Psalms 81:15]]*).

(NASB)

[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A19&version=ESV][John 3:19]] connects faith with deeds. Evil deeds come from a love of darkness. [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A45&version=ESV][Luke 6:45]] also connects faith with deeds. Good deeds come from a love of the truth.

For confidence in the day of judgement, we need to be those who love one-another as we have been commanded to, we need to be those who give "God the glory",
and we need to be those who have "repented of our evil deeds" and that means to change our minds to love Jesus rather than the evil:

And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent his Son to be the Savior of the world. Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him, and he in God. By this is love perfected with us, so that we may have confidence for the day of judgment, because as he is so also are we in this world. There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear. For fear has to do with punishment, and whoever fears has not been perfected in love. We love because he first loved us. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

They were scorched by the fierce heat, and they cursed the name of God who had power over these plagues. They did not repent and give him glory. The fifth angel poured out his bowl on the throne of the beast, and its kingdom was plunged into darkness. People gnawed their tongues in anguish and cursed the God of heaven for their pain and sores. They did not repent of their deeds. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A person is led by the spirit to fulfill the law. Fulfilling the law doesn't mean being under the law. Fulfilling the law and loving one-another as commanded and having the love of God perfected in us is certainly not contrary to faith or to walking by the spirit. God gives us grace in order to do this. And we can have confidence for the day of judgement when walking in this way, as Jesus walked.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A4-6&version=ESV][I John 2:4-6]]* - Whoever says I know him but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, but whoever keeps his word, in him truly the love of God is perfected. By this we may be sure that we are in him: whoever says he abides in him ought to walk in the same way in which he walked. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A2-3&version=ESV][Galatians 3:2-3]]* - Let me ask you only this: Did you receive the Spirit by works of the law or by hearing with faith? Are you so foolish? Having begun by the Spirit, are you now being perfected by the flesh? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A13-18&version=ESV][Galatians 5:13-18]]* - For you were called to freedom, brothers. Only do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another. For the whole law is fulfilled in one word: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. But if you bite and devour one another, watch out that you are not consumed by one another. But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh. For the desires of the flesh are against the Spirit, and the desires of the Spirit are against the flesh, for these are opposed to each other, to keep you from doing the things you want to do. But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Walking in the light is following Jesus. We must abide in Him and so we accept He loved us first, and we must love in the same way that He loves (confess the truth, love the truth and hate evil, laying our lives down for one-another):

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A12-15&version=ESV][I John 4:12-15]]* - No one has ever seen God; if we love one another, God abides in us and his love is perfected in us. By this we know that we abide in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit. And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent his Son to be the Savior of the world. Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him, and he in God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A7&version=ESV][I John 1:7]]* - But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God is love, and whoever abides in love abides in God, and God abides in him. By this is love perfected with us, so that we may have confidence for the day of judgment, because as he is so also are we in this world. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness beyond your companions. (ESV)

When it comes to walking by the Spirit, I don't think a person can cheat on it because the desires of the flesh are against the desires of the spirit and the desires of the spirit are against the desires of the flesh.

Genuine repentance, genuine faith and genuine love, I strongly believe, involve "doing the word in reality".
We must desire God in reality.

The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%20111%3A10&version=ESV][Psalms 111:10]]*) and it is to hate evil (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%208%3A13&version=ESV][Proverbs 8:13]]*).

Though a Christian hates evil, what is more precedent is their love for Jesus as [[https://youtube.com/watch?v=UjCgttduUFU&t=329][evil is outbalanced by good]], evil and death *is* defeated by Jesus from His perspective (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A10&version=ESV][Romans 6:10]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A9&version=ESV][Romans 6:9]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%201%3A18&version=ESV][Revelation of John 1:18]]*) but from our perspective is being defeated (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A25-28&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:25-28]]*) as Jesus puts Satan under our feet (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2016%3A19-20&version=ESV][Romans 16:19-20]]*) as we endeavour to be wise for what is good and innocent of evil and present our members to God as instruments for righteousness (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A10-13&version=ESV][Romans 6:10-13]]*). The darkness will never overcome the light (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A5&version=ESV][John 1:5]]*).

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2016%3A33&version=ESV][John 16:33]]* - I have said these things to you, that in me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation. But take heart; I have overcome the world. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A5&version=ESV][I John 5:5]]* - Who is it that overcomes the world except the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Notice, though, how even during the Rev 12:7 period people are saved through Jesus Christ *amidst* a spiritual war (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%2012%3A7-12&version=ESV][Revelation of John 12:7-12]]*).

Fear of God and love for God go hand in hand:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2037%3A4&version=ESV][Psalms 37:4]]* - Delight yourself in the LORD, and he will give you the desires of your heart. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%20145%3A19&version=ESV][Psalms 145:19]]* - He fulfills the desire of those who fear him; he also hears their cry and saves them. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Fear of God and faith in God go hand in hand (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%20115%3A11&version=ESV][Psalms 115:11]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A7-9&version=ESV][Galatians 3:7-9]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%2022%3A12&version=ESV][Genesis 22:12]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A17&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:17]]*). Love for God and hatred of evil go hand in hand (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2097%3A10&version=ESV][Psalms 97:10]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2012%3A9&version=ESV][Romans 12:9]]*). Deeds come from what's in the heart (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A19&version=ESV][John 3:19]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A45&version=ESV][Luke 6:45]]*). Good deeds come from the love of good and evil deeds come from the love of evil. Abraham did not cheat (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%2014%3A21-24&version=ESV][Genesis 14:21-24]]*). He was a doer in reality (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A37-45&version=ESV][John 8:37-45]]*).

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2016%3A6&version=ESV][Proverbs 16:6]]* - By steadfast love and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of the LORD one turns away from evil. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2078%3A37&version=ESV][Psalms 78:37]]* - Their heart was not steadfast toward him; they were not faithful to his covenant. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2010%3A6&version=ESV][I Corinthians 10:6]],11* - Now these things took place as examples for us, that we might not desire evil as they did. Now these things happened to them as an example, but they were written down for our instruction, on whom the end of the ages has come. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2019%3A23&version=ESV][Proverbs 19:23]]* - The fear of the LORD leads to life, and whoever has it rests satisfied; he will not be visited by harm. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A22&version=ESV][I Peter 1:22]]* - Having purified your souls by your obedience to the truth for a sincere brotherly love, love one another earnestly from a pure heart, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15&version=ESV][John 14:15]]* - If you love me, you will keep my commandments. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ Limited analogy :: _Fear of God_ is strongly related to faith in God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%20115%3A11&version=ESV][Psalms 115:11]]*) and love for God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2097%3A10&version=ESV][Psalms 97:10]]*). And so, what is the fear of God like? God gives us commandments for us to obey for our own good. For example, God commands us to love Him from all our heart, with all our soul, mind and strength. God wants us to love Him so that we will live. God is a consuming fire (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A28-29&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:28-29]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy%204%3A23-26&version=ESV][Deuteronomy 4:23-26]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2010%3A26-27&version=ESV][Hebrews 10:26-27]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2066%3A15&version=ESV][Isaiah 66:15]]*) and we should fear Him who can destroy body and soul in hell (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2010%3A28&version=ESV][Matthew 10:28]]*). And God has adversaries and we don't want to be God's adversaries (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2010%3A23-31&version=ESV][Hebrews 10:23-31]]*). God commands us to love our neighbour as ourself. God commands us to not steal from one-another, and to not bear false witness of one another, and to not commit adultery and to not murder, etc. These commandments are for our good. If God were to command us to not put our hand on a hot stove, that would be for our good. To have a healthy fear of the stove would be good. And with a healthy fear of God, we would not want to sin against God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2016%3A6&version=ESV][Proverbs 16:6]]*). And I think that Christians must have a healthy fear of God. We should love God and hate evil. And that's for our own good (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%208%3A35-36&version=ESV][Proverbs 8:35-36]]*).

    With the fear of God we want to please God, not displease Him, and it's for our own good:

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%206%3A16-19&version=ESV][Proverbs 6:16-19]]* - There are six things that the LORD hates, seven that are an abomination to him: haughty [[strongs:H7311][(H7311 rā·mō·wṯ; haughty, proud)]] eyes, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, a heart that devises wicked plans, feet that make haste to run to evil, a false witness who breathes out lies, and one who sows discord among brothers. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%205%3A9-12&version=ESV][II Corinthians 5:9-12]]* - So whether we are at home or away, we make it our aim to please him. For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each one may receive what is due for what he has done in the body, whether good or evil. Therefore, knowing the fear of the Lord, we persuade others. But what we are is known to God, and I hope it is known also to your conscience. We are not commending ourselves to you again but giving you cause to boast about us, so that you may be able to answer those who boast about outward appearance and not about what is in the heart. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

We have to be "doers" [[strongs:G4160][(G4160 poiōn; doing)]] of Jesus' words, "doers" of the truth:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A21&version=ESV][John 3:21]]* - The [one] however practicing [[strongs:G4160][(G4160 poiōn; doing)]] the truth [[strongs:G225][(G225 alētheian)]] comes [[strongs:G2064][(G2064 erchetai)]] to the Light [[strongs:G5457][(G5457 phōs)]] that may be manifest [[strongs:G5319][(G5319 phanerōthē)]] his works [[strongs:G2041][(G2041 erga)]] that in God [[strongs:G2316][(G2316 Theō)]] have been [[strongs:G1510][(G1510 estin)]] done [[strongs:G2038][(G2038 eirgasmena)]] (Interlinear)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A17-21&version=ESV][John 3:17-21]]* - For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but in order that the world might be saved through him. Whoever believes in him is not condemned, but whoever does not believe is condemned already, because he has not believed in the name of the only Son of God. And this is the judgment: the light has come into the world, and people loved the darkness rather than the light because their deeds were evil. For everyone who does wicked things hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his deeds should be exposed. But whoever does [[strongs:G4160][(G4160 poiōn; doing)]] what is true comes to the light, so that it may be clearly seen that his deeds have been carried out in God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A47-49&version=ESV][Luke 6:47-49]]* - Everyone who comes to me and hears my words and does [[strongs:G4160][(G4160 poiōn; doing)]] them, I will show you what he is like: he is like a man building a house, who dug deep and laid the foundation on the rock. And when a flood arose, the stream broke against that house and could not shake it, because it had been well built. But the one who hears and does not do them is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation. When the stream broke against it, immediately it fell, and the ruin of that house was great. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

When *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A9-16&version=ESV][Romans 2:9-16]]* says "all who have sinned under the law will be judged by the law", think about that for a moment.

Have I personally sinned while having some knowledge of the Law (for example, the 10 commandments)? Yes, it's happened before. Before I was born-again, I was hopelessly enslaved to sin, but there is a difference now where I love Jesus and hope in Him and striving against sin while challenging, I believe is worth the fight. I do not feel enslaved to sin. I feel enslaved to righteousness from a love of rightetousness who is Jesus Christ, as God is teaching me His precepts and His will. The Apostle Paul had been judged by the Law in the past (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A9-13&version=ESV][Romans 7:9-13]]*). But do I *always* sin while having knowledge of the law? Certainly not (*Romans 6:15-23*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%201%3A21-25&version=ESV][James 1:21-25]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A6-18&version=ESV][I John 3:6-18]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A16-18&version=ESV][Romans 6:16-18]]*). I have personally found the Law of God to be a valuable resource in my fight against bad doctrine and to stand secure in beliefs that I have about what God loves and hates, as I endeavour to seek to please God. So God has given me a heart that fears Him and when I read His law I naturally concur with it. It seems to me that God is teaching me and helping me to walk in His precepts as I'm holding faith in Jesus. I'm certainly not being conformed to the full Mosaic Law! That would be like an actual artwork (God's workmanship) being conformed to a sketch (shadow), rather than the finished product (the image of Christ to some degree of glory). But Jesus' commandments depend on the Great 2 commandments, so I'm certainly being conformed to do those. Also, the 10 commandments I believe are still to be kept (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2010%3A17-23&version=ESV][Mark 10:17-23]]*), but in the Christian way (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Malachi%201%3A6&version=ESV][Malachi 1:6]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A9&version=ESV][Matthew 23:9]]*).

A saved person who is walking by faith in Jesus Christ in love for Jesus Christ loving righteousness is under grace and does deeds out of a love of righteousness. Their heart becomes oriented in a particular way to be doing the will of God and in doing God's will for us which is our sanctification through faith in Jesus we are under grace. That makes sense because God wants us to be cleaned up through faith.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%204%3A3-8&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 4:3-8]]* - For this is the will of God, your sanctification: that you abstain from sexual immorality; that each one of you know how to control his own body in holiness and honor, not in the passion of lust like the Gentiles who do not know God; that no one transgress and wrong his brother in this matter, because the Lord is an avenger in all these things, as we told you beforehand and solemnly warned you. For God has not called us for impurity, but in holiness. Therefore whoever disregards this, disregards not man but God, who gives his Holy Spirit to you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So when a person is actually operating from that love of Jesus Christ as their first agape love, doing faith, the law isn't judging them. That person is being a doer in reality of Jesus Christ's commandments under grace and getting cleaned up, being sanctified to keep God's commandments better as they hold Jesus as their first love (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2010%3A32-38&version=ESV][Matthew 10:32-38]]*). That makes sense to me because Jesus said that whoever is believing (is doing faith) in Him is not judged. Through faith in Jesus Christ we become "doers in reality" of God's law, and we get better at it because God teaches us and sanctifies us as we trust and obey Jesus Christ from the heart. So we are justified by doing faith in Jesus and this doing of faith in Jesus is God's commandment for us being done and this brings us into keeping God's commandments in reality, and we get better at keeping God's commandments in reality as we continue doing this commandment of faith in Jesus. We get better at loving God and people (the way God commands) as we continue in faith in Jesus Christ. So being a doer in reality of the word, of Jesus Christ, of Jesus Christ's commandments, justifies because being commandments given by Christ Himself, to truly obey them implies that they are done out of a loving faith in Jesus Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2081%3A12-15&version=ESV][Psalms 81:12-15]]*). So a person is saved by obeying Jesus Christ and that salvation is inclusive of sanctification as we are saved by sanctification that happens as we hold faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%202%3A10-13&version=ESV][II Thessalonians 2:10-13]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%203%3A18&version=ESV][II Corinthians 3:18]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A16-18&version=ESV][Acts 26:16-18]]*) in Jesus Christ.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

For God shows no partiality. For all who have sinned without the law will also perish without the law, and all who have sinned under the law will be judged by the law. For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but the doers of the law who will be justified. For when Gentiles, who do not have the law, by nature do what the law requires, they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the law. They show that the work of the law is written on their hearts, while their conscience also bears witness, and their conflicting thoughts accuse or even excuse them on that day when, according to my gospel, God judges the secrets of men by Christ Jesus. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ Analogy :: In mathematics, you may have met the concept of a "gradient". If the gradient is positive then the function is increasing in value as its input is increasing. In sanctification, having a "positive gradient" is having "faith and love for God" (the love of the truth, receptive to Jesus) where a person draws near to God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A6&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:6]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%207%3A25&version=ESV][Hebrews 7:25]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%204%3A7-8&version=ESV][James 4:7-8]]*). Having a negative gradient (hatred for the truth) leads to death. - https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient

The LORD will break down their altars and destroy their pillars. For now they will say: We have no king, for we do not fear the LORD; and a king—what could he do for us? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A person is justified by having faith in Jesus Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%202%3A15-16&version=ESV][Galatians 2:15-16]]*) in their heart (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A10&version=ESV][Romans 10:10]]*).
A person is sanctified (cleaned up, conformed to Christ's image) by faith in Jesus Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A16-18&version=ESV][Acts 26:16-18]]*) and love for family in Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A22&version=ESV][I Peter 1:22]]*).
A person is saved through sanctification (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%202%3A10-13&version=ESV][II Thessalonians 2:10-13]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%203%3A18&version=ESV][II Corinthians 3:18]]*).
The propitiation for sin that empowers this sanctification is the shed blood of Jesus Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%209%3A22&version=ESV][Hebrews 9:22]]*).

In engineer language, the "justification", therefore, I'd liken to a gradient, and that is the heart posture towards God by having a loving faith in Jesus Christ.
And the "sanctification", I'd liken to be the "transformation" of the person towards conforming to Christ's image.

Salvation involves both justification (which comes from having a commendable heart attitude: *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2045%3A22-25&version=ESV][Isaiah 45:22-25]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%201%3A30&version=ESV][I Corinthians 1:30]]*) and sanctification (which is the transformation unto Christ's image from one degree of glory to the next: *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%202%3A13&version=ESV][II Thessalonians 2:13]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%203%3A18&version=ESV][II Corinthians 3:18]]*).

(ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

For this comes from the Lord who is the Spirit. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ Analogy :: Let's say you have genuine faith and love for Jesus which involves loving one's family. Holding this faith, you see a brother in need. They look hungry and you have cookies, so you ask them if they would like a cookie and they say yes. So far so good. Now along the way to give them a cookie you change your mind and heart attitude and secretly start to hope that they choke on the cookie. Now when you meet them with the cookie, would it still be a good deed you are doing now that you desire evil for this person? Of course it would no longer be a good deed you are doing. We need to be overcome by practicing righteousness (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A17-20&version=ESV][Romans 6:17-20]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Peter%202%3A19&version=ESV][II Peter 2:19]]*).

We make God our strength when our heart is turned towards God. We are relying on God when we are trusting Jesus Christ and from a love of the truth in our hearts, obedient to Him, so relying on God, and having faith in God and hoping in Him and doing good from our own hearts is not in opposition (i.e. relying on God and doing good are not in opposition), Biblically speaking:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Jeremiah%2017%3A5&version=ESV][Jeremiah 17:5]]* - Thus says the LORD: Cursed is the man who trusts in man and makes flesh his strength, whose heart turns away from the LORD. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

In order to have a genuine faith in Jesus, we need to be people who are after God's commendation. So rather than those who seek appraisal in this world and commendation from even fellow Christians, we need to instead be seeking commendation from God Himself. If a person is a "seeker of the glory that comes from man" then they are not "seekers of the glory that comes from God" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A6-11&version=ESV][Romans 2:6-11]]*) and they can't have genuine faith in Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A28-29&version=ESV][John 5:28-29]],37-47* - Do not marvel at this, for an hour is coming when all who are in the tombs will hear his voice and come out, those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment. And the Father who sent me has himself borne witness about me. His voice you have never heard, his form you have never seen, and you do not have his word abiding in you, for you do not believe the one whom he has sent. You search the Scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that bear witness about me, yet you refuse to come to me that you may have life. If another comes in his own name, you will receive him. *How can you believe, when you receive glory from one another and do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?* Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father. There is one who accuses you: Moses, on whom you have set your hope. If you believed Moses, you would believe me; for he wrote of me. #+END_QUOTE
