+ Analogy :: Let's just say you wanted to do something nice for somebody for their birthday and so you make them a chocolate cake. But when it came to giving the cake, it was rejected. You didn't know but it just so happened that chocolate cakes remind that person of something bad that they experienced. You didn't know, but you thought you had good motivations (at least you thought you were doing a good thing, or perhaps thought what you were doing was more good than bad, let's just say). Someone else might accuse you of bad intentions and say that it was a very bad thing that you did. But Christians aim to receive praise from God who sees even our hearts, rather than from anyone else. This isn't reason enough alone to by default act presumptuously (and ask forgiveness later). If a person is by faith obeying Jesus' instructions (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1-2&version=ESV][I John 5:1-2]]*) they have done nothing wrong in doing that, even if they are criticised by others for having done wrong. But acting out of sincerity and out of good intention could potentially also be done not out of a trust for the truth, but rather out of trusting some other thing that is not the truth. For example, a person's personal truth (i.e. their beliefs) may not be in agreement with the truth of God. It's important that when we do act out of sincerity, that it's also out of faith in God (in agreement with God to our knowledge). What is not done in faith is sin (faith being trust in and love for the truth).

Whatever does not proceed from faith sin (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]*), and sin is lawlessness (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A4&version=ESV][I John 3:4]]*), and any obedience that doesn't come from a love for the truth is feigned (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A45&version=ESV][Luke 6:45]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2081%3A15&version=ESV][Psalms 81:15]]*). We must be law of faith abiding (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15&version=ESV][John 14:15]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A27&version=ESV][Romans 3:27]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%209%3A21&version=ESV][I Corinthians 9:21]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2013%3A41&version=ESV][Matthew 13:41]]*).

We are justified by faith in Jesus, and what is not done in faith is sin. So if a person really were to commit sin, then they have done so without faith:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%203%3A2&version=ESV][II Thessalonians 3:2]]* - and that we may be delivered from wicked and evil men. For not all have faith. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]* - But whoever has doubts is condemned if he eats, because the eating is not from faith. For whatever does not proceed from faith is sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

As a slave of righteousness, one's actions are done while holding faith in the truth, trusting, believing, loving that which is the Truth (i.e. trusting even the teaching). Being "obedient from the heart" implies that one "loves the Truth" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A45&version=ESV][Luke 6:45]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2081%3A15&version=ESV][Psalms 81:15]]*):

But thanks be to God, that you who were once slaves of sin have become obedient from the heart to the standard of teaching to which you were committed, and, having been set free from sin, have become slaves of righteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]* - But whoever has doubts is condemned if he eats, because the eating is not from faith. For whatever does not proceed from faith is sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

For example, where Jesus says it's more blessed to give than to receive ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2020%3A35&version=ESV][Acts 20:35]]), the person with faith in Jesus Christ trusts that this is true. Worldly wisdom would say that trusting God's advice is folly. But faith in Jesus Christ invests in God rather than investing in perishable things:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%209%3A6&version=ESV][II Corinthians 9:6]]* - The point is this: whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows bountifully will also reap bountifully. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The Spirit whom those who have faith in Jesus receive works through us:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%207%3A39&version=ESV][John 7:39]]* - Now this he said about the Spirit, whom those who believed in him were to receive, for *as yet the Spirit had not been given, because Jesus was not yet glorified*.
#+END_QUOTE

O righteous Father, even though the world does not know you, I know you, and these know that you have sent me.  I made known to them your name, and I will continue to make it known, that the love with which you have loved me may be in them, and I in them.

Connecting *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A6-11&version=ESV][Romans 2:6-11]]* to *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A28-29&version=ESV][John 5:28-29]],37-47*. We must be those who do good from a love of the Truth and be those who seek the glory that comes from the only God (i.e. seek God's commendation, seek to please God). So we must love Jesus Christ and from the love of Jesus Christ and His words and His deeds.

So without the love of God in us, and a desire to please God seeking the glory from God, seeking God's approval (as opposed to man's approval), we can't even have genuine faith. Thankfully, God is pleased with us if we receive Jesus, if we love Him, if we have faith in Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2016%3A25-28&version=ESV][John 16:25-28]]* - I have said these things to you in figures of speech. The hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in figures of speech but will tell you plainly about the Father. In that day you will ask in my name, and I do not say to you that I will ask the Father on your behalf; for *the Father himself loves [[strongs:G5368][(G5368 philei)]] you, _because you have loved [[strongs:G5368][(G5368 pephilēkate)]] me and have believed that I came from God._* I came from the Father and have come into the world, and now I am leaving the world and going to the Father.
#+END_QUOTE

God loved us first in sending Jesus Christ to die for our sins and raised to life for our justification so that we might live through faith in Jesus Christ (trusting and abiding in Jesus' teachings out of a love for the truth, out of a love for the light, out of a love for Jesus Christ and His word).

It's not a belief in God that is devoid of love which saves a person.
It's faith in God that loves the Truth that saves a person (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%202%3A9-10&version=ESV][II Thessalonians 2:9-10]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15&version=ESV][John 14:15]]*).
It's trusting belief in God that understands God's worth that saves, knowing we need God, in the heart of a person valuing Jesus the Messiah.
When we call on Jesus to save us, it's with love for Jesus because we know we need Him (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%201%3A28-31&version=ESV][Proverbs 1:28-31]]*).
Though He loved us first, before we have loved Him and we recognise that.
From a sincere faith, a pure heart and good conscience, we love one-another.
It's obedience from the start to the finish (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%202%3A12-16&version=ESV][Philippians 2:12-16]]*).
It's not faith then obedience. Faith *is* obedient, and it is loving (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A23&version=ESV][I John 3:23]]*).

Love:
- God loved us first (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A19&version=ESV][I John 4:19]]*).
- If anyone loves God, he is known by God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%208%3A3&version=ESV][I Corinthians 8:3]]*).
- Whoever loves, keeping Jesus' commandments, knows God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A7&version=ESV][I John 4:7]]*).
- Father God loves those who love Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2016%3A25-28&version=ESV][John 16:25-28]]*).
- Whoever keeps Jesus' commandments loves Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A21&version=ESV][John 14:21]]*).
- Whoever loves Jesus must also love their family in Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A19-21&version=ESV][I John 4:19-21]]*).
- Whoever hates their brother doesn't have eternal life in them (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A13-16&version=ESV][I John 3:13-16]]*).

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
   *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A13-16&version=ESV][I John 3:13-16]]* - Do not be surprised, brothers, that the world hates you. _We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers._ Whoever does not love abides in death. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him. By this we know love, that he laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We should examine ourselves to see if we are sound in the faith (in the teaching of Jesus Christ):

For we are glad when we are weak and you are strong. Your restoration is what we pray for. (ESV)

Jesus loved us first:

So, real agapé love for Jesus saves. Real agapé love for Jesus loves Father God (*John 5:37-42*). And hatred for Jesus hates Father God (*John 15:22-24*).

And those who hate Father God will be repayed (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy%2032%3A43&version=ESV][Deuteronomy 32:43]]*).

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy%207%3A9-10&version=ESV][Deuteronomy 7:9-10]]* - Know therefore that the LORD your God is God, the faithful God who keeps covenant and steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments, to a thousand generations, and repays to their face those who hate him, by destroying them. He will not be slack with one who hates him. He will repay him to his face. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

In giving Jesus, in sending Jesus to us, and in Christ dying for us, God demonstrates His love for us (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A16&version=ESV][John 3:16]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%205%3A7-10&version=ESV][Romans 5:7-10]]*).

    people ahead of his own when he was on this earth.
    He helped all people in need, not just
    those who were his followers. Jesus loved all.

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%205%3A1&version=ESV][Ephesians 5:1]]* - Therefore be imitators of God, as beloved children. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A person who truly loves Jesus is forgiven by necessity just as it is that someone who is truly forgiven by Jesus must also have love for Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%207%3A47&version=ESV][Luke 7:47]]*).
But God loved us first (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A19&version=ESV][I John 4:19]]*), so it follows that someone can have been loved without having yet loved back.
While Jesus may intercede for those who act ignorantly in disbelief (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2023%3A34&version=ESV][Luke 23:34]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%201%3A13&version=ESV][I Timothy 1:13]]*), Jesus calls a person guilty of sin for knowing God's will but not doing it (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A22-24&version=ESV][John 15:22-24]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2012%3A47-48&version=ESV][Luke 12:47-48]]*).
A person is forgiven by faith in Jesus' name (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2010%3A43&version=ESV][Acts 10:43]]*), which necessitates the fear of God, so a love for truth (i.e. the truth of who Jesus is: Son of God, Son of Man, Messiah), rather than a hatred of the truth. A person is condemned for rejecting Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2016%3A16&version=ESV][Mark 16:16]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A22-24&version=ESV][John 15:22-24]]*).
Continuing in faith in God and love for God is necessary for ongoing forgiveness (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A18&version=ESV][Acts 26:18]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A42&version=ESV][John 8:42]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A12&version=ESV][John 1:12]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A10&version=ESV][I John 3:10]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%201%3A13-14&version=ESV][Colossians 1:13-14]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A7&version=ESV][I John 1:7]]*), then God bears with us in hope (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2013%3A7&version=ESV][I Corinthians 13:7]]*) that we will love Him back (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%202%3A4&version=ESV][I Timothy 2:4]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A7-21&version=ESV][I John 4:7-21]]*) so that we will live (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy%2030%3A6&version=ESV][Deuteronomy 30:6]]*).
A person must not remain hateful towards God, nor towards those who are their family in Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A2&version=ESV][I John 5:2]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A21&version=ESV][I John 4:21]]*).

#+END_QUOTE

So even though God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2018%3A20-24&version=ESV][Ezekiel 18:20-24]]*),
God doesn't force us to love Him, but we need to (*John 5:37-42*, *John 15:22-24*).

God hands people who resist Him over to their own counsel, leading to their self-destruction. As God speaks through the prophet Ezekiel [ in *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2018%3A30&version=ESV][Ezekiel 18:30]]* ], "Repent and turn from all your transgressions, lest iniquity be your ruin":

Those who hate the LORD would feign obedience, and their doom would last forever. (engbsb2020eb)

So we come to Jesus, as the woman did in *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%207%3A40-50&version=ESV][Luke 7:40-50]]*, by faith and love for Jesus.

How do we love Jesus? Well, we treasure Him (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2013%3A44-46&version=ESV][Matthew 13:44-46]]*).
We understand He loved us first (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A10&version=ESV][I John 4:10]]*).
We confess Jesus Christ is the Son of God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A15-17&version=ESV][I John 4:15-17]]*) from a heart of love for the truth (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2012%3A33-37&version=ESV][Matthew 12:33-37]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A8-10&version=ESV][Romans 10:8-10]]*).

(ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus does intercede to Father God but it's those who are drawing near to God through Him who are being saved by Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%207%3A25&version=ESV][Hebrews 7:25]]* - Consequently, he is able to save to the uttermost those who draw near to God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them. (ESV)

    Being yoked primarily to Christ to follow Jesus primarily, we do the will of God for us, and we know that the will of God for is us our sanctification. But God not only has a will for us that is universal to all believers, but also He has a unique will for us individually. And being yoked to Christ means that Christ is our Master primarily rather than even one another. We have to be yoked to Christ first and foremost, even above religious leaders such as pastors. Obedience to other people must be "in the Lord" and "in the Lord" we abide in Christ's commandments. So even to one's previous father, or to their employer, or other earthly masters, the Christian's obedience has to be whilst abiding in Christ's teachings. For example, if one's previous father commanded, "Call me father." or if they, say, instructed you to "Abort your baby." when the disciple of Jesus is trying to obey Jesus Christ's commandment to call no man on earth father and to resist sin because to abort the baby would be sin, then, the disciple of Jesus is obligated to obey Jesus Christ rather than this person they previously called father, and to not abort the baby. Because the Christian's obedience must be "in the Lord" and thus ultimate duty is to Christ Himself rather than anyone else. We should just aim to follow Christ and that may lead us to do God's will for us individually but it's still in Christ. If there is a disagreement between two followers of Jesus, it may still be the case that both are "in Christ" but can't see the end of another's journey. But Jesus being Alpha and Omega can see the end of all of our journeys:

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2021%3A21-23&version=ESV][John 21:21-23]]* - When Peter saw him, he said to Jesus, Lord, what about this man? Jesus said to him, If it is my will that he remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me! So the saying spread abroad among the brothers that this disciple was not to die; yet Jesus did not say to him that he was not to die, but, If it is my will that he remain until I come, what is that to you? (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2015%3A37-40&version=ESV][Acts 15:37-40]]* - Now Barnabas wanted to take with them John called Mark. But Paul thought best not to take with them one who had withdrawn from them in Pamphylia and had not gone with them to the work. And there arose a sharp disagreement, so that they separated from each other. Barnabas took Mark with him and sailed away to Cyprus, but Paul chose Silas and departed, having been commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    If someone wants forgiveness from me then it would go along way for them to confess to me that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, or that Jesus Christ died for their sins. If someone makes a confession of faith to me of the truth about Jesus then I might consider them to be family in Christ and then I am obligated to bear no grudge against them, but I am still allowed to reprove them. But not knowing where they stand on any issue of what they consider to be sin committed against me, whether it was or was not sin, I would leave it to the just judgement/discipline of God, but I'm still not under obligation to be yoked to that person, but if they have done something grievous in the sight of God. Now if that person came to me and confessed to me that they have sinned against me but that they repent of it (i.e. they presently do not want to sin like that because they want to walk as God wants them to) then I am obligated to forgive them for it if I believe they have actually sinned against me because they have turned away from sinning against me, they have confessed it to me, agreeing with me on it, and we are both in agreement that Jesus Christ is the Son of God and that He died for our sins.

    A born-again Christian's true Father is God. They do not have a father on earth. The Christian's mother, brothers and sisters are those who hear the word of God and do it. We must all love one-another who are in Christ and not bear grudges against one-another. Jesus testified that the world's works are evil. Whoever is having faith in Jesus Christ is not condemned. Whoever is disfaithing (disbelieving, distrusting, hating the truth) of Jesus is condemned. If someone rejects Jesus' word, that same word they rejected will judge them on the last day. So in Christ, having faith in Jesus we can have forgiveness and be reconciled to one-another. But if one person is anti-Jesus, how can there be reconciliation? Can a person forgive what God will pour His wrath out on? Are we not to separate from and not be unequally yoked with unbelievers? If someone sins against only me, I can forgive them if I choose to. But if they don't repent, then am I under obligation to forgive them? Only if they are family in Christ am I under obligation to forgive them for sin done against me personally. If I do not know if they are family in Christ, then I still might forgive them. But that doesn't mean God will forgive them. I might petition to God to forgive them. But it's up to God whether He wants to forgive them or not. I might pray to Father God asking that He forgive them because they act in ignorance, asking to grant them grace to come to know God through faith in Jesus.
    
    Forgiveness is in Christ. In Christ, we abide in Christ's commandments. When Jesus petitioned His Father to forgive those for they do not know what they do, those people were in ignorance. The Apostle Paul received mercy because he acted ignorantly in disbelief. But when people sin against the truth, not in ignorance, but are genuinely unrepentant and against the truth, trying to deter you from following Jesus, it's actually fine to withhold forgiveness until they repent, but hope they will repent, and then if your "brother" (family in Christ so now trusting Jesus rather than not trusting Jesus) comes to you and says they repent (change their mind), or listens to you as you explain their fault (i.e. the word you are saying finds place in them), we must forgive them. Nothing wrong with rebuking someone who is trying to deter you from following Jesus. It's not unloving to rebuke. 
    
    *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Leviticus%2019%3A17-18&version=ESV][Leviticus 19:17-18]]* - *‘You shall not hate your fellow countryman in your heart; you may surely reprove your neighbor, but shall not incur sin because of him*. You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the sons of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself; I am the LORD. (NASB)
    
    Jesus rebuked the Apostle Peter, but I think it's implied that Peter listened to Jesus and received correction. Jesus reproved Peter. Christians are supposed to exhort and admonish one another. No-one can forgive antichrist spirit because they're against receiving forgiveness because forgiveness is to be had in Christ having faith in Christ (faith in Jesus and His words). Those who are antichrist will perish in their sin. Someone walking by antichrist spirit must repent or perish.

    #+END_QUOTE

      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2017%3A3-4&version=ESV][Luke 17:3-4]]* - Pay attention to yourselves! If your brother sins, rebuke him, and if he repents, forgive him, and if he sins against you seven times in the day, and turns to you seven times, saying, I repent, you must forgive him. (ESV)

    #+END_QUOTE

One's family in Christ is their neighbour (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%202%3A44-45&version=ESV][Acts 2:44-45]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%204%3A25&version=ESV][Ephesians 4:25]]*).
One's 'neighbour' is not necessarily their family in Christ.

In Christ we *must* be neighbours who love one-another (fellow believers) as ourselves. And we can make a neighbour by "being" a neigbour to them. But if they become or remain an unrepentant sinner (idolator, adulterer, etc.), then it's not wrong to separate from them (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%205%3A1-13&version=ESV][I Corinthians 5:1-13]]*). Show the love of Jesus to people, sure (Jesus loved us while we were sinners), and give them the gospel, but also separate from people who are stubbornly unrepentant.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2010%3A36-37&version=ESV][Luke 10:36-37]]* - Which of these three, do you think, proved to be a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers? He said, The one who showed him mercy. And Jesus said to him, You go, and do likewise. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A person who hates their family in Christ neither loves Christ. We are called to separate from "neighbours" who are idolators (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%206%3A14-18&version=ESV][II Corinthians 6:14-18]],7:1*). But one's family in Christ is their neighbour. And *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2022%3A37-40&version=ESV][Matthew 22:37-40]]* is really saying to love one's family in Christ /as if/ they are were yourself. In Christ we are not exactly one-another, but we are members of one-another (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%204%3A25&version=ESV][Ephesians 4:25]]*). Those who are in Christ are one in spirit (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%206%3A17-20&version=ESV][I Corinthians 6:17-20]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A19-21&version=ESV][I John 4:19-21]]* - We love because he first loved us. If anyone says, I love God, and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen cannot love God whom he has not seen. And this commandment we have from him: *whoever loves God must also love his brother*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God desires all people to be saved and come to the knowledge of the truth (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%202%3A3-6&version=ESV][I Timothy 2:3-6]]*). But not all will (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2013%3A38-43&version=ESV][Matthew 13:38-43]]*). But it should be in our heart also that other people are saved (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%202%3A24-25&version=ESV][II Timothy 2:24-25]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%202%3A24-25&version=ESV][II Timothy 2:24-25]]* - And the Lord's servant must not be quarrelsome but kind to everyone, able to teach, patiently enduring evil, correcting his opponents with gentleness. God may perhaps grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Consider that those who are generous to the needy honour God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2014%3A31&version=ESV][Proverbs 14:31]]* - Whoever oppresses a poor man insults his Maker, but he who is generous to the needy honors him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Now consider the genuineness of love and the way this love exhibits itself. Just be aware that what matters to God is our heart attitudes, the intentions as to why we do a thing, the faith and the love in the heart which is governing our actions:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2012%3A33-37&version=ESV][Matthew 12:33-37]]* - Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad, for the tree is known by its fruit. You brood of vipers! How can you speak good, when you are evil? For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks. The good person out of his good treasure brings forth good, and the evil person out of his evil treasure brings forth evil. I tell you, on the day of judgment people will give account for every careless word they speak, for by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We're under grace, still law-abiding to Christ, but not "under the law" relying on the works of the law. We don't rely on being able to carry out perfect deeds:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%208%3A1-10&version=ESV][II Corinthians 8:1-10]]* - We want you to know, brothers, about the grace of God that has been given among the churches of Macedonia, for *in a severe test of affliction, their abundance of joy and their extreme poverty have overflowed in a wealth of generosity* on their part. For they gave according to their means, as I can testify, and beyond their means, of their own free will, begging us earnestly for the favor of taking part in the relief of the saints— and this, not as we expected, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and then by the will of God to us. Faith and obedience to Jesus seem to be inseparable, like two sides of a coin, but faith is commanded (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A23&version=ESV][I John 3:23]]*).

Real agape love (love for the truth and in reality) "loves people" the way we're commanded to (i.e. the correct way) and loves the children of God the way we're commanded.

People don't have a legitimate (in the truth) claim to say "You're not loving me" if you're keeping God's commandments:

#+END_QUOTE

How do we love people on the outside of the faith? Here's a couple of ways: Show courtesy to them and pray for them (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%202%3A1&version=ESV][I Timothy 2:1]]*):

But "doing good to all" doesn't mean "love all people in the same way". Christians are called to imitate God's love. God loves us without partiality. God gives us all opportunity to repent. And God actually hands unrepentant people over to their own lusts, without partiality. God's friendship is offered without partiality, but that doesn't mean everyone is God's friend. So God loves people equally only in the sense of His "common grace". Loving one's enemies . God has both unconditional love and conditional love:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%205%3A14-15&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 5:14-15]]* - We urge you, brethren, admonish the unruly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, be patient with everyone. See that no one repays another with evil for evil, but always seek after that which is good for one another and for all people. (NASB)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A8-9&version=ESV][James 2:8-9]]* - If you really fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, You shall love your neighbor as yourself, you are doing well. But if you show partiality, you are committing sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God's universal love for people is demonstrated in what He has done already in sending Jesus Christ. But God has also conditional love that does in fact depend on our heart posture towards God. But everyone is offered this conditional love but not everyone takes it. God offers all without partiality but with conditions His friendship and His eternal love, but by free choice some people reject God's offer by not meeting the conditions:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A8-13&version=ESV][James 2:8-13]]* - If you really fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, You shall love your neighbor as yourself, you are doing well. So speak and so act as those who are to be judged under the law of liberty. For judgment is without mercy to one who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

To love one's enemies is to do good to them and to not render evil for evil to them, and to bear with them in patience, hoping for their sake that they will turn away from the love of evil:

If someone is "of the world" and acting ignorantly in unbelief being mean and nasty and greedy etc. then a Christian is really called to "do good" to them.
But if someone who claims to be a believer but is unrepentant and without the fear of God, then that person is very sinful and should be rebuked and avoided,
and left to be chastised (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%205%3A1-13&version=ESV][I Corinthians 5:1-13]]*).

This is what God's love looks like. So in imitating God's love, we should "do good to all" but doing good to a person who professes to have faith in Jesus Christ, might look like avoiding them, and letting them receive discipline.

I believe that Jesus Christ has come into the world from God as flesh (Word of God made flesh). I believe that we need to trust God rather than any voice that is speaking contrary to God. We have to be corrected by the Truth rather than led astray by some other voice. This is part of the reason why I wouldn't trust to be led by someone who does not affirm to me that Jesus is the Christ (the Messiah) who has come from God into the world as flesh (Word of God made flesh). I feel as though it's fine to ask someone questions about their faith and compare what they confess with the Scripture in order to test whether or not to trust that person. If someone confesses that Jesus is the Son of God or that Jesus is Lord, these confessions are a so far a good indication but it's OK to ask more questions. And in this way I think trust can be earned. It's important to not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. If someone hasn't made the I John 4:2 confession to you then it's OK to ask them to make this confession of faith in order to gain trust with them. If someone refuses to confess the real Jesus then it's OK to not trust them. Since one person might affirm that Jesus is the Christ but not affirm that He is the Son of God, for example, it's OK to continue asking more questions about what they believe until satisfied. We are commanded to not trust every spirit but test the spirits to see if they are from God. This type of trust is earned.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A1-3&version=ESV][I John 4:1-3]]* - Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone out into the world. By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God, and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist, which you heard was coming and now is in the world already. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%206%3A14-18&version=ESV][II Corinthians 6:14-18]],7:1* - Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership has righteousness with lawlessness? Or what fellowship has light with darkness? What accord has Christ with Belial? Or what portion does a believer share with an unbeliever? What agreement has the temple of God with idols? For we are the temple of the living God; as God said, I will make my dwelling among them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. Therefore go out from their midst, and be separate from them, says the Lord, and touch no unclean thing; then I will welcome you, and I will be a father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty. Since we have these promises, beloved, *let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of body and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hosea%204%3A17&version=ESV][Hosea 4:17]]* - Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Benefit of the doubt is not necessarily earned but trust is earned. God is worthy of our trust, but not everyone else is. I mean, sure, do good to all people, especially those of the household of faith. Even to give mercy to someone (if it's within one's power to) in hope they will not abuse grace/mercy, providing opportunities to build trust with you, this is OK. For example, a person can and should do good for their enemies in hope they will be saved and come to the knowledge of Jesus. That does not mean we should trust all people. And, also, I believe Jesus' saying, "Do not give what is holy to the dogs" applies too.
When somebody is confessing to me that Jesus Christ is the Son of God and that He died for their sins and rose from the dead, and confessing and agreeing with His teachings, then I give them the benefit of the doubt. Basically, when someone is leaning on Jesus' righteousness, I have to give them the benefit of the doubt, and be willing to serve them if they need help. But God is not mocked, and the Scripture says, let those who name the name of the Lord depart from iniquity. We trust God to take care of the unknown, and just do our duty which is to fear God and keep His commandments for us, to have faith in Jesus and love one another, abiding in Jesus' teachings. It's not our duty to do what is God's role. God discerns the hearts and minds, we can rely on God for justice. Vengeance belongs to God.

I believe that we can trust any spirit who confesses that Jesus Christ has come [from God] into the world as flesh (i.e. the Word of God made flesh) that that spirit is from God. Until they've made that confession though, so long as they are confessing truth about Jesus Christ, such as pronouncing that "Jesus is the Son of God", I give the benefit of the doubt:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A1-3&version=ESV][I John 4:1-3]]* - Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone out into the world. By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God, and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist, which you heard was coming and now is in the world already. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A22&version=ESV][I John 2:22]]* - Who is the liar but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist, he who denies the Father and the Son. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A44&version=ESV][John 8:44]]* - You are of your father the devil, and your will is to do your father's desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, and has nothing to do with the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks out of his own character, for he is a liar and the father of lies. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus has come from God into the world in the form of flesh (as in, the Word of God having *become* flesh) is the meaning of the Scripture means where it is written that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh. It's an important detail and distinction from Jesus being merely *in* an ordinary body of flesh. The word "incarnate" when used may incorrectly convey an idea that He was merely the Son of God as a spirit inside of ordinary flesh and His flesh holding no real significance. But His flesh was not ordinary flesh as His flesh is Word *become* flesh (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A1-14&version=ESV][John 1:1-14]]*), and for the propitiation of our sins He has suffered in His fleshly body, having been scourged in his flesh (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2010%3A5-14&version=ESV][Hebrews 10:5-14]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2053%3A5&version=ESV][Isaiah 53:5]]*), that is the flesh of the Son of God (it's Word of God flesh). And He had Father God and the Holy Spirit in Him (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A8-10&version=ESV][John 14:8-10]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A1-17&version=ESV][Romans 8:1-17]]*).

When testing the spirits, we must be examining the Scripture for ourselves to see if what is being said is true. Even regarding what I've said on my blog, I want people to be doing this:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2017%3A10-11&version=ESV][Acts 17:10-11]]* - The brothers immediately sent Paul and Silas away by night to Berea, and when they arrived they went into the Jewish synagogue. Now these Jews were more noble than those in Thessalonica; they received the word with all eagerness, *examining the Scriptures daily to see if these things were so*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must test everything:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%205%3A20-23&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 5:20-23]]* - Do not despise prophecies, but test everything; hold fast what is good. Abstain from every form of evil. Now may the God of peace himself sanctify you completely, and may your whole spirit and soul and body be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Love is also commanded, so is inseparable from obedience (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A23&version=ESV][I John 3:23]]*).

Jesus' flesh was sown and raised a spiritual body, just as ours will be if we have the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead in us:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A42-48&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:42-48]]* - So is it with the resurrection of the dead. What is sown is perishable; what is raised is imperishable. It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power. It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body. Thus it is written, The first man Adam became a living being; the last Adam became a life-giving spirit. But it is not the spiritual that is first but the natural, and then the spiritual. The first man was from the earth, a man of dust; the second man is from heaven. As was the man of dust, so also are those who are of the dust, and as is the man of heaven, so also are those who are of heaven.
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A9-12&version=ESV][Romans 8:9-12]]* - You, however, are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if in fact the Spirit of God dwells in you. Anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him. But if Christ is in you, although *the body is dead because of sin*, the Spirit is life because of righteousness. If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you. So then, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I believe that the power by which Jesus Christ was resurrected belongs to Father God but that Father God gave Jesus Christ authority to lay down His life that He might take it back up again.
Jesus rose from the dead under his own authority, empowered by Father God.
Jesus lays down His life that He may take it up again.

A person who does evil deeds is someone who from the love of darkness does deeds. So a person who does evil deeds does them from the love of darkness and a person who loves darkness rather than light (i.e. without excuse) is someone who receives judgement:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A19&version=ESV][John 3:19]]* - And this is the judgment: the light has come into the world, and people loved the darkness rather than the light because their deeds were evil. (ESV)

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A22-24&version=ESV][John 15:22-24]]* - If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have been guilty of sin, but now they have no excuse for their sin. #+END_QUOTE

What's quoted in the New Testament from Jesus is that Jesus spoke with His physical mouth that God is His Father. This offended some people a lot. Jesus instructs us to call God our Father as well. I believe we are not merely supposed to pray to God as Father, but also, literally, put a stop to using the title to refer to any man on earth:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A17-18&version=ESV][John 5:17-18]]* - But Jesus answered them, My Father is working until now, and I am working. The Apostle Paul here is not instructing people to call him father, but he does seem to be claiming the title. At best I'd say it's only true that Paul can claim the title until someone begins calling God the Father of Jesus Christ their own father. Jesus' commandments trump Paul's instruction:

Walking by the spirit involves obeying our Master Jesus Christ. Even though we are not "under law", it's still necessary to by faith obey Jesus Christ:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A14-18&version=ESV][Romans 6:14-18]]* - For sin will have no dominion over you, since you are not under law but under grace. What then? Are we to sin because we are not under law but under grace? By no means! Do you not know that if you present yourselves to anyone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin, which leads to death, or of obedience, which leads to righteousness? But thanks be to God, that you who were once slaves of sin have become obedient from the heart to the standard of teaching to which you were committed, and, having been set free from sin, have become slaves of righteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must receive, believe, treasure and obey Jesus Christ and His words ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2013%3A3-46&version=ESV][Matthew 13:3-46]]). We must continue in faith in Jesus, in His word, and desire God more than anything else (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%204%3A18-19&version=ESV][Mark 4:18-19]]*). These Jews had believed in Jesus but they needed to become free from sin, and Jesus promised that if they abide in His word then they are *truly* His disciples, and will come to know the truth and be set free from sin. Jesus lets these "believers" in him know that if they were "of God" then they would "love" him. We have to hear, receive, believe and treasure (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%208%3A13&version=ESV][Luke 8:13]]*) Jesus Christ and His words. The word of God must be rooted securely in our heart, so we must treasure and guard God's word in our heart (*Luke 8:13*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A31-47&version=ESV][John 8:31-47]]* - So Jesus said to the Jews who had believed ([[strongs:G4100][G4100 pepisteukotas: having believed]] [[https://biblehub.com/grammar/v-rpa-amp.htm]['V-RPA-AMP past tense']]) in him, If you abide in my word, you are truly my disciples, and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free. They answered him, We are offspring of Abraham and have never been enslaved to anyone. How is it that you say, You will become free? Jesus answered them, Truly, truly, I say to you, everyone who commits sin is a slave to sin. The slave does not remain in the house forever; the son remains forever. So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed. I know that you are offspring of Abraham; yet you seek to kill me because my word finds no place in you. I speak of what I have seen with my Father, and you do what you have heard from your father. They answered him, Abraham is our father. Jesus said to them, If you were Abraham's children, you would be doing what Abraham did, but now you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. This is not what Abraham did. You are doing what your father did. They said to him, We were not born of sexual immorality. We have one Father—even God. Jesus said to them, If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came from God and I am here. I came not of my own accord, but he sent me. Why do you not understand what I say? It is because you cannot bear to hear my word. You are of your father the devil, and your will is to do your father's desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, and has nothing to do with the truth, because there is no truth in him. If I tell the truth, why do you not believe me? Whoever is of God hears the words of God. The reason why you do not hear them is that you are not of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Receiving forgiveness from Jesus, having faith in Jesus and loving Jesus all go hand in hand. In fact, someone who truly has been forgiven by God must love in the truth and someone who does't love in the truth neither has been forgiven because if they were forgiven they would love. And notice how the woman's faith is linked with the love she has:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%207%3A40-50&version=ESV][Luke 7:40-50]]* - And Jesus answering said to him, Simon, I have something to say to you. And he answered, Say it, Teacher. A certain moneylender had two debtors. One owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty. When they could not pay, he cancelled the debt of both. Now which of them will love him more? Simon answered, The one, I suppose, for whom he cancelled the larger debt. And he said to him, You have judged rightly. Then turning toward the woman he said to Simon, Do you see this woman? I entered your house; you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair. You gave me no kiss, but from the time I came in she has not ceased to kiss my feet. You did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment. Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven—for she loved much. But he who is forgiven little, loves little. And he said to her, Your sins are forgiven. Then those who were at table with him began to say among themselves, Who is this, who even forgives sins? And he said to the woman, Your faith has saved you; go in peace. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

With the love of the truth (loving God rather than evil), we hold faith in Jesus and abide in His commandments, and by faith obeying Jesus just like Abraham did, loving righteousness and hating wickedness as Jesus did, Jesus helps us by His spirit to "love our enemies and pray for those who persecute us" so that we may be sons of our Father who is in heaven. Jesus helps us to love in the way that Jesus loves us, and Jesus loved us while we were yet sinners and bears with us and intercedes to Father God for us and saves us as we draw near to God through Him by loving God and hating evil:

Be merciful, even as your Father is merciful. (ESV)

I have a long sleeve shirt with the three nails on it which I wear sometimes.

[[./3nails.png]]

To me it represents that Jesus was pierced for our transgressions (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2053%3A5&version=ESV][Isaiah 53:5]]*).

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2053%3A5&version=ESV][Isaiah 53:5]]* - But He was pierced through for our transgressions, He was crushed for our iniquities; The chastening for our well-being fell upon Him, And by His scourging we are healed. (NASB)
#+END_QUOTE

I know that I need and will always need Jesus, and will always need God's mercy and grace.
And I know that it's really what Jesus has done in His passion, death and resurrection that I can have peace with God through faith in Him. I know that whoever presently is exercising genuine faith in Jesus Christ has forgiveness for sin and eternal life.
This faith entails trust in, confidence in and love for Jesus and His word.

And if someone presently has no agape love for Jesus then neither can they presently have real faith in God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2016%3A22&version=ESV][I Corinthians 16:22]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A31-47&version=ESV][John 8:31-47]]*) because real faith loves the truth (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%202%3A10&version=NASB][II Thessalonians 2:10]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%2022%3A9-14&version=ESV][Genesis 22:9-14]]*).
And if they do not agape love their family in Christ, but rather hate them, then neither do they love God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A19-21&version=ESV][I John 4:19-21]]*). Real agape love rejoices with the truth (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2013%3A1-8&version=ESV][I Corinthians 13:1-8]]*).
And if they agape love the world and the things of the world then they do not love Father God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A15-17&version=ESV][I John 2:15-17]]*).
A person should test themselves to see if they're in the faith and come into agreement with Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2013%3A5&version=ESV][II Corinthians 13:5]]*).
And when a person reads Jesus' word and finds themself in agreement with Him and tests themselves to see if they're in the faith and they are making decisions out of love for Jesus and His word, they don't hate their family in Christ and are abiding in Jesus' commandments etc. then they should feel peace, forgiven, hopeful, good expectation of the future (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A21-24&version=ESV][I John 3:21-24]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2010%3A28&version=ESV][Proverbs 10:28]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2010%3A24&version=ESV][Proverbs 10:24]]*).

John the Baptist's call of repentance, to repent, turn from sin, forsake sin and to love our neighbour the way we are commanded to is still for Christians to heed and do. And the wrath to come is still on its way for those who reject Jesus. But how do we accept Jesus? By doing what Abraham did. By faith we must obey Jesus Christ. We must keep Jesus' commandments and forsake sin to come to know Jesus Christ:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%203%3A4-14&version=ESV][Luke 3:4-14]]* - As it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet, The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight. Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be made low, and the crooked shall become straight, and the rough places shall become level ways, and all flesh shall see the salvation of God. He said therefore to the crowds that came out to be baptized by him, You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from [[strongs:G575][(G575 apo; from, away from, of, by)]] the wrath to come? Bear fruits in keeping with repentance. And do not begin to say to yourselves, We have Abraham as our father. For I tell you, God is able from these stones to raise up children for Abraham. Even now the axe is laid to the root of the trees. Every tree therefore that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire. And the crowds asked him, What then shall we do? And he answered them, Whoever has two tunics is to share with him who has none, and whoever has food is to do likewise. Tax collectors also came to be baptized and said to him, Teacher, what shall we do? And he said to them, Collect no more than you are authorized to do. Soldiers also asked him, And we, what shall we do? And he said to them, Do not extort money from anyone by threats or by false accusation, and be content with your wages. (ESV)

#+END_QUOTE

Our faith mustn't be a superficial faith but we must trust God's word and do it so that in time of testing we do not fall away:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%208%3A13&version=ESV][Luke 8:13]]* - And the ones on the rock are those who, when they hear the word, receive it with joy. But these have no root; they believe for a while, and in time of testing fall away. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A47-49&version=ESV][Luke 6:47-49]]* - Everyone who comes to me and hears my words and does them, I will show you what he is like: he is like a man building a house, who dug deep and laid the foundation on the rock. And when a flood arose, the stream broke against that house and could not shake it, because it had been well built. But the one who hears and does not do them is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation. When the stream broke against it, immediately it fell, and the ruin of that house was great. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%204%3A20&version=ESV][Mark 4:20]]* - But those that were sown on the good soil are the ones who hear the word and accept it and bear fruit, thirtyfold and sixtyfold and a hundredfold. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Clearly we must continue in the faith:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A1-2&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:1-2]]* - Now I would remind you, brothers, of the gospel I preached to you, which you received, in which you stand, and by which you are being saved, if you hold fast to the word I preached to you—unless you believed in vain. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%201%3A21-23&version=ESV][Colossians 1:21-23]]* - And you, who once were alienated and hostile in mind, doing evil deeds, he has now reconciled in his body of flesh by his death, in order to present you holy and blameless and above reproach before him, if indeed you continue in the faith, stable and steadfast, not shifting from the hope of the gospel that you heard, which has been proclaimed in all creation under heaven, and of which I, Paul, became a minister. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%203%3A5-6&version=ESV][Hebrews 3:5-6]]* - Now Moses was faithful in all God's house as a servant, to testify to the things that were to be spoken later, but Christ is faithful over God's house as a son. And we are his house if indeed we hold fast our confidence and our boasting in our hope. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%203%3A14&version=ESV][Hebrews 3:14]]* - For we share in Christ, if indeed we hold our original confidence firm to the end. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Maintain faith in Jesus. Remain in Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A4-7&version=ESV][John 15:4-7]]* - Remain in Me, and I will remain in you. Just as no branch can bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in Me. I am the vine and you are the branches. The one who remains in Me, and I in him, will bear much fruit. For apart from Me you can do nothing. If anyone does not remain in Me, he is like a branch that is thrown away and withers. Such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire, and burned. If you remain in Me and My words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you. (engbsb2020eb)
#+END_QUOTE

It's one thing to say, "I have been displeasing to God." And haven't we all.
It's another thing to say, "Nothing I can do can please God."
It's not true that nothing we can do can please God.
Faith pleases God and love for God's Son pleases God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A6&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:6]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2016%3A27&version=ESV][John 16:27]]*).
To say that nothing we can do can please God is to say that, there is no way to be saved, and that not even by having faith in Jesus.
To say that nothing we can do can please God is to say that, not even to turn away from sin would please God, and that not even to trust in God's promises would please God,
and that not even to love God could please God.
To say that nothing we can do can please God is an "anti-gospel".

Yet, if we have come to love Jesus Christ then it's by God's grace:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%206%3A40-44&version=ESV][John 6:40-44]]* - For this is the will of my Father, that everyone who looks on the Son and believes in him should have eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day. So the Jews grumbled about him, because he said, I am the bread that came down from heaven. They said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How does he now say, I have come down from heaven? Jesus answered them, Do not grumble among yourselves. No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him. And I will raise him up on the last day. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%202%3A21&version=ESV][Revelation of John 2:21]]* - I gave her time to repent, but she refuses to repent of her sexual immorality. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ Analogy for abiding in Jesus :: Since Jesus is the Telos of the Law and we're not "under the Law" but "law-abiding" to Christ's law then the person "under the Law" trying to fulfill the whole law might be compared to a person who is walking to a train station but the journey is impossibly difficult. God has done this in Jesus Christ. What is impossible for man to have done, Jesus did. And the other thing God does which is impossible for man to do without God is put us into Christ. According to the metaphor, then, God then puts us at the train station. And the person who is "law-abiding" to Christ's law would be someone who has come to Jesus, someone who Father God has drawn to Christ, and is now at the metaphorical train station (Jesus Christ who is the Telos of the law). God put them at the train station in Jesus. And Jesus asks us to "remain in Him". And so the analogy would be "remain at the train station" (i.e. You're already there, just don't leave the train station). Jesus won't expell you (i.e. no-one can snatch us from His hand) but He asks you to remain (i.e. abide) in Him. Don't go off wondering away. Don't leave the metaphorical train station. We examine ourselves to see if we are in the faith. For example, if we hate our brother then we have left the train station. If we do not believe Jesus is the Son of God then we have left the train station, and like the prodigal son, we must return to God by repentance. If we the branches remain in a place of not abiding in Christ then we wither. And at the end of the age the branches that are not abiding in Jesus are collected and burned.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%201%3A30&version=NASB][I Corinthians 1:30]]* - But *by His doing you are in Christ Jesus,* who became to us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification, and redemption, (NASB)
#+END_QUOTE

I believe we say thank you to God in advance with hope of salvation. But it's not without seeking commendation from God. If we pat ourselves on the back and commend ourselves for having done the will of God and think we "did it already" and then stop actually doing it, then that's not abiding in Jesus Christ anymore. Because Jesus' family continues doing the will of God. Everything we do should be done in faith. In Christ, no-one hates one-another:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%205%3A8&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 5:8]]* - But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, having put on *the breastplate of faith and love*, and for a helmet the hope of salvation. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%209%3A62&version=ESV][Luke 9:62]]* - Jesus said to him, No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We have to continue walking in love for one-another:

For it is written; Enter into the closet for a very little while until Mine anger and Mine wrath shall pass away, and I will remember a good day and will raise you from your tombs. Blessed were we, dearly beloved, if we should be doing the commandments of God in concord of love, to the end that our sins may through love be forgiven us.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2026%3A20&version=ESV][Isaiah 26:20]]* - Come, my people, enter your chambers, and shut your doors behind you; hide yourselves for a little while until the fury has passed by. (ESV)

It's *prideful* to think that a person does not need to continue on in faith and abide in Jesus Christ's teachings including confessing and forsaking sin after coming to have faith in His blood:

Jesus Christ is the Baptizer, and Jesus baptises us with Holy Spirit and with fire (rather than with H₂O water), although "living water" is an expression used to refer to Holy Spirit (*John 7:37-39*). Jesus who is greater in the Kingdom of God than that John the Baptist baptizes with a baptism that is greater and more power than John's baptism:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%203%3A16&version=ESV][Luke 3:16]]* - John answered them all, saying, I baptize you with water, but he who is mightier than I is coming, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie. He will baptize you with *the Holy Spirit* and with fire.
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2011%3A16&version=ESV][Acts 11:16]]* - And I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said, John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%204%3A10&version=ESV][John 4:10]]* - Jesus answered her, If you knew the gift of God, and who it is that is saying to you, Give me a drink, you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Heal me, O LORD, and I shall be healed; save me, and I shall be saved, for you are my praise. Behold, they say to me, Where is the word of the LORD? Let it come! (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So we should trust and obey Jesus and Jesus will baptise us with Holy Spirit:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A9-14&version=ESV][John 15:9-14]]* - As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you. Abide in my love. If you keep my commandments, you will abide in my love, just as I have kept my Father's commandments and abide in his love. *These things I have spoken to you, that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be full.* This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you. Greater love has no one than this, that someone lays down his life for his friends. You are my friends if you do what I command you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Although they express love with their mouths, their hearts pursue dishonest gain. Indeed, you are to them like a singer of love songs with a beautiful voice, who skillfully plays an instrument. They hear your words but do not put them into practice. (engbsb2020eb)
#+END_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

We should just do what the Lord Jesus Christ says and disregard the advice of those who would deter us:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%201%3A1-6&version=ESV][Psalms 1:1-6]]* - Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the wicked, nor stands in the way of sinners, nor sits in the seat of scoffers; but his delight is in the law of the LORD, and on his law he meditates day and night. He is like a tree planted by streams of water that yields its fruit in its season, and its leaf does not wither. In all that he does, he prospers. The wicked are not so, but are like chaff that the wind drives away. #+END_QUOTE

It's Jesus Christ who is our teacher, and we should direct those who we teach to follow Jesus Christ directly and for themselves. Jesus' word is authoritative. But Jesus' instruction to not call ourself 'teacher', or 'instructor', or 'rabbi' (, and it follows also 'master', 'Lord' etc.) doesn't mean we should not progress into teaching others after we have become skilled in the word of righteousness. At some point we should get to the point where we can teach and disciple others, but we should be directing people to have their own faith in Jesus Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A8-11&version=ESV][Matthew 23:8-11]]* - But you are not to be called rabbi, for you have one teacher, and you are all brothers. And call no man your father on earth, for you have one Father, who is in heaven. Neither be called instructors, for you have one instructor, the Christ. The greatest among you shall be your servant. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%205%3A12-14&version=ESV][Hebrews 5:12-14]]* - For though by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to teach you again the basic principles of the oracles of God. You need milk, not solid food, for everyone who lives on milk is unskilled in the word of righteousness, since he is a child. But solid food is for the mature, for those who have their powers of discernment trained by constant practice to distinguish good from evil. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus isn't saying in *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2011%3A2-13&version=ESV][Luke 11:2-13]]* that the one knocking is *not* a friend of the one who gets up, but Jesus is saying the friend is impudent/persistent in asking his friend. And so, we should certainly be friends with God, doing what Jesus commands us as friends of Jesus do as He commands (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A9-14&version=ESV][John 15:9-14]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A13-17&version=ESV][John 15:13-17]]*). And we should persist and ask God for Holy Spirit. So what I'd say is that we should be keeping Jesus' commandments and when we ask God for something, we knock on His door for it, at any time. And we should ask God for Holy Spirit (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2011%3A2-13&version=ESV][Luke 11:2-13]]*).

Thanks to Jesus condemning sin in the flesh, now for those who live according to the Spirit (trusting, treasuring and obeying God, His Word, Jesus Christ, Jesus' teachings in reality in the heart) setting their minds on the Spirit, we can fulfill the requirement of the law, having the law-fulfilling love of God in us that does not want to harm our neighbour (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2013%3A8-10&version=ESV][Romans 13:8-10]]*), that loves agape (from the heart) the children of God in the way that God commands us to (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1-2&version=ESV][I John 5:1-2]]*), the way that is keeping Jesus' commandments (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2033%3A31-32&version=ESV][Ezekiel 33:31-32]]*), and keeping Jesus' commandments is what it means to love Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A21&version=ESV][John 14:21]]*).
Whoever abides in Jesus Christ (whoever is *presently holding their faith in Him*, by faith obeying Jesus Christ) is not condemned by God. So there is peace with God in Christ, as we trust and obey Jesus Christ. We should use our freedom to serve one another:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A3-4&version=ESV][Romans 8:3-4]]* - For God has done what the law, weakened by the flesh, could not do. By sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, he condemned sin in the flesh, *in order that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us*, who walk not according to the flesh but according to the Spirit. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1-2&version=ESV][I John 5:1-2]]* - Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the Father loves whoever has been born of him. _By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God *and* obey his commandments._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A13-14&version=ESV][Galatians 5:13-14]]* - For you were called to freedom, brothers. Only do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but *through love serve one another.* For the whole law is fulfilled in one word [[strongs:G3056][(G3056 logō)]]: *You shall love your neighbor as yourself.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://biblehub.com/greek/25.htm][G25 agapáō]] :: [Agapé love] focuses on value-driven (a decision-based) love – which of course does not exclude affection! ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/5384.htm][quote]])

God has done a thing for us freely, that is giving Jesus Christ and that is how God demonstates His agape (treasuring, valuing) love for us (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%205%3A7-8&version=ESV][Romans 5:7-8]]*).
The sacrifice was made before the offer was received by us.
God does not want people to perish (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2018%3A20-24&version=ESV][Ezekiel 18:20-24]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Peter%203%3A9-13&version=ESV][II Peter 3:9-13]]*).
Therefore it was a completely unconditional act of love on God's part.

God's sacrifice in giving Jesus was God's greatest act of love towards us, and it was an unconditional act of love. No-one can say God hasn't loved them unconditionally:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A13&version=ESV][John 15:13]]* - Greater love has no one than this, that someone lays down his life for his friends. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God has made the "first move":

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A8-10&version=ESV][I John 4:8-10]]* - Anyone who does not love does not know God, because God is love. In this the love of God was made manifest among us, that God sent his only Son into the world, so that we might live through him. In this is love, not that we have loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

In God's unconditional love He has paid the price for us to be saved from sin and death and hell. John 3:16 is not only saying that God has done what is needed for our sins to be forgiven, but is also saying that Jesus has come into the world as light so we can even turn away from darkness and towards light. Whoever stops following darkness and instead follows Jesus, whoever trusts in Jesus, whoever looks to Jesus and does what Jesus instructs, turns away from doing evil and in coming to faith in Jesus they will live. Jesus came into the darkness of the world as light so that we can turn to the light and in doing so, live. If Jesus didn't come then we could not receive the light of correction:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2012%3A46&version=ESV][John 12:46]]* - I have come into the world as light, so that whoever believes in me may not remain in darkness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A9-12&version=ESV][I John 4:9-12]]* - In this the love of God was made manifest among us, that God sent his only Son into the world, so that we might live through him. In this is love, not that we have loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins. Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another. No one has ever seen God; *if we love one another, God abides in us and his love is perfected in us.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2011%3A25-26&version=ESV][Matthew 11:25-26]]* - At that time Jesus said, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that You have hidden these things from the wise and intelligent and have revealed them to infants. Yes, Father, for this way (*[[https://biblehub.com/greek/3779.htm][Houtōs; in this way]]*) was well-pleasing in Your sight [[strongs:G2107][(G2107 eudokia; [good] desired, well-pleasing)]]. (NASB)
