Whoever has faith in Jesus Christ is able to not remain in darkness. Because we have all fallen short of Jesus' glory, we all need forgiveness and God has provided the means for that to happen. If we are presently trusting in Jesus Christ abiding in His commandments, we are receiving forgiveness and being washed by the blood of Jesus. We receive a "clean slate" with God and the means, the power, to fulfill the requirement of the law, to love God and one-another as commanded, and if we love God as He has commanded then we will live (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy%2030%3A6&version=ESV][Deuteronomy 30:6]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A7-21&version=ESV][I John 4:7-21]]* - Beloved, let us love one another, for love is from God, and whoever loves has been born of God and knows God. Anyone who does not love does not know God, because God is love. In this the love of God was made manifest among us, that God sent his only Son into the world, so that we might live through him. In this is love, not that we have loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins. Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another. No one has ever seen God; if we love one another, God abides in us and his love is perfected in us. By this we know that we abide in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit. And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent his Son to be the Savior of the world. Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him, and he in God. So we have come to know and to believe the love that God has for us. God is love, and whoever abides in love abides in God, and God abides in him. By this is love perfected with us, so that we may have confidence for the day of judgment, because as he is so also are we in this world. There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear. For fear has to do with punishment, and whoever fears has not been perfected in love. We love because he first loved us. If anyone says, I love God, and hates his brother, he is a liar; for *he who does not love his brother whom he has seen cannot love God whom he has not seen*. And this commandment we have from him: whoever loves God must also love his brother. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

By faith we walk believing the truth and loving one-another. In doing so we have forgiveness for sins past, and it frees us from condemnation and enables us to worship God in reality and to love one-another in reality. In other words, we can focus on doing what God wants us to do, rather than our past mistakes, and God helps us to do that. If we keep walking in the light, the blood of Jesus continues washing us. Whoever has real faith in Jesus Christ is able to and also must necessarily love their family in Christ. We need to "walk in the light" while we have the light (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2012%3A35-43&version=ESV][John 12:35-43]]). In other words we must walk righteously while we can see the light of Jesus. We want to get "ignited" by Jesus. And being ignited, we would have faith in Jesus and love one-another as commanded. And from that love of the truth, we live, and we do good:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2012%3A35-43&version=ESV][John 12:35-43]]* - So Jesus said to them, The light is among you for a little while longer. *Walk while you have the light, lest darkness overtake you. The one who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going. While you have the light, believe in the light, that you may become sons of light.* When Jesus had said these things, he departed and hid himself from them. Though he had done so many signs before them, they still did not believe in him, so that the word spoken by the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled: Lord, who has believed what he heard from us, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? Therefore they could not believe. For again Isaiah said, He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, lest they see with their eyes, and understand with their heart, and turn, and I would heal them. Isaiah said these things because he saw his glory and spoke of him. Nevertheless, many even of the authorities believed in him, but for fear of the Pharisees they did not confess it, so that they would not be put out of the synagogue; for they loved the glory that comes from man more than the glory that comes from God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=3%20John%201%3A11&version=ESV][III John 1:11]]* - Beloved, do not imitate evil but imitate good. Whoever does good is from God; whoever does evil has not seen God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A8-12&version=ESV][I John 2:8-12]]* - At the same time, it is a new commandment that I am writing to you, which is true in him and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining. Whoever says he is in the light and hates his brother is still in darkness. Whoever loves his brother abides in the light, and in him there is no cause for stumbling. But whoever hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness, and does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes. I am writing to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven for his name's sake. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%205%3A2-5&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 5:2-5]]* - For you yourselves are fully aware that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night. While people are saying, There is peace and security, then sudden destruction will come upon them as labor pains come upon a pregnant woman, and they will not escape. But you are not in darkness, brothers, for that day to surprise you like a thief. For you are all children of light, children of the day. We are not of the night or of the darkness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%205%3A8-10&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 5:8-10]]* - But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, having put on the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet the hope of salvation. For God has not destined us for wrath, but to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ, who died for us so that whether we are awake or asleep we might live with him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God gave Jesus Christ as a ransom because He loves us. Without Father God sending Jesus into the world as light, we would have remained in darkness:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%206%3A5&version=ESV][Genesis 6:5]]* - The LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every intention of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A5&version=ESV][Romans 2:5]]* - But because of your hard and impenitent heart you are storing up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath when God's righteous judgment will be revealed. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Peter%203%3A7&version=ESV][II Peter 3:7]]* - But by the same word the heavens and earth that now exist are stored up for fire, being kept until the day of judgment and destruction of the ungodly. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%202%3A1-3&version=ESV][Ephesians 2:1-3]]* - And you were dead in the trespasses and sins in which you once walked, following the course of this world, following the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that is now at work in the sons of disobedience— among whom we all once lived in the passions of our flesh, carrying out the desires of the body and the mind, and were by nature children of wrath, like the rest of mankind. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6CKCThJB5w0&list=RD6CKCThJB5w0&start_radio=1][youtube.com:  Here I Am To Worship / The Call - Hillsong Worship {@ hillsongworship }]] :: Light of the world,
    You stepped down into darkness,
    Opened my eyes, let me see

    Hope of a life spent with You.

    Here I am to bow down

    Altogether wonderful to me!

By faith in Jesus we are justified and saved through sanctification while holding faith in Jesus. This justification by faith is required for us to continue being sanctified. We're saved through sanctification:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%205%3A9-10&version=ESV][Romans 5:9-10]]* - Since, therefore, we have now been justified by his blood, much more shall we be saved by him from the wrath of God. For if while we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, now that we are reconciled, shall we be saved by his life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A23-25&version=ESV][Romans 8:23-25]]* - And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body. For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for? But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it. (KJV)
#+END_QUOTE

A person is justified by faith in Jesus Christ in their heart, and they are saved as they hold that faith. As they hold that faith, they produce deeds done in faith. For example, a person may get water baptised while holding faith in Jesus Christ, or while holding faith in Jesus Christ they may confess to another that "Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, who came into the world from God and died for our sins on a tree and rose from the dead on the third day and has ascended into heaven":

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A14-17&version=ESV][James 2:14-17]]* - What good is it, my brothers, if someone says he has faith but does not have works? Can that faith save him? If a *brother or sister* is poorly clothed and lacking in daily food, and one of you says to them, Go in peace, be warmed and filled, without giving them the things needed for the body, what good is that? So also faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A9-10&version=ESV][Romans 10:9-10]]* - because, if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. For with the heart one believes and is justified, and with the mouth one confesses and is saved. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2016%3A16&version=ESV][Mark 16:16]]* - Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The type of faith we need is loving the truth, (i.e. loving Jesus, God's Word). The type of faith we need is faith which loves our family in Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A14-17&version=ESV][James 2:14-17]]* - What good is it, my brothers, if someone says he has faith but does not have works? Can that faith save him? If a *brother or sister* is poorly clothed and lacking in daily food, and one of you says to them, Go in peace, be warmed and filled, without giving them the things needed for the body, what good is that? So also faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A19-21&version=ESV][I John 4:19-21]]* - We love because he first loved us. If anyone says, I love God, and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen cannot love God whom he has not seen. And this commandment we have from him: *whoever loves God must also love his brother*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A10&version=ESV][I John 3:10]]* - By this it is evident who are the children of God, and who are the children of the devil: whoever does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is the one who does not love his brother. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Yes, love *values*. That means to agape love God and God's word involves valuing God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2010%3A45&version=ESV][Mark 10:45]]* - For even the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2043%3A3-4&version=ESV][Isaiah 43:3-4]]* - For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior. I give Egypt as your ransom, Cush and Seba in exchange for you. Because you are precious in my eyes, and honored, and I love you, I give men in return for you, peoples in exchange for your life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2012%3A7&version=ESV][Luke 12:7]]* - Why, even the hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not; you are of more value than many sparrows. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A17-19&version=ESV][I Peter 1:17-19]]* - And if you call on him as Father who judges impartially according to each one's deeds, conduct yourselves with fear throughout the time of your exile, knowing that you were ransomed from the futile ways inherited from your forefathers, not with perishable things such as silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without blemish or spot. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2017%3A22-23&version=ESV][Matthew 17:22-23]]* - As they were gathering in Galilee, Jesus said to them, The Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men, and they will kill him, and he will be raised on the third day. And they were greatly distressed. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2010%3A17-18&version=ESV][John 10:17-18]]* - For this reason the Father loves me, because I lay down my life that I may take it up again. No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of my own accord. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it up again. This charge I have received from my Father. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus Christ is *worthy*! Jesus Christ has worth! We must think so because we must have love for Him. And if a person gives no value to Jesus then it can't be love they have for Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%205%3A9-10&version=ESV][Revelation of John 5:9-10]]* - And they sang a new song, saying, Worthy [[strongs:G514][(G514 Axios)]] are you to take the scroll and to open its seals, for you were slain, and by your blood you ransomed people for God from every tribe and language and people and nation, and you have made them a kingdom and priests to our God, and they shall reign on the earth. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We treasure God and His word. We value God and His word and prefer God and His word:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A45&version=ESV][Luke 6:45]]* - The good person out of the good treasure of his heart produces good, and the evil person out of his evil treasure produces evil, for out of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaks. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2013%3A44-46&version=ESV][Matthew 13:44-46]]* - The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and covered up. Then in his joy he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field. Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant in search of fine pearls, who, on finding one pearl of great value, went and sold all that he had and bought it. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The fact that God has agape loved us first doesn't make void the commandment that we must love God and one another, but rather sets the context. God loved us first:

If you keep my commandments, you will abide in my love, just as I have kept my Father's commandments and abide in his love. *These things I have spoken to you, that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be full.* This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you. Greater love has no one than this, that someone lays down his life for his friends. You are my friends if you do what I command you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy%2030%3A6&version=ESV][Deuteronomy 30:6]]* - And the LORD your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your offspring, so that you will love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, that you may live. (ESV)

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2011%3A19-20&version=ESV][Ezekiel 11:19-20]]* - And I will give them one heart, and a new spirit I will put within them. And they shall be my people, and I will be their God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2016%3A22&version=ESV][I Corinthians 16:22]]* - If anyone has no love for the Lord, let him be accursed. Our Lord, come! (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A14-20&version=ESV][I John 3:14-20]]* - We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love (*[[https://biblehub.com/interlinear/1_john/3-14.htm][agapōmen]]*) the brothers. But we have free will and still need to receive the salvation, and that's why there is still a conditional aspect to this. God, through His word and in sending Jesus (God's Word made flesh) has instructed us in receiving the salvation He has bought:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%203%3A14-15&version=ESV][II Timothy 3:14-15]]* - But as for you, continue in what you have learned and have firmly believed, knowing from whom you learned it and how from childhood you have been acquainted with the sacred writings, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God's friendship is conditional on our friendship with Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2016%3A25-28&version=ESV][John 16:25-28]]* - I have said these things to you in figures of speech. In that day you will ask in my name, and I do not say to you that I will ask the Father on your behalf; for *the Father himself loves [[strongs:G5368][(G5368 philei)]] you, _because you have loved [[strongs:G5368][(G5368 pephilēkate)]] me and have believed that I came from God._* I came from the Father and have come into the world, and now I am leaving the world and going to the Father.
#+END_QUOTE

We must be friends with God rather than with the world. So we need real faith in God, faith that has the fear of God that has a real obedience based on love for the truth and hatred of evil:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%2022%3A12&version=ESV][Genesis 22:12]]* - He said, Do not lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him, for now I know that *you fear God*, seeing you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A20-23&version=ESV][James 2:20-23]]* - Do you want to be shown, you foolish person, that faith apart from works is useless? Was not Abraham our father justified by works when he offered up his son Isaac on the altar? You see that faith was active along with his works, and faith was completed by his works; and the Scripture was fulfilled that says, Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness—and he was called a friend of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%204%3A4&version=ESV][James 4:4]]* - You adulterous people! Do you not know that _friendship with the world is enmity with God_? Therefore whoever wishes to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Whoever is keeping Jesus' commandments in reality, loving one-another as He does, is loving Jesus with agape love. So having a genuine agape love for the truth involves having a genuine agape love for those who are in Jesus Christ who is the truth, and since God's Word is also truth, we must love in the truth, the way God loves:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A9-14&version=ESV][John 15:9-14]]* - As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you. Abide in my love. If you keep my commandments, you will abide in my love, just as I have kept my Father's commandments and abide in his love. *These things I have spoken to you, that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be full.* This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you. Greater love has no one than this, that someone lays down his life for his friends. You are my friends if you do what I command you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A21&version=ESV][John 14:21]]* - Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves [[strongs:G25][(G25 agapōn; loving)]] me. And *he who loves me will be loved by my Father*, and I will love him and manifest myself to him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus loved us, so in remaining faithful and obedient to Father God He was resisting committing sin, and the resisting of committing sin was done in love for our sake. And that's how we should also love one-another, by trusting and obeying God and resisting committing sin:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A1-4&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:1-4]]* - Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight, and sin which clings so closely, and let us run with endurance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is seated at the right hand of the throne of God. Consider him who endured from sinners such hostility against himself, so that you may not grow weary or fainthearted. In your struggle against sin you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%203%3A6-15&version=ESV][II Timothy 3:6-15]]* - For among them are those who creep into households and capture weak women, burdened with sins and led astray by various passions, always learning and never able to arrive at a knowledge of the truth. But they will not get very far, for their folly will be plain to all, as was that of those two men. You, however, have followed my teaching, my conduct, my aim in life, my faith, my patience, my love, my steadfastness, my persecutions and sufferings that happened to me at Antioch, at Iconium, and at Lystra—which persecutions I endured; yet from them all the Lord rescued me. Indeed, all who desire to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted, while evil people and impostors will go on from bad to worse, deceiving and being deceived. But as for you, continue in what you have learned and have firmly believed, knowing from whom you learned it and how from childhood you have been acquainted with the sacred writings, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2022%3A37-40&version=ESV][Matthew 22:37-40]]* - And he said to him, You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind. This is the great and first commandment. And a second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments depend all the Law and the Prophets. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

If a person genuinely loves Jesus then they have the fear of God in them and thus a hatred of evil and a desire to please God:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%205%3A9-12&version=ESV][II Corinthians 5:9-12]]* - So whether we are at home or away, we make it our aim to please him.   *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Peter%203%3A15&version=ESV][II Peter 3:15]]* - And count the patience of our Lord as salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote to you according to the wisdom given him, (ESV)

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A53-58&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:53-58]]* - For this perishable body must put on the imperishable, and this mortal body must put on immortality. Salvific, sanctifying faith in Jesus and in the blood of Jesus continues. It's not just a single-moment thing:

+ [[https://youtube.com/watch?v=6EBKeGC1LOo&t=626][youtube.com: Robert Henderson | 6. Courts of Heaven {@VictoryChristianCentre} @time: 10 min 26 sec]] :: I use the blood to silence the voice [of the accuser]. Of course that's Hebrews 12:24:

       *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A24&version=ESV][Hebrews12:24]]* - _and to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel. (ESV)_
    #+END_QUOTE

    Now let me just show you one scripture.

    Why it's important to repent:

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
       *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A7&version=ESV][I John 1:7]]* - _But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin. (ESV)_
    #+END_QUOTE

    It literally says *keeps on* cleansing us from all sin.

    That's actually the verbiage - it keeps on cleansing us. Why? Because
    the blood is _'not that which was *spoke*, it is that which is *speaking*'_.

    That's what it said.

    There is a blood that /speaks/ better things.

    The blood isn't something that was spoke about you.

    The blood is *speaking* concerning you.

    So watch, it says that the blood _keeps on
    cleansing us from all sin, but only when we
    walk in the light as he is in the light.

    What does that mean?

    That means I come out of darkness into the
    light.

    That means I have to repent.

    Repentance is coming out of darkness and
    into light.

    So you cannot get the benefits of the
    blood, you cannot agree with what the
    blood is saying about you unless you come
    out of darkness and into light.

Jesus being the telos of the Law, doesn't mean the abolishment of the Law, but more like the goal of it. So we must "abide" in the "telos" of the law. We're not trying to replace Jesus. We're endeavouring to imitate His love while holding faith in Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A4-11&version=ESV][Romans 10:4-11]]* - For Christ is the end [[strongs:G5056][(G5056 telos)]] of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes. For Moses writes about the righteousness that is based on the law, that the person who does the commandments shall live by them. But the righteousness based on faith says, Do not say in your heart, Who will ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down) or Who will descend into the abyss? (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead). But what does it say? The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart (that is, the word of faith that we proclaim); because, if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you *will be saved*. For with the heart one believes and is justified, and with the mouth one confesses and is saved. For the Scripture says, Everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2029%3A13-14&version=ESV][Isaiah 29:13-14]]* - And the Lord said: Because this people draw near with their mouth and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me, and their fear of me is a commandment taught by men, therefore, behold, I will again do wonderful things with this people, with wonder upon wonder; and the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the discernment of their discerning men shall be hidden. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

As the Law can find fault in any of us imperfect humans, and as Jesus Christ fulfilled the Law without sinning, we have to receive Jesus and recognise that He's good. How we respond to Jesus Christ is important. If we love Jesus Christ and believe He came from God, then Father God loves us as friends:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A19&version=ESV][Romans 3:19]]* - Now we know that whatever the law says it speaks to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be stopped, and the whole world may be held accountable to God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A19&version=ESV][John 3:19]] connects faith with deeds. Evil deeds come from a love of darkness. [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A45&version=ESV][Luke 6:45]] also connects faith with deeds. Good deeds come from a love of the truth.

Abraham's faith being active along with his "deeds" is a more accurate way to put this, because as He had faith and the fear of God in His heart Abraham was producing good deeds. That doesn't mean "works" (i.e. as in "working for"). So the faith that justifies is faith that not only "believes" but "loves". There is an allegiance to the object of the belief:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A22-24&version=ESV][James 2:22-24]]* - You see that faith was active along with his works, and faith was completed by his works [[strongs:G2041][(G2041 ergois; works/deeds)]]; and the Scripture was fulfilled that says, Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness—and he was called a *friend of God*. You see that a person is justified by works and not by faith alone. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2025%3A14&version=ESV][Psalms 25:14]]* - The friendship of the LORD is for those who fear him, and he makes known to them his covenant. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We are Jesus' friends if we do what He commands us. So we need to be people who agapé love one another as commanded to have this friendship. We need to be loving others with the type of "no strings attached, selfless agape love" that Father God demostrates by giving Jesus Christ. We need to be those who do Jesus' commandments in reality to have the friendship of Jesus and the friendship of God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A9-14&version=ESV][John 15:9-14]]* - As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you. Abide in my love. These things I have spoken to you, that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be full. This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you. Greater love has no one than this, that someone lays down his life for his friends. *You are my friends if you do what I command you.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus didn't ask to be paid back directly. Jesus wants us to pass forwards grace and mercy to our neighbour:

If a person has been baptised into Christ Jesus' death then their old self was crucified in order than the body of sin might be brought to nothing. So a person has an "old self" that was crucified and they also have "indwelling sin in the flesh". One day we will have incorruptible resurrection flesh, but a person who has been born-again spiritually carries their old flesh around until they receive this new resurrection body:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

So I find it to be a law that when I want to do right, evil lies close at hand. For I delight in the law of God, in my inner being, but I see in my members another law waging war against the law of my mind and making me captive to the law of sin that dwells in my members. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Only God carries out perfect deeds. Any mere created human being on earth will always fall short of God's goodness. The closest we might get towards "being good" might be as one of those mentioned in *Revelation of John 14:4-5*:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

It is these who follow the Lamb wherever he goes. These have been redeemed from mankind as firstfruits for God and the Lamb, and in their mouth no lie was found, for they are blameless. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Faith versus the works of the law:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A20&version=ESV][Romans 3:20]]* - For by works [[strongs:G2041][(G2041 ergōn; works)]] of the law [[strongs:G3551][(G3551 nomou; of [the] Law)]] no human being will be justified in his sight, since through the law comes knowledge of sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A28&version=ESV][Romans 3:28]]* - For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from works [[strongs:G2041][(G2041 ergōn; works)]] of the law [[strongs:G3551][(G3551 nomou; of the Law)]]. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

(ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

James connects faith with works, like flesh is to spirit.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A26&version=ESV][James 2:26]]* - For as the body apart from the spirit is dead, so also faith apart from works is dead. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Paul also connects faith with works, like flesh is to spirit.
The connection is between the external deeds (flesh/works) that come from the faith in the heart (faith/spirit).
But Paul emphasises that we should not *rely* on the *works* of the law, but rather that we are justified by *faith*.
Like it is normal for a human spirit to have a body, it is normal for faith to have works.
But we do not rely on the works for justification, but we do have confidence if we have faith ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%203%3A13&version=ESV][I Timothy 3:13]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2010%3A19&version=ESV][Hebrews 10:19]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A21&version=ESV][I John 3:21]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A17&version=ESV][I John 4:17]]). To rely on the works would be to rely on the appearances of the completion of the works, and feeling commended by that. The obvious danger with that is that mere humans, or statistics or AI look at appearances. A computer might calculate, or humans may estimate that "some person had bad intent in their heart" based on physical "measurements", or a human may feel condemned because they were unable to complete some deed perfectly.
However, God looks at the faith in the heart.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A28&version=ESV][Matthew 23:28]]* - So you also outwardly appear righteous to others, but within you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A2-14&version=ESV][Galatians 3:2-14]]* - Let me ask you only this: Did you receive the Spirit by _works [[strongs:G2041][(G2041 ergōn; works)]] of the law [[strongs:G3551][(G3551 nomou; of [the] Law)]]_ or by hearing with faith? Are you so foolish? Having begun by the Spirit, are you now being perfected by the flesh? Did you suffer so many things in vain—if indeed it was in vain? Does he who supplies the Spirit to you and works miracles among you do so by _works (G2041 ergōn; works) of the law (G3551 nomou; of the Law)_, or by hearing with faith— just as Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness? Know then that it is those of faith who are the sons of Abraham. And the Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, preached the gospel beforehand to Abraham, saying, In you shall all the nations be blessed. So then, those who are of faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith. For all who rely on _works (G2041 ergōn; works) of the law (G3551 nomou; of [the] Law)_ are under a curse; for it is written, Cursed be everyone who does not abide by all things written in the Book of the Law, and do them. Now it is evident that no one is justified before God by the law, for The righteous shall live by faith. But the law is not of faith, rather The one who does [[strongs:G4160][(G4160 poiēsas; having done, i.e. completing the doing; V-AAP-NSM)]] them [[strongs:G846][(G846 auta; these things)]] shall live by them. Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us—for it is written, Cursed is everyone who is hanged on a tree— so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles, so that we might receive the promised Spirit through faith. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ V-AAP-NSM Aorist :: Is characterized by its emphasis on _punctiliar action_; that is, the concept of the verb is considered without regard for past, present, or future time. There is no direct or clear English equivalent for this tense, though it is generally rendered as a simple past tense in most translations. The events described by the aorist tense are classified into a number of categories by grammarians. The most common of these include a view of the action as having begun from a certain point ("inceptive aorist"), or having ended at a certain point ("cumulative aorist"), or merely existing at a certain point ("punctiliar aorist").

We need to do the deeds of Abraham ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A39-40&version=ESV][John 8:39-40]]), "by faith obey" God ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A8&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:8]]) but although we intend to do the deeds that come from that faith, we do not rely on if we are able to carry them out, nor commend ourselves when we think we have. This is why it's wrong to pit obedience up against faith when we are saved by faith in Jesus ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%202%3A16&version=ESV][Galatians 2:16]]) and we are saved by obedience to Jesus ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%205%3A9&version=ESV][Hebrews 5:9]]).

The son of the promise is the one who loves God, who treasures His word and hopes in His promise because the kingdom is promised to those who love God. So we need to walk by love for Jesus Christ and Jesus Christ's word (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2016%3A25-28&version=ESV][John 16:25-28]]*):

But you have dishonored the poor man. Are not the rich the ones who oppress you, and the ones who drag you into court? Are they not the ones who blaspheme the honorable name by which you were called? If you really fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, You shall love your neighbor as yourself, you are doing well. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A28&version=ESV][Romans 8:28]]* - And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The Adamic flesh is the "old creature" inclusive of both the literal biological flesh and the mind of the person from before they are born-again of the spirit.
A person gets born-again of the spirit, but is still inside the Adamic flesh, and retains some memory of the flesh, but they await to receive the redemption of their flesh, (i.e. await to receive the resurrection body).

If there is a "3rd" birthday, then that would be the redemption of the body (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A23-25&version=ESV][Romans 8:23-25]]*):
- First birthday: born of woman (Adamic flesh and spirit)
  - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2051%3A5&version=ESV][Psalms 51:5]]*
  - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2011%3A11-12&version=ESV][I Corinthians 11:11-12]]*
- Second birthday: born of the spirt (new spirit, new creation)
  - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A5-7&version=ESV][John 3:5-7]]*
  - *[[https://biblehub.com/interlinear/2_corinthians/5-17.htm][II Corinthians 5:17]]*
  - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%203%3A8-10&version=ESV][Colossians 3:8-10]]*
- Third birthday ?: redeption of body (resurrection body)
  - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A23-25&version=ESV][Romans 8:23-25]]*

+ Journal <2026-05-19 Tue> :: I believe that when a person is born-again of the spirit and grafted into Christ, they receive a clean slate.
    Generational sin is totally wiped out, as far as the spirit is concerned.
    So along as they walk by the spirit there will be no problems with the generational sin from being in Adam.
    But until a person receives their incorruptible resurrection body, there may still be issues with the flesh.
    Consider that the Apostle Paul retained his memories of when he was persecuting the church of Jesus Christ.
    The flesh still has indwelling sin.
    A person's conscience is fixed and guilt is taken awaya when they are given a new heart and spirit.
    Having a fixed conscience means that it isn't a seared conscience. It's functions properly.
    Having a healthy conscience helps a person to walk in godliness and serve God.

Just because aquitted from sin, doesn't mean "cannot" sin, but at the point of death, their sin they had is erased, and going forth they have an advocate with Father God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A7&version=ESV][Romans 6:7]]* - For one who has died has been set free (G1344 dedikaiōtai; has been freed, aquitted) from sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A1-6&version=ESV][I John 2:1-6]]* - My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you may not sin. *But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous. He is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only but also for the sins of the whole world.* And by this we know that we have come to know him, if we keep his commandments. Whoever says I know him but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, but whoever keeps his word, in him truly the love of God is perfected. By this we may be sure that we are in him: whoever says he abides in him ought to walk in the same way in which he walked. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Q & A | RC Sproul # shorts {@ MarialynClapano }]] :: I believe this is correct teaching except I'm unsure if "regeneration" must always be instantaneous. I believe it was instantaneous for me. On [[https://web.archive.org/web/20220402091720/https://mullikine.github.io/posts/astral-projection/][2 April 2022]] I was regenerated and saw my regenerated spirit and called out to Jesus to save me because I didn't know what was happening. I was a "believer" before that but very much a slave to sin. Not long after that, about a month after, on [[https://web.archive.org/web/20220702053809/https://mullikine.github.io/posts/astral-projection-pt-3/][12 May 2022]], I experienced what felt like being "refilled" or topped up with more regeneration. This time I had a vision of healing people with compassion coming out of my soul.

    However, being born-again a person still has the flesh. If someone who lives by the spirit isn't walking by the spirit then the mind of the flesh is dominating. But we should be walking by the spirit which is the truth. So, for example, walking by the spirit a person does not call any man on earth their father, because Jesus Christ has said we have one Father who is in heaven. So if someone is regenerate, sometimes they still obey the flesh. But we have to stop doing that. So until sanctified it appears like a person has 2 personalities. One personality is actually the flesh (the man who died in baptism). The other is the one born of God, the one who loves their brother and agrees with God about the facts concerning Jesus such that He is Christ the Word of God made flesh, that He came from God, that He's the Son of God, that He's Yahweh the Son of God, that He died on a tree and rose from the dead on the 3rd day and ate a broiled fish.

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%207%3A18&version=ESV][John 7:18]]* - The one who speaks on his own authority seeks his own glory, but the one who seeks the glory of him who sent him is true, and in him there is no falsehood. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    So a person who is born-again of the spirit on earth before their flesh is resurrected is a person with a spirit with a mind agreeing with God but in a "meat suit" flesh from the people who used to be their father and mother on earth who are now no longer their father and mother because God is the father of our spirits and God is their true Father and Holy Jerusalem is their true mother.

The soul is who the person really is. New soul, new person:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%202%3A7&version=ESV][Genesis 2:7]]* - And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul [[strongs:H120][(H120 hā·’ā·ḏām; the man)]] [[strongs:H5315][(H5315 lə·ne·peš; a soul; Soul, life, self, person, heart, creature, mind, living being)]] [[strongs:H2416][(H2416 ḥay·yāh; living)]]. (KJV)
#+END_QUOTE

The way these Scriptures talk about "two in one bed, one will be taken and the other left" makes sense to me if thinking of a person as a person born of God inside the sinful flesh:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2017%3A32-37&version=ESV][Luke 17:32-37]]* - Remember Lot's wife. Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life will keep it. I tell you, in that night there will be two in one bed. One will be taken and the other left. There will be two women grinding together. One will be taken and the other left. And they said to him, Where, Lord? He said to them, Where the corpse is, there the vultures will gather. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A25&version=ESV][Galatians 5:25]]* - If we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

An in, the people who gave the "meat suit", but not the new spirit) (Psalms 51:5) are born-again believers, then as a born-again person who's father is now Father God, the Father of Jesus Christ, then the best way to honour them (one's previous parents) is to not call one's previous father "father" because we should be walking by faith obedient to Jesus Christ like Abraham's faith, walking like Jesus did, referring to Father God as father and Heavenly Jerusalem as mother.

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A2&version=ESV][I John 5:2]]* - By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and obey his commandments. (ESV)

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE

    I believe that the fullness of the meaning of faith alone is not faith alone in Jesus' faith "apart from" [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] our faith in Him.
    
    Jesus says "apart from" [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] from Him a person can do nothing and that "apart from" [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] from Him a person is destined to be gathered to be burned. *To not be* "apart from" [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] Him (as in, to abide in Him) is to keep His commandments (and so have union with Him):
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A4-7&version=ESV][John 15:4-7]]* - Abide in me, and I in you. Whoever abides in me and I in him, he it is that bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing. If anyone does not abide in me he is thrown away like a branch and withers; and the branches are gathered, thrown into the fire, and burned. If you abide in me, and my words abide in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2013%3A24-30&version=ESV][Matthew 13:24-30]]* - He put another parable before them, saying, The kingdom of heaven may be compared to a man who sowed good seed in his field, but while his men were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat and went away. So when the plants came up and bore grain, then the weeds appeared also. And the servants of the master of the house came and said to him, Master, did you not sow good seed in your field? How then does it have weeds? He said to them, An enemy has done this. So the servants said to him, Then do you want us to go and gather them? But he said, No, lest in gathering the weeds you root up the wheat along with them. Let both grow together until the harvest, and at harvest time I will tell the reapers, Gather the weeds first and bind them in bundles to be burned, but gather the wheat into my barn. (ESV)

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE

    #+END_QUOTE
    
    I do believe, though, that if a person has no confidence in their own faith but have faith in Jesus, relying on Jesus' righteousness rather than their own,
    asking God for mercy as they believe that they are a sinner, asking God to take pity on them, then although that person doubts their own faith, they actually do have faith.

    In Christ Jesus, no-one condemns each-another and all love one-another:
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A14&version=ESV][I John 3:14]]* - We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. Whoever does not love abides in death. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A15&version=ESV][I John 3:15]]* - Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A1&version=ESV][Romans 8:1]]* - There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A37&version=ESV][Luke 6:37]]* - , Judge not, and you will not be judged; condemn not, and you will not be condemned; forgive, and you will be forgiven; (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2053%3A6&version=ESV][Isaiah 53:6]]* - All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE
    
    It is certainly possible to have a brother in Christ who is also a "brother of the flesh", but it *isn't possible" to have a "father of the flesh" if a person is the new creation born of the spirit. The person who is born of the spirit, when they speak, they are doing the word in reality and so they do not refer to any man on earth as their father, since they have been born of God, not of woman. The previous self was the one born of woman. The new creation who is born of the spirit, their Father is God. God is the father of our spirits:
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philemon%201%3A15-16&version=ESV][Philemon 1:15-16]]* - For this perhaps is why he was parted from you for a while, that you might have him back forever, no longer as a slave but more than a slave, as a beloved brother—especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE
    
    One's previous parents ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A9&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:9]]), if they are born-again Christians would now be one's "brother and sister" in the Lord.
    Walking by the spirt, a person would properly refer to them as one's "brother and sister", rather than "father and mother".
    Walking by the flesh, a person would still refer to them as "father and mother".
    
    We need to be those who walk by the spirit, walk in the truth, in reality [[strongs:G225][(G225 alētheia)]]:
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A21&version=ESV][John 3:21]]* - The [one] however practicing [[strongs:G4160][(G4160 poiōn; doing)]] the truth [[strongs:G225][(G225 alētheian)]] comes [[strongs:G2064][(G2064 erchetai)]] to the Light [[strongs:G5457][(G5457 phōs)]] that may be manifest [[strongs:G5319][(G5319 phanerōthē)]] his works [[strongs:G2041][(G2041 erga)]] that in God [[strongs:G2316][(G2316 Theō)]] have been [[strongs:G1510][(G1510 estin)]] done [[strongs:G2038][(G2038 eirgasmena)]] (Interlinear)
    #+END_QUOTE
    
    If a person wants to evangelise effectively to a "brother of the flesh" then I believe the best way is to stop calling them brother. If the person wanting to lead them to Jesus continues referring to them as a brother when they are not a believer, then it's in a way approving of them being an unbeliever.
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%208%3A21&version=ESV][Luke 8:21]]* - But he answered them, My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE
    
    There are only 2 ways of walking. One is the Jesus way (the narrow way that leads to life, walking in the love of the truth), and the other is the "not Jesus" way (the way that leads to death, walking in darkness).
    
    It's important to be abiding in Jesus' commandments.
    If a person does what Jesus instructs then they abide in Him.
    
    Some intuition about how abiding in Jesus works. I'm not like, totally certain about these logical implications, but I hope it helps to show that in Christ Jesus, no-one condemns one-another and all love one-another.
    - If a person (A) hates someone else (B) then at least one of those people cannot be in Jesus Christ.
    - If a person (A) hates someone else (B) who definitely abides in Jesus Christ then the person (A) is not in Jesus Christ.
    - If a born-again believer in Jesus Christ (A) condemns another person (B) then person (A) will not be seeing person (B) in heaven because there is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.

+ God being our only Father :: The implanted word is the new person and this person agrees with who Jesus Christ is, and hears and agrees with what Jesus says, and so after first coming to believe in Jesus Christ we need to continue holding our faith in Him and renewing our mind which means thinking more and more like Jesus thinks and what He commands. The mind of the flesh is the mind of the previous person. The person born-again of the spirit needs to learn who their new family is in Christ, who their new brothers and sisters are in Christ, but we must reject the idea that we have 2 fathers. The person born of God has has only one father now and he is not on the earth but is in heaven. The person born of God doesn't identify with the flesh (which is like a tent), but rather with the new spirit that they have.
    In heaven, one's previous father, if there, would be "brother" or "friend".
    
    - If someone tells you, "I saw your dad on the train." You might respond, "You must be mistaken because my dad Jehovah is in heaven."
    - If someone tells you, "I saw your dad." You might respond from *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A17-18&version=ESV][John 1:17-18]]*, "No one has ever seen God; the only God, who is at the Father's side, he has made him known."
    - If someone asks you, "How is your dad?" You might respond, "God is always good. He is good all the time. I think He's still drawing people to Jesus Christ His Only-Begotten Son."
    - If you tell someone, "I have only one dad and He is Jehovah in heaven." And they respond, "You have two dads." And you say nothing in response, (though you could have mentioned "I have only one dad who is God in heaven") then you have not sinned by not saying anything. You are blameless in this situation. Someone may say something untrue about you, but it's not your fault that they said it. You have already mentioned that your dad is God in heaven. Someone might try to force you to oconfess that you have a dad on the earth. Resist.
    
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A17-18&version=ESV][John 1:17-18]]* - For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth [[https://biblehub.com/greek/225.htm][(*G225 alḗtheia*)]] came through Jesus Christ. No one has ever seen God; the only God, who is at the Father's side, he has made him known. (ESV)

      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2018%3A16-22&version=ESV][Luke 18:16-22]]* - But Jesus called them to him, saying, Let the children come to me, and do not hinder them, for to such belongs the kingdom of God. Truly, I say to you, whoever does not *receive the kingdom of God like a child* shall not enter it. And a ruler asked him, Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life? And Jesus said to him, Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone. You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery, Do not murder, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Honor your father and mother. And he said, All these I have kept from my youth.         When God created the world and put stars in the sky, the light could already be seen from the stars.
        I would consider the rays of light from the star and the star itself to be indivisibly referred to as the "star"
        and the rays of light from the sun and the Sun itself I would consider to be "the Sun". In a way the stars can touch us with their light.

    The natural man does not understand the things of the spirit. So out of love for Jesus who has commanded us to stop calling any man on earth "father", we do indeed stop calling one's previous father "father" and at the same time begin calling God our father, and in doing this it seems to spark offence from anyone who is thinking/walking/talking by the flesh (the natural man) who hears us call God our father while insisting that we no longer have a father on earth.
    
    But if a person who is not doing Christ's commandment to put a stop to calling any man on earth their "father",
    then *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2012%3A44-50&version=ESV][John 12:44-50]]* applies.
    Jesus left words that we must come into agreement with.
    Jesus came not to judge the world, but to save the world.
    Therefore, in imitating Christ's pattern for sharing the gospel, we should teach people to observe and do His commandments, including this one (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A9&version=ESV][Matthew 23:9]]*) to put a stop to calling any man on earth "father",
    and mention that on the last day, that if Jesus Christ and His words are rejected then the word that He has spoken will judge them on the last day (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2012%3A44-50&version=ESV][John 12:44-50]]*).
    I believe that we are instructed keep Jesus' commandments in reality for God to see (rather than seeking commendation from one-another), and examine ourselves to see if we are in the faith, doing Christ's commandments, and to teach other people to do the same, but when they do not still do not condemn them, but to exercise love that bears with people in hope that they will repent. We should be speaking the truth to one-another, and practicing in reality for God to see, and teach other people to do the same, but it's not our duty to police other people's faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A4-6&version=ESV][Romans 14:4-6]]*). It's God who we want other people to be seeking glory from in their own walk of faith in God who can see their hearts.
    
    It's loving God to call Him Father and to stop calling any man on earth "father".
    Jesus says whoever keeps His commandments is the one who loves Him and He also said that whoever hates Him also hates His Father.
    So in reality, because Jesus has commanded it, it's loving to call no man on earth "father" (to literally put a stop to using the title for any man on earth), and this includes "dad", "pa", "pop" or "abba", etc. and the spiritual man (the person who agrees with Jesus Christ) will understand this but the natural/carnal man will not like it at all.
    It's loving to stop calling any man on earth "father" or "dad", etc. if affirming that now God who is in heaven is your only father, out of faith in Jesus Christ the Son of God.
    
    And when a person is of the true circumcision, circumcised in their heart then in keeping Jesus' commandment to stop calling any man on earth their father, in doing so they are not dishonouring their mother and father as their mother and father is now God in heaven and Heavenly Jerulasem:

      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%203%3A3-11&version=ESV][Philippians 3:3-11]]* - For we are the real circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God and glory in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh— though I myself have reason for confidence in the flesh also. If anyone else thinks he has reason for confidence in the flesh, I have more: circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; as to the law, a Pharisee; as to zeal, a persecutor of the church; as to righteousness, under the law blameless. (ESV)

+ Journal <2026-06-23 Tue 16:35> :: I want the testimony of Jesus Christ from Holy Spirit.

    Earlier in the day today someone said to me that I live with my father and mother.
    And at a different time of day, I said to someone else, I want to get out of where I am currently living,
    and they asked, "Well, who are you living with?" And to avoid another one of these bizarre scenarios where people are getting confused and angry when I say God is my Dad, I just said, I don't want to talk about it. If I recall correctly, I'd had the same conversation with them before.
    But various people, even people who have in the past professed with their mouth that they have faith in Jesus, have gotten very confused and angry at me as I have affirmed God as my father and no other.
    
    I'm so sick and tired of this stuff. I want to be set free from this prison of circumstance.
    
    Soon after, I bumped into somebody else on the street, someone who in the past I had met through "church attendance".
    He was with a lady, and upon seeing me he mentioned to her that I am the son of the person who I would only now say "previously" I referred to as my father, as in before I got born-again and began calling God the Father of Jesus Christ my Father.
    I had to say, "That man is not my dad. I've been adopted."
    And this person, a "church goer" initially looked very confused, and I waited and he said, "By who? God?" And I said, "Yes, God is my Dad."
    I said, it would be more appropriate to call my previous father, "bro", than Dad.
    
    However, then walking back to earthly building in which I have been sleeping, the earthly dwelling place of the people who I would say were "previously" my parents,
    I was thinking, 'I actually do not want to refer to even my previous parents as "brother" and "sister" in Christ if they have not given me a confession of their faith.'
    
    As I was walking, the person who I no longer refer to as my father was just there on the other side of the road.
    And so I talked to him about what has been going on. I even mentioned that I feel like nobody wants to confess Jesus to me, and people keep on trying to affirm me as "brother" or want to be "bro" without wanting to confess to me their faith in Jesus.
    But in response he said he'd pray for me. What he should have done is confessed Jesus to me.
    
    I think my family basically consists of God the Father, God the Son, God the Holy Spirit, Jesus Christ's Apostles, and Jesus Christ's family and me.
    
    I feel burdened with just a tonne of resistance from people, resistance to Jesus Christ's teaching.
    The sheer amount of testing which I have been under.
    Honestly, I'm so sick of it.
    
    May God deliver me from this blanket of darkness, this resistance to the knowledge of God, that has been trying to bury me.
    
    If those two people who I previously referred to as mum and dad are truly brother and sister in Christ, then may God allow them to confess their faith to me afresh.
    Otherwise, I do not want to affirm them as brother and sister.
    
    Jesus said, "By this will all men know that you are my disciples, by the love you have for one another."
    
    Truly, in a very real sense, I would not say they have "loved me perfectly", even after I was born-again.
    
    I've been forsaken by them soon after I was born-again (albeit when I was repenting from unsound theology).
    When I came to actually start keeping the commandments of Christ, I began having *so* much discouragement from the many people around me including these people I remember as the parents of my former self.
    I've been slandered by them at times to my pain.
    After I was born-again, I have seen acting through them at times "bad spirits".
    
    And now, people speak of them to me as my parents with a very intense frequency.
    But on top of this I have also been asked often by people if they are "Christians".
    
    Why do people ask *me" if other people are Christians.
    No, the correct way to find out if somebody is a Christian is to ask them personally what they believe, and to check Scripture to see if what they believe about Jesus Christ is sound.
    Do they believe that He is the Son of God? Do they believe that Jesus is the Christ? Do they believe that Jesus Christ died on a tree and rose from the dead?
    Do they believe that Jesus Christ is the Word of God.
    
    Sadly, I did not get any such testimony from the people I interacted with today.
    
    But I do pray for them, that they might profess their faith to me.
    I've heard it from their mouth in the past.
    But I've also subsequently been received a massive amount of resistance from them.
    
    I wouldn't say the person who was previously my father is even a "spiritual father" to me. We were not even going to the same Sunday fellowship together when I was born-again.
    
    It doesn't seem right to immediately just affirm them as "brother and sister in Christ" without hearing from them afresh a confession of faith that I agree with.
    
    After getting born-again, I wasn't discipled by anyone other than Jesus Christ Himself in regard to keeping His commandments.
    Jesus Christ has been my only "Master", my only Teacher who would properly teach me. I've had to go to Scripture to learn about what He has taught.
    Most other people including and almost especially those who profess to be Christian have actually actively tried to discourage me from keeping Jesus Christ's commandments.
    
    I don't think it's right for me to remain in this earthly household of the people who I used to call my parents.
    I want deliverance from circumstances such as:
    - everyone I formerly knew from before I was born-again having ghosted me and not having time for me, and
    - having zero references, etc. and not being able to relocate as a consequence or find a job, and
    - from being denied many God-given rights such as getting married etc, and
    - from an AI obsessed world.
    - I want deliverance from what I can only describe as a spiritual prison that I find myself in.
    - But most of all, I want deliverance from whatever has been obstructing me from hearing the testimony of Jesus Christ from Holy Spirit.
    
    I want the Lord Jesus Christ to just speak plainly to me to instruct me, and to deliver me from the extreme demonic harassment and daily testing.
    I am so sick of it.
    
    I believe I need intervention from God in order to get me out of this spiritual prison that I have found myself in.
    I have had to endure immense spiritual oppression for a very long time now. I would like my Father (who is the Father of Jesus Christ) to deliver me now.
    I have prayed to God for a stupidly long amount of time for Him to deliver me, and have been terrorised by demonic activity day after day, night after night,
    all without the direct spoken instruction and testimony I expect to receive from God as I am putting Jesus Christ's teachings and commandments into practice.
    
    In Jesus Christ's name I rebuke this filty demonic oppression, and the demons which have been working through various people who I have been interacting with, demons that are against sanctification. I rebuke them in Jesus Christ's name.
    
    I want the liberty that Jesus Christ promised, the liberty that he promised that involves walking by the Spirit, according to His commandments.
    Jesus Christ, help me Son of God. Set me free. Amen.

I hope I have these ideas about law and grace correct. God have mercy:

+ Journal <2026-02-16 Mon> :: So I've just been thinking about grace, law, and faith and dying to the law and belonging to Christ Jesus. I'm enduring as I write this some kind of defilement of spirit or flesh. My life is very difficult as a consequence.
    When will I be set free from this "body of death"? In a sense, I am free from it. The sinful flesh is condemned, but my identity is in Christ. I have a new heart and spirit inside me that God gave me, and when my flesh passes away entirely I'll get a new body.
    For the time being, I have to walk by the spirit while lugging around the sinful flesh.

    So a person is killed (at the very least their body is killed) by sin ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A10&version=ESV][Romans 8:10]]), because the sin was strengthened by the law (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A56&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:56]]*) and the wages (due payment) for sin is death (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 6:23]]*).

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2011%3A25-27&version=ESV][John 11:25-27]]* - Jesus said to her, I am the resurrection and the life. *Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live, and everyone who lives and believes in me shall never [[strongs:G3756][(G3756 οὐ)]] [[strongs:G3361][(G3361 μή)]] die*. Do you believe this? She said to him, Yes, Lord; I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who is coming into the world. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    Without the law, sin lies dead (dormant, [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%205%3A12-13&version=ESV][Romans 5:12-13]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A8&version=ESV][Romans 7:8]]). When a person's body is killed beacuse of their sin, they may receive a new spirit, that is the spirit of Christ, if they have faith in Jesus Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2011%3A25-27&version=ESV][John 11:25-27]]*).
    A person who has been baptised into Christ's death must have had genuine faith in Christ, and thus genuine love for Christ as they received forgiveness for their sin.
    And so, with love in the heart, even love that has come through having been forgiven, they have the means now, the grace to love God and their neighbour and their family in Christ.
    And they also have a duty to love in that way. Because the law is laid down for the lawless and the disobedient, not for the "obedient" (those who love the truth, who obey Jesus).

    OK, so law-abidingness I think also certainly entails a recognition that we need to have faith in Jesus Christ who was delivered up for our sins, who's cross we need (and have needed) our sins to be nailed to.
    Real law-abidingness needs to be in agreement with Jesus Christ and His death and resurrection and Lordship (because we've been bought to belong to Christ).
    Real law-abidingnness isn't the overthrowing of the Law, but sees the law in view that we haven't been able to keep it faultlessly to be justified, and accepts that we rely on Jesus Christ's atoning work.

    Real law-abidingness accepts Jesus Christ and loves Him.

    We do not need to adhere to all of what is in the Book of the Law beacuse the Law is for the lawless and the disobedient, and is not laid down for those who keep the requirement of the law, that is to love the way God has commanded us to love (loving our neighbour as ourself), which we are only able to do in /reality/ (the way God wants us to truly love one another) if we abide in Jesus and have His Spirit in us.

    Basically, a person doesn't get "hit by the book" if they have the spirit of Jesus Christ in them and are fulfilling the law of Christ.
    We are disciplined to be obedient to Jesus Christ, most importantly the commandments to have faith in Him and love one another as commanded.
