+ Stopping sinning analogy :: When I woke up from sleep, I stopped sleeping. It doesn't mean I might not attempt to go back to sleep and pretend it's not day time, or perhaps "doze off" during the day, or have a lapse of awareness. But I had definitively woken up. Similarly, a person who has been born-again needs to stop sinning.

+ Another stopping sinning analogy :: If a person had a car that they did lots of doughnuts with, skids and jumps and the car was quite damaged through wear and tear, then "having sin" would be the damage to the car, but "committing sin" would be when someone does skids with the car and damages the car. If a person confesses (agrees) with the AAA that the tires are damaged, then they can be replaced, but if they don't agree with the AAA that there is anything wrong with the tires they can't be. If a person has sin then they can confess/come into agreement with God about that sin and be healed from it. But if they don't think it's sin then I guess they won't be. If a person is a compulsive liar, for example, then they need to agree with God that lying is not good. If a person thinks that lying and stealing and committing adulterly etc. are not evil then they are enslaved to that sin. They need to confess their sin.

When a person gets born-again, they stop sinning because God heals the heart and soul. But the Apostle Paul talks about "having indwelling sin" and the Apostle John about "having sin". So just because a person has stopped making more sin, we still "have it". After all, no-one can suprass the holiness of God. Even the heavens are not pure in God's sight. So a person may still have damage from sin and this is what is meant by "having sin" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A6-10&version=ESV][I John 1:6-10]]*). The person receives a new heart and spirit, but "indwelling sin in the flesh" remains an issue.  If a person commits sin after getting born-again then that is not wise or good because committing sin enslaves a person to sin, but we still have Jesus Christ as our advocate with Father God, and He can help us put the sin to death. But we really do need to stop committing sin. The more knowledge of the truth a person has the more important it is to have stopped committing sin. Someone who commits sin doesn't remain in the house forever. It doesn't mean they're immediately cast out. But a person must put sin to death by sanctification in order to remain in God's house forever. God's will for us is our sanctification. The one who does the will of God abides forever.

For the unsaved, all sin leads to death:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A12&version=ESV][Romans 2:12]]* - For all who have sinned without the law will also perish without the law, and all who have sinned under the law will be judged by the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

For the person who has faith in Jesus Christ, there is sin which when committed does not lead to death. However I wonder what John means by "death" here, and I think he probably means only the death of the flesh, but not the death of the spirit (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%205%3A1-13&version=ESV][I Corinthians 5:1-13]]*). I believe that the Apostle Paul was acting in love when pronouncing judgement for the sake of the person who he judged (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%205%3A1-13&version=ESV][I Corinthians 5:1-13]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A16-17&version=ESV][I John 5:16-17]]* - If anyone sees his brother committing a sin not leading to death, he shall ask, and God will give him life—to those who commit sins that do not lead to death. There is sin that leads to death; I do not say that one should pray for that. All wrongdoing is sin, but there is sin that does not lead to death. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's not possible for someone "in Christ" to hate their family in Christ. The person who hates their brother abides in death:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
   *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A13-16&version=ESV][I John 3:13-16]]* - Do not be surprised, brothers, that the world hates you. _We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers._ Whoever does not love abides in death. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him. By this we know love, that he laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The light (love for the truth) must be in us:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2011%3A10&version=ESV][John 11:10]]* - But if anyone walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A believer has "woken up". Someone walking in the light is walking in the love of the truth. And we should "stay awake" acting in the love of the truth, walking by the spirit, by faith obeying the God, by faith obeying Christ, walking in the love of the truth because we'd like to be "awake" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2024%3A40-42&version=ESV][Matthew 24:40-42]]*) when our Lord comes:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2024%3A40-42&version=ESV][Matthew 24:40-42]]* - Then two men will be in the field; one will be taken and one left. Two women will be grinding at the mill; one will be taken and one left. Therefore, stay awake, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We need to go on in the love of the truth:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A9&version=ESV][1 John 1:9]]* - If we confess [[https://biblehub.com/greek/3670.htm][(G3670 homologeó)]] our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A7&version=ESV][I John 1:7]]* - But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

When a person gets born-again of the spirit, they do need to not then double-down on the passions of the flesh. They do need to not "walk by the corpse/flesh" letting the corpse dictate one's actions, but rather "walk by the spirit" doing the will of God. New spirit in old flesh needs to not be carnal and walk by the flesh, but should rather try to use the old flesh to practice righteousness from an inward desire to do the will of God. The flesh does seem to resist the will of the spirit though (consider, for example, if one's body was craving nicotine or something, but the born-again person knows in their heart that they should not squander their resources). It's right for a person who has been born-again of the spirit to strive to then walk by the spirit, as in not just be driven by the cravings of the flesh, but to actually by faith practice righteousness, resisting carnality, the way that we have been instructed to do, using ones' body for practicing righteousnessness, putting to death the "passions of the flesh". Being born-again of the spirit, a person has "woken up" and is in the light where all things are visible and the right thing to do is to put off the old self and to walk like Christ, as He has instructed:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A24&version=ESV][Galatians 5:24]]* - And those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I believe that additionally to the need of "receiving a heart transplant" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2018%3A31&version=ESV][Ezekiel 18:31]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2036%3A25-28&version=ESV][Ezekiel 36:25-28]]*), we should "divorce ourselves" from our "sinning members". And what I mean by that is, for example, if a person were, for example, practicing something sinful with their hands, such as stealing, then instead of making time to practice that, use one's hands for doing good works instead. And this is metaphorically, "cutting off the 'sinful flesh'".

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%209%3A45&version=ESV][Mark 9:45]]* - And if your foot causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than with two feet to be thrown into hell. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Not only does this point to the fact that we need a new heart. But if you are using your members for doing evil, then instead of doing evil with them, do good with them, effectively "cutting off the sinful flesh" from the heart (i.e. nipping it at the bud happens with a change of heart):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A29-30&version=ESV][Matthew 5:29-30]]* - If your right eye causes you to sin, tear it out and throw it away. For it is better that you lose one of your members than that your whole body be thrown into hell ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/1067.htm][1067. geenna]]). And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. For it is better that you lose one of your members than that your whole body go into hell. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A19-20&version=ESV][Romans 6:19-20]]* - I am speaking in human terms, because of your natural limitations. For just as you once presented your members as slaves to impurity and to lawlessness leading to more lawlessness, so now present your members as slaves to righteousness leading to sanctification. When you were slaves of sin, you were free in regard to righteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%204%3A28&version=ESV][Ephesians 4:28]]* - Let the thief no longer steal, but rather let him labor, doing honest work with his own hands, so that he may have something to share with anyone in need. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%202%3A11-14&version=ESV][Colossians 2:11-14]]* - In him also you were circumcised with a circumcision made without hands, by putting off the body of the flesh, by the circumcision of Christ, having been buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him through faith in the powerful working of God, who raised him from the dead. And you, who were dead in your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, God made alive together with him, having forgiven us all our trespasses, by canceling the record of debt that stood against us with its legal demands. This he set aside, nailing it to the cross. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Sinning is when a person commits hatred of the light, i.e. actively hates the truth, loves evil. On the other hand, the breastplate of faith and love (the breastplate of righteousness) love the truth and hopes in Jesus Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A34&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:34]]* - Wake up from your drunken stupor, as is right, and do not go on sinning. For some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%205%3A8&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 5:8]]* - But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, having put on the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet the hope of salvation. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's important to stop sinning and to go on in a love for the truth rather than in a love of evil.
Light, as I've mentioned is effectively, the love of the truth in the heart.
Walking in the light, we are being washed by the blood of Jesus Christ. So we should be agreeing with the person of Jesus Christ and agreeing with the words of God.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
   *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A6-7&version=ESV][I John 1:6-7]]* - If we say we have fellowship with him while we walk in darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth. But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A34&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:34]]* - Wake up from your drunken stupor, as is right, and do not go on sinning. For some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%204%3A1-2&version=ESV][I Peter 4:1-2]]* - Since therefore Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves with the same way of thinking, for whoever has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin, so as to live for the rest of the time in the flesh no longer for human passions but for the will of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus didn't sin at all and He suffered in the flesh. Disciples of Jesus suffer in the flesh too as the have "ceased from committing sin".

Because whoever abstains from sin subsequently suffers in the flesh (e.g. the Adamic flesh rebels against the will to do the will of God, and the world hates the person because they're a disciple of Jesus), then whoever suffers in the flesh has "ceased from sin". That's how to read this. As in, someone who now holds their faith in Jesus Christ abstains from sin (because they now obey Christ, from the love of God rather than the love of evil; they now obey Christ instead of sin), as consequence that person suffers in the flesh. And someone who has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%204%3A1-3&version=ESV][I Peter 4:1-3]]* - Since therefore Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves with the same way of thinking, for whoever has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin, so as to live for the rest of the time in the flesh no longer for human passions but for the will of God. The time that is past suffices for doing what the Gentiles want to do, living in sensuality, passions, drunkenness, orgies, drinking parties, and lawless idolatry. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

In Jesus' flesh, the enmity between Jew and Gentile is 'abolished' (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%202%3A14-16&version=ESV][Ephesians 2:14-16]]*). That is, "the law of commandments and decrees" no longer divides Jew from Gentile so long as they hold faith in Jesus Christ.
Jesus didn't come to abolish the law, but to fulfill it. So we must be found in Him. And in Him, Jews and Gentiles may be united by their faith in Jesus rather than united by each themselves keeping all of the Old Covenant Law.
The person who abides in Jesus, abides in His commandments, and His commandments are to have faith in Him and to love one another as He did.
So in Jesus Christ, keeping Jesus' commandments in reality, we don't need to adhere to the "Book of the Law".

OK, so if a person has been "born-again" (i.e. resurrected spiritually), then they have _"died to the law" so that they may belong to another_, that is, belong to Jesus Christ.

It's very important to go on serving Christ Jesus because we want to reap eternal life and not corruption.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%206%3A8&version=ESV][Galatians 6:8]]* - For the one who sows to his own flesh will from the flesh reap corruption, but the one who sows to the Spirit will from the Spirit reap eternal life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Thus a married woman is bound by law to her husband while he lives, but if her husband dies she is released from the law of marriage. Accordingly, she will be called an adulteress if she lives with another man while her husband is alive. But if her husband dies, she is free from that law, and if she marries another man she is not an adulteress. But now we are released from the law, having died to that which held us captive, *so that we serve not under the old written code but in the new life of the Spirit.* (ESV)

While in the flesh, the "passions of sins" empowered by the law were producing fruit leading to death:

So what the law does is empower sin's passions (if a person is walking by the flesh, that is):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A56&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:56]]* - The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law. (ESV)

For the desires of the flesh are against the Spirit, and the desires of the Spirit are against the flesh, for these are opposed to each other, to keep you from doing the things you want to do. But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law. Now the works of the flesh are evident: sexual immorality, impurity, sensuality, idolatry, sorcery, enmity, strife, jealousy, fits of anger, rivalries, dissensions, divisions, envy, drunkenness, orgies, and things like these. I warn you, as I warned you before, that those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God. But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control; against such things there is no law. And those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires. If we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit. (ESV)

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%206%3A63&version=ESV][John 6:63]]* - It is the Spirit who gives life; the flesh is of no avail. The words that I have spoken to you are spirit and life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

If we are born-again (living by the Spirit) then it's important to also walk by the Spirit, trusting and doing Jesus' words.

So a person is "purchased", "bought", "redeemed", baptised into Christ's death, in order to belong to Jesus (purchased to serve Jesus) in order that they may love God and their family in Christ in *reality* (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%204%3A23-24&version=ESV][John 4:23-24]]*), abiding in Jesus' commandments from a position of having received forgiveness for sin through faith in Jesus.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A1-4&version=ESV][Romans 8:1-4]]* - There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life has set you free in Christ Jesus from the law of sin and death. For God has done what the law, weakened by the flesh, could not do. By sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, he condemned sin in the flesh, *in order that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us*, who walk not according to the flesh but according to the Spirit. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It does seem like, those "under the old code" have a hard time keeping up with gentiles who keep the precepts of the law. But that all created human beings have violated the law, so from the outside it just appears like fallible people accusing each other of various things but they're all guilty of something.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A26-27&version=ESV][Romans 2:26-27]]* - So, if a man who is uncircumcised keeps the precepts of the law, will not his uncircumcision be regarded as circumcision? Then he who is physically uncircumcised but keeps the law will condemn you who have the written code and circumcision but break the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But it also seems like knowledge of "the law" to those who endeavour to be justified by it will end up pointing out their failings to keep the law. But through faith in Jesus, a person can be "set free from the condemnation" that comes from having sinned, and be set free from sin, their body being killed by sin for violating the law but being given a new spirit that is alive which does submit to God's law.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2011%3A25-27&version=ESV][John 11:25-27]]* - Jesus said to her, I am the resurrection and the life. *Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live, and everyone who lives and believes in me shall never [[strongs:G3756][(G3756 οὐ)]] [[strongs:G3361][(G3361 μή)]] die*. Do you believe this? She said to him, Yes, Lord; I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who is coming into the world. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

At some point a person is going to have to have their body killed "by sin for trangressing the law" for the wages of sin is death. In order to return to the truth they must accept this fact that their sin has been condemned, but that by faith in Jesus Christ, that they can belong to Jesus and be in a position of righteous standing with God, and have a living spirit (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A9-12&version=ESV][Romans 8:9-12]]*). This faith does entail agreement with and love for Jesus Christ. So being in this position of trusting in Jesus, believing that He was delivered over for our transgressions, believing that He was raised for our justification, that we can agree with God that Jesus is God's Son and deserved to be raised from the dead, and with love for Jesus, Jesus is now our Master. And so we will keep His commandments, empowered by Jesus' spirit, even though the sinful flesh is condemned and will perish. Jesus' commandments are essentially to have faith in Him and love one another as He commanded. So our duty remains to keep God's commandments for us even after we are born-again and we're bought that we might have the requirement of the law fulfilled in us in reality, in light of the facts about Jesus.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A19-25&version=ESV][Romans 3:19-25]]* - Now we know that whatever the law says it speaks to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be stopped, and the whole world may be held accountable to God. For by works of the law no human being will be justified in his sight, since through the law comes knowledge of sin. But now the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, although the Law and the Prophets bear witness to it— the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe. For there is no distinction: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, and are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God put forward as a propitiation by his blood, to be received by faith. This was to show God's righteousness, because in his divine forbearance he had passed over *former sins*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So a person has to have "died" with Christ that they might belong to Christ. When a person is judged by the law (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A9-13&version=ESV][Romans 7:9-13]]*), their "body" is "dead/killed" because of sin in the body because they are unable to keep the requirement of the law (by themself), because the law is holy. The body is dead because of sin (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A9-12&version=ESV][Romans 8:9-12]]*) because God has condemned sin in the flesh ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A3&version=ESV][Romans 8:3]]). But for a person who holds their faith in Jesus Christ, the spirit is alive because of righteousness i.e. because of faith in Jesus in the heart of the person and they receive the Spirit of Jesus Christ through faith in Jesus. So although their sinful body of death is "killed by sin" because of sin's "power" from the law (i.e. the law condemns the sin), they are also baptized into Jesus' death if they had faith in Jesus and they're raised with Jesus as they continue holding their faith in Jesus. Imagine being "killed by sin" without faith in Jesus (that would be tragic). But if a person has faith in Jesus when the body is killed because of sin when they are judged by the law then they are also alive spiritually. So how does a person continue on after that? Being authentically forgiven, with an authentic love for Jesus with the spirit of Jesus in them, "belonging to Jesus", rather than "belonging to the law", they hold their faith in Jesus, trusting and obeying Jesus. And from the position of having been forgiven, having faith in Jesus and His death and resurrection, we endeavour then to fulfill the requirement of the law which is to love God and our neighbour with our whole heart. And though the spirit is willing, the flesh is weak. The definition of "fulfulling the requirement of the law" is not "abiding in all things written in the book of the law", but rather it is to love God and one another in reality from a position of having been justified through faith in Jesus. That is only truly possible for someone who has the Spirit of Christ in them. So we're given the means, the grace in order to fulfill the 2 Great Commandments.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A3-8&version=ESV][Romans 6:3-8]]* - Do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? We were buried therefore with him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life. For if we have been united with him in a death like his, we shall certainly be united with him in a resurrection like his. We know that our old self was crucified with him in order that the body of sin might be brought to nothing, so that we would no longer be enslaved to sin. For one who has died has been set free from sin. Now if we have died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

As they hold their faith in Jesus and love Him understanding that He was delivered over for their sins and raised for their justification, they are forgiven and their spirit is alive, but their body is dead:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A36&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:36]]* - You foolish person! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A9-13&version=ESV][Romans 7:9-13]]* - I was once alive apart from the law, but when the commandment came, sin came alive and I died. The very commandment that promised life proved to be death to me. For sin, seizing an opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me. So the law is holy, and the commandment is holy and righteous and good. Did that which is good, then, bring death to me? By no means! It was sin, producing death in me through what is good, in order that sin might be shown to be sin, and through the commandment might become sinful beyond measure. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A person becomes "forgiven" and then holds an ongoing "loving faith" in Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%202%3A19-21&version=ESV][Galatians 2:19-21]]* - For through the law I died to the law, so that I might live to God. I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me. I do not nullify the grace of God, for if justification were through the law, then Christ died for no purpose. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

And Jesus must come to live inside a person:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A9-12&version=ESV][Romans 8:9-12]]* - You, however, are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if in fact the Spirit of God dwells in you. Anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him. But if Christ is in you, although *the body is dead because of sin*, the Spirit is life because of righteousness. If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you. So then, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A1-17&version=ESV][Romans 7:1-17]]* - Or do you not know, brothers—for I am speaking to those who know the law—that the law is binding on a person only as long as he lives? Thus a married woman is bound by law to her husband while he lives, but if her husband dies she is released from the law of marriage. Accordingly, she will be called an adulteress if she lives with another man while her husband is alive. But if her husband dies, she is free from that law, and if she marries another man she is not an adulteress. Likewise, my brothers, you also have *died to the law through the body of Christ*, so that you may belong to another, to him who has been raised from the dead, in order that we may bear fruit for God. For while we were living in the flesh, our sinful passions, aroused by the law, were at work in our members to bear fruit for death. But now we are released from the law, having died to that which held us captive, so that we serve not under the old written code but in the new life of the Spirit. What then shall we say? That the law is sin? By no means! Yet if it had not been for the law, I would not have known sin. I would not have known what it is to covet if the law had not said, You shall not covet. But sin, seizing an opportunity through the commandment, produced in me all kinds of covetousness. Apart from the law, sin lies dead. I was once alive apart from the law, but when the commandment came, sin came alive and I died. The very commandment that promised life proved to be death to me. For sin, seizing an opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me. So the law is holy, and the commandment is holy and righteous and good. Did that which is good, then, bring death to me? By no means! It was sin, producing death in me through what is good, in order that sin might be shown to be sin, and through the commandment might become sinful beyond measure. For we know that the law is spiritual, but I am of the flesh, sold under sin. I do not understand my own actions. For I do not do what I want, but I do the very thing I hate. Now if I do what I do not want, I agree with the law, that it is good. So now it is no longer I who do it, but sin that dwells within me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%202%3A14-16&version=ESV][Ephesians 2:14-16]]* - For He Himself is our peace, who has made the two one and has torn down the dividing wall of hostility by abolishing in His flesh the law of commandments and decrees. He did this to create in Himself one new man out of the two, thus making peace and reconciling both of them to God in one body through the cross, by which He extinguished their hostility. (engbsb2020eb)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%202%3A14-16&version=ESV][Ephesians 2:14-16]]* - For He Himself is our peace, who made both groups into one and broke down the barrier of the dividing wall, by abolishing in His flesh the enmity, which is the Law of commandments contained in ordinances, so that in Himself He might make the two into one new man, thus establishing peace, and might reconcile them both in one body to God through the cross, by it having put to death the enmity. (NASB)
#+END_QUOTE

A "law-abiding faith" is a faith that agrees with the law in the heart, and wants to do what pleases God and do what is right in God's eyes. But sometimes even if we do want to / desire to do what is right, because of indwelling sin *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A16-20&version=ESV][Romans 7:16-20]]*), we sometimes don't, even though we do want to. God who is without sin always fulfills His promises. God carries out perfect deeds (Deuteronomy 32:4). And as Jesus Christ is the telos [[strongs:G5056][(G5056 telos)]] of the Law for righteousnes to everyone who is believing, a "law-abiding faith" *must* continue to agree with and come into agreement with Jesus Christ and His teachings. We must be correctable by Jesus ongoingly. Jesus is our Master, so we trust and obey Jesus. We recognise that we are distinct from the indwelling sin that rebels against the law of God (Romans 7:18-20), but that the indwelling sin is condemned, and God is going to deliver us from every evil deed and bring us safely into His heavenly kingdom. So God is going to sanctify us. We still set our minds on the "things of the Spirit", keeping Jesus' commandments, and the "law of the Spirit of life", as we abide in Jesus keeping Jesus' commandments, sets us free from the law of sin and death. Trusting and obeying Jesus, we are cleaned up. Trusting and obeying temptation to sin, that would dirty us (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2015%3A18-21&version=ESV][Matthew 15:18-21]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=3%20John%201%3A11&version=ESV][III John 1:11]]* - Beloved, do not imitate evil but imitate good. Whoever does good is from God; whoever does evil has not seen God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A16-20&version=ESV][Romans 7:16-20]]* - Now if I do what I do not want, I agree with the law, that it is good. So now it is no longer I who do it, but sin that dwells within me. For I know that nothing good dwells in me, that is, in my flesh. For I have the desire to do what is right, but not the ability to carry it out. For I do not do the good I want, but the evil I do not want is what I keep on doing. Now if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but sin that dwells within me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

And by this we know that he abides in us, by the Spirit whom he has given us. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

By sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, he condemned sin in the flesh, in order that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the flesh but according to the Spirit. For those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, but those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit. To set the mind on the flesh is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace. For the mind that is set on the flesh is hostile to God, for it does not submit to God's law; indeed, it cannot. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

The distinction is being under the law vs being Christ's-law-"abiding" through faith. The law isn't abolished, but established:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A23-24&version=ESV][Galatians 3:23-24]]* - Now before faith came, we were held captive under the law, imprisoned until the coming faith would be revealed. So then, the law was our guardian until Christ came, in order that we might be justified by faith. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A31&version=ESV][Romans 3:31]]* - Do we then overthrow the law by this faith? By no means! On the contrary, we uphold the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We don't rely on our works. How many times have we written an email or CV with good intent, but made a mistake? We must not be those who rely on our works:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A28&version=ESV][Romans 3:28]]* - For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from works of the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God's power is made perfect in our weaknesses. And so, God, I believe can actually use our shortcomings for His purposes:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2012%3A9&version=ESV][II Corinthians 12:9]]* - But he said to me, My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness. Therefore I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Real law-abidingness is having "willing" obedience to God's commandments for us (to Jesus Christ) and "actual" doing of them in reality, from the heart, out of a love for the truth (out of real faith in God), like Abraham:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A27-28&version=ESV][Romans 3:27-28]]* - Then what becomes of our boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? By a law of works? No, but by the law of faith. For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from works of the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%209%3A21&version=ESV][I Corinthians 9:21]]* - To those outside the law I became as one outside the law (not being outside the law of God but under [[strongs:G1772][(G1772 ennomos)]] the law of Christ) that I might win those outside the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A8&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:8]]* - By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to a place that he was to receive as an inheritance. And he went out, not knowing where he was going. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%2026%3A4-5&version=ESV][Genesis 26:4-5]]* - I will multiply your offspring as the stars of heaven and will give to your offspring all these lands. And in your offspring all the nations of the earth shall be blessed, because Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A13-18&version=ESV][Romans 4:13-18]]* - For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world did not come through the law but through the righteousness of faith. For if it is the adherents of the law who are to be the heirs, faith is null and the promise is void. For the law brings wrath, but where there is no law there is no transgression. *That is why it depends on faith, in order that the promise may rest on grace and be guaranteed to all his offspring—not only to the adherent of the law but also to the one who shares the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all*, as it is written, I have made you the father of many nations—in the presence of the God in whom he believed, who gives life to the dead and calls into existence the things that do not exist. In hope he believed against hope, that he should become the father of many nations, as he had been told, So shall your offspring be. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Know then that it is those of faith who are the sons of Abraham. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Amazing talk:

+ [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FYfdDOJ4PpQ][youtube.com:  Charlie Kirk : HOW BEING OBEDIENT TO GOD WILL CHANGE YOUR LIFE | TPUSA Faith {@ TPUSAFaith }]]

I'd just mention though, that without justifying myself, I want to clarify my position regarding some comments Charlie Kirk made towards the end. While we do fall short of the glory of God, we are justified by faith in Jesus Christ and a person who has true faith in Jesus has been made good even though they fall short of the glory of God. A person who has the love of Jesus Christ in them is justified by that fact that they love Jesus. A person *is* justified by being good but only in that the good that justifies them is the love for Jesus Christ that they have in their heart:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A21-25&version=ESV][Romans 3:21-25]]* - But now the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, although the Law and the Prophets bear witness to it— the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe. For there is no distinction: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, and are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God put forward as a propitiation by his blood, to be received by faith. This was to show God's righteousness, because in his divine forbearance he had passed over former sins. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

False obedience is where there is no love for God in the heart:

#+END_QUOTE

God can also compel the elements of nature to do His will:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%208%3A25&version=ESV][Luke 8:25]]* - He said to them, Where is your faith? And they were afraid, and they marveled, saying to one another, Who then is this, that he commands [[strongs:G2004][(G2004 epitassei; To command, to order, to charge)]] even winds and water, and they obey him? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We don't want to be those who resist God's will to the point where we are compelled to be summonned by God to receive judgement. Every knee will bow and every tongue confess that Jesus is Lord to the glory of God the Father (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%202%3A9-11&version=ESV][Philippians 2:9-11]]*). We don't want to be those who are compelled unwillingly to do that in feigned obedience ([[https://biblehub.com/hebrew/yechachashu_3584.htm][H3584 yə·ḵa·ḥă·šū-]]). Being "being summonned to the Principal's office to receive the eternal cain" (the wrath of God, lake of fire, second death), a person would go to the Principal but have no love for the Principal ([[https://biblehub.com/hebrew/yechachashu_3584.htm][H3584 yə·ḵa·ḥă·šū-]]), and they would receive the second death (lake of fire) which is what they want for hating God since they hate Jesus and love death. God gives us time to repent (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%201%3A9-10&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 1:9-10]]*) in advance of the final judgement to come to a love for the truth and acknowledge Jesus Christ's lordship. We don't want to ignore this (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A22-25&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:22-25]]*) warning.

With respect to this they are surprised when you do not join them in the same flood of debauchery, and they malign you; but they will give account to him who is ready to judge the living and the dead. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2010%3A9-14&version=ESV][I Corinthians 10:9-14]]* - We must not put Christ to the test, as some of them did and were destroyed by serpents, nor grumble, as some of them did and were destroyed by the Destroyer. Now these things happened to them as an example, but they were written down for our instruction, on whom the end of the ages has come. Therefore let anyone who thinks that he stands take heed lest he fall. No temptation has overtaken you that is not common to man. God is faithful, and he will not let you be tempted beyond your ability, but with the temptation he will also provide the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it. Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

If we sin then we confess the sin, we agree with God about it, and God is faithful and just to forgive us. So we come to faith and we go on abiding in the truth, and when we stuff up, then we repent and return to the truth, like in the story of the prodigal son (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2015%3A10&version=ESV][Luke 15:10]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A9&version=ESV][1 John 1:9]]* - If we confess [[https://biblehub.com/greek/3670.htm][(G3670 homologeó)]] our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2015%3A7&version=ESV][Luke 15:7]]* - Just so, I tell you, there will be more _joy in heaven over one sinner who repents_ than over ninety-nine righteous persons _who need no repentance._
#+END_QUOTE

What is not done in faith is sin and being justified depends on having faith in Jesus.

I do not think it's possible to, for example, murder in faith.
I do not think it's possible to lie to one-another in faith.
I do not think it's possible to commit rape in faith.
I do not think it's possible to commit sin in faith.

What is not done in faith is sin, and so when a person sins, they are not justified in that moment because they do not have faith in that moment.
The very nature of committing sin is that it's done without faith.

It's possible to have sin/defilement while having faith:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%207%3A1&version=ESV][II Corinthians 7:1]]* - Since we have these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of body and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A8&version=ESV][I John 1:8]]* - If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A17-23&version=ESV][Romans 7:17-23]]* - So now it is no longer I who do it, but sin that dwells within me. For I know that nothing good dwells in me, that is, in my flesh. For I have the desire to do what is right, but not the ability to carry it out. For I do not do the good I want, but the evil I do not want is what I keep on doing. Now if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but sin that dwells within me. So I find it to be a law that when I want to do right, evil lies close at hand. For I delight in the law of God, in my inner being, but I see in my members another law waging war against the law of my mind and making me captive to the law of sin that dwells in my members. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But it's not possible to simultaneously have faith while committing sin:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%203%3A2&version=ESV][II Thessalonians 3:2]]* - and that we may be delivered from wicked and evil men. For not all have faith. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]* - But whoever has doubts is condemned if he eats, because the eating is not from faith. For whatever does not proceed from faith is sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2016%3A9&version=ESV][John 16:9]]* - concerning sin, because they do not believe in me; (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A9&version=ESV][I John 3:9]]* - No one born of God makes a practice of sinning, for God's seed abides in him, and he cannot keep on sinning because he has been born of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Clearly, then, it's possible to have sinful lapses of faith, and if it's possible to have sinful lapses of faith, then it's possible, I think, to have lapses of justification (i.e. in the act of committing the sin, anyway).
Of course, God is the justifier, but we know that God justifies those who have faith in Jesus. So if God were to "not consider someone justified presentnly", even someone who He had previously deemed justified, then it's reasonable to think that the reason God may not presently be justifying the person would be because they are without faith.

Now, I believe that a person who humbles themself, though, like in this story in *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2018%3A9-14&version=ESV][Luke 18:9-14]]*, surely can be justified and I would say that in this story, this person who humbled himself appears to me to actually demonstrate faith in appealing to God for mercy. It's important to not trust in ourselves that we are righteous. The humble person seeks to please God. God is the justifier. We can reason about how He justifies. But God is the justifier. God is person we seek commendation from. But we are told in Scripture that it is faith that pleases Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2018%3A9-14&version=ESV][Luke 18:9-14]]* - He also told this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and treated others with contempt: Two men went up into the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector. The Pharisee, standing by himself, prayed thus: God, I thank you that I am not like other men, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even like this tax collector. I fast twice a week; I give tithes of all that I get. But the tax collector, standing far off, would not even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, God, be merciful to me, a sinner! I tell you, this man went down to his house justified, rather than the other. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I think it's not possible to be sanctified by committing sin, so that's why I say that there would be a lapse of justification:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2012%3A3&version=ESV][Proverbs 12:3]]* - No one is established by wickedness, but the root of the righteous will never be moved. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%202%3A19&version=ESV][II Timothy 2:19]]* - But God's firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: The Lord knows those who are his, and, Let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from iniquity. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%203%3A3-8&version=ESV][II Thessalonians 3:3-8]]* - But the Lord is faithful. He will establish you and guard you against the evil one. And *we have confidence in the Lord about you, that you are doing and will do the things that we command*. May the Lord direct your hearts to the love of God and to the steadfastness of Christ. Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you *keep away from any brother who is walking in idleness and not in accord with the tradition that you received from us*. For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, because we were not idle when we were with you, nor did we eat anyone's bread without paying for it, but with toil and labor we worked night and day, that we might not be a burden to any of you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2011%3A19&version=ESV][Proverbs 11:19]]* - Whoever is steadfast in righteousness will live, but he who pursues evil will die. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But that doesn't mean they are unable to confess their sin and ask Jesus for forgiveness, because I believe that they can.
We can confess our sin and walk in the light, the love of the truth, and the blood of Jesus cleanses us from all sin.

We can return to walking in faith. *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2018%3A20-24&version=ESV][Ezekiel 18:20-24]]* seems to also show that we must continue on in the love of the truth. Also the parable of the prodigal son seems to echo this. If a person sins, that doesn't meana they are booted out of the house immediately. But the slave to sin does not remain in the house forever, though (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A34-35&version=ESV][John 8:34-35]],36,42,51*). We can confess our sin and walk in the light and be cleaned from it. And we should put sin to death so we can remain in God's household forever.

A person who is holding their faith in Jesus Christ is abiding in Him.
A person who is presently sinning is someone who is not holding their faith.
A person who is not abiding in Jesus is cast out like a branch and withers.

If they remain not abiding in Jesus, stubbornly unrepentant, then eventually those branches not abiding are gathered and burned.
So we must continue on in faith in Jesus Christ and if we do commit sin then we must repent from them, and as we continue walking in the love of the truth, the blood of Jesus continues to wash us clean from sin.

Jesus wants us to continue to abide in Him. To continue on abiding in Him we must return to faith if we have departed from faith. If someone is a slave to sin after having committed to sin, they need to get out of being a slave to sin, and they can do so by returning to faith in Jesus Christ. When a person commits sin, they commit an act from a lapse of faith and what is not done in faith is sin. So they must turn away from their wickedness and back to the love of the truth (i.e. repent). If we walk in the light, the love of the truth, then the blood of Jesus cleanses us from all sin.

No murderer has eternal life in them: *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A6-18&version=ESV][I John 3:6-18]]*.
But whoever is holding faith in Jesus has eternal life and will do the works that He does, so then whoever is holding faith in Jesus is not a murderer.
If someone hates their brother then they are a murderer and so don't have faith.

We must continue in faith, and we do that by continuing in faith in Jesus Christ, and returning to faith if having wandered from the faith. We know that God justifies those who have faith in Jesus Christ. And without justification (faith and love for the truth), we cannot be sanctified. Even Moses, in a lapse of faith struck the rock instead of speaking to it. But we must return to the love of the truth if we wander from it:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2018%3A20-24&version=ESV][Ezekiel 18:20-24]]* - The soul who sins shall die. The son shall not suffer for the iniquity of the father, nor the father suffer for the iniquity of the son. The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon himself, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon himself. But if a wicked person turns away from all his sins that he has committed and keeps all my statutes and does what is just and right, he shall surely live; he shall not die. None of the transgressions that he has committed shall be remembered against him; for the righteousness that he has done he shall live. Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked, declares the Lord GOD, and not rather that he should turn from his way and live? But when a righteous person turns away from his righteousness and does injustice and does the same abominations that the wicked person does, shall he live? None of the righteous deeds that he has done shall be remembered; for the treachery of which he is guilty and the sin he has committed, for them he shall die. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A4-7&version=ESV][John 15:4-7]]* - Remain in Me, and I will remain in you. Just as no branch can bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in Me. I am the vine and you are the branches. The one who remains in Me, and I in him, will bear much fruit. For apart from [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] Me you can do nothing. If anyone does not remain in Me, he is like a branch that is thrown away and withers. Such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire, and burned. If you remain in Me and My words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you. (engbsb2020eb)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A31-47&version=ESV][John 8:31-47]]* - So Jesus said to the Jews who had believed ([[strongs:G4100][G4100 pepisteukotas: having believed]] [[https://biblehub.com/grammar/v-rpa-amp.htm]['V-RPA-AMP past tense']]) in him, If you abide in my word, you are truly my disciples, and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free. They answered him, We are offspring of Abraham and have never been enslaved to anyone. How is it that you say, You will become free? Jesus answered them, Truly, truly, I say to you, everyone who commits sin is a slave to sin. The slave does not remain in the house forever; the son remains forever. So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed. I know that you are offspring of Abraham; yet you seek to kill me because my word finds no place in you. I speak of what I have seen with my Father, and you do what you have heard from your father. They answered him, Abraham is our father. Jesus said to them, If you were Abraham's children, you would be doing what Abraham did, but now you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. This is not what Abraham did. You are doing what your father did. They said to him, We were not born of sexual immorality. We have one Father—even God. Jesus said to them, If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came from God and I am here. I came not of my own accord, but he sent me. Why do you not understand what I say? It is because you cannot bear to hear my word. You are of your father the devil, and your will is to do your father's desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, and has nothing to do with the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks out of his own character, for he is a liar and the father of lies. But because I tell the truth, you do not believe me. Which one of you convicts me of sin? If I tell the truth, why do you not believe me? Whoever is of God hears the words of God. The reason why you do not hear them is that you are not of God. (ESV)
