Theorising about faith and justification and sin:
- Someone who is committing sin does so without faith, which means they "believeth not" while they commit the sin and so in committing sin they are practicing lawlessness, not abiding to the law of faith in Christ Jesus, and are under judgement and condemnation while they "believeth not".

However, God is the one who commends faith. God is the justifier. God discerns the thoughts and intentions of the heart. Also God will have mercy on those He has mercy.
So just because I say this is how I think it generally works, as I want to help others to understand, I still trust that God is sovereign to commend faith, and sovereign to dispense His blessing, grace, chastisement and wrath.

Committing sin happens from the heart and defiles a person because it proceeds from the heart:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2015%3A18&version=ESV][Matthew 15:18]]* - But what comes out of the mouth proceeds from the heart, and this defiles a person. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Once defiled, the person gets enslaved into doing that sin until they repent and are cleaned from the sin through faith in Jesus.
So we should resist obeying sin and rather from a love of righteousness, from a love of Jesus, practice righteousness.

What is not done in faith is sin.
So while committing sin a person is not justified because they commit sin without faith.
If someone is distrusting of Jesus then they are condemned presently.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%205%3A19-20&version=ESV][James 5:19-20]]* - My brothers, if anyone among you wanders from the truth and someone brings him back, let him know that whoever brings back a sinner from his wandering will save his soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Abraham had not read the Book of Genesis when he "believed God and it was accounted to him as righteousness" ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%2015%3A6&version=ESV][Genesis 15:6]]), so Abraham didn't know he was commended but God had commended his faith.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A9-10&version=ESV][Romans 4:9-10]]* - Is this blessing then only for the circumcised, or also for the uncircumcised? We say that faith was counted to Abraham as righteousness. How then was it counted to him? Was it before or after he had been circumcised? It was not after, but before he was circumcised. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Now that we can read this Scripture that Abraham's faith was accounted as righteousness when He was trusting in God's promise, we can understand that God justifies a person for their faith.

It's clear that part of the contributing factor into God commending Abraham's faith is that "No distrust made him waver concerning the promise of God, but he grew strong in his faith"
so it is clear that not only is this about trust, but also about the perseverance of his faith (i.e. faith with patience, continuing faith). So God justifies faith as the faith is held, even from the start.

Abraham wasn't justified for "saying" that he believes, at least not "merely" by saying he believes, but rather by "actually" believing from the heart.
It is with the heart that one is justified.
Sure, it's with the mouth that one confesses unto salvation, but it's with the heart that one is justified. God looks at our hearts.
We're not justified merely by saying that we are justified.
The external action alone (without real faith in the heart) is not what justifies.
So we want to be please God with our faith which he sees us actually having.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A20-25&version=ESV][Romans 4:20-25]]* - No distrust made him waver concerning the promise of God, but he grew strong in his faith as he gave glory to God, fully convinced that God was able to do what he had promised. That is why his faith was counted to him as righteousness. But the words it was counted to him were not written for his sake alone, but for ours also. It will be counted to us who believe in him who raised from the dead Jesus our Lord, who was delivered up for our trespasses and raised for our justification. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We're supposed to have faith like Abraham's faith, but faith that is in the person of Jesus Christ and that includes in His words and deeds.

So we should be seeking God's commendation, not commending ourself, but entrusting ourselves to God while practicing righteousness by faith:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%204%3A19&version=ESV][I Peter 4:19]]* - Therefore let those who suffer according to God's will entrust their souls to a faithful Creator while doing good. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So when we turn up in heaven, God commends us, not the other way around:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2025%3A40&version=ESV][Matthew 25:40]]* - And the King will answer them, Truly, I say to you, as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2025%3A31-46&version=ESV][Matthew 25:31-46]]* - When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, then he will sit on his glorious throne. Before him will be gathered all the nations, and he will separate people one from another as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats. And he will place the sheep on his right, but the goats on the left. Then the King will say to those on his right, Come, you who are blessed by my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry and you gave me food, I was thirsty and you gave me drink, I was a stranger and you welcomed me, I was naked and you clothed me, I was sick and you visited me, I was in prison and you came to me. Then the righteous will answer him, saying, Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you drink? And when did we see you a stranger and welcome you, or naked and clothe you? And when did we see you sick or in prison and visit you? And the King will answer them, Truly, I say to you, as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me. Then he will say to those on his left, Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels. For I was hungry and you gave me no food, I was thirsty and you gave me no drink, I was a stranger and you did not welcome me, naked and you did not clothe me, sick and in prison and you did not visit me. Then they also will answer, saying, Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not minister to you? Then he will answer them, saying, Truly, I say to you, as you did not do it to one of the least of these, you did not do it to me. And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

If someone turns up to the judgement seat of Christ seeking to commend themself, saying, "This is when I had faith", or "This is when I fed you", etc. then that is self-justifying. I truly believe that our faith must *continue* to seek commendation from God.

Notice how the penitent criminal put His hope in Jesus in reality. Jesus would welcome him in (remembering him, remembering his faith in Jesus). Maybe Jesus points out to him in the coming of His Kingdom, "This is when you had faith, when you first began puting your faith in me, hoping in me." and Jesus would know his heart better than himself:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2023%3A40-43&version=ESV][Luke 23:40-43]]* - But the other answered, and rebuking him said, “Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same sentence of condemnation? And we indeed are suffering justly, for we are receiving what we deserve for our deeds; but this man has done nothing wrong.” And he was saying, “Jesus, remember me when You come in Your kingdom!” And He said to him, “Truly I say to you, today you shall be with Me in Paradise.”
#+END_QUOTE

From faith, a person practices rightousness:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A12&version=ESV][John 14:12]]* - Truly, truly, I say to you, whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do; and greater works than these will he do, because I am going to the Father. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Without faith, a person practices wickedness:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]* - But whoever has doubts is condemned if he eats, because the eating is not from faith. For whatever does not proceed from faith is sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Whoever does not have faith in Jesus will be condemned:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2016%3A16&version=ESV][Mark 16:16]]* - Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A36&version=ESV][John 3:36]]* - Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life; whoever does not obey the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God remains on him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Whoever has no love for Jesus Christ is also unsaved:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2016%3A22&version=ESV][I Corinthians 16:22]]* - If anyone has no love for the Lord, let him be accursed. Our Lord, come! (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Anyone who is antichrist is against Christ and is condemned:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A2-3&version=ESV][I John 4:2-3]]* - By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God, and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist, which you heard was coming and now is in the world already. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A14-19&version=ESV][John 3:14-19]]* - And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life. For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God. And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than [[strongs:G3123][(G3123 mallon, rather/more than, in preference to, instead of)]] light, because their deeds were evil. (KJV)
#+END_QUOTE

A person gets born-again (made alive) but must go on as a believer with the circumcision of the heart to love God with their heart, practicing righteousness abiding in Jesus' commandments which involves having love for God and for God's children:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2011%3A25-27&version=ESV][John 11:25-27]]* - Jesus said to her, I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live, and everyone who lives and believes in me shall never (G3756 οὐ) (G3361 μή) die. Do you believe this? She said to him, Yes, Lord; I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who is coming into the world. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A9-13&version=ESV][Romans 7:9-13]]* - I was once alive apart from the law, but when the commandment came, sin came alive and I died. The very commandment that promised life proved to be death to me. For sin, seizing an opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me. So the law is holy, and the commandment is holy and righteous and good. Did that which is good, then, bring death to me? By no means! It was sin, producing death in me through what is good, in order that sin might be shown to be sin, and through the commandment might become sinful beyond measure. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

For a born-again believer, practicing righteousness becomes the normal mode of operation. The person born of God has stopped sinning and has started practicing righteousness. If they resist God's ongoing discipline to put off ungodly behaviour then they put Christ to the test and God is an avenger in these matters. But if someone commits sin, even someone who believes they are/were born of God (found by God to be a sinner rather than someone born of God), then there is propitiation for that sin. We must be those who endeavour to be justified in Christ, rather than those who self-commmend.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%202%3A17&version=ESV][Galatians 2:17]]* - But if, in our endeavor to be justified in Christ, we too were found to be sinners, is Christ then a servant of sin? Certainly not! (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We need to confess our sins. We need to repent of them:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A7&version=ESV][I John 3:7]]* - Little children, let no one deceive you. Whoever practices righteousness is righteous, as he is righteous. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%203%3A8-10&version=ESV][Colossians 3:8-10]]* - But now you must put them all away: anger, wrath, malice, slander, and obscene talk from your mouth. Do not lie to one another, seeing that you have put off the old self with its practices and have put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge after the image of its creator. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A1-6&version=ESV][I John 2:1-6]]* - My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you may not sin. *But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous. He is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only but also for the sins of the whole world.* And by this we know that we have come to know him, if we keep his commandments. Whoever says I know him but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, but whoever keeps his word, in him truly the love of God is perfected. By this we may be sure that we are in him: whoever says he abides in him ought to walk in the same way in which he walked. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

When a person gets "born of God", they are now have an identity which is apart from [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] their flesh.
They are now really the person who is "born of God".
Now, to the person who has been "born of God", observing other people's behaviour, it may appear that sometimes other people are sometimes walking by the flesh, and sometimes walking by the spirit.

Walking "by the flesh" is a different concept to walking "in the flesh".
Walking "by the flesh" is a mind will thing where a person is obeys the old nature, i.e. not believing God's words nor believing in God. Walking a person can walk "by the spirit" "in the flesh", but a person cannot walk "by the spirit" and "by the flesh".

Jesus instructed His disciples to call no man on earth "father". This instruction, therefore, is for the Christian:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A1&version=ESV][Matthew 23:1]]* - Then Jesus said to the crowds and to his disciples, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A9&version=ESV][Matthew 23:9]]* - And call no man your father on earth, for you have one Father, who is in heaven. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Don't let people who are walking by the flesh be your guides on what you should believe. There's no need to judge/condemn if other people are not, for example, "calling no man on earth their father" because Jesus Christ came to save and we should be imitators of His patience. Rather, we should teach others to obey Christ, and teach them His commandments, and ourselves take every thought captive for obedience to Christ Jesus. We, ourselves, should try to obey Jesus Christ in His teaching, i.e. try to put Jesus' teaching into practice in reality:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%205%3A1-13&version=ESV][I Corinthians 5:1-13]]* - It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and of a kind that is not tolerated even among pagans, for a man has his father's wife. And you are arrogant! Ought you not rather to mourn? Let him who has done this be removed from among you. For though absent in body, I am present in spirit; and as if present, I have already pronounced judgment on the one who did such a thing. When you are assembled in the name of the Lord Jesus and my spirit is present, with the power of our Lord Jesus, you are to deliver this man to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord. Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump? Cleanse out the old leaven that you may be a new lump, *as you really are unleavened*. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed. Let us therefore celebrate the festival, not with the old leaven, the leaven of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. I wrote to you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people— not at all meaning the sexually immoral of this world, or the greedy and swindlers, or idolaters, since then you would need to go out of the world. But now I am writing to you not to associate with anyone who bears the name of brother if he is guilty of sexual immorality or greed, or is an idolater, reviler, drunkard, or swindler—not even to eat with such a one. For what have I to do with judging outsiders? Is it not those inside the church whom you are to judge? God judges those outside. Purge the evil person from among you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

To be overcomers, we must continue to hold our faith in who Jesus is, that is that He is the Messiah and the Son of God who has come into the world from God, who has come in His Father's name Yahweh (Jehovah), and who has died on a tree and rose from the dead 3 days later, and we should not only believe who He is and what He has done, but love Him and seek know more about Him from the Scripture and grow in our faith to maturity:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A4&version=ESV][I John 5:4]]* - For everyone who has been born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that has overcome the world—our faith. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A3-5&version=ESV][I John 5:3-5]]* - For this is the love of God, that *we keep his commandments. And his commandments are not burdensome. For everyone who has been born of God overcomes the world.* And this is the victory that has overcome the world—our faith. *Who is it that overcomes the world except the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We want to be overcome by practicing righteousness (faith and love for the truth).
We need to continue holding Jesus Christ as the top love of our heart so that desires for other things do not grow up and attack our faith.
With Jesus Christ Son of God as our top love, we should be able to put to death the deeds of the sinful flesh as we walk by the spirit trusting and obeying Jesus Christ.:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A8-13&version=ESV][Romans 8:8-13]]* - Those who are in the flesh cannot please God. You, however, are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if in fact the Spirit of God dwells in you. Anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him. But if Christ is in you, although the body is dead because of sin, the Spirit is life because of righteousness. If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you. So then, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh. For if you live according to the flesh you will die, but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2016%3A19-20&version=ESV][Romans 16:19-20]]* - For your obedience is known to all, so that I rejoice over you, but I want you to be wise as to what is good and innocent as to what is evil. The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The way we must follow is not the way that is to be enslaved by corruption. Rather, the way we follow is Jesus Christ, and we follow Jesus by loving the Truth as opposed to evil:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Peter%202%3A19&version=ESV][II Peter 2:19]]* - They promise them freedom, but they themselves are slaves of corruption. For whatever overcomes a person, to that he is enslaved. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

If a person has presently the law-abiding faith then they are trusting and obeying Jesus Christ and, therefore,
in the grand scheme of things, that person has been perfected (i.e. that person's sanctification will be completed):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2010%3A14&version=ESV][Hebrews 10:14]]* - For by a single offering he has perfected for all time those who are *being sanctified*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

If a person's faith is /not/ law-abiding then actions done out of that are not done in faith (real faith) (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]*) or not done in a
non-idolatrous (I Peter 4:3 says idolatry is unlawful, abominable) agape love for God and their neighbour (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2016%3A13-14&version=ESV][I Corinthians 16:13-14]]*) and that type of faith, not being love for the Truth, is not the faith of a son or daughter of God. A law-abiding faith agrees with the law of God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A16-25&version=ESV][Romans 7:16-25]]* - Now if I do what I do not want, I agree with the law, that it is good. So now it is no longer I who do it, but sin that dwells within me. For I know that nothing good dwells in me, that is, in my flesh. For I have the desire to do what is right, but not the ability to carry it out. For I do not do the good I want, but the evil I do not want is what I keep on doing. Now if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but sin that dwells within me. So I find it to be a law that when I want to do right, evil lies close at hand. For I delight in the law of God, in my inner being, but I see in my members another law waging war against the law of my mind and making me captive to the law of sin that dwells in my members. Wretched man that I am! Who will deliver me from this body of death? Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, I myself serve the law of God with my mind, but with my flesh I serve the law of sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Faith in Jesus Christ looks like having confidence in Him, in the Word of God, in God's promises, even the conditional promises:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A5&version=ESV][James 2:5]]* - Listen, my beloved brothers, has not God chosen those who are poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom, which he has promised to those who love him? (ESV)

Honor your father and mother (this is the first *commandment with a promise*), that it may go well with you and that you may live long in the land. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

For example, where Jesus says it's more blessed to give than to receive ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2020%3A35&version=ESV][Acts 20:35]]), the person with faith in Jesus Christ trusts that this is true. Worldly wisdom would say that trusting God's advice is folly. But faith in Jesus Christ invests in God rather than investing in perishable things:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%209%3A6&version=ESV][II Corinthians 9:6]]* - The point is this: whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows bountifully will also reap bountifully. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A24&version=ESV][I John 3:24]]* - Whoever keeps his commandments abides in him, and he in them. And by this we know that he abides in us, by the Spirit whom he has given us. (ESV)

and _a person who is obedient to Jesus has the love of God in their heart_ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A45&version=ESV][Luke 6:45]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15-17&version=ESV][John 14:15-17]]*) and it's the love of the Truth that saves (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%202%3A10&version=NASB][II Thessalonians 2:10]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%205%3A32&version=ESV][Acts 5:32]]* - And we are witnesses to these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him. (ESV)

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2081%3A15&version=ESV][Psalms 81:15]]* - Those who hate the LORD would feign obedience, and their doom would last forever. (engbsb2020eb)
#+END_QUOTE

Faith in Jesus Christ looks like trusting, believing, receiving, accepting, having confidence in Jesus Christ and what Jesus Christ has said. The one who is receptive to, the one who who receives Jesus Christ, the one who loves Jesus Christ, the one who continues to receive Jesus Christ, the one who does not push Jesus away but who accepts Jesus Christ and His words and His deeds, that is the person who has eternal life:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A24&version=ESV][John 5:24]]* - Truly, truly, I say to you, whoever hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life. He does not come into judgment, but has passed from death to life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

If a person believes what He said and has confidence what would come out of trusting Him above what would come out of, trusting in man's own strength, then they such a person would act on Jesus' commandments and with confidence in God and the outcome of obeying His instructions, they would walk in the light.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Jeremiah%2017%3A5&version=ESV][Jeremiah 17:5]]* - Thus says the LORD: Cursed is the man who trusts in man and makes flesh his strength, whose heart turns away from the LORD. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The faith we have is a faith that trusts Jesus Christ in Jesus saying that whoever is trusting in Him has eternal life. The faith is counted as righteousness apart from our works. Previous works don't factor into gaining God's forgiveness so long as the person is presently trusting in, holding their faith in, trusting Christ. Trusting Christ, not something else. So we must believe truly what Jesus Christ says. And if we truly believe the truth then we'll produce good:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A3-8&version=ESV][Romans 4:3-8]]* - For what does the Scripture say? Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness. Now to the one who works, his wages are not counted as a gift but as his due. And to the one who does not work but trusts him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted as righteousness, just as David also speaks of the blessing of the one to whom God counts righteousness apart from works: Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven, and whose sins are covered; blessed is the man against whom the Lord will not count his sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's possible to have faith without "working for payment" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A5&version=ESV][Romans 4:5]]*), even though God does reward "working for payment" (*Romans 4:4*): good work with blessing and evil work with wrath and fury (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A6-8&version=ESV][Romans 2:6-8]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%206%3A5-8&version=ESV][Ephesians 6:5-8]]*).
It's possible to have "faith that works" (producing good deeds) without "working for God's acceptance" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A19-25&version=ESV][Romans 4:19-25]]*).

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%2014%3A13&version=ESV][Revelation of John 14:13]]* - And I heard a voice from heaven saying, Write this: *Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on. Blessed indeed, says the Spirit, that they may rest from their labors, for their deeds *follow* them!* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's possible to be justified through humility before God, recognising one's own moral bankrupcy and asking God for mercy ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2018%3A13-14&version=ESV][Luke 18:13-14]]).

It's the faith (trust, love of the truth) in Jesus Christ that God is pleased with (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A6&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:6]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%208%3A17&version=ESV][Prov 8:17]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Jeremiah%2029%3A13-14&version=ESV][Jer 29:13-14]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%206%3A33&version=ESV][Matt 6:33]]*).

Faith (heart attitudes of trust, love, obedience, hope) must continue until the outcome. In other words, a good outcome comes from good intent. It is incorrect to separate the outcome from the faith/intent and say that a person can be justified if the outcome is good even if the intent was evil. In criminal law there is "mens rea" and "actus reus".
But a person can commit evil and break God's law from the heart (i.e. "mens rea"-alone). When it comes to God judging, "mens rea" is all that is needed to convict a person and God sees:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A28&version=ESV][Matthew 5:28]]* - But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has *already committed adultery with her in his heart*.
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2015%3A10-11&version=ESV][Matthew 15:10-11]]* - And he called the people to him and said to them, Hear and understand: it is not what goes into the mouth that defiles a person, but what comes out of the mouth; this defiles a person. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Outcome comes from faith. Outcome comes from deed (external action done from faith). Outcome doesn't come from "external deed minus the faith":

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A6-9&version=ESV][I Peter 1:6-9]]* - In this you rejoice, though now for a little while, if necessary, you have been grieved by various trials, so that the tested genuineness of your faith—more precious than gold that perishes though it is tested by fire—may be found to result in praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ. *Though you have not seen him, you love him. Though you do not now see him, you believe in him and rejoice with joy that is inexpressible and filled with glory, obtaining the outcome of your faith, the salvation of your souls.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://www.youtube.com/shorts/ortVt2B6qIA][youtube.com:  Faith = Justification + Works {@ ligonier }]] :: According to Sproul, Martin Luther believed something like =Faith ≟ Justification + Works=. And so it follows that:
    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      - =Justification ≟ Faith - Works=
        - i.e. justification by faith alone
      - =Works ≟ Faith - Justification=
    #+END_QUOTE

    I know that it's faith in Jesus Christ in our heart that is what justifies us (=Justification ∵ (because) Faith=):

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A10&version=ESV][Romans 10:10]]* - For with the heart one believes and is justified, and with the mouth one confesses and is saved. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    And it's apart from [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] the works of the law that we are justified. Faith is counted distinctly from any corresponding external actions:

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A28&version=ESV][Romans 3:28]]* - For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from works [[strongs:G2041][(G2041 ergōn; works)]] of the law [[strongs:G3551][(G3551 nomou; of the Law)]]. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    Deeds are external actions done either out of love for light or for darkness (i.e. either out of faith in the truth or out of faith in darkness):
    - =Deed = Faith + ExternalActions=

    The word [[strongs:G5565][chōris]] in a statement "A chōris B" doesn't mean that B does not exist. Rather, the statement means "A where B is not taken into account", or "A distinct from B". So [[strongs:G5565][chōris]] means "without taking into account" or "as distinct from":

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2014%3A21&version=ESV][Matthew 14:21]]* - And those who ate were about five thousand men, besides [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] women and children. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    The Hebrew word for Adam can mean either just Adam the man, or it can mean both Adam and Eve.
    It would be semantically correct to say "Adam apart from [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] Eve", or "Eve apart from Adam".

    Man and woman, husband and wife are a single unit called Adam:

    It would also be semantically correct to say, "deeds [[strongs:G2041][(G2041 ergōn; works)]] apart from [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] faith".
    Deeds apart from faith would be the external actions.

    For example, giving a cookie to someone is an external action.
    But was it done in faith or not? Was the cookie given out of faith in God's word?
    And was it done in love or not? Was the cookie given to someone hoping they would enjoy the cookie, or hoping they would choke on it?
    And was it done in obedience to God's word or not?
    Faith is the heart attitudes of trust and obedience from a love of the truth.

    It's semantically correct to say, "faith apart from [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] works" also. But I do believe that when God judges on "deeds/works" [[strongs:G2041][(G2041 ergōn; works)]], He looks at the faith:

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A19&version=ESV][John 3:19]]* - And this is the judgment: the light has come into the world, and people loved the darkness rather than the light because their deeds were evil. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    The formula that Sproul has given is meant to convey 2 things:
    - justification is by faith alone (apart from works)
    - a person who has the faith will also have works

    Sadly, I don't think the formula is able to do that accurately because it's "incorporating the external actions of deeds" into the very definition of what faith is.
    The way that the word [[strongs:G2041][(G2041 ergōn; works)]] is used in the NT, it would be more accurate to say that deeds incorporate faith, than to say faith incorporates deeds.

    We are justified by the faith in Jesus Christ apart from [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] works of the law. The use of the word [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] means that it's the faith rather than any existing works that justifies. So the faith could certainly have associated works, but it's the faith one is justified by rather than the external actions:

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A28&version=ESV][Romans 3:28]]* - For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from works [[strongs:G2041][(G2041 ergōn; works)]] of the law [[strongs:G3551][(G3551 nomou; of the Law)]]. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    The word [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] is used not to show that Jesus doesn't exist, but that separate from Him, we cannot bear fruit. Just as how, even if separate from Jesus, Jesus would still exist, so too even if faith is counted separate from the works, the works still [may] exist:

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A4-7&version=ESV][John 15:4-7]]* - Remain in Me, and I will remain in you. Just as no branch can bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in Me. I am the vine and you are the branches. The one who remains in Me, and I in him, will bear much fruit. For apart from [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] Me you can do nothing. If anyone does not remain in Me, he is like a branch that is thrown away and withers. Such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire, and burned. If you remain in Me and My words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you. (engbsb2020eb)
    #+END_QUOTE

    I think that a person can be justified by deeds, as Abraham was also justified by works of faith, but the basis for this justification is the faith (Abraham was seen to have the fear of God).

    When "the footsteps of faith" are mentioned in *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A9-12&version=ESV][Romans 4:9-12]]*, it does not specifically describe particular external actions to do.

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A9-12&version=ESV][Romans 4:9-12]]* - Is this blessing then only for the circumcised, or also for the uncircumcised? We say that faith was counted to Abraham as righteousness. How then was it counted to him? Was it before or after he had been circumcised? It was not after, but before he was circumcised. He received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. The purpose was to make him the father of all who believe without being circumcised, so that righteousness would be counted to them as well, and to make him the father of the circumcised who are not merely circumcised but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    For example, in order to follow in the footsteps of faith that Abraham had before he was circumcised,
    doesn't mean to replicate the external actions of Abraham, as if faith is just some kind of ritual of external actions.

    Following in the footsteps of faith does not literally mean
    to find a king of a city called Sodom and decline goods from him
    and do a pilgrimage from Abraham's geographic departure point to Canaan, the place that Abraham settled,
    and along the way take an "only-begotten son" with you and build an altar and attempt to sacrifice him on it.

    However, what following in Abraham's footsteps of faith should look like is by faith obeying Jesus Christ from the heart, receiving Jesus Christ and His words, with love for Him:

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A31-47&version=ESV][John 8:31-47]]* - So Jesus said to the Jews who had believed ([[strongs:G4100][G4100 pepisteukotas: having believed]] [[https://biblehub.com/grammar/v-rpa-amp.htm]['V-RPA-AMP past tense']]) in him, If you abide in my word, you are truly my disciples, and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free. They answered him, We are offspring of Abraham and have never been enslaved to anyone. How is it that you say, You will become free? Jesus answered them, Truly, truly, I say to you, everyone who commits sin is a slave to sin. The slave does not remain in the house forever; the son remains forever. So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed. I know that you are offspring of Abraham; yet you seek to kill me because my word finds no place in you. I speak of what I have seen with my Father, and you do what you have heard from your father. They answered him, Abraham is our father. Jesus said to them, If you were Abraham's children, you would be doing what Abraham did, but now you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. This is not what Abraham did. You are doing what your father did. They said to him, We were not born of sexual immorality. We have one Father—even God. Jesus said to them, If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came from God and I am here. I came not of my own accord, but he sent me. Why do you not understand what I say? It is because you cannot bear to hear my word. You are of your father the devil, and your will is to do your father's desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, and has nothing to do with the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks out of his own character, for he is a liar and the father of lies. But because I tell the truth, you do not believe me. Which one of you convicts me of sin? If I tell the truth, why do you not believe me? Whoever is of God hears the words of God. The reason why you do not hear them is that you are not of God. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    Having the faith of Abraham in Jesus Christ should certainly result in deeds done in faith that are Jesus' works. So we should be trusting and obeying Jesus Christ and His words with love for Him and in doing so be trusting and obeying Father God and His words with love for Father God:

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A12&version=ESV][John 14:12]]* - Truly, truly, I say to you, whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do; and greater works than these will he do, because I am going to the Father. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2012%3A41-46&version=ESV][John 12:41-46]]* - Isaiah said these things because he saw his glory and spoke of him. _Nevertheless, many even of the authorities believed in him, but for fear of the Pharisees they did not confess it, so that they would not be put out of the synagogue;_ for *they loved the glory that comes from man more than the glory that comes from God*. And Jesus cried out and said, Whoever believes in me, believes not in me but in him who sent me. And whoever sees me sees him who sent me. I have come into the world as light, so that whoever believes in me may not remain in darkness. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    The Bible makes it abundantly clear that faith in God's word involves trusting God's word with what He has revealed (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%201%3A18-19&version=ESV][Romans 1:18-19]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A14-15&version=ESV][I John 5:14-15]]*), and that might just be a promise without details on who you will encounter or what that will look like or what specific things will take place to make the result come about:

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A8&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:8]]* - By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to a place that he was to receive as an inheritance. And he went out, not knowing where he was going. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A1-3&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:1-3]]* - Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen. For by it the people of old received their commendation. By faith we understand that the universe was created by the word of God, so that what is seen was not made out of things that are visible. (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%203%3A20&version=ESV][Ephesians 3:20]]* - Now to him who is able to do far more abundantly than all that we ask or think, according to the power at work within us, (ESV)
    #+END_QUOTE

    On the contrary, what is does mean to follow in the footsteps of faith that Abraham had before he was circumcised is that one's faith (the heart attitudes of faith, love, confidence, hope, obedience and perseverance) should be modelled on Abraham's faith.
    So to follow in the footsteps of faith that Abraham had before he was circumcised, one should have the fear of God in one's heart,
    and trust and obey God, and love God more than anything or anyone else, and continue on in faith and as a person does deeds with that faith, the external actions will look different for different people.

    And I've also come to believe that it's really what is in the heart that counts (the faith) that God judges, rather than or above the external actions that are done distict from the faith.

    I believe a "deed" is "external action that is done from faith". A good deed from good faith, and a bad deed from bad faith. So I believe that God when judging on deeds, judges on the basis of the faith that the deed came from.

    I commented on ligonier's video,

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      “Faith is I believe to be the heart attitudes (trust in the truth, love-for the truth, hoping in the truth). External actions are the 'works'. Faith to works is like spirit to flesh.
  
      Love for the truth saves. Love for God's word saves. Love for Jesus Christ saves. Hatred for the truth leads to condemnation and death.
  
      God loved us first, sending Jesus Christ to be propitiation for our sin. We must have a loving faith in Jesus Christ to be saved.
  
      In mathematics, you may have met the concept of a "gradient". If the gradient is positive then the function is increasing in value as its input is increasing. In sanctification, having a "positive gradient" is having "faith and love for God" (the love of the truth, receptive to Jesus) where a person draws near to God (Hebrews 11:6, Hebrews 7:25, James 4:7-8). Having a negative gradient (hatred for the truth) leads to death.‟
    #+END_QUOTE

If someone wants a good outcome, sin cannot be committed in order to achieve it:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A1-2&version=ESV][Romans 6:1-2]]* - What shall we say then? Are we to continue in sin that grace may abound? By no means! How can we who died to sin still live in it? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

When it comes to keeping God's commandments, both intention (e.g. Mens rea) and action matter to God but it's from His perspective.
God sees a human being's external actions clearer than mere human beings can.
It's not right to say that "external actions/outcome matter more than than the faith/intent/obedience" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A1&version=ESV][Romans 6:1]]*), otherwise, why not just commit sin so we can receive more grace?
Why not just steal from lots and lots of people to keep the economy going thinking God will forgive us?

The basis of justification is the faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2011%3A6-7&version=ESV][Romans 11:6-7]]*).

When it comes to man's law-enforcement "endeavouring" to do justice, "Every charge must be established by the evidence of two or three witnesses."
Just because man's law-enforcement "endeavours" to do justice, that doesn't mean they always get it right.
Even if a person is charged and convicted of a crime, the evidence or witnesses may be faulty.
God sees when a person is persecuted for righteousness-sake.

See how here, Paul says that we should *test ourselves* to see if we are in the faith, and that "appearance-wise" it may "seem" to those people as though he (Paul) had "failed the test", but he (Paul) hopes that they will see that he has "not failed the test":

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2013%3A1-9&version=ESV][II Corinthians 13:1-9]]* - This is the third time I am coming to you. Every charge must be established by the evidence of two or three witnesses. I warned those who sinned before and all the others, and I warn them now while absent, as I did when present on my second visit, that if I come again I will not spare them— since you seek proof that Christ is speaking in me. He is not weak in dealing with you, but is powerful among you. For he was crucified in weakness, but lives by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but in dealing with you we will live with him by the power of God. Examine yourselves, to see whether you are in the faith. Test yourselves. Or do you not realize this about yourselves, that Jesus Christ is in you?—unless indeed you fail to meet the test! I hope you will find out that we have not failed the test. *But we pray to God that you may not do wrong—not that we may appear to have met the test, but that you may do what is right, though we may seem to have failed.* For *we cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the truth*. For we are glad when we are weak and you are strong. Your restoration is what we pray for. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's possible to be justified by faith alone ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%202%3A8-9&version=ESV][Ephesians 2:8-9]]).
All justifcation depends on God who has mercy ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%209%3A16&version=ESV][Romans 9:16]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%201%3A28-31&version=ESV][I Corinthians 1:28-31]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A20&version=ESV][Romans 3:20]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A2&version=ESV][Romans 4:2]]).

It's possible to be justified by deeds (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A21-26&version=ESV][James 2:21-26]]*), but those are deeds that are done in justifying faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%2022%3A12&version=ESV][Genesis 22:12]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2011%3A6&version=ESV][Rom 11:6]]*).

But while a person might be justified by deeds ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2025%3A34-37&version=ESV][Matthew 25:34-37]]), the faith is the basis of the justification ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A6&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:6]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2011%3A6&version=ESV][Romans 11:6]]).
The justifying faith (even if it has accompanying works) is not based on our own works ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Titus%203%3A3-5&version=ESV][Titus 3:3-5]]).

+ Intuition about works of the old covenant law :: To rely on justification by "works of the Old Covenant Law" is trying to reify perfect law with perfect external actions, end-to-end without fault. Only Jesus Christ has managed to do this. As a point of difference, works of faith in Jesus Christ are based on Jesus Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%203%3A7-15&version=ESV][I Corinthians 3:7-15]]*) and His righteousness, rather than on one's own righteousness independent from Jesus Christ. These works of faith are done trusting in the Saviour Messiah Jesus Son of God and His word. For example, (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2019%3A2-10&version=ESV][Luke 19:2-10]]*)

It's also possible to have "works" (deeds) without "working for payment" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A22&version=ESV][James 2:22]]*). Because "working for payment" means trying to earn something from God based on one's own works/deeds whereas "works" merely means deeds that everyone has regardless of whether or they are intentionally "working for" something, whether good or evil.
So when [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A5-6&version=ESV][Romans 4:5-6]] says "to the one who does not work", it doesn't exactly mean "to the one who doesn't do or have deeds". What it means is, "to the one who isn't in their mind working to earn something from God".

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2012%3A12&version=ESV][Matthew 12:12]]* - Of how much more value is a man than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So our faith should be one which recognises that what God wants of us is to simply trust and obey Him and hope in Him, seeking Him in faith, and that means trusting and obeying and hoping in Jesus Christ.

And it's the faith trusting Jesus that is not "working for" justification but readily accepts the truth that God justifies whoever is presently trusting in Jesus Christ, even if they are ungodly, that is the faith that is counted as righteousness apart from [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] works.
It's a faith that receives forgiveness from God while trusting Jesus Christ. So that means when we truly are trusting and obeying Jesus Christ from the heart, there is forgiveness and peace with God.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2015%3A13&version=ESV][Romans 15:13]]* - May the God of hope fill you with all joy and *peace in believing*, so that by the power of the Holy Spirit you may abound in hope. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2015%3A13&version=NIV][Romans 15:13]]* - May the God of hope fill you with all joy and *peace as you trust in him*, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit. (NIV)
#+END_QUOTE

The "Law" and the "works of the Law" can in part be described like this:
- The "Law" says "do not bear false witness."
  - Therefore the Law points out sin in sinners.
  - And the Law points to Jesus who is without sin.
- The "works of the Law" would then involve going about doing things without bearing false witness
  - One does deeds without lying.

The law still does its work:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A15&version=ESV][Romans 2:15]]* - They show that the work of the law is written on their hearts, while their conscience also bears witness, and their conflicting thoughts accuse or even excuse them (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

To be justified all the points of the Law would have to be kept simultaneously, not just the commandment to not bear false witness, but also the other commandments.
Only Jesus Christ has kept the works of the law flawlessly, being without sin, and He did this in reality by faith.

If the Law were pursued by faith then for sure that person who is pursuing the Law by faith would be seeking to not bear false witness in reality from the heart, with the fear of God, seeking God's commendation.
If the Law were pursued by works then that person who is pursuing the Law by works may inwardly be lusting over their neighbour's wife but outwardly thinking they're righteous because they'd never physically slept with her.

So when it comes to faith in Jesus, the heart attitudes of love for the truth, trust, hope and obedience still absolutely matter.
Are we trusting in, hoping in, obedient to, loving Jesus Christ who has come into the world as light so that we might not remain in darkness?
Are we abiding in His commandments from the heart in reality?

Christians have:
- faith in Jesus
  - having the mind of Jesus
    - willing to do the will of God
      - trusting, obedient, loving
- works of faith in Jesus
  - doing the deeds of Jesus
  - but works may burn up, yet they would still be saved

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%202%3A16&version=ESV][I Corinthians 2:16]]* - For who has understood the mind of the Lord so as to instruct him? But we have the mind of Christ. (ESV)

Receiving forgiveness from Jesus, having faith in Jesus and loving Jesus all go hand in hand. In fact, someone who truly has been forgiven by God must love in the truth and someone who does't love in the truth neither has been forgiven because if they were forgiven they would love. And notice how the woman's faith is linked with the love she has:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%207%3A40-50&version=ESV][Luke 7:40-50]]* - And Jesus answering said to him, Simon, I have something to say to you. And he answered, Say it, Teacher. A certain moneylender had two debtors. One owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty. When they could not pay, he cancelled the debt of both. Now which of them will love him more? Simon answered, The one, I suppose, for whom he cancelled the larger debt. And he said to him, You have judged rightly. Then turning toward the woman he said to Simon, Do you see this woman? I entered your house; you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair. You gave me no kiss, but from the time I came in she has not ceased to kiss my feet. You did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment. Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven—for she loved much. But he who is forgiven little, loves little. And he said to her, Your sins are forgiven. Then those who were at table with him began to say among themselves, Who is this, who even forgives sins? And he said to the woman, Your faith has saved you; go in peace. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The faith that receives peace and forgiveness with God is not a "working for payment for ones deeds" faith, even though a person still will "do" / produce good deeds when they have good treasure (the love of God) in their heart.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Titus%201%3A15&version=ESV][Titus 1:15]]* - To the pure, all things are pure, but to the defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure; but both their minds and their consciences are defiled. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Good deeds will naturally flow from having the love of God in us (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A45&version=ESV][Luke 6:45]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A42&version=ESV][John 5:42]]*).

False obedience is where there is no love for God in the heart:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2081%3A15&version=ESV][Psalms 81:15]]* - Those who hate the LORD would feign obedience, and their doom would last forever. (engbsb2020eb)

That faith that is not based on one's past works is a presently trusting faith (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A1&version=ESV][John 14:1]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A1-4&version=ESV][Romans 8:1-4]]*) that will produce good deeds naturally.

There will be tribulation and distress for every human being who does [[strongs:G2716][(G2716 katergazomenou)]] evil, the Jew first and also the Greek, but glory and honor and peace for everyone who does [[strongs:G2038][(G2038 ergazomenō; is working for payment)]] good, the Jew first and also the Greek. For God shows no partiality. (ESV)

And to the one who does not work [[strongs:G2038][(G2038 ergazomenō; is working for payment)]] but trusts him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted as righteousness, just as David also speaks of the blessing of the one to whom God counts righteousness apart from [[strongs:G5565][(G5565 chōris)]] works [[strongs:G2041][(G2041 ergōn)]]: (ESV)

In order to have a genuine faith in Jesus, we need to be people who are after God's commendation. So rather than those who seek appraisal in this world and commendation from even fellow Christians, we need to instead be seeking commendation from God Himself. If a person is a "seeker of the glory that comes from man" then they are not "seekers of the glory that comes from God" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A6-11&version=ESV][Romans 2:6-11]]*) and they can't have genuine faith in Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A28-29&version=ESV][John 5:28-29]],37-47* - Do not marvel at this, for an hour is coming when all who are in the tombs will hear his voice and come out, those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment. And the Father who sent me has himself borne witness about me. His voice you have never heard, his form you have never seen, and you do not have his word abiding in you, for you do not believe the one whom he has sent. You search the Scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that bear witness about me, yet you refuse to come to me that you may have life. I do not receive glory from people. But I know that you do not have the *love of God* within you. I have come in my Father's name, and you do not receive me. If another comes in his own name, you will receive him. *How can you believe, when you receive glory from one another and do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?* Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father. There is one who accuses you: Moses, on whom you have set your hope. If you believed Moses, you would believe me; for he wrote of me. But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A8&version=ESV][John 15:8]]* - By this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit and so prove to be my disciples.
#+END_QUOTE

Connecting *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A6-11&version=ESV][Romans 2:6-11]]* to *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A28-29&version=ESV][John 5:28-29]],37-47*. We must be those who do good from a love of the Truth and be those who seek the glory that comes from the only God (i.e. seek God's commendation, seek to please God). So we must love Jesus Christ and from the love of Jesus Christ and His words and His deeds.

So without the love of God in us, and a desire to please God seeking the glory from God, seeking God's approval (as opposed to man's approval), we can't even have genuine faith. Thankfully, God is pleased with us if we receive Jesus, if we love Him, if we have faith in Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2016%3A25-28&version=ESV][John 16:25-28]]* - I have said these things to you in figures of speech. The hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in figures of speech but will tell you plainly about the Father. In that day you will ask in my name, and I do not say to you that I will ask the Father on your behalf; for *the Father himself loves [[strongs:G5368][(G5368 philei)]] you, _because you have loved [[strongs:G5368][(G5368 pephilēkate)]] me and have believed that I came from God._* I came from the Father and have come into the world, and now I am leaving the world and going to the Father.
#+END_QUOTE

The person who loves Jesus is the person who loves His word (from the treasuring love of God's word) *and* keeps His commandments (have faith in Jesus Christ and love one another the way we've been commanded to):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A21-24&version=ESV][John 14:21-24]]* - Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves me. And he who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him. Judas (not Iscariot) said to him, Lord, how is it that you will manifest yourself to us, and not to the world? Jesus answered him, If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him. Whoever does not love me does not keep my words. And the word that you hear is not mine but the Father's who sent me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A23&version=ESV][I John 3:23]]* - And this is his commandment, that we believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as he has commanded us. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God loved us first in sending Jesus Christ to die for our sins and raised to life for our justification so that we might live through faith in Jesus Christ (trusting and abiding in Jesus' teachings out of a love for the truth, out of a love for the light, out of a love for Jesus Christ and His word).

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2012%3A35-43&version=ESV][John 12:35-43]]* - So Jesus said to them, The light is among you for a little while longer. Walk while you have the light, lest darkness overtake you. The one who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going. While you have the light, believe in the light, that you may become sons of light. When Jesus had said these things, he departed and hid himself from them. Though he had done so many signs before them, they still did not believe in him, so that the word spoken by the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled: Lord, who has believed what he heard from us, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? Therefore they could not believe. For again Isaiah said, He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, lest they see with their eyes, and understand with their heart, and turn, and I would heal them. Isaiah said these things because he saw his glory and spoke of him. Nevertheless, many even of the authorities believed in him, but for fear of the Pharisees they did not confess it, so that they would not be put out of the synagogue; for they loved the glory that comes from man more than the glory that comes from God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Something has a velocity but the distance travelled is a different thing. Likewise, the Christian can have faith but the works done is a different thing.
I'm likening the faith (the heart attitudes) to the velocity, and the works of the past (deeds done) to the distance travelled.
So long as a person's heart has been made right and that they are now exercising faith in Jesus working through love, then their past sins are forgiven.
That "faith working through love" is what counts doesn't mean it's the works which merit justification:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A6-7&version=ESV][Galatians 5:6-7]]* - For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but only faith working through love. You were running well. Who hindered you from obeying the truth? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%201%3A5&version=ESV][I Timothy 1:5]]* - The aim of our charge is love that issues from a pure heart and a good conscience and a sincere faith. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

See how there is an attitude change going from being a slave to sin to being being a slave to righteousness (a slave to Jesus Christ). With the correct understanding of grace, we must still be obedient to Jesus, *ready* to do good works, consciously applying Jesus' teachings and commandments, doing the will of God seeking to please God, awake for our Master to come. Being under grace rather than law doesn't mean we no longer need to be obedient:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A10-18&version=ESV][Romans 6:10-18]]* - For the death he died he died to sin, once for all, but the life he lives he lives to God. So you also must consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus. Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal bodies, to make you obey their passions. Do not present your members to sin as instruments for unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life, and your members to God as instruments for righteousness. For sin will have no dominion over you, since you are not under law but under grace. What then? Are we to sin because we are not under law but under grace? By no means! Do you not know that if you present yourselves to anyone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin, which leads to death, or of obedience, which leads to righteousness? But thanks be to God, that you who were once slaves of sin have become obedient from the heart to the standard of teaching to which you were committed, and, having been set free from sin, have become slaves of righteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We need to "share Abraham's faith" so our faith needs to look like Abraham's faith, and not "working for" justification but resting from "working for" (and that doesn't mean resting from works):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A13-18&version=ESV][Romans 4:13-18]]* - For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world did not come through the law but through the righteousness of faith. For if it is the adherents of the law who are to be the heirs, faith is null and the promise is void. For the law brings wrath, but where there is no law there is no transgression. That is why it depends on faith, in order that the promise may rest on grace and be guaranteed to all his offspring—not only to the adherent of the law but also to the one who shares the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all, as it is written, I have made you the father of many nations—in the presence of the God in whom he believed, who gives life to the dead and calls into existence the things that do not exist. In hope he believed against hope, that he should become the father of many nations, as he had been told, So shall your offspring be. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A18-25&version=ESV][Romans 4:18-25]]* - In hope he believed against hope, that he should become the father of many nations, as he had been told, So shall your offspring be. No distrust made him waver concerning the promise of God, but he grew strong in his faith as he gave glory to God, fully convinced that God was able to do what he had promised. That is why his faith was counted to him as righteousness. But the words it was counted to him were not written for his sake alone, but for ours also. It will be counted to us who believe in him who raised from the dead Jesus our Lord, who was delivered up for our trespasses and raised for our justification. (ESV)

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2012%3A12&version=ESV][Matthew 12:12]]* - Of how much more value is a man than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A5&version=ESV][Romans 4:5]] is saying that whoever is simply actively believing (trusting, faithing) in God, even obeying Him, accepting what God has said as true, just like Abraham did, but not "working for" what God has already promised, as in, accepts that God forgives the one who is presently trusting in Jesus Christ (just as Abraham who simply trusted that God was telling the truth was not "working for" what God had already promised), that person's faith is counted as righteousness. The type of faith in Jesus Christ that we have believes that as long as we are walking by faith in Jesus Christ, our sins are forgiven. Christ's commandments are a law of faith, not works.

+ [[https://biblehub.com/interlinear/romans/4-5.htm][Romans 4:5 (Interlinear)]] :: To the [one] however not [[strongs:G3361][(G3361 mē)]] working [[strongs:G2038][(G2038 ergazomenō)]] believing [[strongs:G4100][(G4100 pisteuonti)]] however on the [One] justifying the ungodly is reckoned the faith of him for righteousness

But this faith continues to be correctable by God from His word. If the word of God contradicts a false belief which someone has, then the person who has faith in Jesus receives God's word as correction and comes into agreement with God.

Faith in Jesus Christ looks like by faith obeying Him, just as Abraham did (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A8&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:8]]*) and continues to agree with the same Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20John%201%3A9-10&version=ESV][II John 1:9-10]]*).

So we mere human persons of God's creation are not justified on the basis of our own righteousness (how good we are, even how good we endeavour to be):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2045%3A22-25&version=ESV][Isaiah 45:22-25]]* - Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth! For I am God, and there is no other. By myself I have sworn; from my mouth has gone out in righteousness a word that shall not return: To me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear allegiance. *Only in the LORD, it shall be said of me, are righteousness and strength; to him shall come and be ashamed all who were incensed against him. In the LORD all the offspring of Israel shall be justified and shall glory.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A4&version=ESV][Romans 3:4]],20,26-28,31* - By no means! Let God be true though every one were a liar, as it is written, That you may be justified in your words, and prevail when you are judged. For by works of the law no human being will be justified in his sight, since through the law comes knowledge of sin. It was to show his righteousness at the present time, so that he might be just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus. Then what becomes of our boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? By a law of works? No, but by the law of faith. For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from works of the law. Do we then overthrow the law by this faith? By no means! On the contrary, we uphold the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Titus%201%3A15&version=ESV][Titus 1:15]]* - To the pure, all things are pure, but to the defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure; but both their minds and their consciences are defiled. (ESV)

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A15-17&version=ESV][I John 4:15-17]]* - Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him, and he in God. So we have come to know and to believe the love that God has for us. God is love, and whoever abides in love abides in God, and God abides in him. By this is love perfected with us, so that we may have confidence for the day of judgment, because as he is so also are we in this world. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A19&version=ESV][I John 4:19]]* - We love because he first loved us. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20John%201%3A6&version=ESV][II John 1:6]]* - And this is love, that we walk according to his commandments; this is the commandment, just as you have heard from the beginning, so that you should walk in it. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's not enough to rely on one's own righteousness, to rely on "being law-abiding enough". We do need to rely on God that through faith in Jesus we can be forgiven our lawless deeds. Because we all need forgiveness from God in order to be able to move forward with a good conscience:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A4-8&version=ESV][Romans 4:4-8]]* - Now to the one who works, his wages are not counted as a gift but as his due. And to the one who does not work but trusts him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted as righteousness, just as David also speaks of the blessing of the one to whom God counts righteousness apart from works: Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven, and whose sins are covered; blessed is the man against whom the Lord will not count his sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%201%3A5&version=ESV][I Timothy 1:5]]* - The aim of our charge is love that issues from a pure heart and a good conscience and a sincere faith. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So what matters is who you have faith in because we follow who we have faith in (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2015%3A13-14&version=ESV][Matthew 15:13-14]]*; *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2012%3A23-26&version=ESV][John 12:23-26]]*). A person is justified by their faith in Jesus Christ. We're not justified by having faith in ourself. We need to be found by God as doers *[[strongs:G4163][(G4163 poiētai)]]* of the law of Christ which is a law of faith, and it's faith in Him, Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A26-28&version=ESV][Romans 3:26-28]]* - It was to show his righteousness at the present time, so that he might be just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus. Then what becomes of our boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? By a law of works? No, but by the law of faith. For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from works of the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%20103%3A17-18&version=ESV][Psalms 103:17-18]]* - But the steadfast love of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear him, and his righteousness to children's children, to those who keep his covenant and remember to do his commandments. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE
