When it comes to following the 10 commandments, we must be followers of them from the heart (the way Jesus commanded).

Jesus Christ's Dad is God, not Joseph, but He kept the commandment to honor one's father and mother.
Jesus Christ, Son of God, honored God who is His father and His mother who is of those who "hear the word of God and do it".

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%208%3A21&version=ESV][Luke 8:21]]* - But he answered them, My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So as a born-again Christian, the commandment to honor one's father and mother is applied in imitation of the same way that Jesus Christ applied it:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A8-11&version=ESV][Matthew 23:8-11]]* - But you are not to be called rabbi, for you have one teacher, and you are all brothers. And call no man your father on earth, for you have one Father, who is in heaven. Neither be called instructors, for you have one instructor (2519. kathégétés), the Christ. The greatest among you shall be your servant. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

What about keeping the Sabbath? By the sounds of it, since the Sabbath was made "for man", we should be feel free to rest on the Sabbath.
And we should not pervert the purpose of the Sabbath by turning the commandment into a heavy an unnecessary yoke that defeats the purpose of the Sabbath.
And we should not cease to do good. A person is supposed to walk by faith and in love:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%202%3A27&version=ESV][Mark 2:27]]* - And he said to them, The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A9&version=ESV][Luke 6:9]]* - And Jesus said to them, I ask you, is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save life or to destroy it? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We're not under law because Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, but only if we are led by the Spirit:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A12-14&version=ESV][Galatians 3:12-14]]* - But the law is not of faith, rather The one who does them shall live by them. Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us—for it is written, Cursed is everyone who is hanged on a tree— so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles, so that we might receive the promised Spirit through faith. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We've got to follow after Jesus, obediently, sure, having confidence by doing in reality from the heart, sure, but not relying on the external success (in our own eyes) of deeds for our own confidence:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A11-14&version=ESV][Galatians 3:11-14]]* - Now it is evident that no one is justified before God by the law, for The righteous shall live by faith. But the law is not of faith, rather The one who does [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g4160/kjv/tr/0-1/][(G4160 poiēsas; having done)]] them [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g846/kjv/tr/0-1/][(G846 auta; these things)]] shall live by them. Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us—for it is written, Cursed is everyone who is hanged on a tree— so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles, so that we might receive the promised Spirit through faith. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

When a the righteous comes before the throne of Jesus Christ, they won't be self-commending, but rather Jesus will let them know when they such things for Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2025%3A44-45&version=ESV][Matthew 25:44-45]]* - Then they also will answer, saying, Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not minister to you? Then he will answer them, saying, Truly, I say to you, as you did not do it to one of the least of these, you did not do it to me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Benig led by the Spirit, a person is not under the Law and sin has no dominion over them:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A13-18&version=ESV][Galatians 5:13-18]]* - For you were called to freedom, brothers. Only do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another. For the whole law is fulfilled in one word: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. But if you bite and devour one another, watch out that you are not consumed by one another. But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh. For the desires of the flesh are against the Spirit, and the desires of the Spirit are against the flesh, for these are opposed to each other, to keep you from doing the things you want to do. But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A14-18&version=ESV][Romans 6:14-18]]* - For sin will have no dominion over you, since you are not under law but under grace. What then? Are we to sin because we are not under law but under grace? By no means! Do you not know that if you present yourselves to anyone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin, which leads to death, or of obedience, which leads to righteousness? But thanks be to God, that you who were once slaves of sin have become obedient from the heart to the standard of teaching to which you were committed, and, having been set free from sin, have become slaves of righteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But rather, we are under grace (Jesus helps us as we by faith in Him do what He has commanded, and as we imitate [but not replace] His faith and love out of faith and obedience to Him and to God). We still are saved by faith and obedience to Jesus Christ Himself (rather than to simply the Law of God).

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A1-6&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:1-6]]* - Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight, and sin which clings so closely, and let us run with endurance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is seated at the right hand of the throne of God. Consider him who endured from sinners such hostility against himself, so that you may not grow weary or fainthearted. In your struggle against sin you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood. And have you forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons? My son, do not regard lightly the discipline of the Lord, nor be weary when reproved by him. For the Lord disciplines the one he loves, and chastises every son whom he receives. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

"The one having completed all of these external deeds will live" is probably an accurate way to understand "the one who does [[strongs:G4160][(G4160 poiēsas; having done)]] them shall live by them", as if there entire future is dependent on the completion of all of these external tasks. But in doing Christ's law of faith, we should be doing from the heart:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A10-13&version=ESV][Galatians 3:10-13]]* - For all who rely on works [[strongs:G2041][(G2041 ergōn: works, deed, action, task, labor)]] of the law are under a curse; for it is written, Cursed be everyone who does not abide by all things written in the Book of the Law, and do them. Now it is evident that no one is justified before God by the law, for The righteous shall live by faith. But the law is not of faith, rather The one who does [[strongs:G4160][(G4160 poiēsas; having done)]] them shall live by them. Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us—for it is written, Cursed is everyone who is hanged on a tree— (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Abraham was tested to see if He had the fear of God in Him. Our faith must be like that. When we talk about "justification by works", it has to be _on the basis of_ faith, on the basis of what's in the heart (in this case, the fear of God), rather than the external deed, otherwise it's no longer grace, but the exterior deed is an indicator of what is going on inside:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%2022%3A12&version=ESV][Genesis 22:12]]* - He said, Do not lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him, for now I know that you fear God, seeing you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Fear of God and hoping in God's steadfast love are strongly associated. Hoping in God's steadfast love and having the fear of God (wanting to please God, not wanting to sin against God), are strongly linked together. And because the faith we have is one which loves the truth of God, having the fear of God and having a love for the truth and a hatred of evil are all strongly linked together:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2033%3A18-19&version=ESV][Psalms 33:18-19]]* - Behold, the eye of the LORD is on those who fear him, on those who hope in his steadfast love, that he may deliver their soul from death and keep them alive in famine. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Abiding by Christ's law (Christ's commandments), which is a law of faith (we're not under the curse of the law of Moses) and is not a law of works (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A21-31&version=ESV][Romans 3:21-31]]*), is not being under a curse, but, rather is being under grace:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2016%3A22&version=ESV][I Corinthians 16:22]]* - If anyone has no love for the Lord, let him be accursed. Our Lord, come! (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A21&version=ESV][John 14:21]]* - Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves me. And he who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A17&version=ESV][John 1:17]]* - For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

When contrasting being "under law" to being "under grace", Paul is takling about people who "rely" on the "works" (the exterior stuff) of the law, the Mosaic Law (which came in after Abraham), who are under law. But the law of Christ which we are 'under' (abide in) *is* a different type of law, and the kind of law that it is is a law of faith. It's about the heart. And like Abraham, we should believe in, trust in, trust, agape love and obey Jesus. And just like Abraham's faith, our faith may be tested and a person may be justified by works, like Abraham's faith and that wasn't "works of the law of Moses" which came in later (to increase the trespass). But we don't "rely" on the justification by works of faith in Jesus, though that type of thing may happen.

Paul in *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A10-13&version=ESV][Galatians 3:10-13]]* is takling about people who "rely" on the "works" of the law.

Christian joy doesn't mean the opposite of sorrow. Christian joy is not merely "happiness":

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2014%3A32-36&version=ESV][Mark 14:32-36]]* - And they went to a place called Gethsemane. And he said to his disciples, Sit here while I pray. And he took with him Peter and James and John, and began to be greatly distressed and troubled. And he said to them, My soul is very sorrowful, even to death. Remain here and watch. And going a little farther, he fell on the ground and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from him. And he said, Abba, Father, all things are possible for you. Remove this cup from me. Yet not what I will, but what you will. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A1-3&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:1-3]]* - Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight, and sin which clings so closely, and let us run with endurance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of our faith, who *for the joy that was set before him endured the cross*, despising the shame, and is seated at the right hand of the throne of God. Consider him who endured from sinners such hostility against himself, *so that you may not grow weary or fainthearted.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

When we talk about 'merit' or 'credit', we were enabled to even be able to have merit in suffering for righteousness sake _because_ *Jesus bore our sins on the tree* that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. 'Live to righteousness' means walking in the light, walking in love and truth, practicing works that please God, making spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ. [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2013%3A1-8&version=ESV][I Corinthians 13:1-8]] says that without love (love that rejoices with the truth) we gain nothing. God loved us first and has chosen us to be a holy people for His possession, and we can now make spiritual sacrficies which God finds acceptable through Jesus Christ our Lord who we are holding faith in and who has loved us first, laying down His life for us first:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%202%3A15-25&version=ESV][I Peter 2:15-25]]* - For this is the will of God, that by doing good you should put to silence the ignorance of foolish people. *Live as people who are free, not using your freedom as a cover-up for evil, but living as servants of God.* _Honor everyone. *Love the brotherhood.* Fear God. Honor the emperor._ Servants, be subject to your masters with all respect, not only to the good and gentle but also to the unjust. For this is a gracious thing, when, mindful of God, one endures sorrows while suffering unjustly. For *what _credit_ is it if, when you sin and are beaten for it, you endure? But if when you do good and suffer for it you endure, this is a gracious thing in the sight of God*. For to this you have been called, because *Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you might follow in his steps*. He committed no sin, neither was deceit found in his mouth. When he was reviled, he did not revile in return; when he suffered, he did not threaten, but continued entrusting himself to him who judges justly. *He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we might die to sin and live to righteousness*. By his wounds you have been healed. For you were straying like sheep, but have now returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%202%3A4-5&version=ESV][I Peter 2:4-5]]* - As you come to him, a living stone rejected by men but in the sight of God chosen and precious, you yourselves like living stones are being built up as a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, to offer *spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

All have died. Those who now live should live for him who for their sake died and was raised, therefore we no longer regard other people according to the flesh. All things are now new.

 #+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%205%3A14-15&version=ESV][II Corinthians 5:14-15]]* - For the love of Christ controls us, because we have concluded this: that one has died for all, therefore all have died; and he died for all, that _those who live *might no longer* live for themselves but for him who for their sake died and was raised._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Believing in God and believing that He *rewards* those who seek Him, whilst holding our faith in Jesus Christ, we endeavour to do good out of obedience to Jesus Christ. We want to please God with our lives. God purchased our redemption with Jesus' blood and the blood of Jesus Christ washes us as we walk in the light as He is in the light. Just because God purchased us, that doesn't take away our free will to choose who we will continue to obey. God wants us to choose to continue obediently holding faith in Him, trusting Him and obeying Him, and we want to ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A6&version=ESV][John 5:6]]) do that too because we want eternal life:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%203%3A2&version=ESV][I Peter 3:2]]* - He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. By his wounds you have been healed. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

If we choose instead to obey the flesh (the sinful nature) then that would lead to corruption ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%206%3A7-8&version=ESV][Gal 6:7-8]]). If we choose to obey sin instead of obey God then that would lead to death ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 6:23]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%201%3A12-15&version=ESV][James 1:12-15]]) as sin in the flesh has been condemned ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A1-6&version=ESV][Romans 8:1-6]]). If we choose to obey Christ instead of sin then we will be saved ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%205%3A8-9&version=ESV][Hebrews 5:8-9]]). If we obey the One True God then we'll receive the Holy Spirit ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%205%3A8-9&version=ESV][Hebrews 5:8-9]]). It's much better to have eternal life and nice rewards from God than it is to be overcome by sin, so we should sow to the Spirit ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%206%3A7-8&version=ESV][Gal 6:7-8]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%203%3A18&version=ESV][James 3:18]]).

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%201%3A12-15&version=ESV][James 1:12-15]]* - Blessed is the man who remains steadfast under trial, for when he has stood the test he will receive the crown of life, which God has promised to those who love him. Let no one say when he is tempted, I am being tempted by God, for God cannot be tempted with evil, and he himself tempts no one. But each person is tempted when he is lured and enticed by his own desire. Then desire when it has conceived gives birth to sin, and sin when it is fully grown brings forth death. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%203%3A18&version=ESV][James 3:18]]* - And a harvest of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace. (ESV)

If you are believing in your heart that God raised Jesus Christ from the dead and confessing that Jesus is Lord then you will be saved.
God sees your heart and you have a relationship with God through Jesus Christ.

+ So try to hold these two things together in your heart and make a vocal confession with your mouth if possible, otherwise "think" it becase God can hear our thoughts: :: Believe in your heart that God raised Jesus from the dead and while believing that also confess Jesus is Lord.

In doing this, it should give a person relief and confidence that they have been heard by God. That message got through.
When you do this, it's like putting out an SOS signal, or calling International Rescue (a reference to Thunderbirds), and knowing you've been heard by
God and He is rescuing you. God sees the thoughts of our hearts. That's one reason why the Thunderbirds analogy is cool.
In the Thunderbirds, they listen to radios worldwide on any frequency for distress calls. So if you're
in slavery to sin and perishing and want hope for eternal life, then you call out to God like it says in [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A4&version=ESV][Romans 10:4]], believing in your heart that God raised Jesus from the dead and confessing
Jesus is Lord then your next thoughts can be "I'm OK. I'm safe. Jesus is saving me." because He is.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2018%3A10&version=ESV][Proverbs 18:10]]* - The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous man runs into it and is safe. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A lot of English translations insert the words "at the present time" into [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A26&version=ESV][Romans 3:26]], but I don't see it in the [[https://biblehub.com/interlinear/romans/3-25.htm][original text]]. But it's clearly linked to and understood better alongside *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A8-11&version=ESV][I Peter 1:8-11]]*. We must continue abiding in Christ's teachings. Yes, we believe that God has put forward Christ Jesus as a propitiation by His blood which is to be received by faith. God has full sovereignty (because He is the justifier) to determine and justify and commend whoever He deems has faith in Jesus Christ. What must we do? What is our duty? Fear Him and keep His commandments. He commanded faith. We must have faith in Jesus Christ. God tests our hearts.
The righteousness in the actual doing of the law above (even doing it whilst not having necessarily heard it) is still upheld but there is now the righteousness that is by faith in Jesus Christ. In other words, keeping the commandments of God and following Jesus are not mutually exclusive. And the law still describes what good behaviour looks like and what bad behaviour looks like. But through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, as we follow and place our faith in Jesus, obeying Jesus to repent from sin and to do good and to pass forward love and forgiveness, etc., we can be justified by our faith in Jesus. As we go on living, we keep our obedient believing faith in Jesus, and no longer want to rebel against God's law. Perfect compliance to the law is no longer the basis of our justification but we seek to not break the law. One of Paul's points here is that the Gentiles did not have the Law given through Moses. So the works of the Law that Paul is talking about are the works of the Mosaic Law:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A21-31&version=ESV][Romans 3:21-31]]* - But now the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, although the Law and the Prophets bear witness to it— the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe. For there is no distinction: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, and are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God put forward as a propitiation by his blood, to be received by faith. This was to show God's righteousness, because in his divine forbearance he had passed over former sins. It was to show his righteousness at the present time, so that he might be just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus. Then what becomes of our boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? By a law of works? No, but by the law of faith. For we hold that *one is justified by faith apart from works of the law.* Or is God the God of Jews only? Is he not the God of Gentiles also? Yes, of Gentiles also, since God is one. *He will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through faith.* Do we then overthrow the law by this faith? By no means! On the contrary, we uphold the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We can have and should have a faith that loves the truth, loves Jesus, even if we haven't seen Him yet:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A8-11&version=ESV][I Peter 1:8-11]]* - Though you have not seen him, you love him. Though you do not now see him, you believe in him and rejoice with joy that is inexpressible and filled with glory, obtaining the outcome of your faith, the salvation of your souls. Concerning this salvation, *the prophets who prophesied about the grace that was to be yours searched and inquired carefully*, inquiring what person or time [[strongs:G2540][(G2540 kairós)]] the Spirit of Christ in them was indicating when he predicted the sufferings of Christ and the subsequent [[strongs:G3326][(G3326 meta, contingent)]] glories. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

"Kairós" is qualitative and "xrónos" is quantitative:

+ G2540 kairós :: time as opportunity. 2540 /kairós ("opportune time") is derived from kara ("head") referring to things "coming to a head" to take full-advantage of.

+ G5550 xrónos :: time (in general), especially viewed in sequence (a "succession of moments"); time in duration in the physical-space world, sovereignly apportioned by God to each person.

In the ESV translation of [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A11&version=ESV][I Peter 1:11]], the word 'subsequent' represents the Greek word 'meta' [[strongs:G3326][(G3326 meta, contingent)]], but I think that an English translation would better translate 'meta' as "contingent" because that opens up to the reader the potential to be understood in a quantitatively chonological timelessness way as 'kairós' is also chronologically quantitatively neither here nor there. So in the original text, I think the Greek word 'meta' fits well alongside the word 'kairós'. It's not 'xrónos' which is in [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A11&version=ESV][I Peter 1:11]], but 'kairós' and so it's talking about the opportune moment in a qualitative way. The issue, I think, with using 'subsequent' is that it introduces into the text subliminally an idea that God had to "wait" for the "xrónos" time in order to commend the righteousness that is by faith, but that's evidently not true, and also in the very same verse, [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A11&version=ESV][I Peter 1:11]], it says there in the text that the Spirit of Christ was in them.

# *Hebrews 11:39-40* - And all these, though commended through their faith, did not receive what was promised, since God had provided something better for us, that apart from us they should not be made perfect. (ESV)

Sincerely, in the sight of God, I am seeking to speak the truth about Jesus accurately, and let people know that we should be faithfully waiting for a future salvation, and not trying to give people false comfort with a false gospel:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%202%3A14-17&version=ESV][II Corinthians 2:14-17]]* - But thanks be to God, who in Christ always leads us in triumphal procession, and through us spreads the fragrance of the knowledge of him everywhere. For _we are the aroma of Christ to God among those *who are being saved* and among those who are perishing, to one a fragrance from death to death, to the other a fragrance from life to life_. Who is sufficient for these things? For we are not, like so many, peddlers of God's word, but as men of sincerity, as commissioned by God, in the sight of God we speak in Christ. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I believe that Jesus will judge according to the Truth. Even though my theology has imperfections, I think that ultimately, Jesus will judge according to His word and I'm at His mercy.

I recognize that I am a sinful person and still need God to justify me through faith in Jesus Christ, not of my own works. I think that "sinful" (i.e. having indwelling sin) is more accurate than saying "sinner" for someone who God has given a new heart and spirit.

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%205%3A8-10&version=ESV][Luke 5:8-10]]* - But when Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus' knees, saying, Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord. For he and all who were with him were astonished at the catch of fish that they had taken, and so also were James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. And Jesus said to Simon, Do not be afraid; from now on you will be catching men. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

By no means! *Let God be true though every one were a liar*, as it is written, That you may be justified in your words, and prevail when you are judged. But if *our unrighteousness serves to show the righteousness of God*, what shall we say? That God is unrighteous to inflict wrath on us? (I speak in a human way.) By no means! For then how could God judge the world? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A21-28&version=ESV][Romans 3:21-28]]* - But now the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, although the Law and the Prophets bear witness to it — *the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe*. For there is no distinction: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, and are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God put forward as a propitiation by his blood, to be received by faith. This was to show God's righteousness, because in his divine forbearance he had passed over former sins. It was to show his righteousness at the present time, so that he might be just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus. Then what becomes of our boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? By a law of works? No, but by the law of faith. For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from works of the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

      leading to sanctification, and the end, eternal life.  For the wages of sin is
      death, but the gracious gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%203%3A11-13&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 3:11-13]]* - Now may our God and Father himself, and our Lord Jesus, direct our way to you, and *may the Lord make you increase and abound in love for one another and for all*, as we do for you, *so that he may establish your hearts blameless in holiness before our God and Father*, at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all his saints. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

This blamelessness involes approving of what is right/excellent. So if we still have issues, but confess our sin, and we know what is right, and know we still need God's grace and are still holding to our confession of faith in Jesus (and I am still holding to it), and haven't turned away from Jesus, I think we might still be in a position of _blamelessness_. I think it's looks like a transformed life, transformed into Christ's love, keep His commandments, and agreeing with God and walking in the light, walking in the love of the truth, and as we do that the blood of Jesus Christ cleanses us from all sin. So there's justification first which is the breastplate of faith and love, loving the truth, and there is sanctification which is being cleaned up:

(ESV)

(KJV)
#+END_QUOTE

Being '[[https://www.google.com/url?sa=t&source=web&rct=j&opi=89978449&url=http://biblehub.com/greek/5384.htm][philos with (friends with, allured by, attracted to)]]', money , self, pleasure, rather than ([[strongs:G3123][(G3123 mallon: rather [Adv])]]) being allured by God (wanting to be around God) is bad. But we should avoid those who are attracted to such things rather than/instead of God. We want to be attracted to God, and certainly must be attracted to God moreso than by pleasure, money, self, etc. And we are instructed to avoid such people who are drawn to such things in preference to God. I still think that we really do need to have the fear of God, actually, to be sound in our faith. Otherwise people will actually just say things like "God loves our sinfulness too and doesn't want us to be cleaned up but really just loves us as we are and wouldn't change a thing", and that is not true about God because God would change things about us. God's will is our sanctification (it's what He wants). God disciplines us and cleans us up as we trust and obey Jesus Christ. Also, the agape love we have for family in Christ is a "yoking" love which is not to be shared with those who are enemies of Jesus Christ. It's similar to the way in which a married man has certain duties to His wife that is not extended to other people.

Love is certainly to do with *duty* / *obligation* and our duties are described to us through God's word:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ecclesiastes%2012%3A13-14&version=ESV][Ecclesiastes 12:13-14]]* - The end of the matter; all has been heard. Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole duty of man. For God will bring every deed into judgment, with every secret thing, whether good or evil. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A Christian does not love all people with the same duty, actually, but rather loves all people in the way that God has commanded us to love them.
If we have different duties to different people, then we actually do love people differently, but so long as it's in accordance with sound teaching.

God's universal love for people is demonstrated in what He has done already in sending Jesus Christ. But God has also conditional love that does in fact depend on our heart posture towards God. But everyone is offered this conditional love but not everyone takes it. God offers all without partiality but with conditions His friendship and His eternal love, but by free choice some people reject God's offer by not meeting the conditions:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A8-13&version=ESV][James 2:8-13]]* - If you really fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, You shall love your neighbor as yourself, you are doing well. But if you show partiality, you are committing sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors. For whoever keeps the whole law but fails in one point has become accountable for all of it. For he who said, Do not commit adultery, also said, Do not murder. If you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law. So speak and so act as those who are to be judged under the law of liberty. For judgment is without mercy to one who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I heard this from somebody this morning, "God wants us to love everybody equally." Really? And what is meant by that?
God doesn't love everybody equally.

In the imitation of God's love for those who hate Him (i.e. sending rain on the good and the evil alike), to love one's enemies doesn't mean that they are one's friends. To love one's enemies is to do good to them and to not render evil for evil to them, and to bear with them in patience, hoping for their sake that they will turn away from the love of evil:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A43-48&version=ESV][Matthew 5:43-48]]* - You have heard that it was said, You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy. But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the just and on the unjust. For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same? And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing than others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same? You therefore must be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

If someone is "of the world" and acting ignorantly in unbelief being mean and nasty and greedy etc. then a Christian is really called to "do good" to them.
But if someone who claims to be a believer but is unrepentant and without the fear of God, then that person is very sinful and should be rebuked and avoided,
and left to be chastised (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%205%3A1-13&version=ESV][I Corinthians 5:1-13]]*).

This is what God's love looks like. So in imitating God's love, we should "do good to all" but doing good to a person who professes to have faith in Jesus Christ, might look like avoiding them, and letting them receive discipline.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2013%3A10&version=ESV][Romans 13:10]]* - Love does no wrong to a neighbor; therefore love is the fulfilling of the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A4-8&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:4-8]]* - In your struggle against sin you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood. And have you forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons? My son, do not regard lightly the discipline of the Lord, nor be weary when reproved by him. For the Lord disciplines the one he loves, and chastises every son whom he receives. It is for discipline that you have to endure. God is treating you as sons. For what son is there whom his father does not discipline? If you are left without discipline, in which all have participated, then you are illegitimate children and not sons. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%205%3A14-15&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 5:14-15]]* - We urge you, brethren, admonish the unruly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, be patient with everyone. See that no one repays another with evil for evil, but always seek after that which is good for one another and for all people. (NASB)
#+END_QUOTE

To bear with a person, hoping that they will repent, is not to "yoke" oneself to them.
A Christian living "in the world" would live in obedience to Christ, with love for Christ,rather than with love for the world or for evil.

The "God loving everyone the same way and equally and doesn't want you to change" gospel is actually an antigospel that prevents people from receiving the salvation that Jesus bought. Salvation involves sanctification, and God's friendship and eternal love is for those who fear Him and abide in His commandments with love for Jesus Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2025%3A14&version=ESV][Psalms 25:14]] - The friendship of the LORD is for those who fear him, and he makes known to them his covenant. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Malachi%202%3A17&version=ESV][Malachi 2:17]]* - You have wearied the LORD with your words. But you say, How have we wearied him? By saying, Everyone who does evil is good in the sight of the LORD, and he delights in them. Or by asking, Where is the God of justice? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A21-24&version=ESV][John 14:21-24]]* - Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves me. And he who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him. Judas (not Iscariot) said to him, Lord, how is it that you will manifest yourself to us, and not to the world? Jesus answered him, If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him. Whoever does not love me does not keep my words. And the word that you hear is not mine but the Father's who sent me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%206%3A24&version=ESV][Matthew 6:24]]* - *No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other*, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and money. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2016%3A27&version=ESV][John 16:27]]* - for the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came from God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A2&version=ESV][I John 5:2]]* - By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and obey his commandments. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15&version=ESV][John 14:15]]* - If you love me, you will keep my commandments. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A21&version=ESV][John 14:21]]* - Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves me. And he who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God *loved* all people in the same way, for sure, in sending Jesus Christ into the world. God has demonstrated His love for us in that while we were sinners, Christ died for us. That is true for everyone.
But God loves those who love Jesus in a different way altogether compared with how He loves those who have rejected Jesus.
God's friendship is for those who love Jesus and believe that He came from God.

I mean, on the surface saying that "God wants us to love everybody equally because God loves everybody equally" may sound nice to ears that are not trained to perceive the lie.
But God doesn't love everybody equally, and since Christians ought to be imitating God's love, then Christians shouldn't love everyone equally.
Father God's friendship is for those who love Jesus and believe that He came from God.
Jesus Christ's friendship is for those who have learned from Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A13-17&version=ESV][John 15:13-17]]*) and do what He says (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A9-14&version=ESV][John 15:9-14]]*).
Jesus Christ's agape love is for those who keep Jesus' commandments (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A10&version=ESV][John 15:10]]*).
It's right to say God has loved us. This is correct. It's also correct to say, God loves us in bearing with us in patience for us to repent and come to love Him back through faith in Jesus.
And it's right to say that to remain in God's love we must be keeping Jesus' commandments.
A person who rejects Jesus and continues on that path eventually receives the wrath of God.
The Christians' friendship should be for our family in Christ, and not for the world:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%204%3A4&version=ESV][James 4:4]]* - You adulterous people! Do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity with God? Therefore whoever wishes to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A Christian should not be "led" by evil people. And real love loves in the way prescribed by God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A2-3&version=ESV][I John 5:2-3]]*).

I think Mari would be better to have said, "By loving God and keeping His commandments, a person loves their neighbour, which is our duty as Christians." Sure, love everyone, even no-believres, but in the way that Jesus Christ loves them and that includes speaking the truth to them and bearing with them in patience that they will repent. But loving them doesn't mean affirming error or endorsing a sinful way of life:

+ [[https://youtube.com/watch?v=11z22HR1KHo&t=421][Quote from Mari Mari Emmanuel]] :: So fear nothing, love everyone, but be firm when it comes to speaking the truth. Truth cannot be compromised. ... The one who is all love, He was sharper than a sword; When it came to holding the Truth, fighting for the Truth, He stood firm, never gave way, never compromised. Now that is love. If you truly love someone, wouldn't you want them to be living in the Truth? If you truly love the person, you will tell them, "This is right... This is wrong..."

As Christians we must not "turn back" like Lot's wife did, and so we must not "love our former life", nor the world, etc., but rather take hold of what is truly life (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%206%3A17-19&version=ESV][I Timothy 6:17-19]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2017%3A32-37&version=ESV][Luke 17:32-37]]* - Remember Lot's wife. Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life will keep it. I tell you, in that night there will be two in one bed. One will be taken and the other left. There will be two women grinding together. One will be taken and the other left. And they said to him, Where, Lord? He said to them, Where the corpse is, there the vultures will gather. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%206%3A14-18&version=ESV][II Corinthians 6:14-18]],7:1* - Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership has righteousness with lawlessness? Or what fellowship has light with darkness? What accord has Christ with Belial? Or what portion does a believer share with an unbeliever? What agreement has the temple of God with idols? For we are the temple of the living God; as God said, I will make my dwelling among them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. Therefore go out from their midst, and be separate from them, says the Lord, and touch no unclean thing; then I will welcome you, and I will be a father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty. Since we have these promises, beloved, *let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of body and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
   *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A13-16&version=ESV][I John 3:13-16]]* - Do not be surprised, brothers, that the world hates you. _We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers._ Whoever does not love abides in death. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him. By this we know love, that he laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%208%3A35-36&version=ESV][Proverbs 8:35-36]]* - For whoever finds me finds life and obtains favor from the LORD, but he who fails to find me injures himself; all who hate me love death. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A12&version=ESV][I John 5:12]]* - Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%206%3A10&version=ESV][Galatians 6:10]]* - So then, as we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone, and especially to those who are of the household of faith. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We may love our enemies (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A43-48&version=ESV][Matthew 5:43-48]]*) but that doesn't involve lying to one another. Love agrees with God. So speaking the truth in love, etc. this is good. But speaking what is false about God is not love at all.

If someone hates us personally then there is certainly nothing wrong with loving that person. If someone is a hater of Jesus Christ, it's still not wrong to "do good" to them. It's not wrong to loving them in the way that God loves them. But the fact is, God's love for evil people generally is not one that is controlling or forcing them to love God back. And the fact is, we need to love God to live. Someone who remains a God-hater is someone who perishes in their way, even though they were loved by God, because they don't end up loving God back, they perish.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%203%3A18-21&version=ESV][Philippians 3:18-21]]* - For many, of whom I have often told you and now tell you even with tears, walk as enemies of the cross of Christ. Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and they glory in their shame, with minds set on earthly things. But our citizenship is in heaven, and from it we await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ, who will transform our lowly body to be like his glorious body, by the power that enables him even to subject all things to himself. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God's way is best. We should learn what God wants of us:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%201%3A28-31&version=ESV][Proverbs 1:28-31]]* - Then they will call upon me, but I will not answer; they will seek me diligently but will not find me. Because they hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the LORD, would have none of my counsel and despised all my reproof, therefore they shall eat the fruit of their way, and have their fill of their own devices. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We are not seeking to [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_hHkeOEu2nw][please those who of the world]]. We are not seeking to
please God-haters. God-haters might congratulate someone on denying being a
disciple of Christ. God-haters might say you did the right thing by
ignoring your family in Christ's needs.

We have to love our family in Christ
especially, even called to lay down our own lives for our family in Christ, as
Jesus did for us. That's the type of love we *must* have for one another in Christ. In
Christ we are united in the truth and in agape love. True, selfless, agape love
which loves Jesus our family in Christ in the truth:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
   *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A13-16&version=ESV][I John 3:13-16]]* - Do not be surprised, brothers, that the world hates you. We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. Whoever does not love abides in death. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him. By this we know love, that he laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A15-21&version=ESV][I John 3:15-21]]* - Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him. By this we know love, that he laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers. But if anyone has the world's goods and sees his brother in need, yet closes his heart against him, how does God's love abide in him? Little children, let us not love in word or talk but in deed and in truth. By this we shall know that we are of the truth and reassure our heart before him; for whenever our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and he knows everything. Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence before God; (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

Q & A | RC Sproul # shorts {@ MarialynClapano }]] :: I believe this is correct teaching except I'm unsure if "regeneration" must always be instantaneous. I believe it was instantaneous for me. On [[https://web.archive.org/web/20220402091720/https://mullikine.github.io/posts/astral-projection/][2 April 2022]] I was regenerated and saw my regenerated spirit and called out to Jesus to save me because I didn't know what was happening. I was a "believer" before that but very much a slave to sin. Not long after that, about a month after, on [[https://web.archive.org/web/20220702053809/https://mullikine.github.io/posts/astral-projection-pt-3/][12 May 2022]], I experienced what felt like being "refilled" or topped up with more regeneration. This time I had a vision of healing people with compassion coming out of my soul.

    However, being born-again a person still has the flesh. If someone who lives by the spirit isn't walking by the spirit then the mind of the flesh is dominating. But we should be walking by the spirit which is the truth. So, for example, walking by the spirit a person does not call any man on earth their father, because Jesus Christ has said we have one Father who is in heaven. So if someone is regenerate, sometimes they still obey the flesh. But we have to stop doing that. So until sanctified it appears like a person has 2 personalities. One personality is actually the flesh (the man who died in baptism). The other is the one born of God, the one who loves their brother and agrees with God about the facts concerning Jesus such that He is Christ the Word of God made flesh, that He came from God, that He's the Son of God, that He's Yahweh the Son of God, that He died on a tree and rose from the dead on the 3rd day and ate a broiled fish.

    So a person who is born-again of the spirit on earth before their flesh is resurrected is a person with a spirit with a mind agreeing with God but in a "meat suit" flesh from the people who used to be their father and mother on earth who are now no longer their father and mother because God is the father of our spirits and God is their true Father and Holy Jerusalem is their true mother.

Sanctification *is* the salvation: We are sanctified while having faith in the Truth. This sanctification *is* the salvation. We are saved through sanctification and faith. This sanctification is sanctification of the heart and soul:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%202%3A13&version=ESV][II Thessalonians 2:13]]* - But we ought always to give thanks to God for you, brothers beloved by the Lord, because God chose you as the firstfruits to be *saved, through sanctification by the Spirit and belief in the truth*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

By faith in Jesus we are justified and saved through sanctification while holding faith in Jesus. This justification by faith is required for us to continue being sanctified. We're saved through sanctification:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%205%3A9-10&version=ESV][Romans 5:9-10]]* - Since, therefore, we have now been justified by his blood, much more shall we be saved by him from the wrath of God. For if while we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, now that we are reconciled, shall we be saved by his life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for? But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it. (KJV)
#+END_QUOTE

Which commandments must we keep? Jesus' commandments - Jesus' sayings and commandments which Father God commanded Him to speak. Also, it's worth learning from the Apostles who were with Jesus. Some commandments of Jesus are divulged and better understood from their writings.

Jesus kept Father God's commandments including the commandment of what to say and speak to us. Jesus' words and sayings and commandments which God gave Him to speak to us are what we should keep. His commandments are eternal life for us:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2012%3A44-50&version=ESV][John 12:44-50]]* - And Jesus cried out and said, Whoever believes in me, believes not in me but in him who sent me. If anyone hears my words and does not keep them, I do not judge him; for I did not come to judge the world but to save the world. The one who rejects me and does not receive my words has a judge; the word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day. For I have not spoken on my own authority, but the Father who sent me has himself given me a commandment—what to say and what to speak. And I know that his commandment is eternal life. So when Paul says "not having my own righteousness which [is] of [the] Law" it's talking about Mosaic law and what the Mosaic Law says about Paul. Rather, in keeping Christ's commandments, particularly the commandment to faith in Him, Paul receives the righteousness from God that depends on Paul's faith in Christ and is given independently of Paul's works, so long as Paul is actually and truly and presently trusting in Jesus Christ which would involve agreeing with Jesus Christ, and having confidence in Jesus and in His words:

+ [[https://biblehub.com/interlinear/philippians/3-9.htm][Philippians 3:9 (Interlinear)]] :: and be found in Him not having my own righteousness which [is] of [the] Law but that through faith from Christ the of God righteousness on the basis of - faith

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2013%3A5&version=ESV][II Corinthians 13:5]]* - Examine yourselves, to see whether you are in the faith. Test yourselves. Or do you not realize this about yourselves, that Jesus Christ is in you?—unless indeed you fail to meet the test! (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

See how here, Paul says that we should *test ourselves* to see if we are in the faith, and that "appearance-wise" it may "seem" to those people as though he (Paul) had "failed the test", but he (Paul) hopes that they will see that he has "not failed the test":

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2013%3A1-9&version=ESV][II Corinthians 13:1-9]]* - This is the third time I am coming to you. Every charge must be established by the evidence of two or three witnesses. I warned those who sinned before and all the others, and I warn them now while absent, as I did when present on my second visit, that if I come again I will not spare them— since you seek proof that Christ is speaking in me. He is not weak in dealing with you, but is powerful among you. For he was crucified in weakness, but lives by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but in dealing with you we will live with him by the power of God. Examine yourselves, to see whether you are in the faith. Test yourselves. Or do you not realize this about yourselves, that Jesus Christ is in you?—unless indeed you fail to meet the test! I hope you will find out that we have not failed the test. *But we pray to God that you may not do wrong—not that we may appear to have met the test, but that you may do what is right, though we may seem to have failed.* For *we cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the truth*. For we are glad when we are weak and you are strong. Your restoration is what we pray for. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

To be sure that we are in Christ, we should be abiding in Jesus' teachings and practicing Jesus' commandments and such a person ought to be walk in the same way Jesus walked:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A4-6&version=ESV][I John 2:4-6]]* - *Whoever says I know him but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, but whoever keeps his word, in him truly the love of God is perfected. By this we may be sure that we are in him*: whoever says he abides in him ought to walk in the same way in which he walked. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

If anyone agape loves Jesus Christ, they agape love the Word of God, agape-loves the Truth, he will keep the Word of God's words. God's word is Truth.
The sum of God's word is the Truth.
When the Bible mentions "keeping" Jesus' word (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A4-6&version=ESV][I John 2:4-6]]*), it's really stressing not only holding onto/being mindful of his word but doing His word:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A23&version=ESV][John 14:23]]* - Jesus answered him, If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Yes, we have faith, confess Jesus to others, and hold the faith, but we also progress into sanctification through faith in Jesus and obedience to Jesus, with Him as our first agape love:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2010%3A32-38&version=ESV][Matthew 10:32-38]]* - So everyone who acknowledges me before men, I also will acknowledge before my Father who is in heaven, but whoever denies me before men, I also will deny before my Father who is in heaven. Do not think that I have come to bring peace to the earth. I have not come to bring peace, but a sword. For I have come to set a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. And a person's enemies will be those of his own household. Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me, and whoever loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me. And whoever does not take his cross and follow me is not worthy of me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

By remaining faithful to Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2011%3A19-24&version=ESV][Acts 11:19-24]]*) and loving Jesus more than any created thing (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2010%3A37-38&version=ESV][Matthew 10:37-38]]*) which includes loving our family in Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A19-21&version=ESV][I John 4:19-21]]*) and in so doing resisting sin (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A3-4&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:3-4]]*), we are sanctified ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A18&version=ESV][Acts 26:18]]).

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A22&version=ESV][I Peter 1:22]]* - Having purified your souls by your obedience to the truth for a sincere brotherly love, love one another earnestly from a pure heart, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We have to love Jesus more than anything that is created:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2010%3A37-38&version=ESV][Matthew 10:37-38]]* - Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me, and whoever loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me. And whoever does not take his cross and follow me is not worthy of me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Carrying our cross is resisting sin while remaining faithful to Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A3-4&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:3-4]]* - Consider him who endured from sinners such hostility against himself, so that you may not grow weary or fainthearted. In your struggle against sin you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood. (ESV)

God has loved us. Jesus has loved us. Now we must love Him back, keeping His commandments, loving Him and one-another:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A6-19&version=ESV][I John 4:6-19]]* - We are from God. Whoever knows God listens to us; whoever is not from God does not listen to us. By this we know the Spirit of truth and the spirit of error. Beloved, let us love one another, for love is from God, and whoever loves has been born of God and knows God. Anyone who does not love does not know God, because God is love. In this the love of God was made manifest among us, that God sent his only Son into the world, so that we might live through him. In this is love, not that we have loved God but that *he loved us and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins*. Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another. No one has ever seen God; if we love one another, God abides in us and his love is perfected in us. By this we know that we abide in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit. And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent his Son to be the Savior of the world. Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him, and he in God. So we have come to know and to believe the love that God has for us. God is love, and whoever abides in love abides in God, and God abides in him. By this is love perfected with us, so that we may have confidence for the day of judgment, because as he is so also are we in this world. There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear. For fear has to do with punishment, and whoever fears has not been perfected in love. We love because *he first loved us*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%202%3A20&version=ESV][Galatians 2:20]]* - I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, *who loved me* and gave himself for me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I don't like how [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%202%3A20&version=ESV][Galatians 2:20]] has been interpreted with "that [[strongs:G3588][(G3588 tē)]] from the [[strongs:G3588][(G3588 tou)]] Son [[strongs:G5207][(G5207 Huiou)]]" as meaning that it's not our faith in Jesus that we need to have as if to place that requirement says a person is no longer relying on Jesus' finished work of the cross. And how people use this reasoning to refute needing to have faith in Jesus Christ to have eternal life, or even to continue having faith in Jesus Christ to continue having eternal life.

I actually believe that the phrase "that [[strongs:G3588][(G3588 tē)]] from the [[strongs:G3588][(G3588 tou)]] Son [[strongs:G5207][(G5207 Huiou)]]" is talking about the life from the Son of God that we can have through faith in Him, rather than as they put it, "His (Jesus') faith", rather than our faith in Him. And I think that using this verse in this way is evil because it contradicts [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A16&version=ESV][John 3:16]], and also because what is not done in faith is sin and we need to have faith in Jesus Christ in order to live.

Some people use the premise that because Jesus "did all the work" that we do not need to continue having faith to continue as a saved person - that if a person once believed they were totally sanctified and saved at that moment and that by adding your own [ongoing] faith as a requirement, it is now faith + works. But true faith in God having a love for God's word, and thus a love of God, is needed for eternal life.

[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%202%3A20&version=ESV][Galatians 2:20]] does not contradict [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A16&version=ESV][John 3:16]].

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%206%3A20-21&version=ESV][I Timothy 6:20-21]]* - O Timothy, guard the deposit entrusted to you. Avoid the irreverent babble and contradictions [[strongs:G477][(G477 antitheseis; opposing ideas)]] of what is falsely called knowledge, for by professing it some have swerved from the faith. Grace be with you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE
