#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A23-24&version=ESV][I John 3:23-24]]* - And this is his commandment, that we believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as he has commanded us. Whoever keeps his commandments abides in him, and he in them. And by this we know that he abides in us, by the Spirit whom he has given us. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Being justified by the law of faith in Christ (trusting and obeying Christ) rather than being justified by keeping the whole Mosaic law under the old covenant is, I believe, the correct way to understand what Paul is saying. Because I believe we need a law-abiding faith (true faith in Jesus Christ being a non-idolatrous, agape-loving of the truth faith, and loving neighbour as yourself faith):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A1-7&version=ESV][Galatians 5:1-7]]* - For freedom Christ has set us free; stand firm therefore, and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery. Look: I, Paul, say to you that if you accept circumcision, Christ will be of no advantage to you. I testify again to every man who accepts circumcision that he is obligated to keep the whole law. You are severed from Christ, you who would be justified by the law; you have fallen away from grace. For through the Spirit, by faith, we ourselves eagerly wait for the hope of righteousness. For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but only faith working through love. You were running well. Who hindered you from obeying the truth? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Obey the Truth means obey Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A6&version=ESV][John 14:6]]* - Jesus said to him, I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A20&version=ESV][I John 5:20]]* - And we know that *the Son of God has come and has given us understanding, so that we may know him who is true*; and we are in him who is true, in his Son Jesus Christ. He is the true God and eternal life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A3-6&version=ESV][I John 2:3-6]]* - And by this we know that we have come to know him, if we keep his commandments. Whoever says I know him but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, but *whoever keeps his word, in him truly the love of God is perfected*. By this we may be sure that we are in him: whoever says he abides in him ought to [[strongs:G3784][(G3784 opheilei; ought to, obligated to, has a duty to)]] walk in the same way in which he walked. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus wants us to love God and we certainly must love Jesus. The person who receives Jesus, as in accepts His words and His person, agrees with Him and does not reject Him; the person who trusts and treasures Jesus and His words, and doesn't distrust Jesus and His words, but keeps Jesus' words and doesn't disagree with them, that is the person who has the love of God in him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A42-43&version=ESV][John 5:42-43]]* - But I know that you do not have the love of God within you. I have come in my Father's name, and you do not receive me. If another comes in his own name, you will receive him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The old nature that we lug around until God delivers us completely from it is what rebels against God and is what doesn't want to do what God wants us to do:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A16-21&version=ESV][Romans 7:16-21]]* - Now if I do what I do not want, I agree with the law, that it is good. So now it is no longer I who do it, but sin that dwells within me. For I know that nothing good dwells in me, that is, in my flesh. For I have the desire to do what is right, but not the ability to carry it out. For I do not do the good I want, but the evil I do not want is what I keep on doing. Now if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but sin that dwells within me. So I find it to be a law that when I want to do right, evil lies close at hand. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The person who has been born-again but still carries around the old creation, the sin in the flesh, has an inner-man who is the new creation who loves, receives, accepts, treasures Jesus Christ and continues to love and abiding in God. But the sinful nature doesn't submit to God. We must be getting sanctified, so we must continue on abiding in God's commandments for us (I John 3:24), because in Him there is no condemnation (Romans 8:1):

+ [[https://biblehub.com/interlinear/john/3-16.htm][John 3:16 (Interlinear)]] :: Thus so (*[[https://biblehub.com/greek/3779.htm][Houtōs]]*) (in this way) did God love ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/25.htm][G25 agapaó]] - /value,treasure/) the world, that He gave His Only-Begotten [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g3439/kjv/tr/0-1/][(G3439. monogenēs - /unique,only begotten/)]] Son that [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g2443/kjv/tr/0-1/][(G2443 hina - /in order that/)]] everyone who is trusting/believing [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g4100/kjv/tr/0-1/][(G4100 pisteuo)]] in Him may not perish, but may have life everlasting

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A7-11&version=ESV][I John 3:7-11]]* - Little children, let no one deceive you. Whoever practices righteousness is righteous, as he is righteous. Whoever makes a practice of sinning is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. The reason the Son of God appeared was to destroy the works of the devil. No one born of God makes a practice of sinning, for God's seed abides in him, and he cannot keep on sinning because he has been born of God. By this it is evident who are the children of God, and who are the children of the devil: whoever does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is the one who does not love his brother. For this is the message that you have heard from the beginning, that we should love one another. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But the old creation in the sinful flesh rejects Jesus. We want to be sanctified, so as we trust and obey Jesus, continuing to receive Jesus, we are cleaned up to love Him with everything. In the grand scheme of things,

+ [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0cnEDUMfPXs&list=RD0cnEDUMfPXs&start_radio=1][youtube.com: I Asked The Lord by John Newton - Indelible Grace]] ::
    1. I asked the Lord that I might grow;
    In faith and love and every grace;
    Might more of His salvation know;
    And seek more earnestly His face;

    2. Twas He who taught me thus to pray;
    And He I trust has answered prayer;
    But it has been in such a way;
    As almost drove me to despair;

    3. I hoped that in some favored hour;
    At once He'd answer my request;
    And by His love's constraining power;
    Subdue my sins and give me rest;

    4. Instead of this He made me feel;
    The hidden evils of my heart;
    And let the angry powers of Hell;
    Assault my soul in every part;

    6. Lord why is this, I trembling cried;
    Wilt Thou pursue thy worm to death?;
    "Tis in this way" The Lord replied;
    "I answer prayer for grace and faith";

    7. "These inward trials I employ;
    From self and pride to set thee free;
    And break thy schemes of earthly joy;
    That thou mayest seek thy all in me,;
    That thou mayest seek thy all in me.";

It's in Jesus Christ, abiding in His commandments, that we walk in the light and have fellowship with our family in Christ, and are washed clean by the blood of Jesus Christ. So having fellowship with Jesus isn't contrived. To go to where Jesus is we keep His commandments. The "roadmap" for finding Jesus would be instructions like, 1) have faith in God, have faith also in Jesus Christ, 2) love one another as Jesus Christ commanded. So when the Scripture says in I John 2:19, "They went out from us, but they were not of us", we should not fear separation from a congregation if they are teaching against Jesus' teachings, fearing that we are not born-again if we leave the congregation or something like that. Rather, what we're supposed to do is simply, trust and obey God's commandments for us as Christians and we will come into fellowship as a result of trusting and obeying Jesus Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A6-7&version=ESV][I John 1:6-7]]* - If we say we have fellowship with him while we walk in darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth. But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A19&version=ESV][I John 2:19]]* - They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would have continued with us. But they went out, that it might become plain that they all are not of us. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%206%3A17&version=ESV][II Corinthians 6:17]]* - Therefore go out from their midst, and be separate from them, says the Lord, and touch no unclean thing; then I will welcome you, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%201%3A9-10&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 1:9-10]]* - For they themselves report concerning us the kind of reception we had among you, and how you turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God, and to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, Jesus who delivers us from [[strongs:G1537][(G1537 ek; from, out of, by, away from)]] the wrath to come. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

In sanctification (God's work of cleaning us up), God redeems every part of us, rescues us, purifies us from every lawless/evil deed, from every deed which is not done in faith or not done in love:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%204%3A18&version=ESV][II Timothy 4:18]]* - The Lord will rescue me from every evil deed and bring me safely into his heavenly kingdom. To him be the glory forever and ever. Amen. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]* - But whoever has doubts is condemned if he eats, because the eating is not from faith. For whatever does not proceed from faith is sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Loving God and desiring to do what God wants us to do and even trying to do what God wants us to do is commendable by God, despite the false teaching against that which says that's trusting in oneself. If a person is trusting Jesus that it's more blessed to give than to receive, and with confidence in God's word over the confidence of man's word, a person entrusts God with their earthly posessions, then that is making God their strength, and trusting in God. Endeavouring to keep God's commandments for us from the heart is trusting in God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2040%3A4&version=ESV][Psalms 40:4]]* - Blessed is the man who makes the LORD his trust, who does not turn to the proud, to those who go astray after a lie! (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Desire for God is important, and God's everlasting (Mark 13:31) Word is God (John 1:1). We must love God and must increasingly so. Agreeing and coming into agreement with Jesus Christ (who is God's eternal Word), and loving Jesus' Christ's words, loving God's Word, and retaining His word, is important (John 8:37). Jesus and His words are inseparable, and it's the one who loves Jesus' words who loves Jesus and the one who loves Jesus who loves His words. Doing what Jesus says, treasuring, loving, retaining Jesus' words, doing Jesus' commandments, keeping His commandments, agreeing with them, loving one-another in the way we are commanded just as Jesus Christ loved us, we are getting His word inside of us. God feeds us with Jesus Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A37&version=ESV][John 8:37]]* - I know that you are offspring of Abraham; yet you seek to kill me because my word finds no place in you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A37&version=ESV][John 8:37]]* - I know that you are offspring of Abraham; yet you seek to kill me because my word finds no place in you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A21&version=ESV][John 14:21]]* - Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves me. And he who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2013%3A31&version=ESV][Mark 13:31]]* - Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A1&version=ESV][John 1:1]]* - In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Seeking to please God with our actions is important. Seeking to honour God in resisting sin is important:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A6-8&version=ESV][Romans 2:6-8]]* - He will render to each one according to his works: to those who *by patience in well-doing seek for glory and honor and immortality*, he will give eternal life; but for those who are self-seeking and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, there will be wrath and fury. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A22-25&version=ESV][I Peter 1:22-25]]* - Having purified your souls by your obedience to the truth for a sincere brotherly love, love one another earnestly from a pure heart, since you have been born again, not of perishable seed but of imperishable, through the living and abiding word of God; for All flesh is like grass and all its glory like the flower of grass. The grass withers, and the flower falls, but the word of the Lord remains forever. And this word is the good news that was preached to you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We live in the Lord Jesus Christ while we stand fast in Him. How do we stand fast in Him? By continuing to agree with Him, continuing to have confidence in Him and His promises, even the conditional ones. And by not denying Jesus. We stand fast in Jesus Christ by continuing to receive and accept Jesus and keep His teachings and commandments and by not rejecting them:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%203%3A8&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 3:8]]* - For now we live, if you are standing fast in the Lord. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A5&version=ESV][James 2:5]]* - Listen, my beloved brothers, has not God chosen those who are poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom, which he has promised to those who love him? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%206%3A1-3&version=ESV][Ephesians 6:1-3]]* - Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right. Honor your father and mother (this is the first *commandment with a promise*), that it may go well with you and that you may live long in the land. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We are to obey our earthly masters and parents "in the Lord" (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%206%3A1&version=ESV][Ephesians 6:1]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%206%3A5-6&version=ESV][Ephesians 6:5-6]]*) and as we would Christ, abiding in His teachings, seeking to please Christ. Our first allegiance for obedience is to God, not to men. There may be times we we have to disobey our earthly master in order to obey God (like how Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego had to disobey Nebuchadnezzar: *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Daniel%203%3A10-12&version=ESV][Daniel 3:10-12]]*). God instructs us to obey our earthly masters in a way that serving the Lord Jesus Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%206%3A5-8&version=ESV][Ephesians 6:5-8]]*). If obeying an earthly master is done in a way that is not "doing the will of God", if serving them involves doing evil rather than doing good, or if what they want you to do is not something that you can do in faith and love for the Truth, then we should not obey. Otherwise, we should obey them (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%206%3A5-8&version=ESV][Ephesians 6:5-8]]*). Any type of obedience to God that is not originate from a love for the Truth is not genuine obedience (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2081%3A12-15&version=ESV][Psalms 81:12-15]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A2&version=ESV][I John 5:2]]*).

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%206%3A5-8&version=ESV][Ephesians 6:5-8]]* - Slaves, obey your earthly masters with fear and trembling, with a sincere heart, as you would Christ, not by the way of eye-service, as people-pleasers, but *as servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart, rendering service with a good will as to the Lord and not to man*, knowing that whatever good anyone does, this he will receive back from the Lord, whether he is a slave or free. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%205%3A29&version=ESV][Acts 5:29]]* - But Peter and the apostles answered, We must obey God rather than men. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It matters as Christians that we keep a clear conscience and that we are actually doing as Jesus has instructed. If an employer has told you to lie or steal or murder or commit adultery or do something that would be evil and be against serving Jesus Christ then the Christian is obligated to disobey the earthly master:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2024%3A14-16&version=ESV][Acts 24:14-16]]* - But this I confess to you, that according to the Way, which they call a sect, I worship the God of our fathers, believing everything laid down by the Law and written in the Prophets, having a hope in God, which these men themselves accept, that there will be a resurrection of both the just and the unjust. So I always take pains to have a clear conscience toward both God and man. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2013%3A18&version=ESV][Hebrews 13:18]]* - Pray for us, for we are sure that we have a clear conscience, desiring to act honorably in all things. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A17-18&version=ESV][Romans 6:17-18]]* - But thanks be to God, that you who were once slaves of sin have become obedient from the heart to the standard of teaching to which you were committed, and, having been set free from sin, have become slaves of righteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We can't "earn" salvation on the basis of the "works". But we can "receive what is due for our faith, for being 'doers' of the law of Christ", and what we receive for that is salvation ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A9-10&version=ESV][I Peter 1:9-10]]). So we can still "earn" salvation but it's not earned on the basis of "the works" which accompany the faith. Salvation is received by faith which resides in the heart. So with Abraham putting Isaac on the altar, he was still walking in faith, and he still did works (works of faith), and God tested his heart and saw that he was faithful to God first and agape loved God even more than his monogenes son ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%2022%3A11-12&version=ESV][Genesis 22:11-12]]). Abraham feared God. But God didn't need Isaac to be sacrificed for Abraham to be saved. God had already provided a ram ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%2022%3A13-14&version=ESV][Genesis 22:13-14]]). So while justification by works may happen, it doesn't happen on the basis of works (it doesn't happen without faith), and the type of faith Abraham had was with the fear of God (hatred of sin, wanting to do what pleases God, a repentant heart), with God as his first agape love:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2011%3A6&version=ESV][Romans 11:6]]* - But if it is by grace, it is no longer on the basis of works; otherwise grace would no longer be grace. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must have been changed in the heart so that we "do good" from the heart. That means from the heart having fear of God, faith in God, agape love for God, loving the truth:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%205%3A10&version=ESV][II Corinthians 5:10]]* - For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each one may receive what is due for what he has done in the body, whether good or evil. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So to say, "You can't 'earn' salvation," I think is a bit of a half-truth, or even blatantly incorrect because it makes it sound like God does not commend people for having faith in Him.
But God is both just and merciful:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A13-16&version=ESV][Romans 2:13-16]]* - For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but _the doers *[[strongs:G4163][(G4163 poiētai)]]* of the law who will be justified_. For when Gentiles, who do not have the law, by nature do what the law requires, they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the law. They show that the work of the law is written on their hearts, while their conscience also bears witness, and their conflicting thoughts accuse or even excuse them on that day when, according to my gospel, _God judges the secrets of men by Christ Jesus._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Jeremiah%2017%3A10&version=ESV][Jeremiah 17:10]]* - I the LORD search the heart and test the mind, to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his deeds. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So long as what we mean by it is "We can't boast before God that we earned salvation outside of His grace", then that is OK because even the coming to God and being in a position of being able to receive Jesus is grace. God wants us to seek Him out.

I don't like pitting our obedience up against our faith. It's not actually
correct. Like, we are saved by obedience to Jesus Christ. Whilst it's all grace
and a gift (noone can come to Jesus unless the Father draws them), there are
still things we can certainly do to receive Jesus Christ, such as draw near to
God. Draw near to God and He will draw near to you. Our obedience to Jesus can
be walking into the gift. Justice and mercy are not mutually exclusive (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2018%3A1-14&version=ESV][Luke 18:1-14]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%201%3A5-8&version=ESV][II Thessalonians 1:5-8]]*). Jesus
said blessed are the merciful for they will receive mercy (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A7&version=ESV][Matthew 5:7]]*). So if Jesus Christ
said it, it's still true and it's still through Jesus Christ. When we confess
our sin, He is faithful and just to forgive us of our sin. That's justice and
mercy at the same time. Yes we all need God's mercy, but we also need His
justice. We don't commend ourselves for our faith tho. That's not our duty as
human beings. Our duty is to fear God and keep His commandments. We can't
please God without the spirit of Christ. It's all grace. It's good to be
grateful. It's in the truth that we should be grateful. But at the same time
it's also in the truth that we must love our family in Christ. And it's in the
truth that we should believe God send His Son into the world to die for our
sins and rise from the dead for our justification. It's in the truth that we
must forgive our family in Christ. It's in the truth that the Holy Spirit goes
to those who obey God. All of that is in the truth.

It's in the truth also that we must repent of wickedness:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2012%3A21&version=ESV][II Corinthians 12:21]]* - I fear that when I come again my God may humble me before you, and I may have to mourn over many of those who sinned earlier and have not *repented of the impurity, sexual immorality, and sensuality* that they have practiced. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2013%3A1-9&version=ESV][II Corinthians 13:1-9]]* - This is the third time I am coming to you. Every charge must be established by the evidence of two or three witnesses. I warned those who sinned before and all the others, and I warn them now while absent, as I did when present on my second visit, that if I come again I will not spare them— since you seek proof that Christ is speaking in me. He is not weak in dealing with you, but is powerful among you. For he was crucified in weakness, but lives by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but in dealing with you we will live with him by the power of God. Examine yourselves, to see whether you are in the faith. Test yourselves. Or do you not realize this about yourselves, that Jesus Christ is in you?—unless indeed you fail to meet the test! I hope you will find out that we have not failed the test. But we pray to God that you may not do wrong—not that we may appear to have met the test, but that you may do what is right, though we may seem to have failed. For *we cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the truth*. For we are glad when we are weak and you are strong. Your restoration is what we pray for. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

In my view it's all obedience to the truth and essentially means accepting the gospel and letting it work in your life through faith/obedience to Jesus. The gospel being inclusive of all the sayings which Jesus spoke during His ministry recorded in the books of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John and the deeds which He carried out, including making atonement for sin:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%204%3A18-19&version=ESV][Luke 4:18-19]]* - The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim liberty to the captives and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty those who are oppressed, to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%204%3A42-43&version=ESV][Luke 4:42-43]]* - And when it was day, he departed and went into a desolate place. And the people sought him and came to him, and would have kept him from leaving them, but he said to them, I must preach *the good news of the kingdom of God* to the other towns as well; for I was sent for this purpose. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2012%3A44-50&version=ESV][John 12:44-50]]* - And Jesus cried out and said, Whoever believes in me, believes not in me but in him who sent me. And whoever sees me sees him who sent me. I have come into the world as light, so that whoever believes in me may not remain in darkness. If anyone hears my words and does not keep them, I do not judge him; for I did not come to judge the world but to save the world. The one who rejects me and does not receive my words has a judge; the word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day. For I have not spoken on my own authority, but the Father who sent me has himself given me a commandment—what to say and what to speak. And I know that his commandment is eternal life. What I say, therefore, I say as the Father has told me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%208%3A15&version=ESV][Luke 8:15]]* - As for that in the good soil, they are those who, hearing the word, hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit with patience. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%208%3A21&version=ESV][Luke 8:21]]* - But he answered them, My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

When we are living in faith in God for His promises we are living in an obedient way. Belief and obedience are not separate things in my opinion, but we must have both obedience and belief in the heart - we must agree that gospel of Jesus is Truth and live in that reality holding faith and being obedient to Jesus and God will make it happen. So living by faith walks according to the will of God with hope in His promises, trust in Jesus and faithfulness-obedience to His commandments, walking in the ways of God seeking God's commendation, trusting in God, and living as though He exists:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A22&version=ESV][I Peter 1:22]]* - Having purified your souls by your obedience to the truth for a sincere brotherly love, love one another earnestly from a pure heart, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2015%3A9&version=ESV][Acts 15:9]]* - and he made no distinction between us and them, having cleansed their hearts by faith. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Following Jesus means laying our life down for Jesus and not denying Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2013%3A36-38&version=ESV][John 13:36-38]]* - Simon Peter said to him, Lord, where are you going? Jesus answered him, Where I am going you cannot follow me now, but you will follow afterward. Peter said to him, Lord, why can I not follow you now? I will lay down my life for you. Jesus answered, Will you lay down your life for me? Truly, truly, I say to you, the rooster will not crow till you have denied me three times. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

And it means loving Jesus which involves obeying Jesus including His commandment to trust Him and His other commandments:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A1-7&version=ESV][John 14:1-7]]* - Let not your hearts be troubled. Believe in God; believe also in me. In my Father's house are many rooms. If it were not so, would I have told you that I go to prepare a place for you? And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and will take you to myself, that where I am you may be also. And you know the way to where I am going. Thomas said to him, Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way? Jesus said to him, I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me. If you had known me, you would have known my Father also. From now on you do know him and have seen him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I think John Piper meant to say cleansed your souls here in the first line:

#+END_QUOTE

While I believe that someone who does not know about, say, the doctrine of the Trinity, can be saved by Jesus, I also believe that it's important to not reject the teaching of the Lord Jesus Christ. After all we are sanctified by faith in Jesus ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A18&version=ESV][Acts 26:18]]), and Jesus' words will judge those who reject them on the last day ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2012%3A48&version=ESV][John 12:48]]). Jesus is the judge of this, though. I myself don't claim to know everything. There's teaching I don't fully understand, such as the nature of the 7 spirits of God ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%205%3A6&version=ESV][Revelation of John 5:6]]), and when it comes to the doctrine of the blessed trinity, though I don't claim to be an expert, but I do believe that God is One and God is Father, Son and Holy Spirit. I have confidence this is correct, but not confidence enough in my own understanding to commend myself or to condemn, for example, the Jehovah's Witnesses. While I do absolutely believe in the effectiveness of partaking in the Lord's supper as a means of grace, I believe it has to be done in a worthy manner which means loving Jesus Christ more than any created thing, and also carrying our cross which involves remaining faithful to Jesus.
I do not believe a good case can be made for the only way to have participated is *exclusive* to having imbibed on the Lord's supper (as in the sacrament).

*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A23&version=ESV][I John 3:23]]* says that God's commandment is to have faith in the name of His Son Jesus Christ and love one another just as He has commanded us. I believe this commandment to have faith in Jesus and love one another as commanded is what we should be doing as we do other things including taking the Lord's supper.
Because what is not done in faith is sin and what is not done in love is also sin.
If a person trusting in Jesus Christ blesses a cup and bread in the tradition of the Lord's supper in rememberance of Jesus, and did in such a way that is loving of God and of one another, then that would be feeding on the Lord Jesus Christ because it would be done in faith in Jesus Christ God's Son and in love for one-another and we're meant to do this with one another.
But a person may have faith in Jesus Christ and love one-another as commanded by trusting Jesus Christ not just in obedience to the instruction to "eat and drink of the Lord's supper in rememberance of Jesus", but as well as in other teachings and instructions of Jesus Christ generally, such as "getting baptised in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit", or perhaps in sharing the gospel obeying Jesus' instruction of the Great Commission, for example.
And this is because, I believe, the Life is in Jesus Christ, and Jesus Christ is the Word of God become flesh and Jesus' words are spirit and life and the legacy of Jesus' ministry in the flesh is what we must partake of.
In other words, I do not think that partaking in the blood and body of the Lord Jesus Christ is limited to partaking specifically of the ritual sacrament known as the eucharist, but it is more generally to eat and drink of Jesus' legacy including the teachings about Jesus and the words of Jesus, doing the commandments of Jesus.

Yesterday, a brother of mine from a pentecostal church I have attended gave me a cross keyring (it's like a rosary without the beads) with the following verse on it:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%206%3A35&version=ESV][John 6:35]]* - Jesus said to them, I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me shall not hunger, and whoever believes in me shall never thirst. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I truly believe that we receive the body and blood of Jesus through faith. There is a section in this document talking more about my beliefs regarding communion.

While I do absolutely believe in the effectiveness of partaking in the Lord's supper as a means of grace, I believe it has to be done in a worthy manner which means loving Jesus Christ more than any created thing, and also carrying our cross which involves remaining faithful to Jesus.
I do not believe a good case can be made for the only way to have participated is *exclusive* to having imbibed on the Lord's supper (as in the sacrament).

*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A23&version=ESV][I John 3:23]]* says that God's commandment is to have faith in the name of His Son Jesus Christ and love one anotqoher just as He has commanded us. I believe this commandment to have faith in Jesus and love one another as commanded is what we should be doing as we do other things including taking the Lord's supper.
Because what is not done in faith is sin and what is not done in love is also sin.
If a person trusting in Jesus Christ blesses a cup and bread in the tradition of the Lord's supper in rememberance of Jesus, and did in such a way that is loving of God and of one another, then that would be feeding on the Lord Jesus Christ because it would be done in faith in Jesus Christ God's Son and in love for one-another and we're meant to do this with one another.
But a person may have faith in Jesus Christ and love one-another as commanded by trusting Jesus Christ not just in obedience to the instruction to "eat and drink of the Lord's supper in rememberance of Jesus", but as well as in other teachings and instructions of Jesus Christ generally, such as "getting baptised in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit", or perhaps in sharing the gospel obeying Jesus' instruction of the Great Commission, for example.
And this is because, I believe, the Life is in Jesus Christ, and Jesus Christ is the Word of God become flesh and Jesus' words are spirit and life and the legacy of Jesus' ministry in the flesh is what we must partake of.
In other words, I do not think that partaking in the blood and body of the Lord Jesus Christ is limited to partaking specifically of the ritual sacrament known as the eucharist, but it is more generally to eat and drink of Jesus' legacy including the teachings about Jesus and the words of Jesus, doing the commandments of Jesus.

+ [[https://www.earlychristianwritings.com/text/diognetus-roberts.html][Mathetes to Diognetus]] :: They dwell in their own countries, but simply as sojourners. As citizens, they share in all things with others, and yet endure all things as if foreigners. Every foreign land is to them as their native country, and every land of their birth as a land of strangers. They marry, as do all [others]; they beget children; but they do not destroy their offspring. They have a common table, but not a common bed. They are in the flesh, but they do not live after the flesh. They pass their days on earth, but they are citizens of heaven. They obey the prescribed laws, and at the same time surpass the laws by their lives. They love all men, and are persecuted by all. They are unknown and condemned; they are put to death, and restored to life. They are poor, yet make many rich; they are in lack of all things, and yet abound in all; they are dishonoured, and yet in their very dishonour are glorified. They are evil spoken of, and yet are justified; they are reviled, and bless; they are insulted, and repay the insult with honour; they do good, yet are punished as evil-doers. When punished, they rejoice as if quickened into life; they are assailed by the Jews as foreigners, and are persecuted by the Greeks; yet those who hate them are unable to assign any reason for their hatred. To sum up all in one word--what the soul is in the body, that are Christians in the world. The soul is dispersed through all the members of the body, and Christians are scattered through all the cities of the world. The soul dwells in the body, yet is not of the body; and Christians dwell in the world, yet are not of the world. The invisible soul is guarded by the visible body, and Christians are known indeed to be in the world, but their godliness remains invisible.

When talking about "The Law" the Apostles are usually referring to the Mosaic Law.
And when talking about "being under the law", Paul I believe is saying that such people who are "under the Law" are trying to be justified by the Old Covenant Law, rather than "coming to Jesus":

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A4-7&version=ESV][Galatians 5:4-7]]* - You are severed from Christ, you who would be justified by the law; you have fallen away from grace. For through the Spirit, by faith, we ourselves eagerly wait for the hope of righteousness. For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but only faith working through love. You were running well. Who hindered you from obeying the truth? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I believe that the people Jesus is talking to here are/were "under the Law" (the Mosaic Law):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A39-47&version=ESV][John 5:39-47]]* - You search the Scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that bear witness about me, yet you refuse to come to me that you may have life. I do not receive glory from people. But I know that you do not have the love of God within you. I have come in my Father's name, and you do not receive me. If another comes in his own name, you will receive him. How can you believe, when you receive glory from one another and do not seek the glory that comes from the only God? Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father. There is one who accuses you: Moses, on whom you have set your hope. If you believed Moses, you would believe me; for he wrote of me. But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A23&version=ESV][Galatians 3:23]]* - Now before faith came, we were held captive under the law, imprisoned until the coming faith would be revealed. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So how to come to Jesus (*John 5:39-47*)? Take His yoke. Abide in His commandments. Trust and obey Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2011%3A28-30&version=ESV][Matthew 11:28-30]]* - Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

All Jesus' commandments are grace and truth:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A17&version=ESV][John 1:17]]* - For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2042%3A1-4&version=ESV][Isaiah 42:1-4]]* - Behold my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my Spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations. He will not cry aloud or lift up his voice, or make it heard in the street; a bruised reed he will not break, and a faintly burning wick he will not quench; he will faithfully bring forth justice. He will not grow faint or be discouraged till he has established justice in the earth; and the coastlands wait for his law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2012%3A15-21&version=ESV][Matthew 12:15-21]]* - Jesus, aware of this, withdrew from there. And many followed him, and he healed them all and ordered them not to make him known. This was to fulfill what was spoken by the prophet Isaiah: Behold, my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved with whom my soul is well pleased. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will proclaim justice to the Gentiles. He will not quarrel or cry aloud, nor will anyone hear his voice in the streets; a bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not quench, until he brings justice to victory; and in his name the Gentiles will hope. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2015%3A12-13&version=ESV][Romans 15:12-13]]* - And again Isaiah says, , The root of Jesse will come, even he who arises to rule the Gentiles; in him will the Gentiles hope. May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that by the power of the Holy Spirit you may abound in hope. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2011%3A10&version=ESV][Isaiah 11:10]]* - In that day the root of Jesse, who shall stand as a signal for the peoples—of him shall the nations inquire, and his resting place shall be glorious. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus has taught us *how* to love one another, through commandments:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A13-17&version=ESV][John 15:13-17]]* - Greater love has no one than this, that someone lays down his life for his friends. You are my friends if you do what I command you. No longer do I call you servants, for the servant does not know what his master is doing; but I have called you friends, for all that I have heard from my Father I have made known to you. You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you that you should go and bear fruit and that your fruit should abide, so that whatever you ask the Father in my name, he may give it to you. *These things I command you, so that you will love one another*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

And we *must* love our family in Christ. This commandment to love our brothers in Christ is a commandment to love our whole family in Christ, male or female:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A21&version=ESV][I John 4:21]]* - And this commandment we have from him: whoever loves God *must* also love his brother. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I think saying "neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female" is Paul exhorting people to see that those who have been baptized into Christ are members of Christ, and have an identity in Christ which transcends the worldly categories, similar to saying that a slave has an identity in Christ and so earthly masters should be wary of that fact, being aware that a person in Christ Jesus has an identity that totally transcends the worldly divisions between people:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A25-29&version=ESV][Galatians 3:25-29]]* - But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian, for in Christ Jesus you are all sons of God, through faith. For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is _neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is neither male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus._ And if you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to promise. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We become bondservants (slaves) of God, servants of Christ, and we are also brothers in Christ. We don't give up being servants of Christ. Rather we serve Christ and now see each other as family in Christ. In this passage in Philemon, Paul talks about "family of the flesh" as contrasted with "family in the Lord". Paul encourages Philemon to receive Onesimus as more than a slave (of the flesh, like the person's worldy "employment") but as a brother in Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philemon%201%3A15-16&version=ESV][Philemon 1:15-16]]* - For this perhaps is why he was parted from you for a while, that you might have him back forever, no longer as a slave but more than a slave, as a beloved brother—especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Servants of Christ have the fear of God, seeking to please God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A17-18&version=ESV][Romans 14:17-18]]* - For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking but of righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit. Whoever thus serves Christ is acceptable to God and approved by men. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%201%3A10&version=ESV][Galatians 1:10]]* - For am I now seeking the approval of man, or of God? Or am I trying to please man? If I were still trying to please man, I would not be a servant of Christ. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The Apostle John says to be able to know that we are loving the children of God, we must be keeping His commandments. If people are offended at us while we are sincerely from the heart and in reality abiding by Jesus Christ's commandments, we should not be deterred from continuing to try to abide by Jesus Christ's commandments. We may, sometimes need to be corrected into better obedience, but it's not the commandments which are at fault:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A2&version=ESV][I John 5:2]]* - By this we know that we love the children of God, when _we love God *and* obey his commandments._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Even the Gentiles wait for *His* (Jesus') Law (Torah):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2042%3A1-4&version=ESV][Isaiah 42:1-4]]* - Behold *my servant*, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my Spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations. He will not cry aloud or lift up his voice, or make it heard in the street; a bruised reed he will not break, and a faintly burning wick he will not quench; he will faithfully bring forth justice. He will not grow faint or be discouraged till he has established justice in the earth; and the coastlands wait for *his law*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2012%3A15-21&version=ESV][Matthew 12:15-21]]* - Jesus, aware of this, withdrew from there. And many followed him, and he healed them all and ordered them not to make him known. This was to fulfill what was spoken by the prophet Isaiah: Behold, my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved with whom my soul is well pleased. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will proclaim justice to the Gentiles. He will not quarrel or cry aloud, nor will anyone hear his voice in the streets; a bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not quench, until he brings justice to victory; and in his name the Gentiles will hope. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2015%3A12-13&version=ESV][Romans 15:12-13]]* - And again Isaiah says, , The root of Jesse will come, even he who arises to rule the Gentiles; in him will the Gentiles hope. May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that by the power of the Holy Spirit you may abound in hope. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2011%3A10&version=ESV][Isaiah 11:10]]* - In that day the root of Jesse, who shall stand as a signal for the peoples—of him shall the nations inquire, and his resting place shall be glorious. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must have faith in Jesus to be justified by faith. God justifies the person who trusts in Jesus and since we trust Jesus we should be doers of Christ's law (which is not outside the law of God, so we are doers of the law), and God justifies the person with the blood of Jesus. If we're trusting in Jesus then we're trusting in God who justifies the ungodly. We're not trusting in God to justify our ungodliness, but to justify us as we keep our faith in Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A13-16&version=ESV][Romans 2:13-16]]* - For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but _the doers *[[strongs:G4163][(G4163 poiētai)]]* of the law who will be justified_. For when Gentiles, who do not have the law, by nature do what the law requires, they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the law. They show that the work of the law is written on their hearts, while their conscience also bears witness, and their conflicting thoughts accuse or even excuse them on that day when, according to my gospel, _God judges the secrets of men by Christ Jesus._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Jeremiah%2017%3A10&version=ESV][Jeremiah 17:10]]* - I the LORD search the heart and test the mind, to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his deeds. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God's strength does not guarantee that we will not suffer as a result of following Jesus. But God gives us the power at the time we need it to endure the suffering:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A1-3&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:1-3]]* - Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight, and sin which clings so closely, and let us run with endurance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is seated at the right hand of the throne of God. Consider him who endured from sinners such hostility against himself, *so that you may not grow weary or fainthearted.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Jeremiah%2017%3A5&version=ESV][Jeremiah 17:5]]* - Thus says the LORD: Cursed is the man who trusts in man and makes flesh his strength, whose heart turns away from the LORD. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ Quote from John Piper :: God took the sting out of death and He took the futility out of labour, so that He says, "You will mount up like wings like eagles. You will run and not grow weary. You will walk and not faint."

AMEN to that!

I don't think that it's always the case though that we will not be "excruciatingly weary", particularly if there is a big calling on the person:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2012%3A42-49&version=ESV][Luke 12:42-49]]* - And the Lord said, Who then is the *faithful and wise manager*, whom his master will set over his household, *to give them their portion of food at the proper time?* Blessed is that servant whom his master will find so doing when he comes. Truly, I say to you, he will set him over all his possessions. But if that servant says to himself, My master is delayed in coming, and begins to beat the male and female servants, and to eat and drink and get drunk, the master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in pieces and put him with the unfaithful. And that servant who knew his master's will but did not get ready or act according to his will, will receive a severe beating. But the one who did not know, and did what deserved a beating, will receive a light beating. *Everyone to whom much was given, of him much will be required, and from him to whom they entrusted much, they will demand the more.* I came to cast fire on the earth, and would that it were already kindled! (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%201%3A8&version=ESV][II Corinthians 1:8]]* - For we do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, of the affliction we experienced in Asia. For we were so utterly burdened beyond our strength that we despaired of life itself. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%204%3A8-12&version=ESV][II Corinthians 4:8-12]]* - We are afflicted in every way, but not crushed; perplexed, but not driven to despair; persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed; always carrying in the body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be manifested in our bodies. For we who live are always being given over to death for Jesus' sake, so that the life of Jesus also may be manifested in our mortal flesh. So death is at work in us, but life in you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I think we certainly can get very weary. But waiting on the LORD our strength is renewed:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Daniel%207%3A25&version=ESV][Daniel 7:25]]* - He shall speak words against the Most High, and shall wear out the saints of the Most High, and shall think to *change the times and the law;* and they shall be given into his hand for a time, times, and half a time. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2040%3A31&version=ESV][Isaiah 40:31]]* - but they who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles; they shall run and not be weary; they shall walk and not faint. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://www.youtube.com/post/UgkxDSl5rHxo2G6-wzX1iiaja402AgfjMKIr][youtube.com: Post from Hangin Out With Stan]] :: Commented, 'Satan also "over-encumbers you" too, I think to try to get a person to no longer walk in the truth. We're supposed to walk by faith and love. So we wouldn't "rest" from love ever. Like Jesus also loved till the end. We might rest from our "works", sure, but never from love, and never from faith. Satan tries to wear out the saints of the Most High and steal our rest and tries to pressure us into breaking faith with God. But God provides strength to get through difficult stuff.'

The followers of Paul the Apostle _live by_ (walk by) faith; those are the righteous ones. It's a lifestyle:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A11&version=ESV][Galatians 3:11]]* - Now it is evident that no one is justified before God by the law, for The righteous shall *live by* faith. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The crown of life is gifted to those who are obedient, and have been tested. I think this verse can also be taken in the literal sense:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%202%3A10&version=ESV][Revelation 2:10]]* - Do not fear what you are about to suffer. Behold, the devil is about to throw *some of you* into prison, that you may be *tested,* and for ten days you will have tribulation. Be faithful unto death, and I will give you the _crown of life._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus will manifest to those who keep His commandments:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A21&version=ESV][John 14:21]]* - Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves me. And he who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A2-4&version=ESV][I John 3:2-4]]* - Beloved, we are God's children now, and what we will be has not yet appeared; but we know that _when he appears we shall be like him, because we shall see him as he is._ And *everyone who thus hopes in him purifies himself as he is pure*. Everyone who makes a practice of sinning also practices lawlessness; sin is lawlessness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A22-23&version=ESV][John 14:22-23]]* - Judas (not Iscariot) said to him, Lord, how is it that you will manifest yourself to us, and not to the world? Jesus answered him, If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and _my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him._
#+END_QUOTE

Even the Apostle Paul explains that our freedom is for serving one another:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A13&version=ESV][Galatians 5:13]]* - For you were called to freedom, brothers. Only do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but *through love serve one another.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%202%3A15-25&version=ESV][I Peter 2:15-25]]* - For this is the will of God, that by doing good you should put to silence the ignorance of foolish people. *Live as people who are free, not using your freedom as a cover-up for evil, but living as servants of God.* _Honor everyone. *Love the brotherhood.* Fear God. Honor the emperor._ Servants, be subject to your masters with all respect, not only to the good and gentle but also to the unjust. For this is a gracious thing, when, mindful of God, one endures sorrows while suffering unjustly. For *what _credit_ is it if, when you sin and are beaten for it, you endure? But if when you do good and suffer for it you endure, this is a gracious thing in the sight of God*. For to this you have been called, because *Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you might follow in his steps*. He committed no sin, neither was deceit found in his mouth. When he was reviled, he did not revile in return; when he suffered, he did not threaten, but continued entrusting himself to him who judges justly. *He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we might die to sin and live to righteousness*. By his wounds you have been healed. For you were straying like sheep, but have now returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Our freedom is so that we might live to God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%202%3A19&version=ESV][Galatians 2:19]]* - For through the law I died to the law, so that I might live to God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%20119%3A45&version=ESV][Psalms 119:45]]* - And I will walk at liberty, For I seek Your precepts. (NASB)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A13&version=ESV][Galatians 5:13]]* - For you were called to freedom [[strongs:G1657][(G1657 eleutheria; freedom)]], brothers. Only do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God is our life. We must love, *obey*, and hold fast to Him. Faith is not without obedience, but we are to obey Jesus Christ and to believe in Jesus is to have begun to obey Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy%2030%3A20&version=ESV][Deuteronomy 30:20]]* - *loving the LORD your God, obeying his voice and holding fast to him, for _he is your life_* and length of days, that you may dwell in the land that the LORD swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God is our life because Christ is our life. Our life is hidden with Christ in God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%203%3A1-4&version=ESV][Colossians 3:1-4]]* - If then you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God. Set your minds on things that are above, not on things that are on earth. For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God. When Christ who is your life appears, then you also will appear with him in glory. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Obey God, obey Jesus. This doesn't say that obeying the 10 commandments is not important. To love God and your neighbour in truth from the heart is the way to do this. But *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2010%3A17-21&version=ESV][Mark 10:17-21]]* does say that following Jesus (treasuring Jesus, His words and putting them into practice) is vitally important:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2010%3A17-21&version=ESV][Mark 10:17-21]]* - And as he was setting out on his journey, a man ran up and knelt before him and asked him, Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life? And Jesus said to him, Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone. You know the commandments: Do not murder, Do not commit adultery, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Do not defraud, Honor your father and mother. And he said to him, Teacher, all these I have kept from my youth. And Jesus, looking at him, loved him, and said to him, *You lack one thing: go, sell all that you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.*
#+END_QUOTE

To get to know Jesus, we *must obey* His commandments:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A3-4&version=ESV][I John 2:3-4]]* - And _by this we know that we have come to_ *know him*, _if we_ *keep his commandments*. Whoever says I know him but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Christ Jesus has set us free to serve God, living for Him. Obeying Christ Jesus, we are found in Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2013%3A34&version=ESV][John 13:34]]* - A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another: just as I have loved you, you also are to love one another. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A22&version=ESV][Matthew 5:22]],28,32,34-37,39,44-45,27-28,30-31,35,40* - But I say to you that everyone who is angry with his brother will be liable to judgment; whoever insults his brother will be liable to the council; and whoever says, You fool! will be liable to the hell of fire. But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart. But I say to you that everyone who divorces his wife, except on the ground of sexual immorality, makes her commit adultery. And whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery. But I say to you, Do not take an oath at all, either by heaven, for it is the throne of God, or by the earth, for it is his footstool, or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King. And do not take an oath by your head, for you cannot make one hair white or black. Let what you say be simply Yes or No; anything more than this comes from evil. But I say to you, Do not resist the one who is evil. But if anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also. But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the just and on the unjust. You have heard that it was said, You shall not commit adultery. But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart. And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. For it is better that you lose one of your members than that your whole body go into hell. It was also said, Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce. or by the earth, for it is his footstool, or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King. And if anyone would sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

In Christ Jesus seek to follow the pattern of His life to get to know Him, and He gave us commandments to follow to do that. Faith in Christ Jesus is not just a belief in the head but faith is trusting Him, and trusting in Him with all our heart, soul, mind and strength. Both our belief in Him and obedience to Him flow from our trust in Him. Anyone who claims to have come to know Jesus but does not do what Jesus says is a liar and they are not in the truth:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A3-6&version=ESV][I John 2:3-6]]* - And by this we know that we have come to know him, if we keep his commandments. Whoever says I know him but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, but whoever keeps his word, in him truly the love of God is perfected. By this we may be sure that we are in him: whoever says he abides in him ought to walk in the same way in which he walked. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I went up because of a revelation and set before them (though privately before those who seemed influential) the gospel that I proclaim among the Gentiles, in order to make sure I was not running or had not run in vain. But even Titus, who was with me, was not forced to be circumcised, though he was a Greek. Yet because of false brothers secretly brought in—who slipped in to spy out our *freedom that we have in Christ Jesus*, so that they might bring us into slavery— to them we did not yield in submission even for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel might be preserved for you. (ESV)

Honor the emperor._ Servants, be subject to your masters with all respect, not only to the good and gentle but also to the unjust. When he was reviled, he did not revile in return; when he suffered, he did not threaten, but continued entrusting himself to him who judges justly. *He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we might die to sin and live to righteousness*. By his wounds you have been healed. For you were straying like sheep, but have now returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls. (ESV)

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%202%3A5-11&version=ESV][II Corinthians 2:5-11]]* - Now if anyone has caused pain, he has caused it not to me, but in some measure—not to put it too severely—to all of you. Even if "[[https://biblehub.com/greek/544.htm][apeitheó]]" is better translated to "not be pursuaded", trusting in Jesus Christ is still obedience. Unless you believe that trusting in Jesus is disobedience, which it is not. It's obedient to trust in Jesus because He commanded it in [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A1&version=ESV][John 14:1]]. They're not separate things. A heart that is pursuaded to trust Jesus is an obedient heart:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A36&version=ESV][John 3:36]]* - Whoever believes ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/pisteuo_n_4100.htm][G4100 pisteuōn]] - /is believing (verb)/) in the Son *has* eternal life; whoever does not obey ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/544.htm][544. apeitheó]]) the Son shall not *see* life, but _the wrath of God remains on him._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://biblehub.com/greek/pisteuo_n_4100.htm][G4100 πιστεύων (pisteuōn)]]: This is the present participle form of the verb "πιστεύω" ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/4100.htm][G4100 pisteuō]]), meaning "to trust" / "to believe" / "to have faith." In the participle form, it functions as a verbal adjective and can be translated as "believing" / "trusting."

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A10-13&version=ESV][I John 5:10-13]]* - Whoever believes ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/pisteuo_n_4100.htm][G4100 pisteuōn]] - /is believing (verb)/) in the Son of God has the testimony in himself. Whoever does not believe God has made him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony that God has borne concerning his Son. And this is the testimony, that God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life. I write these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God that you may know that you have eternal life. (ESV)

But we must not believe in vain. We must continue trusting Jesus. We must believe and hold fast to the gospel:

(ESV)

+ [[https://biblehub.com/greek/2722.htm][2722. katechó]] :: Usage: (a) I hold fast, bind, arrest, (b) I take possession of, lay hold of, (c) I hold back, detain, restrain, (d) I hold a ship, keep its head.

By faith we must continue obeying God, forsaking sin, that we may share in Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%203%3A12-19&version=ESV][Hebrews 3:12-19]]* - Take care, brothers, lest there be in any of you an *evil, unbelieving heart, leading you to fall away from the living God*. But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called today, that _none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin_. For *we share in Christ, if indeed we hold our original confidence firm to the end*. As it is said, Today, _if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion_. For who were those who heard and yet rebelled? Was it not all those who left Egypt led by Moses? And with whom was he provoked for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness? And *to whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest, but to those who were disobedient? So we see that they were unable to enter because of unbelief*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2028%3A13&version=ESV][Proverbs 28:13]]* - Whoever conceals his transgressions will not prosper, but he who *confesses and forsakes* them will obtain mercy. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must not deny the faith. The type of faith we must have is a love for the
truth. Not a demonic faith.

It's unrighteous to take away from those depending on
you what they need to survive on. You can give /yourself/ away for others completely (like how the widow gave all she had), but
not give /other/ people away completely for others. Sacrificing one's own children (especially against their will) to save others isn't right.
If I gave away my family's only provisions that they needed to "survive" on (i.e. they needed it) to someone
else who didn't "need" it, but wanted it or asked for it, then that is a faithless thing to do.
How can a person say they trusted in God if they were to give their baby's food in charity and in doing so put their own baby in mortal danger?
Faith in the truth doesn't sacrifice children or relatives to help. That would be an unlawful way to provide for relatives. It would be more lawless than Robin Hood's stealing to give to the poor and closer to murdering to give to the poor. Obviously if it is not required for dependents to survive on, as the head of the household they can make the call to give family provisions to help others in need. True faith in God trusts God and trusts His precepts and commandments, and loves the truth, loves His precepts. True faith in God doesn't hate the truth (like a demon would hate the truth) but true faith _loves_ the truth:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%205%3A8&version=ESV][I Timothy 5:8]]* - But if anyone does not provide for his relatives, and especially for members of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

In the family of faith, we ultimately share all things, and since all we have belongs to God, and since we *must* love our family in Christ, it's evil to not be a "good Samaritan" to those in the body of Christ who are in need:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%204%3A32&version=ESV][Acts 4:32]]* - Now the full number of those who believed were of one heart and soul, and no one said that any of the things that belonged to him was his own, but they had everything in common. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%203%3A27&version=ESV][Proverbs 3:27]]* - Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in your power to do it. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A17-18&version=ESV][I John 3:17-18]]* - But if anyone has the world's goods and sees his brother in need, yet closes his heart against him, how does God's love abide in him? Little children, let us not love in word or talk but in deed and in truth. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Also those who are in Christ we should treat as family, and I think it's right to share evenly with our wider family, even in a survival situation:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%205%3A1-2&version=ESV][I Timothy 5:1-2]]* - Do not rebuke an older man but encourage him as you would a father. Treat younger men like brothers, older women like mothers, younger women like sisters, in all purity. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

She acted in faith in this situation after hearing "For thus says the LORD the God of Israel, The jar of flour shall not be spent, and the jug of oil shall not be empty, until the day that the LORD sends rain upon the earth":

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Kings%2017%3A8-16&version=ESV][I Kings 17:8-16]]* - Then the word of the LORD came to him, Arise, go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and dwell there. Behold, *I have commanded a widow there to feed you*. So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, a widow was there gathering sticks. And he called to her and said, Bring me a little water in a vessel, that I may drink. And as she was going to bring it, he called to her and said, Bring me a morsel of bread in your hand. And she said, As the LORD your God lives, I have nothing baked, only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. And now I am gathering a couple of sticks that I may go in and prepare it for myself and my son, that we may eat it and die. And Elijah said to her, Do not fear; go and do as you have said. But first make me a little cake of it and bring it to me, and afterward make something for yourself and your son. *For thus says the LORD the God of Israel, The jar of flour shall not be spent, and the jug of oil shall not be empty, until the day that the LORD sends rain upon the earth.* And she went and did as Elijah said. And she and he and her household ate for many days. The jar of flour was not spent, neither did the jug of oil become empty, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke by Elijah. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

On a different but related topic (i.e. not regarding taking care of dependents), I wonder though, did Elijah end up eating it and on this specific teaching regarding "every prophet who orders a meal in the Spirit does not eat it, unless he is indeed a false prophet" is the Didache correct? It seems like Elijah ordered a meal in the Spirit. I agree wholeheartedly with the remainder of this didache excerpt. For example, I agree with "But not every one who speaks in the Spirit is a prophet but only if he holds the ways of the Lord." And I agree with "And every prophet who teaches the truth, but does not do what he teaches, is a false prophet. And every prophet, proved true, working unto the mystery of the Church in the world, yet not teaching others to do what he himself does, shall not be judged among you, for _with God he has his judgment for so did also the ancient prophets.":

+ [[https://www.earlychristianwritings.com/text/didache-roberts.html][I'll let the Didache speak for itself here]] :: But not every one who speaks in the Spirit is a prophet but only if he holds the ways of the Lord. Therefore from their ways shall the false prophet and the prophet be known. And _every prophet who orders a meal in the Spirit does not eat it, unless he is indeed a false prophet._ And every prophet who teaches the truth, but does not do what he teaches, is a false prophet. And every prophet, proved true, working unto the mystery of the Church in the world, yet not teaching others to do what he himself does, shall not be judged among you, for _with God he has his judgment for so did also the ancient prophets._ But whoever says in the Spirit, Give me money, or something else, you shall not listen to him. But if he tells you to give for others' sake who are in need, let no one judge him.
