We must be imitators of Christ Jesus. See what Paul is doing as an example of imitating Christ. We repent from sin, we do what God says, we are accountable to God with His precepts and are doers of His commandments, we forgive others as we've been forgiven and we love others as we've been loved, and we have our minds set on heavenly things and the promises of God. Our eschatological beliefs should not instill fear in us to forsake faith, obedience, love and hope in Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%203%3A12-21&version=ESV][Philippians 3:12-21]]* - Not that I have already obtained this or am already perfect, but I press on to make it my own, because Christ Jesus has made me his own. Brothers, I do not consider that I have made it my own. But one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus. Let those of us who are mature think this way, and if in anything you think otherwise, God will reveal that also to you. Only let us hold true to what we have attained. Brothers, join in imitating me, and keep your eyes on those who walk according to the example you have in us. For many, of whom I have often told you and now tell you even with tears, walk as *enemies of the cross of Christ*. Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and they glory in their shame, with *minds set on earthly things*. But our citizenship is in heaven, and from it we await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ, who will transform our lowly body to be like his glorious body, by the power that enables him even to subject all things to himself. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

** Being born-again of the Spirit
People were being born according to the Spirit for quite some time before Jesus was born of the virgin Mary but it has been restricted to the children of promise i.e. Abraham's descendants through Isaac. They were born of the spirit through promise, but Jesus was not yet glorified, but they would still receive the life-giving glorified spirit of Christ as promised. I think it's also true that the spirit of Christ dwelt in Abraham and his descendants as in Elijah or Isaiah:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%204%3A28-31&version=ESV][Galatians 4:28-31]]* - Now you, brothers, like Isaac, are children of promise. But *just as at that time he who was born according to the flesh persecuted him who was born according to the Spirit, so also it is now.* But what does the Scripture say? Cast out the slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman shall not inherit with the son of the free woman. So, brothers, we are not children of the slave but of the free woman. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Rather than being born according to the flesh, to be born according to the Spirit happens being born through promise:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%204%3A23&version=ESV][Galatians 4:23]]* - But the son of the slave was born according to the flesh, while the son of the free woman was born through promise. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

OK, so the Spirit is received through faith (faith like Abraham's) in Jesus Christ to all who believe. The promise was made to Christ. Now we must be found in Christ. Amen:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A13-16&version=ESV][Galatians 3:13-16]]* - Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us—for it is written, Cursed is everyone who is hanged on a tree— so that in Christ Jesus *the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles, so that we might receive the promised Spirit through faith.* To give a human example, brothers: even with a man-made covenant, no one annuls it or adds to it once it has been ratified. Now _the promises were made to Abraham and to his offspring._ It does not say, And to offsprings, referring to many, but referring to one, And to your offspring, who is Christ. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's a very big mystery to me that I was [[https://web.archive.org/web/20220402091721/https://mullikine.github.io/posts/astral-projection/][born-again of the Spirit on the first day of Nisan]], and had a meeting with the [[https://web.archive.org/web/20220503030344/https://mullikine.github.io/posts/astral-projection-pt-2/][Holy Spirit (apparently)]] at the tail end of Nisan. Well, whatever it was that happened to me happened.

I had confessed Jesus to the spirit, as documented. But I asked, "Are you the Holy Spirit?" They said, "Yes, I'll take a look at you." But that doesn't mean that it was the Holy Spirit.

Interestingly, the 2 April also line up very closely with Ramadan but not quite. Ramadan started in the evening of 1 April 2022, but it was actually the first day of Nisan, which was a Saturday (Shabbat) that I was born-again:

    fulfilled in the crucifixion,
    resurrection and the outpouring of the
    Holy Spirit that we read about in the
    Gospels in the Book of Acts. But it
    wasn't enough for God to merely fulfill
    the prophetic meaning of each feast, He
    orchestrated events so that each one was
    fulfilled on the exact day of the feast.

    God's word is incredibly precise and
    accurate.

This verbiage "take along" does sound like "lead about". So what Paul says he might be written more unambiguously as, "Are we not allowed to take around (bring) with us a wife who is a sister in Christ, as do the other apostles and the brothers of the Lord and Cephas?" If that's the way it was meant, then that still implicitly does carry with it the idea that they are allowed to have a wife. But the passage doesn't necessarily speak about merely "becoming married" (i.e. the right to 'become married') but does seem to entail that idea too because if someone has the right to bring along or spend time with their wife then that presupposes that a state of marriage is something someone has the right to be in:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%209%3A5&version=ESV][I Corinthians 9:5]]* - Do we not have the right [[strongs:G1849][(G1849 exousian: authority [N-AFS])]] to take along [[strongs:G4013][(G4013 periagein: to take about [V-PNA], to lead about with oneself)]] a believing [[strongs:G79][(G79 adelphēn: a sister [N-AFS]. i.e. a sister in Christ)]] wife, as do the other apostles and the brothers of the Lord and Cephas? For those in Christ, we are commanded to agape love others who are in Christ, and that is a must.
But for those outside of Christ, who are of the world, we don't unite ourselves to.
We do good to all, we love all. But those in Christ we *must* love with agape love or else we are in darkness. So there is an upwards call to agape love everybody. I think Christians do typically love everyone. We love the sinner, but we hate the sin. And we do good to all but take care of our own who depend on us. And Jesus is our first love:

#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://biblehub.com/hebrew/6962.htm][H6962. quwt]] :: Definition: To loathe, to be disgusted, to feel a sickening dread.  Usage: The Hebrew verb "quwt" conveys a strong sense of aversion or disgust. It is often used to describe a deep emotional response of loathing or abhorrence, typically in the context of a person feeling repulsed by something or someone. This term can also imply a sense of weariness or being fed up with a situation.

Agape love is defined by God's commandments, rather than by the way in which the world says.
God's commandments tell us how we are supposed to love people.
They tell us how we are supposed to love God's family.
We are supposed to take care of our family in Christ, and provide for them what they need if we are able to.
We should be supporting them as they walk in faith.
God's commandments tell us how we are supposed to love people who profess to be a Christian brother or sister but who make a practice of committing sin.
Loving such people involves discipline which may include putting them out of the assembly.
God's commandments also tell us how we are to love unbelievers. We should do good do them
God's commandments also tell us how we should love our neighbours. One should love their neighbour as theirself.
If one's neighbour is hungry and they need food, and you are going to dinner, then ask them to go to dinner with you, for example.

Love your neighbour as yourself is an interesting command. It's basically saying, do not do wrong to your neighbour, and that is defined how God has defined it. So "loving one's neighbour as oneself" and doing "no wrong to one's neighbour" involves "not lying to them, and not sleeping with one-another's spouses" etc. Just because a person might have their conscience seared to thin it's OK to do evil such as to "commit adultery or commit idolatry etc." it doesn't mean that is now how they love their neighbour as theirself.
Loving one's neighbour as oneself is defined on God's terms, not ours. If somebody is an adulterer then they are *not* loving their neighbour as themself.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2013%3A9-10&version=ESV][Romans 13:9-10]]* - The commandments, You shall not commit adultery, You shall not murder, You shall not steal, You shall not covet, and any other commandment, are summed up in this word: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. Love does no wrong to a neighbor; therefore love is the fulfilling of the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

To love your neighbour as yourself means to love your neighbour the way God wants you to love them.
Is an idolator that you separate from (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%206%3A1%2C6%3A17-18%2C7%3A1&version=ESV][II Corinthians 6:1,6:16-18,7:1]]*) still a neighbour? Or in what way/s are they a neigbour? So longer as we are sharing planet earth then they remain neighbours in some sense. If you've come to the knowledge of God through Jesus Christ, then you'd want them also to come around to the knowledge of God. We are supposed to do good to all people. Sure, we are supposed to separate from idolators. We're not supposed to be yoked with people who are walking their way into to hell. But separating from them doesn't mean to murder them in order to get rid of them. We're still supposed to love even evil people in the way that God wants us to.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%206%3A1%2C6%3A17-18%2C7%3A1&version=ESV][II Corinthians 6:1,6:16-18,7:1]]* - Working together with him, then, we appeal to you not to receive the grace of God in vain. What agreement has the temple of God with idols? For we are the temple of the living God; as God said, I will make my dwelling among them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. Therefore go out from their midst, and be separate from them, says the Lord, and touch no unclean thing; then I will welcome you, and I will be a father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty. Since we have these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of body and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God's commandments also tell us how we should love our enemies.
Maybe there is some wicked person who actively tries to do evil things to you (e.g. slander, steal from, destroy your work, etc.).
We should do good to such people and pray for them, for example.
God's commandments also tell us how we are to love our spouses.
It's not accurate to say we should love all people "equally" and in the same way. But we should love all people in the way that God wants us to love them, without showing partially.
Showing partiality might be treating people differently because they are of a different race, for example.
To show racism would be to show partiality.
But to separate from idolators or to show discipline to sinning people who profess to be believers in Jesus, this can be done without showing partiality.

Not showing partiality means that God is a God of fairness and that God shows [[https://egrammarbook.com/discretion-meaning-and-examples/][discretion]], sound judgement:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2010%3A34-35&version=ESV][Acts 10:34-35]]* - So Peter opened his mouth and said: Truly I understand that God shows no partiality, but in every nation anyone who fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A14-19&version=ESV][I Peter 1:14-19]]* - As obedient children, do not be conformed to the passions of your former ignorance, but as he who called you is holy, you also be holy in all your conduct, since it is written, You shall be holy, for I am holy. And if you call on him as Father who judges impartially according to each one's deeds, conduct yourselves with fear throughout the time of your exile, knowing that you were ransomed from the futile ways inherited from your forefathers, not with perishable things such as silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without blemish or spot. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%207%3A24&version=ESV][John 7:24]]* - Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But we *should* love all people in the way that God commands us to love them, and imitate God's love and God is a God who certainly does love both unconditionally and conditionally:

Christians are instructed to not love the world or the things that are in the world.
Just because there are aeroplanes and telephones and the internet certainly doesn't mean that we are "all one".
The light is not one with the darkness.
Christ's kingdom is not one with Satan's kingdom.
All in Adam die, but all in Christ shall be made alive, and so redeemed humanity is not one with unredeemed humanity.
Father God takes people out of the world and gives them to Jesus.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2017%3A6&version=ESV][John 17:6]]* - I have manifested your name to the people whom you gave me out of the world. Yours they were, and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The Bible says that God "loved" the world in a very specific way, that He gave His Only-Begotten Son so that who ever has faith in Him should not perish but have everlasting life. These people who have faith in Jesus Christ are no longer of the world.
The world is passing away.
Christians should agape love their family in Christ, and treasure them, and they should love those who are their family in Christ in a way which is not fitting to love those outside of their family in Christ.
That's the truth.
Whoever hates their brother does not have eternal life abiding in them.
That's how serious it is.
But not everyone in the world are brothers.
Those in the family in Christ are family and those who are outside of Christ are not family.
Whoever loves God must also love their brother.

#+END_QUOTE

On <2025-01-13 Mon> Monday, I woke up to a voice which said, "What is your faith in?"

I responded like this, "My faith is in the Word of God. Jesus Christ and His finished works is the cornerstone of my faith, and keeping and doing his commandments is the foundation of my faith. I obey Righteousness because I obey Jesus. I believe in the Truth because I believe in Jesus."

I didn't know but it turned out to be the last day of my [[*The criminal conviction has made it more difficult to support myself and other people in need][sentence]].

+ Watch :: [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m__JDReWKQY][youtube.com: FULL REMARKS: President Trump Speaks At White House Easter Prayer Service And Dinner {@ForbesBreakingNews}]]

This is so cool what is happening over in the USA. Praise God! I think my heart just softened a bit more towards Trump after seeing the sincerity in his eyes and voice and words and reverence for God, and I'm encouraged by what's happening at the White House these days. Listening to him confess [[https://biblehub.com/greek/3670.htm][(G3670 homologeó)]] elementary doctrine of Christ, and seeing his reverence for Father God and the Lord Jesus Christ, and for Jesus' words, and his faith in Jesus' atoning sacrifice and having witnessed that he has heard the cornerstone of the gospel of Jesus and how we are called to love as Jesus did, and seeing him give due reverance for the Lord and Trump still confessing his faith in God through Jesus, I'm convinced the man is a genuine Christian with a sincere faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. After listening to him and hearing what he had to say, and his belief in Jesus' atoning sacrifice, His death and resurrection, it eases so much anxiety I had. It's easy to despair when the world gets so dark because there's not a lot of light in it. Jesus is the light of the world and Christ's disciples are also the light of the world. Gotta keep that light shining.

Before I got born-again of the spirit in 2021, I was neck-deep in AI fiction research and was using OpenAI, but I have turned my back on that stuff now after Jesus made me born-again, and are focusing on genuinely keeping Jesus' commandments, and I don't think pursuing AI fits in with that vision at all.

I don't see anything wrong inherently with "Imaginary Programming", as I'd
called it, as I was only using the existing models that
were out there to run my prompts. I was designing prompts, and I was trying to
be responsible and not use the AI systems to do bad things.

Sure, a person could do evil using prompting, and also the models themselves could be made in an unlawful manner.
I think spreading AI fiction everywhere would be very unresponsible.

Imaginary Programming was essentially using LLMs in place of programming tools such as interpreter/compiler/linter
so that a person could program the computer more abstractly at the user's conceptual level.

But after getting born-again several things became apparent:
- I needed to drop everything I was doing to focus on Jesus. Being born-again of the spirit, it was right to focus on God and not on the AI stuff. Obviously, I want other people to be saved as well, so I wouldn't want to brush it under the rug/shrug it off
- I needed more humility. I was feeling quite prideful, and sometimes we just have to decrease
  - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A28-31&version=ESV][John 3:28-31]]* - You yourselves bear me witness, that I said, I am not the Christ, but I have been sent before him. The one who has the bride is the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice. Therefore this joy of mine is now complete. He must increase, but I must decrease. He who comes from above is above all. He who is of the earth belongs to the earth and speaks in an earthly way. He who comes from heaven is above all.
- Not everyone doing the AI research and working on the AI technology was God-fearing, nor law-abiding and pulling out was intuitively the right thing to do in order to be good influencer, I think
- The AI fiction stuff was spreading like cancer
- More moral/ethical issues with how people might use the AI stuff
- How to put it? Feeling like I woke up in [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/faq/don_stewart/don_stewart_114.cfm][Hades]] and just don't want to be here. I want to be on the side of the God-fearing, God-loving people, rather than with the world
  - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%202%3A40&version=ESV][Acts 2:40]]* - And with many other words he bore witness and continued to exhort them, saying, Save yourselves from this crooked generation. (ESV)
- I began receiving extreme amounts of satanic harassment, and needed to focus on Jesus, faith in and obedience to Jesus, getting to know Jesus. There's simply more important things in this life. Christ is our life
  - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%208%3A35-36&version=ESV][Mark 8:35-36]]* - For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel’s, the same shall save it. For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? (KJV)

A way of understanding this might be that the one born of God stops practicing sin and instead practices righteousness and they come out from the power/influence of Satan and turn to the power of God and come into the Kingdom of God.

The Genesis creation story has spiritual significance and seems to be abstract in the way that I was born-again of the Spirit and becoming a new creation  [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g2537/kjv/tr/0-1/][(G2537 kainē; new)]] [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g2937/kjv/tr/0-1/][(G2937 ktisis; creation)]] in Christ seems abstract as the Genesis creation story seems abstract, but nonetheless true. I am emphasising the spiritual reality of the Genesis story while not discounting at all a literal interpretation of Genesis such as the 7 day account of creation and rest.

- Genesis, creation and rest, 1 set of 7 days (abstract)
- Mosaic law (Deuteronomy, Leviticus), weekly (not abstract - literal)
  - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%202%3A16-17&version=ESV][Colossians 2:16-17]]* - Therefore let no one pass judgment on you in questions of food and drink, or with regard to a festival or a new moon or a Sabbath. These are a shadow of the things to come, but the substance belongs to Christ. (ESV)
- New creation in Christ (abstract)
  - Born-again of the Spirit on 1 Nisan
  - Commandments such as these taken spiritually:
    - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%209%3A8-11&version=ESV][I Corinthians 9:8-11]]* - Do I say these things on human authority? Does not the Law say the same? For it is written in the Law of Moses, You shall not muzzle an ox when it treads out the grain. Is it for oxen that God is concerned? Does he not speak entirely for our sake? It was written for our sake, because the plowman should plow in hope and the thresher thresh in hope of sharing in the crop. If we have sown spiritual things among you, is it too much if we reap material things from you? (ESV)
    - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%204%3A8-11&version=ESV][Hebrews 4:8-11]]* - For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken of another day later on. So then, there remains a Sabbath rest for the people of God, for whoever has entered God's rest has also rested from his works as God did from his. Let us therefore strive to enter that rest, so that no one may fall by the same sort of disobedience. (ESV)

    I was born-again of the Spirit on the first day of Nisan on 2 April 2022. During the day in the afternoon I took a nap on my bed and woke up to observing my regenerated spirit man. It looked like a body made of blue light/electricity/fire with a dark bit around the bottom right of my rib cage. I'm unsure if that relates to Adam's rib taken or to the spear in Jesus' side. Anyway, in this state I called out to Jesus to save me because I didn't know what was going on, then I returned to observing the world through my physical body. To this day, I feel this spirit/fire/light energising my body/soul, so it's like being born-again with a second body literally.

    It feels like the whole universe reproduced like a meiosis, and the Bible has really come alive etc. God put the fear of Him in me so I would not turn from Him.

#+END_QUOTE

People were being born according to the Spirit for quite some time before Jesus was born of the virgin Mary but it has been restricted to the children of promise i.e. Abraham's descendants through Isaac. They were born of the spirit through promise, but Jesus was not yet glorified, but they would still receive the life-giving glorified spirit of Christ as promised. I think it's also true that the spirit of Christ dwelt in Abraham and his descendants as in Elijah or Isaiah:

#+END_QUOTE

So God makes us born-again of the spirit through promise. This promise to goes to those who put their faith in Jesus Christ. God sends Jesus' spirit to live in us. So is this one and the same event, being born-again of the spirit and having the spirit of Jesus Christ dwell in us? So I wonder, Isaac being a child of promise, born according to the spirit, did the spirit of Jesus Christ live inside him, or is being born-again of the spirit and receiving the spirit of Jesus Christ two different things?

At this stage, how I would word this is I would say that I have a regenerated spirit, and even with a regenerated spirit, willful disobedience to God is defiling, sin is defiling, so even after being regenerated, it's correct to continue, loving others, especially family in Christ, and forgiving others, and forsaking sinful habits, and being renewed in mind, and endeavour to please God with our thoughts and actions, learning about God's will for us and putting it into practice:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%207%3A1&version=ESV][II Corinthians 7:1]]* - Since we have these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of body and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

And Holy Spirit is the one Who washes us, teaches us, interprets the Scripture for us. Jesus washes us, teaches us reminds us of His words with Holy Spirit as we obey the Truth, as we have faith in Jesus Christ, trusting and obeying Him. And God comes to live in us:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A23&version=ESV][John 14:23]]* - Jesus answered him, If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him. (ESV)

But if Christ is in you, although the body is dead because of sin, the Spirit is life because of righteousness. If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2016%3A7&version=ESV][John 16:7]]* - Nevertheless, I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Helper will not come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

OK, so God's spirit lives in us and there is some kind of distinction between God's Spirit and our spirit.
So that is a little more evidence to me to suggest that being born-again of the Spirit, the regeneration of our spirit may very well easily been going on for

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A16-18&version=ESV][Romans 8:16-18]]* - The Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God, and if children, then heirs—heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ, provided we suffer with him in order that we may also be glorified with him. For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed to us. (ESV)

*** Repentance from sin after being born of the Spirit

It's very clear that even after God's spirit comes to dwell within a person, we must not defile ourselves through committing sin.
And it's also clear that everyone who hope in Jesus Christ, purifies themselves as He is pure.

It's also clear if we are abiding in Jesus, keeping His commandments, then we will not make a practice of sinning, so we should definitely be abiding in Jesus, keeping His commandments.

To put this concisely, I think that we get born of the spirit and then use the spirit to put sin to death, and when we see Him we will be like Him.

We should definitely avoid committing sin after we are born-again. Rather, we purify ourselves as we hope in Him (we will get to see Jesus as He is):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A2-7&version=ESV][I John 3:2-7]]* - Beloved, we are God's children now, and what we will be has not yet appeared; but we know that _when he appears we shall be like him, because we shall see him as he is._ And *everyone who thus hopes in him purifies himself as he is pure*. Everyone who makes a practice of sinning also practices lawlessness; sin is lawlessness. You know that he appeared to take away sins, and in him there is no sin. No one who abides in him keeps on sinning; no one who keeps on sinning has either seen him or /known/ him. Little children, let no one deceive you. Whoever practices righteousness is righteous, as he is righteous. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%203%3A16-17&version=ESV][I Corinthians 3:16-17]]* - Do you not know that you are God's temple and that God's Spirit dwells in you? If anyone destroys God's temple, God will destroy him. For God's temple is holy, and you are that temple. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%206%3A18-20&version=ESV][I Corinthians 6:18-20]]* - Flee from sexual immorality. Every other sin a person commits is outside the body, but the sexually immoral person sins against his own body. Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We should be keeping Jesus' commandments to abide in Him and live:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2010%3A25-37&version=ESV][Luke 10:25-37]]* - And behold, a lawyer stood up to put him to the test, saying, Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life? He said to him, What is written in the Law? How do you read it? And he answered, You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind, and your neighbor as yourself. And he said to him, You have answered correctly; *do this, and you will live.* But he, desiring to justify himself, said to Jesus, And who is my neighbor? Now by chance a priest was going down that road, and when he saw him he passed by on the other side. So likewise a Levite, when he came to the place and saw him, passed by on the other side. But a Samaritan, as he journeyed, came to where he was, and when he saw him, he had compassion. He went to him and bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he set him on his own animal and brought him to an inn and took care of him. And the next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper, saying, Take care of him, and whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I come back. Which of these three, do you think, proved to be a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers? He said, The one who showed him mercy. And Jesus said to him, You go, and do likewise. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A1-17&version=ESV][Romans 8:1-17]]* - There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life has set you free in Christ Jesus from the law of sin and death. For God has done what the law, weakened by the flesh, could not do. By sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, *he condemned sin in the flesh, in order that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the flesh but according to the Spirit*. For those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, but those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit. To set the mind on the flesh [[strongs:G4561][(G4561 sarx)]] is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace. For the mind that is set on the flesh [[strongs:G4561][(G4561 sarx)]] is hostile to God, for it does not submit to God's law; indeed, it cannot. Those who are in the flesh cannot please God. You, however, are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if in fact the Spirit of God dwells in you. Anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him. But if Christ is in you, although the body is dead because of sin, the Spirit is life because of righteousness. If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you. So then, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh. For if you live according to the flesh you will die, but *if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live. For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God*. For you did not receive the spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you have received the Spirit of adoption as sons, by whom we cry, Abba! Father! The Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God, and if children, then heirs—heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ, *provided we suffer with him in order that we may also be glorified with him*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I guess I could take a page from Justin Martyr and the Apostle John. According to Justin Martyr, we need to have come to "know" Jesus, and according to the Apostle John, that means we need to have put a stop to willful sin to have arrived at rest in Him. So we find rest at the end of sanctification, or at some point in that process of sanctification where we stop committing wilful sin. That makes sense to me. I would agree that I am still in need or would desire to have further sanctification. I think it's quite a good thing to want to improve at loving people. That's what I want to do. But now I have confidence that the rest is on the horizon.
All who hope in Him purify themselves. And during this sanctification process, we still get to call ourselves children of God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A1-11&version=ESV][I John 3:1-11]]* - See what kind of love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God; and so we are. The reason why the world does not know us is that it did not know him. Beloved, we are God's children now, and what we will be has not yet appeared; but we know that _when he appears we shall be like him, because we shall see him as he is._ And *everyone who thus hopes in him purifies himself as he is pure*. Everyone who makes a practice of sinning also practices lawlessness; sin is lawlessness. You know that he appeared to take away sins, and in him there is no sin. No one who abides in him keeps on sinning; no one who keeps on sinning has either seen him or /known/ him. Little children, let no one deceive you. Whoever practices righteousness is righteous, as he is righteous. Whoever makes a practice of sinning is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. The reason the Son of God appeared was to destroy the works of the devil. No one born of God makes a practice of sinning, for God's seed abides in him, and he cannot keep on sinning because he has been born of God. By this it is evident who are the children of God, and who are the children of the devil: whoever does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is the one who does not love his brother. For this is the message that you have heard from the beginning, that we should love one another. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Justin Martyr says, "Wherefore *those who follow Him, and know Him, having faith in Him as their proof, shall rest in Him*.":

+ [[https://www.earlychristianwritings.com/text/justinmartyr-resurrection.html][Saint Justin Martyr: Fragments of the Lost Work of Justin on the Resurrection {Roberts-Donaldson}]] :: And God, the Father of the universe, who is the perfect intelligence, is the truth. And the Word, being His Son, came to us, having put on flesh, revealing both Himself and the Father, giving to us in Himself resurrection from the dead, and eternal life afterwards. And this is Jesus Christ, our Saviour and Lord. He, therefore, is Himself both the faith and the proof of Himself and of all things. Wherefore *those who follow Him, and know Him, having faith in Him as their proof, shall rest in Him*. But since the adversary does not cease to resist many, and uses many and divers arts to ensnare them, that he may /seduce the faithful from their faith, and that he may prevent the faithless from believing/, *it seems to me necessary that we also, being armed with the invulnerable doctrines of the faith, do battle against him in behalf of the weak.*

    By the way, some people say, well, the Kingdom of Heaven, that's for the Jews. But what's interesting is Jesus uses those terms, and so does Daniel and others, synonymously. *Kingdom of God* / *Kingdom of Heaven* is talking about where we're all wanting to go. It's not talking about living in a perfect, you know, Earth for the Jews someday, somewhere, or something.

    So it's not those who say the right words, Lord, Lord, that will enter the Kingdom of Heaven. But, Jesus said in verse 21, ""he who does the will of my father in heaven". Jesus said salvation is when you come to the point that you want to do the will of another. Do you know what a slave is? We have all this history in America of the tragic slave trade and everything that went on and all that's happened in our culture since then. Do you know what a slave is? A person that does the will of another. They have to do what someone else wants them to do. They're a slave. Do you know  what God says the inhabitants of heaven will be? Bond slaves of God. That's the only people that are going to heaven. that have, by God's grace, done what... Jesus, by the way, is the one... He's the door of heaven. If anybody can talk about who's coming through the door... I mean, more than Paul and Peter and everybody else. But they, by the way, all say the same thing. Praise the Lord. But Jesus, the door, says, it's not you saying the right words, but it's whether or not you do the will of my Father in heaven.

    Those are the four worst words anybody will ever hear in eternity. But it gets from there downhill, depart from me, you, who practice lawlessness. And that leads to a theological phrase that some have used, that if you've never been saved from sin, you've never been saved from hell.

    ...

    Jesus said salvation is a breaking of the pattern of practicing, verse 23, lawlessness. See, for a believer, we're not sinless. We sin. We we are so far short of the glory of God, God says even the ploughing of the wicked is sin to Him.
    I mean you can't even plough in a righteous way without His grace and mercy and his marvelous work. But, in a believer the hold, the power, the overwhelming desire for sin is broken. The connection. The non-stop pipeline of sin is severed. Now it dribbles out.  You ever seen, you know, like a pipeline spill? You know, or what happened in LA, the water line breaks, and it's broken, but the Lord doesn't say we're sinless, but he says we do not practice. It's not our heart's desire to be lawless.
    We want to submit to him.

    ...

    What is it we're supposed to do to be saved? And look what Peter says. And Peter said to them, repent and let every one of you be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ for the remission of sins and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. Salvation is, first of all, coming to Christ away from religion.

    ...

    There are a lot of people that you ask them when they got saved and they said, I joined the church in, or I went forward in, and it's always I did something. And I always listen to that and I say, yep, I did something too. I called the name of the Lord. But it's Christ that saved me. I didn't do anything. All I did is respond and He transformed me. There has to be a human response. What must I do? Believe. What must I do? Repent. What must I do? Call. So I must do something. But the saving is done by God, not by me.

    ...

    They think that you have to straighten out your life to get saved. That's not ever what the Bible says. Do you know what the Bible says? I'll put it in common terms. You catch the fish, then you clean them. Do you think about that? People get caught by the Lord, then he cleans them. You don't get cleaned up to come to the Lord. You come to the Lord dirty, hopelessly, helplessly lost.

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%204%3A11-15&version=ESV][II Corinthians 4:11-15]]* - For we who live are always being given over to death for Jesus' sake, so that the life of Jesus also may be manifested in our mortal flesh. I affirm that the only way is through Jesus. But I don't believe in subtracting Jesus' teachings or His ongoing work from Jesus when we talk about Him or refer to having faith in Him. Nevertheless, without the work of Christ in His passion, death and resurrection, there'd be no reconciliation to Father God.
Nevertheless, I think Stan has valid concerns here but just want to make out that this is not a call to disobedience to Jesus, but we are saved by grace through faith and become obedient to Christ.
We want relationship with God through Jesus Christ, through faith in Him and in His Word, in obedience to Christ and His teachings.

We're told that we get this at our death and at the second-coming of Jesus if we're here at that time, so we're all going to get this, and that's why you've probably heard of a lot of people having it like on an operating table, this near-death experience, but I was wide-awake.
    So this was kind-of a supernatural, mystical experience I was not expecting, and I believe, I'd spoken to some other people that've had it happen and it's shown in different ways to everybody, so I think according to your personality or how God wants to show you your soul, but for me it was shown in columns. I was shown immediately, like a left column, and my left column had all my sins in it, so my life flashed before my eyes.
    I saw all of my sins. I didn't even know that I was in sin. So this was shocking because I thought I had a 'free' ticket to heaven. Here I'm thinking that I'm a great person, and I'm literally watching in the light of God in His presence, not seeing him but like an illumination of my soul, that I know.

If it's in our heart then it has to be a love for the truth.

We have to agree with and agape love the truth so that we can be sanctified by the truth.

We should certainly be allowed to have faith in Jesus' words:

+ [[https://www.earlychristianwritings.com/text/justinmartyr-resurrection.html][Saint Justin Martyr: Fragments of the Lost Work of Justin on the Resurrection {Roberts-Donaldson}]] :: The word of truth is free, and _carries its own authority, *disdaining to fall under any skilful argument, or to endure the logical scrutiny of its hearers*. But it would be *believed for its own nobility*, and for the confidence due to Him who sends it_. Now the word of truth is sent from God; wherefore the freedom claimed by the truth is /not arrogant/. For *being sent with authority, it were not fit that it should be required to produce proof of what is said*; since *neither is there any proof beyond itself, which is God*. For _every proof is more powerful and trustworthy than that which it proves; since what is disbelieved, until proof is produced, gets credit when such proof is produced_, and is recognised as being what it was stated to be. But *nothing is either more powerful or more trustworthy than the truth*; so that he who requires proof of this is like one who wishes it demonstrated why the things that appear to the senses do appear. For the test of those things which are received through the reason, is sense; but of sense itself there is no test beyond itself. As then we bring those things which reason hunts after, to sense, and by it judge what kind of things they are, whether the things spoken be true or false, and then sit in judgment no longer, giving full credit to its decision; so also we refer all that is said regarding men and the world to the truth, and by it judge whether it be worthless or no. But the utterances of truth we judge by no separate test, giving full credit to itself.

So, for example, a Protestant may simply lean very heavily on their understanding of this verse, and that would be their faith. That's fine. At the end of the day, I'm also trusting on Jesus Himself and His finished work to deliver me from death and receive eternal life or that He has already delivered me from death and I've already received and receiving and awaiting eternal life (because I've been baptised into His death):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A24&version=ESV][John 5:24]]* - Truly, truly, I say to you, whoever hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life. He does not come into judgment, but has passed from death to life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

There's many other things which Jesus has taught though. Jesus didn't drive his points home to inflict harm. Rather, He left words that we need to come into agreement with, trust and obey to be saved:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2012%3A46-48&version=ESV][John 12:46-48]]* - I have come into the world as light, so that whoever believes in me may not remain in darkness. The one who rejects me and does not receive my words has a judge; the word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

For that reason, I would have more confidence before God if I was serving Him endeavouring to be pleasing to God through serving Jesus with a sincere faith, turning away from sin, renouncing ungodliness , loving the brethren, and trying to be holy and selfless and loving in faith towards Jesus, than if like a lawyer looking for a loophole I put confidence on doctrine but had no changed life / love for Jesus.

+ [[https://www.refugeutah.org/hebrews-7-1-10][No, You Do Not Hold The Melchizedek Priesthood]] :: So he is King of Peace and King of Righteousness, serving bread and wine, praising God, a priest, and Abram tithes to him! However, I don’t believe he is actually a preincarnate appearance of Christ—Hebrews 7:3 tells us that Melchizedek resembled Jesus, not that he was Jesus.

    And that is a key point: The text isn’t saying that Jesus is like Melchizedek, but that Melchizedek is like Jesus—that Jesus is the true and better Melchizedek, just as he is the true and better Temple, Lamb, Passover, Moses, David, on forward. This is another case of typology, that this is about that. God wrote the story of Melchizedek in living history, to later teach us something of the Person and work of Jesus. So that is the origin of this designation.

*** My testimony of being born-again of the Spirit

Being born of the Spirit is something which is genuinely unpredictable but we can sense its coming and going. It's not the same thing as getting someone to pray a sinner's prayer, for example, otherwise Jesus would not have used this analogy. We can sense it (hear it's sound, such as making testimony of being born of the Spirit), but we don't know where it comes form or where it goes:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A3-8&version=ESV][John 3:3-8]]* - Jesus answered him, Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born again he cannot see the kingdom of God. Nicodemus said to him, How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother's womb and be born? Jesus answered, Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. That which is born of the flesh is flesh, and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit. Do not marvel that I said to you, You must be born again. The wind blows where it wishes, and you hear its sound, but *you do not know where it comes from or where it goes.* So it is with everyone who is *born of the Spirit.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The Apostles were working with Christ. I believe the Apostles also here are
exhorting believers to work with Christ to receive the grace of God. The Apostles also
practiced what they preached. OK, so imagine a situation where someone is just
being so irrationally abusive, or so irrationally hateful and unloving towards
people. It might be worth picturing that person as Jesus and Jesus putting Himself in that situation so that you can
carry out His commandments and demonstrate God's love towards them.
It might also be worth picturing that person as someone who God has
set before you to love them and so pass forward the love of God, and perhaps
lead them to Jesus. God *bought* that opportunity for you to love them, and He also trust you with it, as you trust His commandments.
He puts us in the position of being able to demonstrate the love of God, and He entrusts you with it, to show that person the love of God, for their sake, and for Jesus' sake, and for your sake.
That's the freedom which Jesus bought for us. Imagine you want to be able to live-out
Jesus' commandments and you feel like they're just so challenging or daunting, or impossible. Fulfilling Christ's law is not impossible.
All things are possible with God. And to fulfill the law of Christ is what Paul challenged us to do.

Well, Jesus bought for us the ability to live out His commandments, and live out Father God's commandments to us authentically and without fear of punishment, and with the hope of a future with God.

Yes, we make mistakes, but God just continues working with us and in us,
and Jesus teaches us to obey His commandments better, and live in this way. And since the Holy Spirit goes to those who obey Jesus, it's as if Jesus helps us to do it. So He gives us His commandments, and we put our faith in Him and obey Him and He helps us to continue doing them:

God put our sin on Jesus:

We shouldn't oversimplify the doctrine of substitution.
For those who abide in Christ, we have an advocate with our Heavenly Father, Jesus Christ the Righteous:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A1&version=ESV][I John 2:1]]* - My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you may not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

There is no sin in Jesus, but in a sense, Father God has laid on Jesus our iniquity. How has that happened? I think it like this: Jesus in entrusting Himself to Father God was essentially delivered from evil when He conquered death, being raised from the dead. Father God has not only taken Him back up to glory but saves all the people putting their trust in Jesus. Jesus remains without sin but the sin that would have brought us death (and we would have stayed down, buried under sin) was put on Jesus who carryied it. Jesus rose from the dead and conquers death for all those who would be saved through Him.
But Jesus wasn't smitten by God, but it did appear like it. Jesus was carrying (G399 anaphérō) our iniquities. Evil people, blasphemers themselves, accused Jesus of blasphemy and had Him crucified, but Jesus did not retaliate. Rather, Jesus was put to death unjustly while having promised through the gospel that if they or anyone repents and does what Abraham did, well, put their trust in Him, then they would be saved. He left us commandments which we abide in and in abiding in His commandments we abide in Him.

+ G399 anaphérō :: (from 303 /aná, "up" and 5342 /phérō, "bring, carry") – properly, bring up to the goal (end point), i.e. carrying something through its sequence to reach its needed consummation (note the prefix, ana).

Bearing, carrying, our sins, Jesus suffered in His flesh. Jesus didn't have sin inside Him at all but He was *carrying* our sin. But Father God treated (past-tense) spotless Jesus Christ, His Son as if He was the sin He was carrying. The past tense is used when the passage says "He made Him to be sin" and the future tense for "in him we might". So, in Jesus saying "not my will but Yours be done" (Luke 22:42) I believe Jesus could have asked for justice, for deliverance, but was perfectly obedient to Father God. With perfect obedience to Father God, Jesus could not have possibly stayed in the grave.  God's will was never for Jesus to be killed off permanently but, rather, for Jesus to fulfill the law and the prophets while not being delivered from the scurging from evil men and for Jesus to defeat death. So what must we do? Well, we must hold our faith in Jesus. We must trust and obey Jesus. We must abide in Jesus' commandments. We *must* do that. And for people who do that, we are able to be forgiven and sanctified (cleaned up), sanctified by faith and obedience to Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%205%3A21&version=ESV][II Corinthians 5:21]]* - For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus did not retaliate but continued entrusting Himself to Father God. So now those who are in Him can die to sin and live for righteousness. And we *must*:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%202%3A22-24&version=ESV][I Peter 2:22-24]]* - He committed no sin, neither was deceit found in his mouth. When he was reviled, he did not revile in return; when he suffered, he did not threaten, but continued entrusting himself to him who judges justly. He himself bore (G399 anaphérō) our sins in his body on the tree, that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. By his wounds you have been healed. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%203%3A18&version=ESV][I Peter 3:18]]* - For Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh but made alive in the spirit, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A5-7&version=ESV][I John 3:5-7]]* - You know that he appeared to take away sins, and in him there is no sin. No one who abides in him keeps on sinning; no one who keeps on sinning has either seen him or known him. Little children, let no one deceive you. Whoever practices righteousness is righteous, as he is righteous. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus was not smitten by God, but rather He was carrying our sins as wicked men afflicted Him and killed Him. Jesus went willingly, knowing what would happen:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2053%3A4-6&version=ESV][Isaiah 53:4-6]]* - Surely he has borne our griefs and carried our sorrows; yet we esteemed him stricken, smitten by God, and afflicted. But he was wounded for our transgressions; he was crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the chastisement that brought us peace, and with his stripes we are healed. All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must go on abiding in Him, abiding in His commandments and put sin to death by the grace of God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A5-7&version=ESV][I John 3:5-7]]* - And ye know that he was manifested to take away our sins; and in him is no sin. Whosoever abideth in him sinneth not: whosoever sinneth hath not seen him, neither known him. Little children, let no man deceive you: he that doeth righteousness is righteous, even as he is righteous. (KJV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%204%3A1-8&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 4:1-8]]* - Finally, then, brothers, we ask and urge you in the Lord Jesus, that as you received from us how you ought to live and to please God, just as you are doing, that you do so more and more. For you know what instructions we gave you through the Lord Jesus. For this is the will of God, your sanctification: that you abstain from sexual immorality; that each one of you know how to control his own body in holiness and honor, not in the passion of lust like the Gentiles who do not know God; that no one transgress and wrong his brother in this matter, because the Lord is an avenger in all these things, as we told you beforehand and solemnly warned you. For God has not called us for impurity, but in holiness. Therefore whoever disregards this, disregards not man but God, who gives his Holy Spirit to you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Being born-again of the spirit was a total gift received through faith in Jesus, none of my own merit at all - simple very imperfect repentance from sin and faith in God exercising faithfulness:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  I don't really know what this is. It was something like a singularity event and my perception of the world is now spiritual. Most of my life I have not been a very faithful Christian. I was a 'nominal' Christian but I didn't really have a lot of faith or knowledge of God. I had not been seeking out Jesus. For the 2 years leading up to 2 April 2022, I can tell now in retrospect that God was working in my life, and I had begun seeking Jesus, and trying out repentance, and eventually arrived at the point where I was crying to God for help. So when was I born-again? Was it when I first believed as a child, or when I was baptised as a teenager? Not in the same way I was born-again on 2 April 2022. On 2 April 2022 I was truly born-again of the Spirit, and my best explanation as to what had changed was that I had begun to *authentically seek God and to be obedient to Jesus, accountable to God who sees in secret*, and not to man, and that activated a real prayer life, and actively believing God exists and sees, and I had asked God to give me His Holy Spirit. Even though I could not yet hear His voice, I was praying and seeking and beginning to repent. On the 2 April 2022 I was born-again the Spirit - I was spiritually regenerated - whatever it was that happened which I described. When that happened God had put the fear of Him in my heart so that I would not turn from Him, and it was receiving a new spiritual light-body like being birthed from a womb. When I first 'believed' the gospel, this had not happened yet, but I had the testimony I guess. This event, what I experienced on 2 April 2022 I consider to me being born of 'water and the Spirit'. But hearing and keeping the gospel of Jesus, and asking God to receive the Holy Spirit, or seeking God I guess they will have some events, probably different to my 2 April 2022 event something similar happen then or in their future some time, I assume, or perhaps it is 'entering the Kingdom of God'. I don't know exactly how it works. I'm retroactively trying to figure things out by reading the Scriptures.
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_XacW3FHajM][Tim Conway]] :: True salvation changes the way you act when nobody is watching because you know that God is watching. Your faith is that real, it is that powerful, it is that controlling -- that when nobody is watching you know God is, and it prevents you from doing things on the computer that otherwise you would rather do.

As I understand it, if someone is "born of God", [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9nlvj9nNVCA][they would love Jesus]]. If someone loves with Christ's love then they are "born of God and know God" and they would love Jesus if presented with Jesus. If someone is "born of the Spirit" then they have been spiritually regenerated. Being born of the Spirit is what I understand is to be "born-again of water and the Spirit".

Maybe these two things are at the same time if a person believes without doubting.

We are sealed when we give our heart to Jesus in believing (trusting) in Him. Holy Spirit is given to us in our hearts:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%201%3A13-14&version=ESV][Ephesians 1:13-14]]* - In him you also, when you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and believed in him, were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, who is the guarantee of our inheritance until we acquire possession of it, to the praise of his glory. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%201%3A21-22&version=ESV][II Corinthians 1:21-22]]* - And it is God who establishes us with you in Christ, and has anointed us, and who has also put his seal on us and given us his Spirit in our hearts as a guarantee. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1&version=ESV][I John 5:1]]* - Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the Father loves whoever has been born of him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A9&version=ESV][Romans 8:9]]* - You, however, are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if in fact the Spirit of God dwells in you. Anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

One way of reading [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2019%3A1-6&version=ESV][Acts 19:1-6]] is that a person may not yet have received the Holy Spirit at the time they 'believed' - believed what exactly though, because [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2019%3A1-6&version=ESV][Acts 19:1-6]] demonstrates that context matters - they hadn't even hear, for example that there is a Holy Spirit. I think it's certainly essential to have trust in God in order to be born of the Spirit, as far as I can tell. When we put our trust in God we have obeyed a commandment from God to put our truth in Him. We should go on obeying Him.

When the following says "they were *baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus*", I'm sure this is baptism in _water_. It's also apparent that a person may receive the Holy Spirit at the time they believed, and the passage also seems to suggest that believing alongside being baptized in water, the person is expected to receive the Holy Spirit:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2019%3A1-6&version=ESV][Acts 19:1-6]]* - And it happened that while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul passed through the inland country and came to Ephesus. There he found some disciples. And he said to them, *Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?* And they said, No, we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit. And he said, Into what then were you baptized? They said, Into John's baptism. And Paul said, John baptized with the baptism of repentance, telling the people to believe in the one who was to come after him, that is, Jesus. On hearing this, they were *baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus*. And when Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them, and they began speaking in tongues and prophesying. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A person may not have been born of the Spirit" when they were baptized in water:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%208%3A14-17&version=ESV][Acts 8:14-17]]* - Now when the apostles at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent to them Peter and John, who came down and prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit, for he had not yet fallen on any of them, but they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. Then they laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Spirit. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2010%3A46-48&version=ESV][Acts 10:46-48]]* - For they were hearing them speaking in tongues and extolling God. Then Peter declared, Can anyone withhold water for baptizing these people, who have received the Holy Spirit just as we have? And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to remain for some days. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus baptises those who have faith in Him with Holy Spirit:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2010%3A46-48&version=ESV][Acts 10:46-48]]* - For they were hearing them speaking in tongues and extolling God. Then Peter declared, Can anyone withhold water for baptizing these people, who have received the Holy Spirit just as we have? And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to remain for some days. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2011%3A16-17&version=ESV][Acts 11:16-17]]* - And I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said, John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit. If then God gave the same gift to them as he gave to us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I that I could stand in God's way? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A25-28&version=ESV][Galatians 3:25-28]]* - But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian, for in Christ Jesus you are all sons of God, through faith. For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is neither male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Also, a person may not have been "Born of the Spirit" (whatever it was that happened to me on 2 April 2022) when they intially believed. But rather, I think they are "born of God", that is if they do in truth believe that Jesus is the Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1&version=ESV][I John 5:1]]* - Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the Father loves whoever has been born of him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I had begun to *authentically seek God and to be obedient to Jesus, accountable to God who sees in secret*. Then I was born of the Spirit.

We must love Jesus by keeping His commandments:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A21&version=ESV][John 14:21]]* - Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves me. And he who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A2-4&version=ESV][I John 3:2-4]]* - Beloved, we are God's children now, and what we will be has not yet appeared; but we know that _when he appears we shall be like him, because we shall see him as he is._ And *everyone who thus hopes in him purifies himself as he is pure*. Everyone who makes a practice of sinning also practices lawlessness; sin is lawlessness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A friend said this at church the very day after I was born again of the Spirit, " *Just because some messages may have been wrong, don't quench the work of God's Spirit among you by banning all prophecies, but rather make sure you test them. Hold onto what is good and dismiss those that are not good* (i.e. those that are evil). "

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%205%3A20-21&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 5:20-21]]* - Do not despise prophecies, but test everything; hold fast what is good. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I feel that way about my experience of being born-again of the Spirit and then undergoing purification and ongoing repentance and correction.

Over the course of 2022, I was actually speaking a lot of prophecy. There was a lot of truth in it, and a lot of error, but my defense is Jesus and I was getting to know Jesus through being washed in the word, and in obedience to Jesus' commandments, and being corrected by the word, but we don't want to throw the baby out with the bathwater.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%2019%3A10&version=ESV][Revelation of John 19:10]]* - Then I fell down at his feet to worship him, but he said to me, You must not do that! I am a fellow servant with you and your brothers who hold to the testimony of Jesus. Worship God. *For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%201%3A4-5&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 1:4-5]]* - For we know, brothers loved by God, that he has chosen you, because our gospel came to you not only in word, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit and with full conviction. You know what kind of men we proved to be among you for your sake. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A9&version=ESV][Romans 8:9]]* - You, however, are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if in fact the Spirit of God dwells in you. Anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%206%3A19&version=ESV][I Corinthians 6:19]]* - Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You are not your own, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

As a result of being born of the Spirit and subsequent obedience to Jesus' commandments has resulted in a huge amount of worldly resistance, and also I've had to fight against a spirit of justification by law compliance, and I've had to fight against a spirit which denies my sins were atoned for and tries to get me to do good works for _justification_. I still do good works out of obedience but I resist the spirit pressuring me to work for justification (it is a very vindictive, Christ-denying spirit, and it is incredibly persistent):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%204%3A29&version=ESV][Galatians 4:29]]* - But just as at that time he who was born according to the flesh persecuted him who was born according to the Spirit, so also it is now. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

** Experiential heart belief through obedience

If you want to really get to know someone then you would learn to walk in their footsteps. Belief must arrive in the heart, not merely the head. There's a confession, an admittance, and a belief in the heart:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A9&version=ESV][Romans 10:9]]* - because, if you confess [[https://biblehub.com/greek/3670.htm][(G3670 homologēsēs, acknowledge, agree)]] with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We should definitely confess [[https://biblehub.com/greek/3670.htm][(G3670 homologeó)]] Jesus to others:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2012%3A8-9&version=ESV][Luke 12:8-9]]* - And I tell you, everyone who acknowledges me before men, the Son of Man also will acknowledge before the angels of God, but the one who denies me before men will be denied before the angels of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Faith presses on to walk the same way Jesus walked - even to spend the rest of the time on earth obedient to Jesus to know Jesus and the power of His resurrection, becoming like Him in His death (i.e. being faithful to God, stopping sin, exercising righteousness, becoming a scapegoat (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%205%3A6&version=ESV][James 5:6]]*), even to death like the Apostles, sharing in His sufferings, living has He lived) and His resurrection:

So by faith we believe we are children of God, and believing on the name of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, God gives us the right and the commandment to be sanctified in the Truth. An analogy I like is that that by believing on Jesus' name as Son of God and Christ, we are allowed to be placed into God's ambulance and brought to God. In other words, we continue in faith and obedience, as slaves of God to be cleaned up as we come to the knowledge of the Truth.
This imputed righteousness enables us to be sanctified by faith in Jesus with his blood:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A11-13&version=ESV][John 1:11-13]]* - He came to his own, and his own people did not receive him. But _to all who did receive him, who believed in his name_, he gave *the right to become children of God*, who were born, not of blood nor of the will of the flesh nor of the will of man, but of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A18&version=ESV][Acts 26:18]]* - to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, *that they may receive* forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are sanctified by faith in me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God continues to heal, sanctify, deliver us and help us to grow in knowledge of Him, as we obey Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%203%3A9-13&version=ESV][Philippians 3:9-13]]* - and *be found in him*, not having a righteousness of my own that comes from the law, but that which comes through _faith in Christ_, the righteousness from God that depends on faith— that I may *know him* and the power of his resurrection, and may *share his sufferings*, *becoming like him in his death*, that by any means possible I may attain the resurrection from the dead. _Not that I have already obtained this or am already perfect_, but I press on to make it my own, because Christ Jesus has made me his own. Brothers, I do not consider that I have made it my own. But one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

** Repentance from sin may come before believing in Jesus

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2019%3A4&version=ESV][Acts 19:4]]* - And Paul said, John baptized with the baptism of repentance, telling the people to believe in the one who was to come after him, that is, Jesus. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

** Born of God

I think being born of God might in some way mean being born of /the will of/ God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A13&version=ESV][John 1:13]]* - who were born, not of blood nor of the will of the flesh nor of the will of man, but of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

By a sovereign act of God in giving us His Word we are born-again of His will by His word - through faith in His Word:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%201%3A16-18&version=ESV][James 1:16-18]]* - Do not err, my beloved brethren. Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning. *Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth*, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures. (KJV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1&version=ESV][I John 5:1]]* - Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the Father loves whoever has been born of him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I find both of these helpful:
- [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s2olQEz1sPE][youtube.com: "Whosoever is Born of God Doth Not Commit Sin" 1 John 3 Explained {@OnoDiamante}]]
- [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x8t22s7iNeI][youtube.com: Does the Bible Say True Christians Never Sin? {@desiringGod}]]

I think this verse could likely mean that the person who is born of God has the power to not sin, as opposed to "never sins", but I'd have to research that. I think it also means we are brought to no longer sin, but rather to be doing the will of God, just as Christ is without sin:

Someone who has just been born of God is a newborn, an infant in Christ.

Keeping Father God's commandments, we love Father God and we love all those who have been born of Him. We must love all those who believes that Jesus is the Messiah because anyone who believes Jesus is the Messiah has been born of God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A5&version=ESV][I John 5:5]]* - Who is it that overcomes the world except the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God? (ESV)

#+END_QUOTE

*** We put away the false gods, and only worship the One True God: Jehovah, and Jesus Christ who He sent

Jehovah is God Almighty who was working through Jesus Christ who is *the* Son of God who also is to be worshiped as Jehovah God, now reigning on the throne of His Father:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Exodus%206%3A3&version=ESV][Exodus 6:3]]* - I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, as God Almighty, but by my name the LORD I did not make myself known to them. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://biblehub.com/interlinear/exodus/6-3.htm][Exodus 6:3 (Interlinear)]] :: and I appear unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, as God Almighty; as to My name Jehovah, I have not been known to them;

Jesus reigns and inherits all things. Jesus is the radiance of the glory of God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%201%3A1-4&version=ESV][Hebrews 1:1-4]]* - Long ago, at many times and in many ways, God spoke to our fathers by the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken to us by his Son, whom he appointed *the heir of all things*, through whom also he created the world. He is the radiance of the glory of God and the exact imprint of his nature, and he upholds the universe by the word of his power.  After making purification for sins, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high, having become as much superior to angels as the name he has inherited is more excellent than theirs. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus is to be honoured just the Father is honoured. Father and Son and Holy Spirit are all Jehovah:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A22-23&version=ESV][John 5:22-23]]* - The Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son, that all may honor the Son, just as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE
