    escape this. And in Christ Jesus we are saved
    from condemnation.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%205%3A9&version=ESV][Romans 5:9]]* - Since, therefore, we have now been justified by his blood, much more shall we be saved by him from the wrath of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must continue in our faith. We must continue to believe Jesus and trust in Jesus:

So by faith we believe we are children of God, and believing on the name of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, God gives us the right and the commandment to be sanctified in the Truth. An analogy I like is that that by believing on Jesus' name as Son of God and Christ, we are allowed to be placed into God's ambulance and brought to God. In other words, we continue in faith and obedience, as slaves of God to be cleaned up as we come to the knowledge of the Truth.
This imputed righteousness enables us to be sanctified by faith in Jesus with his blood:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A11-13&version=ESV][John 1:11-13]]* - He came to his own, and his own people did not receive him. But _to all who did receive him, who believed in his name_, he gave *the right to become children of God*, who were born, not of blood nor of the will of the flesh nor of the will of man, but of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A18&version=ESV][Acts 26:18]]* - to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, *that they may receive* forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are sanctified by faith in me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God continues to heal, sanctify, deliver us and help us to grow in knowledge of Him, as we obey Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%203%3A9-13&version=ESV][Philippians 3:9-13]]* - and *be found in him*, not having a righteousness of my own that comes from the law, but that which comes through _faith in Christ_, the righteousness from God that depends on faith— that I may *know him* and the power of his resurrection, and may *share his sufferings*, *becoming like him in his death*, that by any means possible I may attain the resurrection from the dead. _Not that I have already obtained this or am already perfect_, but I press on to make it my own, because Christ Jesus has made me his own. Brothers, I do not consider that I have made it my own. But one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A31-32&version=ESV][John 8:31-32]]* - So Jesus said to the Jews _who had believed ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/4100.htm][4100. pisteuó]], [[https://biblehub.com/greek/pepisteukotas_4100.htm][pepisteukotas]]) in him_, *If you abide in my word, you are truly my disciples, and you will know the truth*, _and the truth will set you free._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I believe that we are saved not because of our own merit, but, still, obedience to the Gospel leads to righteousness which leads to salvation:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%205%3A9&version=ESV][Hebrews 5:9]]* - And being made perfect, he became the source of eternal salvation to all who obey him, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%205%3A32&version=ESV][Acts 5:32]]* - And we are witnesses to these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15-16&version=ESV][John 14:15-16]]* - If you love me, you will keep my commandments. And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Helper, to be with you forever, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A26&version=ESV][John 15:26]]* - But when the Helper comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, *he will bear witness about me*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Obedience is not strictly the same thing as works. Obedience is a heart attitude and we are to be obedient to Christ's teachings:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Titus%201%3A16&version=ESV][Titus 1:16]]* - They profess to know God, but they _deny him by their works_. They are detestable, *disobedient, unfit for any good work*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A16-18&version=ESV][Romans 6:16-18]]* - Do you not know that if you present yourselves to anyone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin, which leads to death, or of obedience, which leads to righteousness? But thanks be to God, that you who were once slaves of sin have become *obedient from the heart* _to the standard of teaching to which you were committed_, and, having been set free from sin, have become slaves of righteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%201%3A7-10&version=ESV][II Timothy 1:7-10]]* - for God gave us a spirit not of fear but of power and love and self-control. Therefore do not be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord, nor of me his prisoner, but *share in suffering for the gospel by the power of God, who saved us and called us to a holy calling,* not because of our works but because of his own purpose and grace, which he gave us in Christ Jesus before the ages began, and which now has been manifested through the appearing of our Savior Christ Jesus, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The Apostles were working with Christ. I believe the Apostles also here are
exhorting believers to work with Christ to receive the grace of God. The Apostles also
practiced what they preached. OK, so imagine a situation where someone is just
being so irrationally abusive, or so irrationally hateful and unloving towards
people. It might be worth picturing that person as Jesus and Jesus putting Himself in that situation so that you can
carry out His commandments and demonstrate God's love towards them.
It might also be worth picturing that person as someone who God has
set before you to love them and so pass forward the love of God, and perhaps
lead them to Jesus.

God *bought* that opportunity for you to love them, and He also trust you with it, as you trust His commandments.
He puts us in the position of being able to demonstrate the love of God, and He entrusts you with it, to show that person the love of God, for their sake, and for Jesus' sake, and for your sake.
That's the freedom which Jesus bought for us.

Imagine you want to be able to live-out
Jesus' commandments and you feel like they're just so challenging or daunting, or impossible. Fulfilling Christ's law is not impossible.
All things are possible with God. And to fulfill the law of Christ is what Paul challenged us to do.

Well, Jesus bought for us the ability to live out His commandments, and live out Father God's commandments to us authentically and without fear of punishment.

Yes, we make mistakes, but God just continues working with us and in us,
and Jesus teaches us to obey His commandments better, and live in this way. And since the Holy Spirit goes to those who obey Jesus, it's as if Jesus helps us to do it. So He gives us His commandments, and we put our faith in Him and obey Him and He helps us to continue doing them:

Jesus helps us when we are being tempted. So we are trying to be faithful and obedient to Jesus Christ and Jesus helps us:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%202%3A14-18&version=ESV][Hebrews 2:14-18]]* - Since therefore the children share in flesh and blood, he himself likewise partook of the same things, that through death he might destroy the one who has the power of death, that is, the devil, and *deliver all those who through fear of death were subject to lifelong slavery*. For surely it is not angels that he helps, but *he helps the offspring of Abraham*. Therefore he had to be made like his brothers in every respect, so that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in the service of God, to make propitiation for the sins of the people. For because he himself has suffered when tempted, *he is able to help those who are being tempted*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I really wish there was not a chapter break between these two verses because it's revealing to to read them side by side:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%205%3A21-6&version=ESV][II Corinthians 5:21-6:1]]* - For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him *we might become the righteousness of God. Working together with him*, then, we appeal to you not to receive the grace of God in vain. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2010%3A11&version=ESV][II Corinthians 10:11]]* - Let such a person understand that what we say by letter when absent, we do when present. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%207%3A1&version=ESV][II Corinthians 7:1]]* - Since we have these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of body and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%201%3A6&version=ESV][Philippians 1:6]]* - And I am sure of this, that he who began a good work in you will bring it to completion at the day of Jesus Christ. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A22&version=ESV][James 2:22]]* - You see that faith ([[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g4102/kjv/tr/0-1/][G4102 pistis]]) was working with ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/4903.htm][4903. sunergeó]]) his works ([[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g2041/nasb95/mgnt/0-1/][G2041 ergon]]), and as a result of the works ([[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g2041/nasb95/mgnt/0-1/][G2041 ergon]]), faith ([[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g4102/kjv/tr/0-1/][G4102 pistis]]) was perfected ([[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g5048/kjv/tr/0-1/][G5048 teleioo]]);
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://biblehub.com/greek/4903.htm][4903. sunergeó]] :: Definition: to work together. Usage: I cooperate with, work together.

We should disobey sin, and present ourselves to God as those alive from the dead, and our members as *instruments of righteousness to God*. We should be practicing righteousness, practicing love and holiness and truth:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A12-13&version=NASB][Romans 6:12-13]]* - Therefore *do not let sin reign* in your mortal body so that you *obey* its lusts, and *do not go on* presenting the members of your body to sin as instruments of unrighteousness; but _/present yourselves to God as those alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness to God./_ (NASB)
#+END_QUOTE

A person who believes on Jesus' name has the right to become a child of God:
- *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A12-13&version=ESV][John 1:12-13]]* - But to all who did receive him, who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God, who were born, not of blood nor of the will of the flesh nor of the will of man, but of God. (ESV)
A child of God makes a practice of practicing righteousness and does not make a practice of sinning:
- *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A10&version=ESV][I John 3:10]]* - By this it is evident who are the children of God, and who are the children of the devil: whoever does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is the one who does not love his brother. (ESV)
We should definitely have the mindset of having suffered in the flesh and ceased from sinning. Be repentant, be spiritually minded, be trying to do the will of God, be prepared to stand before God:
- *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%204%3A1-5&version=ESV][I Peter 4:1-5]]* - Since therefore Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves with the same way of thinking, for whoever has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin, so as to live for the rest of the time in the flesh no longer for human passions but for the will of God. The time that is past suffices for doing what the Gentiles want to do, living in sensuality, passions, drunkenness, orgies, drinking parties, and lawless idolatry. With respect to this they are surprised when you do not join them in the same flood of debauchery, and they malign you; *but they will give account to him who is ready to judge the living and the dead*. (ESV)

*** We become obedient to Jesus
The righteous try to be obedient. They make mistakes sometimes, they mess up sometimes but they return to God with the fear of God (they repent):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2024%3A15-16&version=ESV][Proverbs 24:15-16]]* - Lie not in wait as a wicked man against the dwelling of the righteous; do no violence to his home; for the righteous falls seven times and rises again, but the wicked stumble in times of calamity. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  John Piper - "Mercy means that *our obedience doesn't have to be perfect, it has to be penitent*."
#+END_QUOTE

*** Eternal life and salvation is a gift received through faith and obedience to God
We put our hope on Him to be our High Priest and Advocate, we obey Him as He saves us.

These should really go hand in hand:
- Believing in Jesus Christ for His finished work to receive justification and eternal life and remain in relationship with Father God and with Jesus
- Obeying Jesus Christ (repenting from sin, loving God and your neighbour) to be saved from the wrath of God should really go hand-in-hand.

When you believe Jesus' words you are trusting of Jesus. If you believe Jesus then you believe when He says He is the Son of God, for example. Someone who hears Jesus' voice and does it is someone who believes Jesus and trusts Him. A person can have a heart of obedience to Jesus and that's a heart of trust, it's a heart of belief. If you trust Jesus you will believe what He says and you will have obedience to Him.

At it's most basic form repentance ([[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g3341/kjv/tr/0-1/][metanoia]]) means a person changes their mind to believe and trust and have a heart of obedience - accepting of the will of God. To repent means =stop distrusting and start trusting= God.

We have believe Jesus and to trust Jesus. When Jesus says He is the Son of God, we must believe it because we trust Him. Likewise when He commands us to repent from sinning we should agree with Jesus and be obedient:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2016%3A8-9&version=ESV][John 16:8-9]]* - And when he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin and righteousness and judgment: *concerning sin, because they do not believe in me;* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We need to heed Jesus' warning that we need to change our minds or perish. We have to stop believing falsehood and believe the truth, believe/trust Jesus and Jesus' words:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2013%3A3&version=ESV][Luke 13:3]]* - No, I tell you; but unless you repent ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/3340.htm][3340. metanoeó]]), you will all likewise perish. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We keep eyes on Jesus and trust Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A2&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:2]]* - looking to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is seated at the right hand of the throne of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2012%3A2&version=ESV][Isaiah 12:2]]* - Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and will not be afraid; for the LORD GOD is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must be taught by Jesus. We must be teachable. We must accept what God says and accept he one He sent (Jesus):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20John%201%3A9&version=ESV][II John 1:9]]* - Everyone who goes on ahead and does not abide in the teaching of Christ, does not have God. Whoever abides in the teaching has both the Father and the Son. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Here is a verse that shows that _repenting from evil deeds_ is important:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

We /*endeavour*/ to be justified in Christ - in Christ means abiding in Christ - through faith; trusting, believing, obedient faith:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%202%3A16-19&version=ESV][Galatians 2:16-19]]* - yet we know that a person is not *justified* by works of the law but *through faith ([[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g4102/kjv/tr/0-1/][G4102 pistis]]) in Jesus Christ*, so we also have believed [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g4100/kjv/tr/0-1/][(G4100 pisteuo)]] in Christ Jesus, in order to be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law, because by works of the law no one will be justified. But if, in our endeavor to be *justified in Christ*, we too were found to be sinners, is Christ then a servant of sin? Certainly not! For if I rebuild what I tore down, I prove myself to be a transgressor. For through the law I died to the law, so that I might live to God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Abraham's *trusting* faith was counted to him as righteousness. I guess it was counted because he was *fully conviced*, and trusting God. This same justification *will be* counted to those who trust in God who raised from the dead Jesus our Lord, who was delivered up for our trespasses and raised for our justification:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A20-25&version=ESV][Romans 4:20-25]]* - No distrust (*[[https://biblehub.com/greek/570.htm][apistia]]*) made him waver concerning the promise of God, but he grew strong in his faith as he gave glory to God, fully convinced that God was able to do what he had promised. That is why his faith was counted to him as righteousness. But the words it was counted to him were not written for his sake alone, but for ours also. It will be counted to us who believe in him who raised from the dead Jesus our Lord, who was delivered up for our trespasses and raised for our justification. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We believe that our justification comes by faith so we place our trust in God and continue trusting; we just get on with living for God and serving God and trusting in God for that justification as we serve God and live in the peace of God. We don't justify ourselves. We have faith in God that He will/does justify us, and we get on with living for and serving God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%205%3A1-2&version=ESV][Romans 5:1-2]]* - Therefore, since we have been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. Through him we have also obtained access by faith into this grace in which we stand, and we rejoice in hope of the glory of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Being justified by Jesus' blood, we are saved by Him from the wrath of God. We have faith in God also to be saved from the wrath of God. That come with God asking us to turn from our sin:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%205%3A9&version=ESV][Romans 5:9]]* - Since, therefore, we have now been justified by his blood, much more shall we be _saved by him from the wrath of God._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Continuing to be sanctified by faith is a process where a person continues in Jesus' words because they are sanctified by faith in Jesus and that means ongoing trust and faithful obedience.

#+END_QUOTE

Persevere to lack in nothing. This perseverance is done in faith:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%201%3A2-4&version=ESV][James 1:2-4]]* - Consider it pure joy, my brothers, when you encounter trials of many kinds, because you know that the testing of your faith develops perseverance. Allow perseverance to finish its work, so that you may be mature and complete, not lacking anything. (engbsb2020eb)
#+END_QUOTE

To be sanctified by faith in Jesus is an applied process, I think:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A18&version=ESV][Acts 26:18]]* - to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are *sanctified by faith in me*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

- Immediately we are reconciled to God by the death of His Son. We are justified,
- and then we are saved from the wrath of God by His life, repenting from sin and keeping His commandments, being sanctified, not resisting the Holy Spirit's work of sanctifying us to correcct out behaviour and thoughts, and separated from the world, since friendship with the world is emnity with God
  - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%202%3A3&version=ESV][Ephesians 2:3]]* - among whom we all once lived in the passions of our flesh, carrying out the desires of the body and the mind, and were by nature children of wrath, like the rest of mankind. (ESV)
- also, we meanwhile rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%205%3A8-11&version=ESV][Romans 5:8-11]]* - but God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us. Since, therefore, we have now been justified by his blood, much more shall we be saved by him from the wrath of God. For if while we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, now that we are reconciled, shall we be saved by his life. More than that, we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Faith presses on, faithful to Jesus, walking in the manner which Jesus walked - even to spend the rest of the time on earth being obedient to Jesus to know Jesus and the power of His resurrection, becoming like Him in His death (i.e. being faithful to God, stopping sin, exercising righteousness, becoming a scapegoat (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%205%3A6&version=ESV][James 5:6]]*), even to death like the Apostles, sharing in His sufferings, living has He lived) and His resurrection:

So by faith we believe we are children of God, and believing on the name of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, God gives us the right and the commandment to be sanctified in the Truth. An analogy I like is that that by believing on Jesus' name as Son of God and Christ, we are allowed to be placed into God's ambulance and brought to God. In other words, we continue in faith and obedience, as slaves of God to be cleaned up as we come to the knowledge of the Truth.
This imputed righteousness enables us to be sanctified by faith in Jesus with his blood:

(ESV)

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A36&version=ESV][John 3:36]]* - Whoever believes ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/pisteuo_n_4100.htm][G4100 pisteuōn]] - /is believing (verb)/) in the Son *has* eternal life; whoever does not obey ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/544.htm][544. apeitheó]]) the Son shall not *see* life, but _the wrath of God remains on him._ (ESV)

I agree that there's actual power in Jesus' actual blood, and after taking a look at the KJV for [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A25&version=ESV][Romans 3:25]] and the Interlinear, I'm convinced that having faith (trusting) in the actual shed blood of Jesus is Scriptural and I think most importantly this means the atoning sacrifice of Jesus His passion and His death. I'm convinced that [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A25&version=ESV][Romans 3:25]] is better translated in the KJV than the ESV.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A25&version=ESV][Romans 3:25]]* - Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; (KJV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%209%3A13-14&version=ESV][Hebrews 9:13-14]]* - For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God? (KJV)
#+END_QUOTE

Isaiah also appears to show that it's the shedding of Jesus' blood which has made atonement for the sin of the one who has faith in Jesus.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2053%3A3-7&version=ESV][Isaiah 53:3-7]]* - He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not. Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted. But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed. All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all. He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth. (KJV)
#+END_QUOTE

I consider doctrines to be helpful but also we need a real relationship with God, so being able to trust God Himself through trusting Jesus Himself is vitally important, I think, and that extends to receiving Jesus and Jesus' words and believing Him and trusting Him and His words. I try to not lean on my own understanding of doctrine but continue trusting in God, and this is dynamic, and while I keep a good conscience with God in this way, I'm content as far as assurance and confidence for the day of judgement goes. The Scripture is useful for correction.

Of course, Jesus' blood made atonement for sin so we can be healed:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%209%3A22&version=ESV][Hebrews 9:22]]* - And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission. (KJV)
#+END_QUOTE

Likewise, without Jesus being raised, our faith in Jesus would be in vain:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A14-17&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:14-17]]* - And if Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain. Yea, and we are found false witnesses of God; because we have testified of God that he raised up Christ: whom he raised not up, if so be that the dead rise not. For if the dead rise not, then is not Christ raised: And if Christ be not raised, your faith is vain; ye are yet in your sins. (KJV)
#+END_QUOTE

Anyway, I think it's faith in Jesus Christ Himself (and God is the Justifier) which is of most importance.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A5&version=ESV][Romans 4:5]]* - But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. (KJV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus' blood bought our redemption. A person who puts their faith in Jesus may receive this redemption which has been purchased with His blood. God justifies and purifies. I think it's faith in Jesus Christ Himself which is most important with God as the Justifier.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2013%3A9-12&version=ESV][I Corinthians 13:9-12]]* - For we know in part, and we prophesy in part. But when that which is perfect is come, then that which is in part shall be done away. When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things. For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known. (KJV)
#+END_QUOTE

The interlinear on biblehub for [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A25&version=ESV][Romans 3:25]] also is reassuring me that faith in the actual blood of Jesus is totally Scriptural. I'm not a "KJV-only" guy but I respect the KJV as a translation although I have found other versions at times to be better translations, and I don't see it as a problem to go into the Greek and to read from other translations, although I think we have to be careful.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  + *[[https://biblehub.com/interlinear/romans/3-25.htm][Romans 3:25]]* - whom set forth as - God a propitiation through - faith in - His blood for a showing forth of the righteousness of Him because of the forbearance of the having taken place beforehand sins in the forbearance - of God (Interlinear)
#+END_QUOTE

*** Salvation is by faith and patience

And disobedience arises from a lack of faith.
We can come to Jesus who is our High Priest, but has been tempted as we are tempted but without sin, and who can sympathise with us.
Therefore, most importantly, we should hold fast to our confession of faith in Jesus and continue in patience unto salvation and to inherit the promises.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%203%3A12-19&version=ESV][Hebrews 3:12-19]]* - Take care, brothers, lest there be in any of you an evil, unbelieving heart, leading you to fall away from the living God. But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called today, that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin. For we share in Christ, if indeed we hold our original confidence firm to the end. As it is said, Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion. For who were those who heard and yet rebelled? Was it not all those who left Egypt led by Moses? And with whom was he provoked for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness? And to whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest, but to those who were disobedient? So we see that they were unable to enter because of unbelief. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We don't want to hear, "I do not know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of evil!":

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2013%3A23-30&version=ESV][Luke 13:23-30]]* - And someone said to him, Lord, will those who are saved be few? And he said to them, Strive to enter through the narrow door. For many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able. When once the master of the house has risen and shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, open to us, then he will answer you, I do not know where you come from. Then you will begin to say, We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets. But he will say, I tell you, I do not know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of evil! In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God but you yourselves cast out. And people will come from east and west, and from north and south, and recline at table in the kingdom of God. And behold, some are last who will be first, and some are first who will be last. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must be from God, confessing the same Jesus Christ with hearts healed by God through faith to do good:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2012%3A33-37&version=ESV][Matthew 12:33-37]]* - Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad, for the tree is known by its fruit. (ESV)

Not being of works doesn't mean "not obedience". What matters is what is that we are doers of God's will for us. What is going on in our heart matters (faith, hope, love):

*** Being saved by faith in Jesus' blood
This is faith-based righteousness.

God's Righteousness is received through faith in Jesus.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A1-5&version=ESV][Romans 10:1-5]]* - Brothers, my heart's desire and prayer to God for them is _that they may be saved_. I bear them witness that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge. For, being ignorant of the righteousness that comes from God, and seeking to establish their own, they did not submit to God's righteousness. For *Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes*. For Moses writes about the righteousness that is based on the law, that the person who does the commandments [[strongs:G4160][(G4160 poiēsas, having done]]) [[strongs:G846][(G846 auta, these things)]] shall live by them. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The righteousness that is by law requires keeping the *entire* law.

The problem is being required to keep the *whole* law to be justified by it. There is no problem with obedience itself. We want faith working through love. Working faith is what we want:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A23-24&version=ESV][I John 3:23-24]]* - And this is his commandment, that we believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as he has commanded us. Whoever keeps his commandments abides in him, and he in them. And by this we know that he abides in us, by the Spirit whom he has given us. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Being justified by the law of faith in Christ (trusting and obeying Christ) rather than being justified by keeping the whole Mosaic law under the old covenant is, I believe, the correct way to understand what Paul is saying. Because I believe we need a law-abiding faith (true faith in Jesus Christ being a non-idolatrous, agape-loving of the truth faith, and loving neighbour as yourself faith):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A1-7&version=ESV][Galatians 5:1-7]]* - For freedom Christ has set us free; stand firm therefore, and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery. Look: I, Paul, say to you that if you accept circumcision, Christ will be of no advantage to you. I testify again to every man who accepts circumcision that he is obligated to keep the whole law. You are severed from Christ, you who would be justified by the law; you have fallen away from grace. For through the Spirit, by faith, we ourselves eagerly wait for the hope of righteousness. For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but only faith working through love. You were running well. Who hindered you from obeying the truth? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Obey the Truth means obey Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A6&version=ESV][John 14:6]]* - Jesus said to him, I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://biblehub.com/interlinear/romans/10-5.htm][Romans 10:5]]* - Moses for writes - [of] the righteousness that [is] of the law that The having done these things man will live by them (Interlinear)
#+END_QUOTE

Paul links actively believing (trusting) in Jesus Himself to trusting in His blood:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A6-13&version=ESV][Romans 10:6-13]]* - But *the righteousness based on faith* says, Do not say in your heart, Who will ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down) or Who will descend into the abyss? (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead). But what does it say? *The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart (that is, the word of faith that we proclaim)*; because, _if you confess [[https://biblehub.com/greek/3670.htm][(G3670 homologeó)]] with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved_. For *with the heart one believes and is justified, and with the mouth one confesses and is saved*. For the Scripture says, _Everyone who believes [[strongs:G4100][(G4100 pisteuōn, believing)]] in him will not be put to shame_. For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek; the same Lord is Lord of all, bestowing his riches on all who call on him. For everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

- We are justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A24&version=ESV][Romans 3:24]]).
- God set Christ Jesus forth as propitiation through faith in His blood
  - Trusting in Jesus Himself has no conflict with trusting in Jesus' blood (His finished works of His passion, death and resurrection)
  - We should have faith in Jesus' blood (His finished works of His passion, death and resurrection) to receive propitiation. The Jesus we believe in, trust in, is the one who died for our sins and rose again from the dead for our justification
    - This doesn't prevent God from justifying anyone who trusts in the Lord Jesus Christ as He is just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus

The redemption is received through faith in Jesus' atoning blood (in His passion and death on a tree and resurrection):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A20-28&version=ESV][Romans 3:20-28]]* - For by works of the law no human being will be justified in his sight, since through the law comes knowledge of sin. But now *the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, although the Law and the Prophets bear witness to it — the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe*. For there is no distinction: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, and are *justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God put forward as a propitiation by his blood, to be received by faith [through [[strongs:G2435][(G2435 dia)]] faith [[strongs:G4102][(G4102 pisteōs)]] in His [[strongs:G846][(G846 autou)]] blood [[strongs:G129][(G129 haimati)]]]*. This was to show God's righteousness, because in his divine forbearance he had passed over former sins. It was to show his righteousness at the present time, so that _he might be just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus_. Then what becomes of our boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? By a law of works? No, but by the law of faith. For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from works of the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

    Eschatology is very important but not as important as, say remaining faithful to Jesus Christ, abiding in His love, loving one-another as commanded.
    But for those who are here on the earth, waiting for the return of Jesus, I think we should be discussing and challenging one-another with eschatology.
    
    If somebody got beheaded for their faith before the second-coming of Christ and they were uncertain about their eschatological views, then I think that person is still saved. Wouldn't you think the same?
    
    The whole duty of man is to fear God and keep His commandments and for the Christian that is to have a love for Jesus Christ, a love that loves Him rather than loving evil, and love our family in Christ as He has commanded us to love them.
    If we're doing that then we're abiding in Him and we're doing our duty. Eschatology is still important, of course. But when debating it we should be doing it out of love for God's word and love for one-another without being hypocrites / whitewashed-walls.
    
    In defense of Lakepoint, when they brought up the [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2012%3A42-49&version=ESV][Luke 12:42-49]] passage, I don't think that the pastor meant that debating eschatology is *always* beating up on servants, but rather that it sometimes can be.
    
    But I think the passage itself is really talking about how we should be anticipating the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ and be serving one another in love while doing that.
    
    So I think there are two warnings in [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2012%3A42-49&version=ESV][Luke 12:42-49]]. One, that people do not compromise their faith and love for one another, and two that we endeavour to remain sound in our eschatological beliefs. And in holding an incorrect echatological viewpoint the person in [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2012%3A42-49&version=ESV][Luke 12:42-49]] (who held the incorrect view that Jesus is delayed), then began to beat on their family in Christ. And rather than doing that, I believe we should be amenable to correction by God's Word, and be able to talk about our eschatological beliefs with one another and challenge one-another from Scripture, without resorting to abusing one another when things haven't gone how we thought they would (i.e. mistakingly thinking the Master is delayed).
    
    I think very imporant is that we are even anticipating the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ at all.
    When someone stops believing that Jesus Christ is coming at all or is coming soon or is delayed, then it sounds like Jesus is saying He'll come back by surprise for that person when they don't expect. But we should be expecting Jesus.
    So there is nothing wrong with holding an eschatological view that is expecting Jesus to come in a particular way according to our present understanding of Scripture. But there are weightier matters that we should not compromising as we hold that faith. Matters such as not denying Jesus' name, for example, or having a love for the truth (love for God's word, love for Jesus Christ), or having love for one's family in Christ.
    
    If less important details of eschatology are considered more important than holding faith in Jesus Christ's name, for example, then that's a massive problem.
    Why would a person want Jesus to return if they are presently hating their family in Christ? Do they want to be judged?

I believe Matt 24 and Luke 21 remain relevant for today and can not merely be attributed to the Siege of Jerusalem 70AD only. Jesus' eschatological prophesy still applies for today, I believe. That makes sense because Jesus says in Luke 21:32-35 that His words will not pass away and "that day" will come upon all who dwell on the face of the whole earth:

Perceptive students [are] fully aware of the disasters in store for mankind should the attitude of *gadget worshipping* gai the dominant role in this highly mechanized age of ours. They know that the danger of machines derives not so much from the machines as from man's attitude towards them. For the crucial issue in the man-machine relationship lies not in what machines can do but in the concepts that man forms about machines and about himself. ... [the current trend in literature, however,], if it goes unchecked, may lead to an upheaval of human values unparalleled in history.

    It is a literature which _blatantly overestimates computers and drastically devalues man._ One may, for instance, read in a college textbook destined for large circulationo that artifical minds shall achieve what the splendid intellectual and technological triumphs of the scientific revolution could not do: come to grips with the value problems of life... for a peaceful and productive international society... + [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g726/kjv/tr/0-1/][G726 harpazō]] :: catch up / take by force
+ [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g726/kjv/tr/0-1/][G726 harpagēsometha]] :: will be caught away (the word used in I Thessalonians 4:17)

Here are places where the word [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g726/kjv/tr/0-1/][harpazō]] and its derivatives are used:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2011%3A12&version=ESV][Matthew 11:12]]* - From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven has suffered violence, and the violent take it (G726 harpazousin; claim) by force. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2013%3A19&version=ESV][Matthew 13:19]]* - When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away (G726 harpazei; snatches away) what has been sown in his heart. This is what was sown along the path. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%206%3A15&version=ESV][John 6:15]]* - Perceiving then that they were about to come and take him by force (G726 harpazein; to seize) to make him king, Jesus withdrew again to the mountain by himself. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2010%3A12&version=ESV][John 10:12]]* - He who is a hired hand and not a shepherd, who does not own the sheep, sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees, and the wolf snatches them (G726 harpazei; snatches) and scatters them. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2010%3A28&version=ESV][John 10:28]]* - I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch (G726 harpasei; will seize) them out of my hand. (ESV)

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2023%3A10&version=ESV][Acts 23:10]]* - And when the dissension became violent, the tribune, afraid that Paul would be torn to pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and take him away from among them by force (G726 harpasai; to take by force) and bring him into the barracks. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%2012%3A5&version=ESV][Revelation of John 12:5]]* - She gave birth to a male child, one who is to rule all the nations with a rod of iron, but her child was caught up (G726 hērpasthē; was caught up) to God and to his throne, (ESV)

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2012%3A2-4&version=ESV][II Corinthians 12:2-4]]* - I know a man in Christ who fourteen years ago was caught up (G726 harpagenta; having been caught up) to the third heaven—whether in the body or out of the body I do not know, God knows.     But you find it logically here. And then
    what did did the evangelical
    church do? They got into the problem of
    traditions over the Word. What's one of
    the clearest ones? We call it
    _invitationalism_.

    That is a real blight.
    Invitationalism is that if you raise
    your hand or pray a prayer you're saved.
    No matter whether God does anything to
    you or not, if you did that, you're saved.
    Now the Bible says *whoever calls the
    name of the Lord shall be saved*, but what
    it says is when God saves you [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A18&version=ESV][Acts 26:18]],
    you get a new heart and a new spirit.

    But invitationalism, which started,
    basically in about 1830 was if you had a
    a good very powerful preacher and he
    told people to come to the front and
    they did, they thought that by them
    coming to the front or praying or doing
    something they got saved, and that's
    where the church gradually got diluted.
    And then of course the charismatic
    renewal church has so much truth in it
    but their excesses and experience has
    taken over the word.

And so, *some* errors are not lethal. I consider, for example, the present Pope
I consider to be a heretic, but that doesn't /necessarily/ mean that he is 'unsaved' or 'unsavable'. But as
well, it also means that certain problems some would consider to be
irreconcilably schismatic may merely be deep but only superficial:

Any issue belonging to 'legalism' is always about the appearance of obedience, rather than inward obedience and good conscience with God.

So I couldn't fully condemn something like "invitationalism". In fact, I think it's potentially a wonderful baby step on a person's faith journey if it's a sincere expression of believing the truth about God.
For example, you could say, who here believes that Jesus Christ rose from the dead? Please raise your hand if you believe.
That's OK. But I think it would be better to hear a person confess with their mouth.
And I think we've really got to teach people to continue on in the teachings of Christ.

** Traditional Roman Catholic understanding
The Roman Catholic view on this as John Barnett explains it is depressing, and really shortchanges the gospel in my view.

However, I think that we receive forgiveness of sin through trusting in Jesus's name as Son of God, Christ, Son of Man, and that through faith in His blood, continued faith in His blood, and walking in the Truth, walking in the light, confessing our sin, etc. Jesus' blood continues washing us. But this is done sincerely and in relationship with God. I believe we have to continue in the commandments of Christ.

** Typical Protestant understanding
I think much closer to this way as John Barnett explains the protestant view, but I have a little bit different understanding regarding glorification because I think that glorification (doing the works of glory) happens while we are on earth and carrying out good works which have been set up for us, and done in Christ (I Peter 3:14-16) in obedience to Christ while holding faith in Christ / done in the will of God for us. Our work may burn up when they are tested by fire but we are still saved. That burning up of work I think definitely applies to work which me might do, say, in say, preaching the gospel, for example, as people often preach false doctrine, and I think that work burns up.

God will uproot false teaching. I pray that if my Bible study writeup is not good in God's sight that He would uproot it.
But I'm not trying to start a church or anything, and don't consider myself to be inerrant. I'm simply doing a Bible study while maintaining a genuine relationship with God because I see the need for this type of testimony for others' benefit.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2015%3A13-14&version=ESV][Matthew 15:13-14]]* - He answered, Every plant that my heavenly Father has not planted will be rooted up. Let them alone; they are blind guides. And if the blind lead the blind, both will fall into a pit. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Also, I think that if found in Christ then we have imputed righteousness. So we must hold to our confession and seek to be found in Christ imitating Christ,
and God is the justifier. And I think the Lord chastises us to clean us up because we will also have to stand before Him later.
Anyway, the following typical protestant view which John Barnett describes also I think has some issues with it because it seems to suggest that it's not possible to fall away at all but that we'd only ever fall short after first having come to believe.
But the rest of my theology document should clarify my stance on it. There might be more nuance. God's the judge. I still think the Protestant view John Barnett describes is more accurate than the Roman Catholic view.

+ [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g3708/kjv/tr/0-1/][(G3708 horaó / opsontai)]] ::  KJV: behold, perceive, see, take heed.  NASB: saw, see, seen, appeared, seeing, looked, look. 3708 horáō – properly, see, often with metaphorical meaning: "to see with the mind" (i.e. spiritually see), i.e. perceive (with inward spiritual perception).

For the Gentiles seek after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all. + [[https://www.bibleref.com/Luke/12/Luke-12-38.html][bibleref.com Luke-12-38.html: What does Luke 12:38 mean? | BibleRef.com]] :: This is part of Jesus' parable about responsible servants (Luke 12:35–37). The servants are awaiting their master's return from a wedding. Jewish weddings could last up to a week, so the servants do not know when the master will arrive. They have kept the lights on, and they are dressed to receive and serve him. When the master returns and sees his servants waiting, he is so overjoyed that he sits them at the table and serves them. If he returns later in the night, and they are still up, he is even more pleased (Luke 12:35–37).  ... The watches of the night are shifts when guards are on duty. The second watch is from 9 to 12 pm; the third watch is from 12 to 3 am. Some scholars interpret this verse to mean Jesus' return will be delayed. It's certainly true that the first generation of His followers expected to see His return in their lifetime. It's also true that God is gracious and wants to give everyone the chance they need to repent (Luke 13:6–9; 2 Peter 3:9).

I received lots of visions and many of them came from the enemy I believe after I had even been reading Apocryphal gospels which I think are misleading and I do not affirm them. Then, after I had said towards the end of 2022 on my blog that we should get ready for Armageddon, war broke out in the middle east soon after. I felt as though I nearly did actually get 'raptured' or it was quickly progressing that way or something like that, and then I made a declaration to court that Jesus is the Truth, I forgive everyone etc. That resulted in some very rapid changes. Things in my life spiritually began to stabilise as I have gone through police corrections and used the time to attend Bible studies, *and be corrected by the Scripture* in my beliefs, obedience and deeds. I'm still trying to be sanctified ongoingly. I am really sorry for misleading people with regards to any error in my writings, but the way to handle this, I believe, is not to throw the baby out with the bath-water but to be corrected by the word of God. I'm still a work in progress.

A friend said this at church the very day after I was born again of the Spirit, " *Just because some messages may have been wrong, don't quench the work of God's Spirit among you by banning all prophecies, but rather make sure you test them. Hold onto what is good and dismiss those that are not good* (i.e. those that are evil). "

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%205%3A20-21&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 5:20-21]]* - Do not despise prophecies, but test everything; hold fast what is good. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I feel that way about my experience of being born-again of the Spirit and then undergoing purification and ongoing repentance and correction.

Over the course of 2022, I was actually speaking a lot of prophecy. There was a lot of truth in it, and a lot of error, but my defense is Jesus and I was getting to know Jesus through being washed in the word, and in obedience to Jesus' commandments, and being corrected by the word, but we don't want to throw the baby out with the bathwater.

*** Agape love for God and one another as opposed to agape love for the world

I'm adding a little section on agape loving God and one another here because although it's right to treat animals with care and respect, and even to have compassion for them and to love and value them even as God certainly does, when we read about "agape" love in the Bible, there are specific commandments that we must abide by where the word "agape" is used. Agape is reserved for God and for fellow humans, particularly our family in Christ.

We want to always be with God, and never want to be cut off from God because we agape love God more than anyone or anything.

We are called to agape love God and one another, especially our family in Christ.

We must not agape love the world or anything in the world with the type of love we have for God and our family in Christ.

The world is passing away and we must not be yoked to it, but those human beings made in the image of God who do the will of God and receive eternal life are made partakers of the divine nature and this is not something which animalkind are given:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A15-29&version=ESV][I John 2:15-29]]* - Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him. For all that is in the world—the desires of the flesh and the desires of the eyes and pride in possessions—is not from the Father but is from the world. And the world is passing away along with its desires, but whoever does the will of God abides forever. Children, it is the last hour, and as you have heard that antichrist is coming, so now many antichrists have come. Therefore we know that it is the last hour. They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would have continued with us. But they went out, that it might become plain that they all are not of us. But you have been anointed by the Holy One, and you all have knowledge. I write to you, not because you do not know the truth, but because you know it, and because no lie is of the truth. Who is the liar but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist, he who denies the Father and the Son. *No one who denies the Son has the Father*. Whoever confesses the Son has the Father also. Let what you heard from the beginning abide in you. If what you heard from the beginning abides in you, then you too will abide in the Son and in the Father. And this is the promise that he made to us—eternal life. I write these things to you about those who are trying to deceive you. But the anointing that you received from him abides in you, and you have no need that anyone should teach you. But as his anointing teaches you about everything—and is true and is no lie, just as it has taught you—abide in him. And now, little children, abide in him, so that when he appears we may have confidence and not shrink from him in shame at his coming. If you know that he is righteous, you may be sure that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Now if someone agape love Father God then they would not agape love the world or anything in the world and they would agape love whoever has been born of Father God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1&version=ESV][I John 5:1]]* - Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and *everyone who loves the Father loves whoever has been born of him.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Also, we must not be lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God. And we must be lovers of good:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%203%3A1-4&version=ESV][II Timothy 3:1-4]]* - But understand this, that in the last days there will come times of difficulty. For people will be lovers of self, lovers of money, proud, arrogant, abusive, disobedient to their parents, ungrateful, unholy, heartless, unappeasable, slanderous, without self-control, brutal, *not loving good*, treacherous, reckless, swollen with conceit, *lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God*, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A16-21&version=ESV][I John 4:16-21]]* - So we have come to know and to believe the love that God has for us. God is love, and whoever abides in love abides in God, and God abides in him. *By this is love perfected with us, so that we may have confidence for the day of judgment*, because as he is so also are we in this world. There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear. For fear has to do with punishment, and whoever fears has not been perfected in love. We love because he first loved us. If anyone says, I love God, and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen cannot love God whom he has not seen. And this commandment we have from him: whoever loves God *must* also love his brother. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%207%3A25-31&version=ESV][I Corinthians 7:25-31]]* - Now concerning the betrothed, I have no command from the Lord, but I give my judgment as one who by the Lord's mercy is trustworthy. I think that in view of the present distress it is good for a person to remain as he is. Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek to be free. Are you free from a wife? Do not seek a wife. But if you do marry, you have not sinned, and if a betrothed woman marries, she has not sinned. Yet those who marry will have worldly troubles, and I would spare you that. This is what I mean, brothers: *the appointed time has grown very short*. From now on, let those who have wives live as though they had none, and those who mourn as though they were not mourning, and those who rejoice as though they were not rejoicing, and those who buy as though they had no goods, and *those who deal with the world as though they had no dealings with it. For the present form of this world is passing away.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2020%3A33-36&version=ESV][Luke 20:33-36]]* - In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife will the woman be? For the seven had her as wife. And Jesus said to them, The sons of this age ([[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g165/kjv/tr/0-1/][G165 aion]]) marry ([[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g1060/kjv/tr/0-1/][G1060 gameo]]) and 'are given' (women are given) in marriage ([[https://www.equipgodspeople.com/lexicons-word-study/new-testament-greek/strongs-g1061][G1061 gamisko]]), but those who are considered worthy to attain to that age ([[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g165/kjv/tr/0-1/][G165 aion]]) and to the resurrection ([[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g386/kjv/tr/0-1/][G386 anastasis]]) from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage, for they cannot die anymore, because they are equal to angels and are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection. (ESV)

** Disobedience towards God is sin. Treasuring anything else more than God is sin

+ Sermon :: [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tqtl-sXeTmA&ab_channel=DesiringGod][God is very happy about obedience, and listening to His word]]. *Disobedience is sin*, and *disobedience is rejecting the word of the LORD*:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Samuel%2015%3A22-23&version=ESV][I Samuel 15:22-23]]* - And Samuel said, Has the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, _to _obey is better than sacrifice__, and __to listen than the fat of rams__. For rebellion is as the sin of divination, and presumption is as iniquity and idolatry. _Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, he has also rejected you from being king._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Leviticus%205%3A17&version=ESV][Leviticus 5:17]]* - If anyone sins, doing any of the things that by the LORD's commandments ought not to be done, though he did not know it, then realizes his guilt, he shall bear his iniquity. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The disobedience of mankind started in the Garden of Eden:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%203%3A17&version=ESV][Genesis 3:17]]* - And to Adam he said, Because you have listened to the voice of your wife and have eaten of the tree of which I commanded you, You shall not eat of it, cursed is the ground because of you; in pain you shall eat of it all the days of your life; (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus helps us to overcome sin. Jesus delivers us from it:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A22-25&version=ESV][Romans 7:22-25]]* - For I delight in the law of God, in my inner being, but I see in my members another law waging war against the law of my mind and making me captive to the law of sin that dwells in my members. Wretched man that I am! Who will deliver me from this body of death? Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, I myself serve the law of God with my mind, but with my flesh I serve the law of sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God's commandments through Jesus is within the Law of God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%209%3A21&version=ESV][I Corinthians 9:21]]* - To those outside the law I became as one outside the law (not being outside the law of God but under the law (G1772 ennomos) of Christ) that I might win those outside the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Everyone who makes a practice of sinning also practices lawlessness; sin is lawlessness. (ESV)

In my understanding, I consider all who are repentantly trusting in the Lord Jesus Christ, who is God the Son, for their salvation, if they are willing _turn to and obey Him_, *if Father God puts them in*, obediently trusting Jesus Christ who is their life, to be _in Christ Jesus,_ no matter what else I say in this document.

I have been just trying to figure out my theology. One God, three persons, Father, Son and Holy Spirit. I don't have the say though. God puts a person in. AMEN!!

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%201%3A30&version=NASB][I Corinthians 1:30]]* - But *by His doing you are in Christ Jesus,* who became to us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification, and redemption, (NASB)
#+END_QUOTE

We are given the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit cleanses our hearts by faith. As we obey Jesus, going against the resistance, our hearts are being cleansed:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2015%3A8-9&version=ESV][Acts 15:8-9]]* - And God, who knows the heart, bore witness to them, by giving them *the Holy Spirit* just as he did to us, and he made no distinction between us and them, having cleansed their hearts by faith.
#+END_QUOTE

If we have faith in Jesus then we obey Jesus' commandments when presented with opportunities. We walk by faith, not sight. When other people discourage you from following Jesus' commandments, but you choose to obey Jesus anyway, this is overcoming the enemy by faith:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%205%3A7&version=ESV][II Corinthians 5:7]]* - for we *walk by faith*, not by sight. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

With God's help, we must drop the old selfish self and allow Jesus to come in with the new obediently loving self:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2037%3A27&version=ESV][Psalms 37:27]]* - Turn away from evil and do good; so shall you dwell forever. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Selfish people killed Jesus. Jesus was selfless. Christian selfless love is based upon God having loved us first; i.e. Christ's love has more nuance to it than mere charity.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A19&version=ESV][I John 4:19]]* - We love _because he first loved us._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus was obedient to God unto death.
We identify with Christ with a death like His (dying to sin and living to serve God), to be united with Him in a resurrection like His!
This is why obedience to Jesus is so important. How can a person be resurrected if they don't die? We need to die a death to be resurrected:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%202%3A11&version=ESV][II Timothy 2:11]]* - The saying is trustworthy, for: If we have died with him, we will also live with him; (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Dying to sin an immediate thing and living to Christ, becoming like Jesus in His death is a lifelong (while on this earth) process. Also, starting to live for God is an immediate thing, and to be with God is the long-term thing:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A8-10&version=ESV][Romans 6:8-10]]* - Now if we have died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him. We know that Christ being raised from the dead will never die again; death no longer has dominion over him. For the death he died he died to sin, once for all, but the life he lives he lives to God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I think that what the following is saying is that in a real sense a person who has died with Christ has already died the death that people typically think of as the death of the body in a real sense. The resurrection body is something that we do look forward to receiving.
I think these verses are saying that as people who have received the Holy Spirit, we expect that later our physical bodies (which are dead) will be made alive again:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A10-11&version=ESV][Romans 8:10-11]]* - But if Christ is in you, although the body is dead because of sin, the Spirit is life because of righteousness. If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A36&version=ESV][1 Cor 15:36]],38* - You foolish person! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies. But God gives it a body as he has chosen, and to each kind of seed its own body. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I think baptism of water is an *appeal* to God and identifying oneself into Christ's death and resurrection but the sacrament *maybe* is not strictly required to be saved (as far as I understand).

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A3&version=ESV][Romans 6:3]]* - Do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A1&version=ESV][Romans 6:1]]* - What shall we say then? Are we to continue in sin that grace may abound? By no means! How can we who died to sin still live in it? Do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? We were buried therefore with him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life. For *if we have been united with him in a death like his, we shall certainly be united with him in a resurrection like his*. We know that our old self was crucified with him in order that the body of sin might be brought to nothing, so that we would no longer be enslaved to sin. For one who has died has been set free from sin. Now if we have died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him. We know that Christ being raised from the dead will never die again; death no longer has dominion over him. For the death he died he died to sin, once for all, but *the life he lives he lives to God.* So you also must consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus.
#+END_QUOTE

Being dead to sin seems to not mean "unable to let indwelling sin reign in our mortal body", so it seems that being dead to sin and having been set free (and sin no longer having power over oneself), it's still possible for a person to then "let sin reign in the mortal body" (allow it to reign), and we definitely do not want to allow sin to reign in our mortal body. I think what Paul is saying here is that we have been set free from sin and that to let sin reign after you've been set free would be something like a king allowing his enemy to reign in his own kingdom. Rather than doing that, we should be walking in faith and obedience to Jesus Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A11&version=ESV][Romans 6:11]]* - So you also must consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A12-14&version=ESV][Romans 6:12-14]]* - Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal bodies, to make you obey their passions. Do not present your members to sin as instruments for unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life, and your members to God as instruments for righteousness. For sin will have no dominion over you, since you are not under law but under grace. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

As I understand it, in water baptism we make an appeal to partake in the resurrection of Christ, and live to serve Christ. Also in being born of the Spirit / regeneration, we definitely die to sin and live to serve Christ, being able to see the Kingdom of God. But then we spend the rest of our lives on earth becoming like Jesus in His death - being obedient to death here on earth, to become like Him in His resurrection:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%203%3A8-11&version=ESV][Philippians 3:8-11]]* - Indeed, I count everything as loss because of the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. For his sake I have suffered the loss of all things and count them as rubbish, in order that I may gain Christ and be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own that comes from the law, but that which comes through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God that depends on faith— that I may know him and the power of *his resurrection*, and may share his sufferings, becoming like him in his death, that by any means possible I may attain the resurrection from the dead. (ESV)

I *think* that water baptism in part is an appeal to partake in the baptism of the Holy Spirit:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2010%3A1-4&version=ESV][I Corinthians 10:1-4]]* - I want you to know, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea, and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea, and all ate the same spiritual food, and all drank the same spiritual drink. #+END_QUOTE

Being baptised into Christ, becoming a slave of righteousness, being set free from sin, I assume, also involves becoming obedient from the heart to the standard of teaching to which were are committed:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A16-18&version=ESV][Romans 6:16-18]]* - Do you not know that if you present yourselves to anyone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin, which leads to death, or of obedience, which leads to righteousness? But thanks be to God, that you who were once slaves of sin have become obedient from the heart to the standard of teaching to which you were committed, and, having been set free from sin, have become slaves of righteousness. Having become a slave of righteousness, the fruit we get leads to sanctification and at its end eternal life:

Nevertheless the one who trusts in Jesus and dies will yet live. AMEN!! And the following verse, I believe actually applies to baptism (identifying with Christ in His death and resurrection)! So a nice way of reading the following is: If someone, while believing in Jesus Christ, dies to their old selfish nature to live as someone who loves selflessly, they will live, and the one who lives abiding in Jesus Christ's love, having died to their old selfish nature, and believes in Him will never die:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2011%3A25-27&version=ESV][John 11:25-27]]* - Jesus said to her, I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live, and everyone who lives and believes in me shall never (G3756 οὐ) (G3361 μή) die. Do you believe this? She said to him, Yes, Lord; I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who is coming into the world. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ ou mé :: Not at all, never, by no means. G3756 (οὐ - no) and G3361 (μή - no)] a double negative strengthening the denial, "not at all" Strong's Exhaustive Concordance anymore, at all, neither, never

I like that way of thinking of it because it encapsulates both belief and obedience to Jesus - both which I think are important.

That rest looks like living for the will of God (i.e. faith in Jesus, faith in God, our sanctification, keeping His commandments, putting a stop to breaking the 10 commandments from the heart, putting a stop to false-witnessing, idolatry etc., so faith in God beliving the gospel, producing agape love especially for our family in Christ):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%204%3A1-2&version=ESV][I Peter 4:1-2]]* - Since therefore Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves with the same way of thinking, for whoever has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin, so as to live for the rest of the time in the flesh no longer for human passions but for the will of God. Jesus is our rest:

These are a shadow of the things to come, but the substance belongs to Christ. (ESV)
