    to marry, or whether to marry. The Bible
    does not tell you which car to drive, or
    buy, rent. The Bible doesn't tell you
    whether to buy a home or not which home
    to buy. [The] Bible doesn't tell you which
    brand of orange juice to drink. There are
    10,000 decisions you must make that are
    not explicitly addressed in the Bible so
    what do you do? If you want to obey the
    will of command my answer is you must
    have a renewed mind. That's what the text
    says.

    *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2012%3A2&version=ESV][Romans 12:2]]* - Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, that *by testing* you may *discern what is the will of God*, what is good and *acceptable* and perfect. (ESV)

We end up thinking in a similar fashion to Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%202%3A16&version=ESV][I Corinthians 2:16]]* - For who has understood the mind of the Lord so as to instruct him? But we have the mind of Christ. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We're must be lawful to Christ (abiding in the 'law of Christ'). Though we don't commend ourselves for doing this. We should normally be doers of Christ's law. What's not done in faith is sin, after all. And whoever has no love for Christ has a curse upon them. And whoever hates their brother who they have seen can't love God who they have not seen. So our duty and normal walk should be doing Christ's commandments such as to have faith in Him and to love one another as He commanded:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%209%3A21&version=ESV][I Corinthians 9:21]]* - To those outside the law I became as one outside the law (not being outside the law of God but under the law of [[strongs:G1772][(G1772 ennomos; lawful to, law-abiding to, in the law of)]] Christ) that I might win those outside the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The word "ennomos" used in I Cor 9:21 for being "law-abiding" is closely related to the word "onnomō" which is used in Acts 19:39:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2019%3A39&version=ESV][Acts 19:39]]* - But if you want anything beyond this, it shall be settled in the lawful [[strongs:G1772][(G1772 ennomō lawful)]] assembly [[strongs:G1577][(G1577 ekklēsia; assembly)]]. (NASB)
#+END_QUOTE

i.e. "settled in the legal / assembly / law-abiding assembly / lawful assembly".

Doing the will of God is what it means to be led by the Spirit. So you have to *do* the will of God, being a servant of Christ, lawful (law-abiding) to Christ, to Christ' commandments, to have the blessing of not being condemned by the law of Moses:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%20143%3A10&version=ESV][Psalms 143:10]]* - _Teach me to do your will,_ for you are my God! *Let your good Spirit lead me* on level ground! (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

And have communion with God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%203%3A4&version=ESV][Revelation of John 3:4]]* - Yet you have still a few names in Sardis, people who have not soiled their garments, and they will walk with me in white, for they are worthy. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://youtube.com/watch?v=J7tfE5yhMtA&t=293][youtube.com: Are There Some Things In The Bible That Christians Shouldn't Know? - Michael Heiser {@stefanlouw6395} @time: 4 min 53 sec]] :: Jesus said, "You have seen me. If you've
    seen me, you've seen the Father."
    And that's what we're supposed to do.
    We're supposed to be disciples of Jesus,
    follow him, and we will be conformed to
    His image, and He is the ultimate imager
    of God. Being a disciple is imaging God.
    You know, Jesus is our example, but
    that little subject has an
    important long history in the Old
    Testament. We talked about the the
    command, "Thou shalt not take the name
    of the Lord thy God in vain" yesterday."
    We think that that refers to verbal
    abuse and misuse of God's name. And
    again, that's bad, but that isn't
    actually what the command means. The
    word "take", here we go back to Hebrew.
    The word /[thou shalt not] *'take'* [the name of
    the Lord thy God in vain]/. Take there is
    נָשָׂא (*[[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/h5375/kjv/wlc/0-1/][H5375 'nāśā']]*, pronounciation: naw-saw'), which means to lift up, to
    support, to carry, to bear, like in
    bearing a burden. So the idea is
    don't bear the name of the Lord in a
    worthless manner in vain. See what does
    it mean to bear the name? If you're an
    employee of a company, you already know
    what it means. You bear the name of that
    company, you're that company's
    representative. If you're, you know,
    just a schmuck or something, then you know, somebody's going to meet you
    and this person treated me bad and so
    that company's bad. I mean, they're
    going to transfer the experience to the
    thing that is named.
    And that's the same thing that that that
    these commands are talking about. The
    New Testament equivalent is kind of the
    verse that Paul gives Timothy in second
    Timothy where he says, "Let everyone who
    names the name of Christ depart from
    iniquity."
    You bear the name. You represent the
    thing named. And that's really what the
    command is about.
    So again, all of these
    things are are have an Old Testament
    backdrop.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%20102%3A15&version=ESV][Psalms 102:15]]* - Nations will fear the name of the LORD, and all the kings of the earth will fear your glory. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%208%3A13&version=ESV][Proverbs 8:13]]* - The fear of the LORD is hatred of evil. Pride and arrogance and the way of evil and perverted speech I hate. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I do agree with what Michael Heiser has said about bearing God's name. I think that breaking the commandment also involves declaring God's name in vain. Taking the Lord's name in vain involves using it in vain.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%206%3A9&version=ESV][Matthew 6:9]]* - Pray then like this: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%20113%3A2&version=ESV][Psalms 113:2]]* - Blessed be the name of the LORD from this time forth and forevermore! (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

** Saved not by my own works done outside of Him but by His work

+ A thought :: If Jesus, your Lord, asked you to buy an icecream for someone to cheer them up, and then you obediently buy them an icecream, giving the glory to Jesus, then could it be said that it was Jesus who bought the icecream? Or could it be said that that work was done in Christ?

Not of our own works means not of works done outside of Jesus. Good works are works which are done out of faith, out of trusting obedience to His will.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2015%3A17&version=ESV][Romans 15:17]]* - In Christ Jesus, then, I have reason to be proud of my work for God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

When Clement says 'justified by works', he's talking about being justified by faith working through love, doing the law of God by doing the law (commandments) of Christ such as to love one another as He has loved us:

+ [[https://www.earlychristianwritings.com/text/1clement-lightfoot.html][1Clem 30:3]] :: Let us therefore cleave unto those to whom grace is given from God. Let us clothe ourselves in concord, being lowlyminded and temperate, holding ourselves aloof from all back biting and evil speaking, being justified by works and not by words.

+ [[https://www.earlychristianwritings.com/text/1clement-lightfoot.html][1Clem 32:3]] :: They all therefore were glorified and magnified, not through themselves or their own works or the righteous doing which they wrought, but through His will.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A12-13&version=ESV][Romans 2:12-13]]* - For all who have sinned without the law will also perish without the law, and all who have sinned under the law will be judged by the law. For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but *the doers of the law who will be justified.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Yes, I believe that Jesus Christ has paid the price in full for me to be saved, and that is surely what I am leaning on.
The price has been paid in full for me to be saved.

We are slaves to Christ and no other. We're not slaves to sin, we're not slaves to law, we're not slaves to men:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%206%3A19-20&version=ESV][I Corinthians 6:19-20]]* - Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%207%3A23&version=ESV][I Corinthians 7:23]]* - *You were bought with a price; do not become slaves of men*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Peter%202%3A1&version=ESV][II Peter 2:1]]* - But false prophets also arose among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you, who will secretly bring in destructive heresies, even denying *the Master who bought them*, bringing upon themselves swift destruction. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We still do not want to allow sin to reign in our bodies. We're dead to sin, and alive to God, we've been set free from sin and now we must let Jesus reign in our bodies. We must go on obeying Christ Jesus, and not obeying sin:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A6-7&version=ESV][Romans 6:6-7]]* - We know that our old self was crucified with Him so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, that we should no longer be slaves to sin. For anyone who has died has been freed from sin. (engbsb2020eb)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%204%3A7&version=ESV][Genesis 4:7]]* - If you do well, will you not be accepted? And if you do not do well, sin is crouching at the door. Its desire is for you, but you must rule over it. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A11-12&version=ESV][Romans 6:11-12]]* - So you also must consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus. Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal bodies, to make you obey their passions. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Yes, I am having faith in Jesus Christ of Nazareth as the Messiah, who paid the price for my sin. It's continuing to live by faith in Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%202%3A20&version=ESV][Galatians 2:20]]* - I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh *I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

As we hold faith in Jesus, we continue to work for the Lord. Price paid in full doesn't mean going back to being a slave to sin. Price paid in full means Jesus bought us and we're slaves/bondservants to Jesus now:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%203%3A23-25&version=ESV][Colossians 3:23-25]]* - Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men, knowing that from the Lord you will receive the inheritance as your reward. You are serving the Lord Christ. For the wrongdoer will be paid back for the wrong he has done, and there is no partiality. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Not by my works done outside of Him am I saved. He bought me. He will save me from the wrath of God. I continue to have faith in Him and serve and obey Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%205%3A9&version=ESV][Romans 5:9]]* - Since, therefore, we have now been justified by his blood, much more shall we be saved by him from the wrath of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

By grace I am saved, through faith. The works that I do were prepared for me in advance that I should walk in them.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%202%3A8-10&version=ESV][Ephesians 2:8-10]]* - For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Through faith in Jesus Christ, Jesus dwells in our hearts. We are able to better comprehend the love of Christ *while* we are rooted and grounded in love:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%203%3A14-21&version=ESV][Ephesians 3:14-21]]* - For this reason I bow my knees before the Father, from whom every family in heaven and on earth is named, that according to the riches of his glory he may grant you to be strengthened with power through his Spirit in your inner being, so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith—that you, being rooted and grounded in love, may have strength to comprehend with all the saints what is the breadth and length and height and depth, and to know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled with all the fullness of God. Now to him who is able to do far more abundantly than all that we ask or think, according to the power at work within us, to him be glory in the church and in Christ Jesus throughout all generations, forever and ever. Amen. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must continue to hold our faith in Jesus,. We are saved to perpetually trust, believe, love and obey God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2011%3A17-23&version=ESV][Romans 11:17-23]]* - But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, although a wild olive shoot, were grafted in among the others and now share in the nourishing root of the olive tree, do not be arrogant toward the branches. If you are, remember it is not you who support the root, but the root that supports you. Then you will say, Branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in. That is true. They were broken off because of their unbelief, but you stand fast through faith. So do not become proud, but stand in awe. For if God did not spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you. Note then the kindness and the severity of God: severity toward those who have fallen, but God's kindness to you, provided you continue in his kindness. Otherwise you too will be cut off. And even they, if they do not continue in their unbelief, will be grafted in, for God has the power to graft them in again. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A2&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:2]]* - and by which you are being saved, if you hold fast to the word I preached to you—unless you believed in vain. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We want to abide in God's love through following Jesus' commandments, and then nothing can separate us from His love. Remember it's nothing in *creation* (that excludes God Himself because God is not 'created') that can separate us from God's love:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%203%3A8&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 3:8]]* - For now *we live, if you are standing fast in the Lord*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2011%3A20-23&version=ESV][Romans 11:20-23]]* - That is true. *They were broken off because of their unbelief, but you stand fast through faith*. So do not become proud, but stand in awe. For if God did not spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you. Note then the kindness and the severity of God: severity toward those who have fallen, but God's kindness to you, provided you continue in his kindness. Otherwise you too will be cut off. And even they, if they do not continue in their unbelief, will be grafted in, for God has the power to graft them in again. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A36-39&version=ESV][Romans 8:36-39]]* - As it is written, For your sake we are being killed all the day long; we are regarded as sheep to be slaughtered. No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us. For I am sure that neither death nor life, nor angels nor rulers, nor things present nor things to come, nor powers, nor height nor depth, *nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord*.
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A4-7&version=ESV][John 15:4-7]]* - Remain in Me, and I will remain in you. Just as no branch can bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in Me. I am the vine and you are the branches. The one who remains in Me, and I in him, will bear much fruit. For apart from Me you can do nothing. If anyone does not remain in Me, he is like a branch that is thrown away and withers. Such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire, and burned. If you remain in Me and My words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you. (engbsb2020eb)
#+END_QUOTE

Worldly wisdom says you don't need to keep Jesus' commandments to abide in Him.
That is because the world cannot receive Holy Spirit.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15-17&version=ESV][John 14:15-17]]* - If you love me, you will keep my commandments. And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Helper, to be with you forever, even the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees him nor knows him. You know him, for he dwells with you and will be in you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The world who does not love the Truth, and does not agree with Jesus cannot accept this teaching from Him.

But God's wisdom says, like in Romans 2, that peace goes to those who do good.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A9-11&version=ESV][Romans 2:9-11]]* - There will be tribulation and distress for every human being who does evil, the Jew first and also the Greek, but glory and honor and peace for everyone who does good, the Jew first and also the Greek. For God shows no partiality. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The issue is, though, that although God's law is correct when it says that we reap what we sow, a person in their time on the earth may not reap all that is due for their faith and for their works, but will reap the rest of what is coming for them at judgement upon/after they die or at the close of the age:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A39-40&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:39-40]]* - And all these, though commended through their faith, did not receive what was promised, since God had provided something better for us, that apart from us they should not be made perfect. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2024%3A14-16&version=ESV][Acts 24:14-16]]* - But this I confess to you, that according to the Way, which they call a sect, I worship the God of our fathers, believing everything laid down by the Law and written in the Prophets, having a hope in God, which these men themselves accept, that *there will be a resurrection of both the just and the unjust*. So I always take pains to have a clear conscience toward both God and man. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A28-29&version=ESV][John 5:28-29]]* - Do not marvel at this, for an hour is coming when all who are in the tombs will hear his voice and come out, *those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2013%3A30-39&version=ESV][Matthew 13:30-39]]* - Let both grow together until the harvest, and at harvest time I will tell the reapers, Gather the weeds first and bind them in bundles to be burned, but gather the wheat into my barn. He put another parable before them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his field. It is the smallest of all seeds, but when it has grown it is larger than all the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and make nests in its branches. He told them another parable. The kingdom of heaven is like leaven that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, till it was all leavened. All these things Jesus said to the crowds in parables; indeed, he said nothing to them without a parable. This was to fulfill what was spoken by the prophet: I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter what has been hidden since the foundation of the world. Then he left the crowds and went into the house. And his disciples came to him, saying, Explain to us the parable of the weeds of the field. He answered, The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man. The field is the world, and the good seed is the children of the kingdom. The weeds are the sons of the evil one, and the enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the close of the age, and the reapers are angels. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Now when a person has faith that Jesus Christ is the Son of God and has faith in His death and His resurrection, then they will naturally be persecuted while in this world if they also strive to love as commanded according to the law. If someone is actively striving to adhere to Christ's commandments without willfully breaking any of them, whilst holding their faith in the blood of Jesus Christ then the world is going to hate them.
That is because "All who desire to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted" and because the world cannot receive Holy Spirit.

As we hold our faith in Jesus Christ's finished work we still continue to obey God and repent from sin and are sanctified into better obedience, better faith, better obedience of faith.
We must get rid of the idols. Holiness is important.

When we believe God's word given through Jesus, we have passed from death to life. We should definitely then listen to Jesus to see what He has actually spoken.

We must be slaves of Christ, not slaves of sin, in order to abide forever in Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A34-36&version=ESV][John 8:34-36]]* - Jesus answered them, Truly, truly, I say to you, everyone who commits sin is a slave to sin. The slave does not remain in the house forever; the son remains forever. So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So what do we mean by "salvation"? In my understanding it's to be saved to continue in the knowledge of Jesus and Father God forever (if anyone claims to know Jesus but do not follow His commandments, they are a liar),  believing the gospel, trusting His Word and obeying God. Abide in love. The one who abides in love abides in God. Important in defining what love is is that God loved us first by sending His Son to be propitiation for our sin. So the gospel and finished works of Christ is the cornerstone but we must not put Christ to the test. We must forsake idols, etc. follow God's commandments. We should be growing in holiness, and being sanctified, and we should be getting closer to Jesus, not futher away. We must continue trusting and obeying Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2010%3A7-12&version=ESV][I Corinthians 10:7-12]]* - Do not be idolaters as some of them were; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play. We must not indulge in sexual immorality as some of them did, and twenty-three thousand fell in a single day. *We must not put Christ to the test, as some of them did and were destroyed by serpents*, nor grumble, as some of them did and were destroyed by the Destroyer. Now these things happened to them as an example, but they were written down for our instruction, on whom the end ([[https://biblehub.com/interlinear/1_corinthians/10-11.htm][G5056 telē; ends i.e. multiple ends]]) of the ages has come. Therefore *let anyone who thinks that he stands take heed lest he fall.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2017%3A1-3&version=ESV][John 17:1-3]]* - When Jesus had spoken these words, he lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son that the Son may glorify you, since you have given him authority over all flesh, to give eternal life to all whom you have given him. And this is eternal life, that they know you the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A3-4&version=ESV][I John 2:3-4]]* - And by this we know that we have come to know him, if we keep his commandments. Whoever says I know him but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2010%3A43&version=ESV][Acts 10:43]]* - To him all the prophets bear witness that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I believe that former sins are forgiven when we trust in His name, but that we must walk in the light, in the truth, confessing sin and loving one another (particularly our family in Christ) as He commanded for Jesus' blood to continue cleaning us. Jesus is our High Priest Advocating for us as we do this.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Peter%201%3A9&version=ESV][II Peter 1:9]]* - For whoever lacks these qualities is so nearsighted that he is blind, having forgotten that he was cleansed from his former sins. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A7-10&version=ESV][I John 1:7-10]]* - But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin. If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess [[https://biblehub.com/greek/3670.htm][(G3670 homologeó)]] our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. If we say we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We obey the Law by obeying Jesus first and foremost. Serving Jesus we are able to fulfill the requirement of the law, so it's not lawlessness:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A4&version=ESV][Romans 7:4]]* - Likewise, my brothers, you also have died to the law through the body of Christ, so that you may belong to another, to him who has been raised from the dead, in order that we may bear fruit for God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://youtube.com/watch?v=QecyvLgSuN8&t=129][youtube.com: John Piper and Tim Keller Wrestle with Sanctification {@desiringGod} @time: 2 min 9 sec]] :: I think [[https://heritagebooks.org/products/the-gospel-mystery-of-sanctification-marshall.html][Walder Marshall's The Gospel Mystery of Sanctification]] says it
    this way, that "you need the comforts of the Gospel in order to fulfill the law".
    So that's pretty much what I would say too.

We've got to follow Jesus to walk in the light:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A12&version=ESV][John 8:12]]* - Again Jesus spoke to them, saying, I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A6-10&version=ESV][I John 1:6-10]]* - If we say we have fellowship with him while we walk in darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth. But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin. If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess [[https://biblehub.com/greek/3670.htm][(G3670 homologeó)]] our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. If we say we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must love our family in Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A13-17&version=ESV][I John 3:13-17]]* - Do not be surprised, brothers, that the world hates you. We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. Whoever does not love abides in death. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him. By this we know love, that he laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers. But if anyone has the world's goods and sees his brother in need, yet closes his heart against him, how does God's love abide in him? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

For eternal salvation it's still vitally important to be getting holy trusting the gospel. The one who practices righteousness is obeying Jesus (obeying righteousness) while holding faith in the finished works of Christ (trusting in His righteousness). We must practice righteousness:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A20-23&version=ESV][Romans 6:20-23]]* - When you were slaves of sin, you were free in regard to righteousness. But what fruit were you getting at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? The end of those things is death. But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of God, the fruit you get leads to sanctification and its end, eternal life. For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A2-7&version=ESV][I John 3:2-7]]* - Beloved, we are God's children now, and what we will be has not yet appeared; but we know that _when he appears we shall be like him, because we shall see him as he is._ And *everyone who thus hopes in him purifies himself as he is pure*. Everyone who makes a practice of sinning also practices lawlessness; sin is lawlessness. You know that he appeared to take away sins, and in him there is no sin. No one who abides in him keeps on sinning; no one who keeps on sinning has either seen him or /known/ him. Little children, let no one deceive you. Whoever practices righteousness is righteous, as he is righteous. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's vitally important for the believer to abide in love, abide in God, and love comes from God.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A15-16&version=ESV][I John 4:15-16]]* - Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him, and he in God. So we have come to know and to believe the love that God has for us. God is love, and whoever abides in love abides in God, and God abides in him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's also vitally important for the believer for their eternal security to love our family in Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%20139%3A20-21&version=ESV][Psalms 139:20-21]]* - They speak against you with malicious intent; your enemies take your name in vain! Do I not hate (H6962. quwt, loathe) those who hate you, O LORD? And do I not loathe those who rise up against you? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%205%3A9&version=ESV][Hebrews 5:9]]* - And being made perfect, he became the source of eternal salvation to all who obey him, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A21&version=ESV][I John 4:21]]* - And this commandment we have from him: whoever loves God *must* also love his brother. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A15&version=ESV][I John 3:15]]* - Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A16-19&version=ESV][Romans 6:16-19]]* - Do you not know that if you present yourselves to anyone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin, which leads to death, or of obedience, which leads to righteousness? But thanks be to God, that you who were once slaves of sin have become *obedient from the heart* to the standard of teaching to which you were committed, and, having been set free from sin, have become slaves of righteousness. I am speaking in human terms, because of your natural limitations. For just as you once presented your members as slaves to impurity and to lawlessness leading to more lawlessness, so now present your members as slaves to righteousness leading to sanctification. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I want to make a distinction between simply "works" (which may be dead, not done in faith) and obedience. There are things such as loving our family in Christ and forgiving them, or not withholding from helping their family in Christ who is in need which is obedience to God which is not dead works. For example, if I choose to not lie to one another that isn't a work.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A17&version=ESV][I John 3:17]]* - But if anyone has the world's goods and sees his brother in need, yet closes his heart against him, how does God's love abide in him? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2013%3A8&version=ESV][Romans 13:8]]* - Owe no one anything, except to love each other, for the one who loves another has fulfilled the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We're saved to live like this.

Could receiving "one such child in Jesus Christ's name" be regarded as a work that is trusting in oneself apart from Christ? No, because trusting Jesus is obeying Jesus and obeying Jesus is trusting Jesus. Trusting and obeying Jesus are not mutually exclusive:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%209%3A37&version=ESV][Mark 9:37]]* - Whoever receives one such child in my name receives me, and whoever receives me, receives not me but him who sent me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2013%3A20&version=ESV][John 13:20]]* - Truly, truly, I say to you, whoever receives the one I send receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I personally believe that we cooperate with God for "salvation". i.e. reception is obedience is working with God. I.e. faith and obedience are not mutually exclusive, but "obedience" shouldn't be misconstrued with Mosaic-law-keeping:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%205%3A21-6&version=ESV][II Corinthians 5:21-6]]:1* - For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God. Working together with him, then, we appeal to you not to receive the grace of God in vain. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2010%3A40&version=ESV][Matthew 10:40]]* - Whoever receives you receives me, and whoever receives me receives him who sent me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We believe him and that's not our work but God's work.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%206%3A28-29&version=ESV][John 6:28-29]]* - Then they said to him, What must we do, to be doing the works of God? Jesus answered them, This is the work of God, that you believe (G4100 pisteuo) in him whom he has sent. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God wants to bring people to the obedience of faith. We have to hear Jesus' word and believe God who sent Him - we have to believe what God has told Jesus to tell us:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%209%3A35&version=ESV][Luke 9:35]]* - And a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my Son, my Chosen One; listen to him! (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Listening to Jesus, we are already obeying the will of God, who commanded us to listen to Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A14-21&version=ESV][Romans 10:14-21]]* - But how are they to call on him in whom they have not believed? And how are they to believe in him of whom they have never heard? And how are they to hear without someone preaching? And how are they to preach unless they are sent? As it is written, How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the good news! But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Isaiah says, Lord, who has believed what he has heard from us? So faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ. But I ask, have they not heard? Indeed they have, for Their voice has gone out to all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world. But I ask, did Israel not understand? First Moses says, I will make you jealous of those who are not a nation; with a foolish nation I will make you angry. Then Isaiah is so bold as to say, I have been found by those who did not seek me; I have shown myself to those who did not ask for me. But of Israel he says, All day long I have held out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God does work in us when we put our trust in Him, when we trust and obey His Word.

*** Under the right conditions, I don't see a problem with 'working' for God

The motivation has to be right. We do work for God to honour God, and as a response to Him loving us first, and as a response of love for Him forgiving us first, and giving us the gift of eternal life.

We are instructed to work for God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20John%201%3A8&version=ESV][II John 1:8]]* - Watch yourselves, so that you may not lose what we have worked for, but may win a full reward. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

In believing in Jesus, we are guaranteed an inheritance in heaven:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%201%3A13&version=ESV][Ephesians 1:13,14]]* -  In him you also, when you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and believed in him, were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, who is the guarantee of our inheritance until we acquire possession of it, to the praise of his glory.  (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The inheritance is in heaven:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A4&version=ESV][I Peter 1:4]]* - to obtain an inheritance which is imperishable and undefiled and will not fade away, reserved in heaven for you, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We work for the Lord while believing in Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%203%3A23-25&version=ESV][Colossians 3:23-25]]* - Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men, knowing that from the Lord you will receive the inheritance as your reward. You are serving the Lord Christ. For the wrongdoer will be paid back for the wrong he has done, and there is no partiality. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So once again, we are actually instructed to work for God, but it's not wrong under the right conditions:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%206%3A10&version=ESV][Hebrews 6:10]]* - For God is not so unjust as to overlook your work and the love that you showed for his sake in serving the saints, as you still do. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

All the Apostle Paul is saying here, I think is that in "working for God" doesn't imply you have accepted a gift. But, yes, you *can* accept the gift (believe in Jesus) and under that condition work for God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A4&version=ESV][Romans 4:4]]* - Now to the one who works, his wages are not counted as a gift but as his due. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We still really do need to accept the free gift! Actually, it's imperative, no matter how much we've been attempting to work for God, that we accept the free gift from God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A5-8&version=ESV][Romans 4:5-8]]* - And to the one who does not work but trusts him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted as righteousness, just as David also speaks of the blessing of the one to whom God counts righteousness apart from works: Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven, and whose sins are covered; blessed is the man against whom the Lord will not count his sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Yes, we must turn from our wicked ways to obey God - absolutely!:

Obedience is not strictly the same thing as works. Obedience is a heart attitude and we are to be obedient to Christ's teachings:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Titus%201%3A16&version=ESV][Titus 1:16]]* - They profess to know God, but they _deny him by their works_. They are detestable, *disobedient, unfit for any good work*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A16-18&version=ESV][Romans 6:16-18]]* - Do you not know that if you present yourselves to anyone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin, which leads to death, or of obedience, which leads to righteousness? But thanks be to God, that you who were once slaves of sin have become *obedient from the heart* _to the standard of teaching to which you were committed_, and, having been set free from sin, have become slaves of righteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The free gift is eternal life *in* Christ Jesus, our Lord:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A20-23&version=ESV][Romans 6:20-23]]* - When you were slaves of sin, you were free in regard to righteousness. But what fruit were you getting at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? The end of those things is death. But now that you have been _set free from sin_ and have *become slaves of God*, the fruit you get leads to sanctification and its end, eternal life. For the wages of sin is death, but the *free gift of God* is *eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

After believing in Jesus, we must turn from our wicked ways and serve God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A46-49&version=ESV][Luke 6:46-49]]* - Why do you call me Lord, Lord, and not do what I tell you? _Everyone who comes to me and hears my words and does them, I will show you *what he is like: he is like* a man building a house, who dug deep and laid the foundation on the rock_. And when a flood arose, the stream broke against that house and could not shake it, because it had been well built. But the one who hears and does not do them is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation. When the stream broke against it, immediately it fell, and the ruin of that house was great. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus is the definitive Son of God. But we may be adopted as sons through faith in Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A14&version=ESV][John 1:14]]* - And *the Word became flesh* and dwelt among us, and we have seen his glory, glory as of *the only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%203%3A26-29&version=ESV][Galatians 3:26-29]]* - for in Christ Jesus you are all sons of God, through faith. For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is neither male nor female, for you are all *one in Christ Jesus*. And if you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to promise. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus has literally taught people that that if we love our enemies, do good and lend, expecting nothing in return we will be rewarded and be sons of the Most High. This shows that obedience to Jesus is just part of having faith in Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A35-36&version=ESV][Luke 6:35-36]]* - But love your enemies, and do good, and *lend, expecting nothing in return,* and your reward will be great, _and you will be sons of the Most High,_ for he is kind to the ungrateful and the evil. Be merciful, even as your Father is merciful. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The prophets, saints, and servants of Jesus will be rewarded:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%2011%3A18&version=ESV][Revelation of John 11:18]]* - The nations raged, but your wrath came, and the time for the dead to be judged, and for rewarding your servants, the prophets and saints, and those who fear your name, both small and great, and for destroying the destroyers of the earth. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%205%3A12-14&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 5:12-14]]* - We ask you, brothers, to respect those who labor among you and are over you in the Lord and admonish you, and to esteem them very highly in love because of their work. Be at peace among yourselves. And we urge you, brothers, admonish the idle, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, be patient with them all. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I just want to be clear that good works we do in obedience to Jesus are still considered a gift to us. We work out what God has worked for. It's even a gift to be in position of being able to do good works in service to Jesus after He has washed us:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%202%3A8-9&version=ESV][Ephesians 2:8-9]]* - For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%202%3A8&version=NASB][Eph 2:8]]* - For by grace you have been saved through faith ([[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g4102/kjv/tr/0-1/][G4102 pistis]]); and that not of yourselves, it is the gift (G1435 doron) of God; (NASB)
  - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%202%3A9&version=NASB][Eph 2:9]]* - not as a result of works ([[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g2041/nasb95/mgnt/0-1/][G2041 ergon]]), so that no one may boast. (NASB)
  - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%202%3A10&version=NASB][Eph 2:10]]* - For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works ([[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g2041/nasb95/mgnt/0-1/][G2041 ergon]]), which God prepared beforehand so that we would walk in them. (NASB)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_SRC text -n :async :results verbatim code :lang text
  :  1435  doron  do'-ron

   a present; specially, a sacrifice:--gift, offering.
#+END_SRC

#+BEGIN_SRC text -n :async :results verbatim code :lang text
  :  2041  ergon  er'-gon

   from a primary (but obsolete) ergo (to work); toil (as an effort or
   occupation); by implication, an act:--deed, doing, labour, work.
#+END_SRC

Work being done by God in us to sanctify us and bring us fruit for everlasting life *is* work done in faith:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A22&version=ESV][Romans 6:22]]* - But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of God, the fruit you get leads to sanctification and its end, eternal life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%203%3A8&version=ESV][Matthew 3:8]]* - Bear fruit in keeping with repentance. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must be abiding in Jesus to produce fruit, and that means we must have faith in Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A4&version=ESV][John 15:4]]* - Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit by itself, unless it abides in the vine, neither can you, unless you abide in me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

OK, so we should confess [[https://biblehub.com/greek/3670.htm][(G3670 homologeó)]] that Jesus is the Son of God and continue obeying Him in faith:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A15&version=ESV][I John 4:15]]* - Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him, and he in God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So the problem isn't work (even work relating to salvation) but the problem is work that is not done in faith (i.e. dead work).

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%206%3A1&version=ESV][Hebrews 6:1]]* - Therefore let us leave the elementary doctrine of Christ and go on to maturity, not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works and of faith toward God, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%203%3A9&version=ESV][Philippians 3:9]]* - and be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own that comes from the law, but that which comes through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God that *depends on faith* — (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I think that the breastplate of righteousness (breastplate of faith and love) *depends* on faith and love. To love God and our neighbour is our duty:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%205%3A8&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 5:8]]* - But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, having put on *the breastplate of faith and love*, and for a helmet the hope of salvation. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ecclesiastes%2012%3A13&version=ESV][Ecclesiastes 12:13]]* - The end of the matter; all has been heard. Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole duty of man. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A3-6&version=ESV][I John 2:3-6]]* - And by this we know that we have come to know him, if we keep his commandments. Whoever says I know him but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, but *whoever keeps his word, in him truly the love of God is perfected*. By this we may be sure that we are in him: whoever says he abides in him ought to [[strongs:G3784][(G3784 opheilei; ought to, obligated to, has a duty to)]] walk in the same way in which he walked. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2022%3A36-40&version=ESV][Matthew 22:36-40]]* - Teacher, which is the great commandment in the Law? And he said to him, *You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.* This is the great and first commandment. And a second is like it: *You shall love your neighbor as yourself.* _On these two commandments *depend* all the Law and the Prophets._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2016%3A22&version=ESV][I Corinthians 16:22]]* - If anyone has no love for the Lord, let him be accursed. Our Lord, come! (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Everything we do should be done in faith in Jesus Christ, trusting, hoping in, obeying Jesus Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 14:23]]* - But whoever has doubts is condemned if he eats, because the eating is not from faith. For *whatever does not proceed from faith is sin.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A36&version=ESV][John 3:36]]* - Whoever believes ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/pisteuo_n_4100.htm][G4100 pisteuōn]] - /is believing (verb)/) in the Son has eternal life; whoever does not obey ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/544.htm][544. apeitheó]]) the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God remains on him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Everything that we do should be done in real agape love for God and our neighbour and family in Christ, in love for the Truth:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2016%3A14&version=ESV][I Corinthians 16:14]]* - Let all that you do be done in love. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2022%3A37-40&version=ESV][Matthew 22:37-40]]* - And he said to him, You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind. This is the great and first commandment. And a second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments depend all the Law and the Prophets.
#+END_QUOTE

Everything we do shuold be to the glory of God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2010%3A31&version=ESV][I Corinthians 10:31]]* - So, whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

** Eternal security for those who follow Jesus

+ Sermon :: [[https://youtube.com/watch?v=i27b4cE4xyo&t=1513][Eternal Security - Charles Spurgeon Sermon - YouTube @time: 25 min 13 sec]]

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  At the stage they trust in Jesus, they may have no work but I believe at that stage they are justified, when in their heart is obedient, trusting, believing faith in Christ who is their life. But I'm not the one to justify them, God is.
  And I assume that Jesus knows who those people are - He knows that they are His sheep, and that Father God draws those people to Him.
  And when they go through Jesus Christ, the door, they are saved.

  I believe that if a person trusts and believe on God in their heart, believing that they need saving and that Jesus Christ is their Lord and that Jesus Christ died for their transgressions and was raised for their justification - that they have a hearing heart and a _heart that follows Him_ - that they will be saved.
#+END_QUOTE

I simply see no enmity between trusting God for justification through the finished work of the cross by Jesus Christ and trusting God by obeying Jesus Christ. I believe that is a false dichotomy. While faith alone saves, I believe that both belief and obedience (willingness to do the will of God) are intrinsic qualities of faith. God justifies the one who places their faith in Jesus. Having faith in Jesus looks like believing Him and obeying Him. Faith in Jesus looks like trusting Jesus. Therefore, I just focus on trusting Jesus in belief and obedience, and assume God is taking care of the justification issue.

Holding faith in Jesus while going through suffering is sanctifying. Obeying Jesus while going through suffering is sanctifying.
Suffering in and of itself is not sanctifying.

When I realise how much I've been forgiven, how can I /not/ forgive you?

Sanctification is always salvific because sanctification is by faith in Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2016%3A31&version=ESV][Acts 16:31]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A16-18&version=ESV][Acts 26:16-18]]*) and by obedience to Jesus Christ (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A22&version=ESV][I Peter 1:22]]*) and both faith and obedience to Jesus Christ is to do with salvation (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%205%3A9&version=ESV][Hebrews 5:9]]*).

If a person by faith in Jesus Christ keeps His instruction to "not worry about tomorrow", for example, while enduring suffering, that is sanctifying. If Jesus instructed it then to keep the instruction by faith in Jesus Christ while enduring suffering is sanctifying:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%206%3A30-34&version=ESV][Matthew 6:30-34]]* - But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today is alive and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, will he not much more clothe you, O you of little faith? Therefore do not be anxious, saying, What shall we eat? or What shall we drink? or What shall we wear? For the Gentiles seek after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all. But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you. Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus' sacrifice is propitiation for sin (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%202%3A24&version=ESV][I Peter 2:24]]*).

+ [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TNAikc8G1DU][youtube.com:  Why Most Christians Misunderstand Sin and Animal Blood Sacrifices - Michael Heiser {@ stefanlouw6395 }]] :: "Take this bird, take this animal, do this and that and you will be 'cleansed from your sin'"... The Hebrew word for sin and "sin offering" [[https://biblehub.com/hebrew/2402.htm][(H2402 chattaah; sin, sin offering)]] in many circumstances has nothing to do with moral violation. It actually refers to being decontaminated. And it's about doing something to the person to decontaminate them so that they don't contaminate sacred space. All these rituals weren't about curing moral violation. If you committed a moral offence, an abomination, there's no sacrifice for you. You're either put to death or exiled from the community. So the writer of Hebrews actually knows what he was talking about:

And thus we are actually able to love properly because we can be healed by Jesus from moral sin to not practice them anymore:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A19-21&version=ESV][I John 4:19-21]]* - We love because he first loved us. If anyone says, I love God, and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen cannot love God whom he has not seen. And this commandment we have from him: *whoever loves God must also love his brother*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

Then we arrive at having done the will of God for us, to the salvation of our souls:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2010%3A36-39&version=ESV][Hebrews 10:36-39]]* - For _you have need of endurance, so that when you have done the *will of God* you may receive what is promised._ For, Yet a little while, and the coming one will come and will not delay; but my righteous one shall live by faith, and if he shrinks back, my soul has no pleasure in him. But we are not of those who shrink back and are destroyed, but of those who have faith and preserve their souls. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A6-9&version=ESV][I Peter 1:6-9]]* - In this you rejoice, though now for a little while, if necessary, you have been grieved by various trials, so that the tested genuineness of your faith—more precious than gold that perishes though it is tested by fire—may be found to result in praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ. Though you have not seen him, you love him. Though you do not now see him, you believe in him and rejoice with joy that is inexpressible and filled with glory, obtaining the outcome of your faith, the salvation of your souls. (ESV)

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%203%3A35&version=ESV][Mark 3:35]]* - Whoever does the will of God, he is my brother and sister and mother. (ESV)

We must receive Jesus, come to Jesus and believe His words, and endeavour to keep His commandments, loving one another in Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A39-47&version=ESV][John 5:39-47]]* - You search the Scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that bear witness about me, yet you refuse to come to me that you may have life. I do not receive glory from people. _But I know that you do not have the love of God within you. I have come in my Father's name, and you do not receive me._ If another comes in his own name, you will receive him. How can you believe, when you receive glory from one another and do not seek the glory that comes from the only God? Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father. There is one who accuses you: Moses, on whom you have set your hope. If you believed Moses, you would believe me; for he wrote of me. But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words? (ESV)
