But I said to you that you have seen me and yet do not believe. *All that the Father gives me will come to me, and whoever comes to me I will never cast out*. For I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will but the will of him who sent me. And this is the will of him who sent me, that I should lose nothing of all that he has given me, but raise it up on the last day. For *this is the will of my Father, that everyone who looks on the Son and believes in him should have eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day*. So the Jews grumbled about him, because he said, I am the bread that came down from heaven. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We come to Jesus by faith obeying Him from the heart:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A8&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:8]]* - By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to a place that he was to receive as an inheritance. And he went out, not knowing where he was going. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2014%3A28-29&version=ESV][Matthew 14:28-29]]* - And Peter answered him, Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the water. He said, Come. So Peter got out of the boat and walked on the water and came to Jesus. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

- Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God
- everyone who loves the Father loves whoever has been born of him. By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and obey his commandments

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1-6&version=ESV][I John 5:1-6]]* - *Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God*, and *everyone who loves the Father loves whoever has been born of him. By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and obey his commandments*. For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments. And his commandments are not burdensome. For everyone who has been born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that has overcome the world—our faith. Who is it that overcomes the world except the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God? This is he who came by water and blood—Jesus Christ; not by the water only but by the water and the blood. And the Spirit is the one who testifies, because the Spirit is the truth. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The Apostle John delivers I John 5 to his audience (and to us) that we can have assurance of eternal life. Receiving Jesus, accepting the gospel and keeping God's commandments given through Jesus certainly should give us assurance of our salvation. God's testimony is greater. We must believe the Gospel.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A9-13&version=ESV][I John 5:9-13]]* - If we receive the testimony of men, *the testimony of God is greater, for this is the testimony of God that he has borne concerning his Son. Whoever believes in the Son of God has the testimony in himself*. Whoever does not believe God has made him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony that God has borne concerning his Son. And this is the testimony, that God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life. I write these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God that you may know that you have eternal life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%206%3A1%2C6%3A17-18%2C7%3A1&version=ESV][II Corinthians 6:1,6:16-18,7:1]]* - Working together with him, then, we appeal to you not to receive the grace of God in vain. What agreement has the temple of God with idols? For we are the temple of the living God; as God said, I will make my dwelling among them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. Therefore go out from their midst, and be separate from them, says the Lord, and touch no unclean thing; then I will welcome you, and I will be a father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty. Since we have these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of body and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://web.sermonaudio.com/sermons/32625652232493][web.sermonaudio.com: DTBM - body, soul and spirit - Dr. John Barnett]] :: The reason we're supposed to keep clean and not let our flesh and spirit get
    defiled is that God made a promise. He says, "I'm going to dwell in you. I'm
    going to walk among you. I'm going to be your God. You're going to be my
    people." And this is what we're supposed to do, verse 17: "Come out from among
    them, be separate. Don't touch what is unclean and I will receive you. I will
    be a Father to you. You'll be my sons and daughters," says the Lord Almighty.
    Boy, that is about the most assuring verse in the Bible. God says, I'm gonna
    live in you. I'm your father, you're my children. You're going to know and go
    through life knowing that you belong to me and that I live within you and
    you're never alone and I'm always with you and all that stuff. What happens if
    you don't obey the "don't touch what is unclean" part, verse 17? You lose that
    assurance.

** Some indicators to know for sure you are saved and being saved

+ Talk :: [[https://youtube.com/watch?v=0y-hQrI_sTA&t=779][This is how you can know for SURE that you are saved | Assurance of Salvation | Kaci Nicole - YouTube @time: 12 min 59 sec]]

For assurance of salvation, here's some indicators:
- Trust in Jesus. Pursuaded by Jesus Christ
  - Believe that He is the Messiah and Son of God
- Humility. Broken over their sin, and grateful by what Jesus has done.
  - A change of heart like the example of the repentant thief (Read: *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2027%3A43-44&version=ESV][Matt 27:43-44]]* and *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2023%3A39-43&version=ESV][Luke 23:39-43]]*).
    - the repentant thief had come to a place of humility and fear of God
    - he had an awareness of his own sin and the reality of judgement
    - he knew that it was only by Jesus, not by his own works that he could be saved
    - he affirmed the Lordship and deity of Christ
  - A hatred of one's own sin
  - Accepted forgiveness from God
- Treasuring and valuing Jesus and His words
- _Obedience_ to Jesus
  - Passing forward forgiveness and mercy to others
- That you have [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9nlvj9nNVCA][kept the faith despite trials and testing]]
  - What I mean by this is that confidence grows as you go through trials
- Receiving the Spirit of God
- Believing the testimony that God has borne of His Son (Read: [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A9-13&version=ESV][I John 5:9-13]] and [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%206%3A17-20&version=ESV][Hebrews 6:17-20]])
- Treasuring our family in Christ (Read: [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A14-20&version=ESV][I John 3:14-20]])
  - It's true that like Abraham, confidence will come as a result of keeping the faith and continuing to obey God

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A21-23&version=ESV][I John 3:21-23]]* - Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence before God; and whatever we ask we receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do what pleases him. And this is his commandment, that we believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as he has commanded us. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

An indication that we have passed from death to life is that we [[https://biblehub.com/interlinear/1_john/3-14.htm][agapé]] / treasure our family in Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A14-20&version=ESV][I John 3:14-20]]* - We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love (*[[https://biblehub.com/interlinear/1_john/3-14.htm][agapōmen]]*) the brothers. Whoever does not love abides in death. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him. By this we know love, that he laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers. But if anyone has the world's goods and sees his brother in need, yet closes his heart against him, how does God's love abide in him? Little children, let us not love in word or talk but in deed and in truth. By this we shall know that we are of the truth and reassure our heart before him; for whenever our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and he knows everything. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must believe God's testimony concerning Jesus. God's testimony is greatest:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A9-13&version=ESV][I John 5:9-13]]* - If we receive the testimony of men, the testimony of God is greater, for this is the testimony of God that he has borne concerning his Son. Whoever believes in the Son of God has the testimony in himself. Whoever does not believe God has made him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony that God has borne concerning his Son. And this is the testimony, that God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life. I write these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God that you may know that you have eternal life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%206%3A17-20&version=ESV][Hebrews 6:17-20]]* - So when God desired to show more convincingly to the heirs of the promise the unchangeable character of his purpose, he guaranteed it with an oath, so that by two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled for refuge might have strong encouragement to hold fast to the hope set before us. We have this as a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul, a hope that enters into the inner place behind the curtain, where Jesus has gone as a forerunner on our behalf, having become a high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Doing what pleases God brings confidence, as *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A21-23&version=ESV][I John 3:21-23]]* says.

/*1. A change of heart towards humility, fear of God, belief and trust in Jesus to be saved, an awareness of one's own sin and the reality of judgement, and acknowledging Jesus' Lordship and deity:*/

All the thief could do was look to Jesus and cry out for mercy but thankfully that is all he needed.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *My thoughts:* I still think that the thief obeyed the gospel by submitting to the righteousness of God. He had obeyed the gospel, even preached the gospel from his cross, and was no longer an enemy of the cross of Christ. I think if given the opportunity he would have continued on in obedience to Jesus and even in good works of service to Jesus because of his repentant heart. He acknowledged Jesus was righteous and did not deserve the punishment that they deserved, he asked Jesus to remember him in His kingdom, and had the fear of God in his heart which would have caused him to not turn from God.
#+END_QUOTE

Is repentance from sin necessary for salvation? It generally is necessary. We renounce the sinful habits and God cleans us up as we obey Him by faith. The liberty that God provides is not being a slave/servant of sin/corruption. God's grace trains us to renounce sin, and it's not for us to double-down on sin:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Peter%202%3A14-20&version=ESV][II Peter 2:14-20]]* - Having *eyes full of adultery*, and that cannot cease from sin; beguiling unstable souls: an *heart they have exercised with covetous practices*; cursed children: Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness; But was rebuked for his iniquity: the dumb ass speaking with man’s voice forbad the madness of the prophet. These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever. For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, *they allure through the lusts of the flesh*, through much wantonness, those that were clean escaped from them who live in error. *While they promise them liberty, they themselves are the servants of corruption*: for of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he brought in bondage. _For *if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning*._ (KJV)
#+END_QUOTE

If a person is unrepentant from sin then it is better that their body is destroyed so their spirit may be saved. In the case of the thief on the cross, his body *was* destroyed. If he stayed around, he probably would have renounced ungodliness and pursued holiness:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%205%3A1-5&version=ESV][I Corinthians 5:1-5]]* - It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and of a kind that is not tolerated even among pagans, for a man has his father's wife. And you are arrogant! Ought you not rather to mourn? Let him who has done this be removed from among you. For though absent in body, I am present in spirit; and as if present, I have already pronounced judgment on the one who did such a thing. When you are assembled in the name of the Lord Jesus and my spirit is present, with the power of our Lord Jesus, you are to deliver this man to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

This was all that was required of him for salvation and the same is true for us (in terms of minimums) but we should continue in faith, love and obedience:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  The thief didn't get to go learn the bible, or get baptised or begin to follow Jesus in the way that he lived, but that is not to say that those things are not important because they are.
  Those are things that God has commanded us to do, and if we love God then we should want to be obedient in doing those things. The distinction is that those things don't earn our salvation but they are the
  fruit of a heart that has truly put faith in Jesus. I think that the thief would have gone on to do those things, he just never had a chance. But you might be thinking: I don't always obey Jesus.
  I still wrestle with sin and the answer is that you won't perfectly obey Jesus. You will still have sin in your life because Jesus will be continuing to work that out in you until the day that you die.
  But if you desire to know the God of the Bible and to love God and to obey God's word, that in itself is evidence that God is at work in your heart because we cannot do those things on our own.
  Even if we aren't yet fully where we know we ought to be with those things, the fact that they're there is an indication and that we are continuing to grow in grace.
#+END_QUOTE

Both robbers start off mocking Jesus but then one of the robbers has a change of heart:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2027%3A43-44&version=ESV][Matthew 27:43-44]]* - He trusts in God; let God deliver him now, if he desires him. For he said, I am the Son of God. And the robbers who were crucified with him also reviled him in the same way. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2015%3A32&version=ESV][Mark 15:32]]* - Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross that we may see and believe. Those who were crucified with him also reviled him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2023%3A39-43&version=ESV][Luke 23:39-43]]* - One of the criminals who were hanged railed at him, saying, Are you not the Christ? Save yourself and us! But the other rebuked him, saying, Do you not fear God, since you are under the same sentence of condemnation? And we indeed justly, for we are receiving the due reward of our deeds; but this man has done nothing wrong. And he said, Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom. And he said to him, Truly, I say to you, today you will be with me in Paradise. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The fear of God should mean we want to do what pleases God - it's a heart that wishes to have a good conscience with God - wishes for God's commendation and not His wrath:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2016%3A6&version=ESV][Proverbs 16:6]]* - By steadfast love and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of the LORD one turns away from evil. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We want to always have the fear of God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2014%3A27&version=ESV][Proverbs 14:27]]* - The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, that one may turn away from the snares of death. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Malachi%201%3A6&version=ESV][Malachi 1:6]]* - A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If then I am a father, where is my honor? And if I am a master, where is my fear? says the LORD of hosts to you, O priests, who despise my name. But you say, How have we despised your name? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's great having a good conscience with God, and a relationship with God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2023%3A17&version=ESV][Proverbs 23:17]]* - Let not your heart envy sinners, but continue in the fear of the LORD all the day. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We're supposed to live this way as Christians:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%209%3A31&version=ESV][Acts 9:31]]* - So the church throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace and was being built up. And walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, it multiplied. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

/*2. We must have a hatred of one's own sin:*/

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%208%3A13&version=ESV][Proverbs 8:13]]* - The fear of the LORD is hatred of evil. Pride and arrogance and the way of evil and perverted speech I hate. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  To be a Christian doesn't mean that we are without sin this side of heaven, but it does mean that we have a hatred for our own sin, that we are wrestling with the flesh that is still inside us even as Jesus is making us new, rather than being complacent over our sin.
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A19-20&version=ESV][Romans 7:19-20]]* - For I do not do the good I want, but the evil I do not want is what I keep on doing. Now if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but sin that dwells within me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's really important to turn from sin:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A5-6&version=ESV][I John 3:5-6]]* - You know that he appeared to take away sins, and in him there is no sin. No one who abides in him keeps on sinning; no one who keeps on sinning has either seen him or /known/ him.
#+END_QUOTE

We endeavour to be justified through faithful obedience to Jesus, and if we fall short, we still believe Christ has us covered. But we do endeavour, we do try:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%202%3A17&version=ESV][Galatians 2:17]]* - But if, in our endeavor to be justified in Christ, we too were found to be sinners, is Christ then a servant of sin? Certainly not! (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%203%3A15&version=ESV][I Peter 3:15]]* - but *in your hearts regard Christ the Lord as holy*, always being prepared to make a defense to anyone who asks you for a reason for the hope that is in you; (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

[[https://youtube.com/watch?v=t76o8Y7AA7M&t=136][youtube.com: Paul Washer - Ongoing Sin @time: 2 min 16 sec]]

/*3. Our faith has been tested, and results in praise and glory and honour at the revelation of Jesus Christ:*/

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A6-7&version=ESV][I Peter 1:6-7]]* - In this you rejoice, though now for a little while, if necessary, you have been grieved by various trials, so that the tested genuineness of your faith—more precious than gold that perishes though it is tested by fire—may be found to result in praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%201%3A22&version=ESV][II Corinthians 1:22]]* - and who has also put his seal on us and given us his Spirit in our hearts as a guarantee. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A13-16&version=ESV][I John 4:13-16]]* - By this we know that we abide in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit. #+END_QUOTE

** Indicators that we are _of the truth_
A strong indicator that we are _of the truth_ is that against every condemnation, we know God is greater than our heart and knows everything

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A18-20&version=ESV][I John 3:18-20]]* - Little children, let us not love in word or talk but in deed and in truth. By this we shall know that we are of the truth and reassure our heart before him; for whenever our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and he knows everything.
#+END_QUOTE

A strong indicator that we are _of the truth_ is that we have the fear of Jehovah God in our hearts, that we do not turn from Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Jeremiah%2032%3A40&version=ESV][Jeremiah 32:40]]* - I will make with them an everlasting covenant, that I will not turn away from doing good to them. And *I will put the fear of me in their hearts, that they may not turn from me.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

More strong indicators that we are _of the truth_ are that:
- if our heart does not condemn us, we  have confidence before God:
- whatever we ask of God, we receive from Him
  - because we keep His commandments and do what pleases Him
    - we know we are believing in the name of His Son Jesus Christ, and
    - we know we are loving one another in just the way He has commanded us (I John 3:14-20, I John 5:1-2),
      - and in deed also gives us extra confidence
      - His commandments have become unburdensome for us

*** The light

+ Light :: Light is effectively, the agape (treasuring, soul-binding) love of the Truth in Truth - in Truth, agape loving the Truth and those who belong to the Truth. Darkness is not having the agape love of the Truth but rather agape-loving darkness. Light is walking in agape love of the Truth and and agape love of those who belong to the Truth. And doing good to all, desiring all to come to the knowledge of the Truth, and for the sake of the Truth and God's desire of all to come to the knowledge of the Truth to demonstrate obedience to the Truth for others and do good to others, even our enemies. We *must* agape those who are in the light, who are our family in Christ. We don't bind ourselves to darkness or to demons.

*** God's kindness is meant to lead us to repentance from sin

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A4&version=ESV][Romans 2:4]]* - Or do you presume on the riches of his kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that God's kindness is meant to lead you to repentance? (ESV)

*** Subsequent behaviour - the Golden Rule and the Royal Law, faith working through love

When it comes to 'works' and 'law-keeping', I believe disciples of Jesus should know they have been forgiven by grace through faith and they should also practice their righteousness, but the "works" is not the "obedience". The works come out of obedience, out of being a "doer of the law". Christians should *both* submit to the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ, having the imputed righteousness of Christ that we believe we have as we are walking with Christ and Christians should practice righteousness too (as Jesus said, "go and sin no more"), and Christians should seek to keep accountability primarily to God in regards to the law because He sees everything, and *secondarily* have good conscience with men, to love as Jesus loved, and give to Caesar what is Caesar's, but give to God what is God's - and God owns our hearts - and we should be prepared to die for Jesus, and remain faithful to Jesus.
When a person practices their righteousness, then they are "doers of the law" from the heart. A person who has accepted forgiveness for their sin by the atonement made in Jesus' blood should certainly endeavour after that to fulfill practically the Royal Law, that is to love one's neighbour as themself, even owing that to other people:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2013%3A8&version=ESV][Romans 13:8]]* - Owe no one anything, except to love each other, for the one who loves another has fulfilled the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%206%3A2-6&version=ESV][Galatians 6:2-6]]* - *Bear one another's burdens*, and so fulfill the law of Christ. For if anyone thinks he is something, when he is nothing, he deceives himself. But _let each one test his own work, and then his reason to boast will be in himself alone and not in his neighbor._ *For each will have to bear his own load.* One who is taught the word *must share* all good things with the one who teaches. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A22&version=ESV][I Peter 1:22]]* - Having *purified your souls by your obedience to the truth for a sincere brotherly love*, love one another earnestly from a pure heart, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The Golden Rule, I think explains that we should behave like a child of Father God who is by nature Good and gives good gifts to His children, and gifts that are truly good, far exceeding any amount of favour we might show our own children. As we behave like a child of Father God, believing the gospel of Jesus, and loving with Christ's love, we can really say our Father is God, as a child takes after their parents, and a child of Father God behaves like Jesus and follows Jesus. We try to follow Jesus, and imitate Christ's pattern, as Christ is *the* Son of God.

I _do *not* think_ the Golden Rule is saying that "God is humanity." _Neither do I think_ the Golden Rule is saying that God treats us precisely how we treat others.

I think the Golden Rule is really telling us to be loving, and love our enemies, as we would want to be loved by our enemies - love people the way Father God loves us:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%207%3A9-12&version=ESV][Matthew 7:9-12]]* - Or which one of you, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone? So *whatever you wish that others would do to you, do also to them*, for this is the Law and the Prophets. (ESV)

Copyright and patents are very different things.
A completed product that may have millions of parts may be copyrighted as it is sent out as a product.
An idea of a machine comprised of a few specified components may be patented without even a finished prduct and that patent might last for decades.

Let's say someone patented the simple idea of a hand rail for a staircase as staircases were coming to mass usage, and it's only natural to have a hand rail,
but now no-one is allowed to make knobs at the end of staircase handrails because it involves making a handrail.
Handrails and knobs at the end of the handrails are very natural progressions.

So it's absurd to patent the handrail.

In reality, two people can independently come up with an invention.

Patents in theory help a fledgling small business to succeed, but software patents actually do far more harm than good now.
There was a time when it was more useful and fair, but it doesn't make much sense anymore because the programming is about as common as writing and algebra.
It wouldn't make sense for it to be allowable to "patent long division", a "literary device", "an art technique" or a verbal technique such as "verbally communicating using clicking, popping and whistling sounds".
Neither does it make sense to be allowable to patent incremental steps in programming now that programming has matured to the point at which it's a basic skill that might be taught in high school.
Why? Because upskilling and basic literacy of humans and the natural development of human beings are important to protect.
It's bizarre that humans would be stymied from developing useful skills and businesses while machines are trained without restraint because big tech are lawless thieves who the government has endorsed their practice of stealing from others to advance their business.
It's parasitic.

Besides those reasons for abolishing software patents,
software these days can be hidden behind APIs, and that is a more reasonable alternative form of protection for software mechanisms than patents,
similar to how, say, the secret recipes of the 11 Herbs and Spices and of Coca-Cola are guarded secrets.

Software patents no longer make any sense.
It would be like patenting a particular arrangement of flowers such that nobody is allowed to make gardens with that arrangement of flowers.

The patent system has been perverted to oppress people and prevent them from thinking and building and doing what is natural with our brains.
Language models do for software something similar to what invention of imaginary/complex numbers did for algebra.
Applied to other forms of media, the technology extends what can be done with existing media.
But new technology isn't licence to boycot the original intention of the protections of the copyright licences on the data,
but rather the licenses should also be able to protect the data from being captured by AI models from Big Tech prospectors who prey on vulnerable people
to gobble up their data, somehow believing that having this technology gives them licence now to steal (because it's transformative technology).
That's as deluded as it would be to think that inventing a gun gives a person licence now to murder with a gun because it's a transformative technology.
It would be right in my view that in face of a so-called "transformative technology" that is being introduced to society,
that the powers of existing copyright licences are likewise projected into this "new area" of application.
As new technology extends what can be feasibly done with existing media, so too the powers of the licences connected with that media
should also extend into what that can be done with that media by that new technology.

If a person wanted to go beyond *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Exodus%2020%3A13&version=ESV][Exodus 20:13]]* to avoid eating meat to spare the lives of animals and make themself accountable to God over that in the hope it pleases God then I admire that commitment actually, but I wouldn't let anyone pass judgement on me over eating meat myself:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2014%3A16&version=ESV][Romans 14:16]]* - So do not let what you regard as good be spoken of as evil. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I definitely think that "killing animals" for no good reason, say for sport, is not good.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2011%3A6-9&version=ESV][Isaiah 11:6-9]]* - The wolf shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the young goat, and the calf and the lion and the fattened calf together; and a little child shall lead them. The cow and the bear shall graze; their young shall lie down together; and the lion shall eat straw like the ox. The nursing child shall play over the hole of the cobra, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the adder's den. *They shall not hurt or destroy in all my holy mountain; for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Christians should *both* submit to the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ, having the imputed righteousness of Christ that we believe we have as we are walking with Christ and Christians should practice righteousness too (as Jesus said, "go and sin no more"), and Christians should seek to keep accountability primarily to God in regards to the law because He sees everything, and *secondarily* have good conscience with men, to love as Jesus loved, and give to Caesar what is Caesar's, but give to God what is God's - and God owns our hearts - and we should be prepared to die for Jesus, and remain faithful to Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A2-7&version=ESV][Matthew 23:2-7]]* - The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses' seat, so practice and observe whatever they tell you—but not what they do. For they preach, but do not practice. They tie up heavy burdens, hard to bear, and lay them on people's shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to move them with their finger. They do all their deeds to be seen by others. For they make their phylacteries broad and their fringes long, and they love the place of honor at feasts and the best seats in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces and being called rabbi by others. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Having placed faith in Christ, been born-again, all things being made new, God making me new, having become a new person entirely, what about worldly debt which I had owed before I was born-again? What are my obligations with that?
Could I for example, "only go to heaven if I payed back that debt?"
As far as my ultimate standing with God goes, no, I don't think I *would* need to pay back all of that debt to go to heaven.
But in order to be found blameless to the people I owe in the eyes of non-Christians in this world, then yes, I would.
But my identity is in Christ and not in the world.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%202%3A13-14&version=ESV][Colossians 2:13-14]]* - And you, who were dead in your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, God made alive together with him, having forgiven us all our trespasses, by canceling the record of debt that stood against us with its legal demands. This he set aside, nailing it to the cross. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So yes, the righteous does give, and pay back what is borrowed, but as far as our legal standing with God goes, our debt was paid, God puts us into Christ and we are made new. He gives us a clean slate in Christ. I've been made new and clean and born-again. Therefore, I have a righteous standing with God. But the principle of the righteous paying back what they borrow and being generous and giving remains. So going forward, debt paid, we must still practice righteousness:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2037%3A21&version=ESV][Psalms 37:21]]* - The wicked borrows but does not pay back, but the righteous is generous and gives; (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2022%3A21&version=ESV][Matthew 22:21]]* - They said, Caesar's. Then he said to them, Therefore render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We love in the knowledge we have already *been* loved first when God sent Jesus Christ to pay for our sin with His blood. I was born-again of the Spirit and regenerated on [[https://web.archive.org/web/20220402091720/https://mullikine.github.io/posts/astral-projection/][2 April 2022]].

That's how we are found *in* God, by accepting that He loved us first through Jesus Christ, and God puts us into Him.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2013%3A6-7&version=ESV][John 13:6-7]]* - He came to Simon Peter, who said to him, Lord, do you wash my feet? Jesus answered him, What I am doing you do not understand now, but afterward you will understand. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

After being born-again of the spirit I don't say I'm completely sinless, or that I could not commit sin - that would be deceiving myself:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A7-9&version=ESV][I John 1:7-9]]* - But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin. If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess [[https://biblehub.com/greek/3670.htm][(G3670 homologeó)]] our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

In fact, it's clear that we must continue on in Jesus Christ's teaching after having been forgiven, and that includes being merciful to other people, as we have received mercy.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2018%3A21-35&version=ESV][Matthew 18:21-35]]* - Then Peter came up and said to him, Lord, how often will my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? As many as seven times? Jesus said to him, I do not say to you seven times, but seventy times seven. Therefore the kingdom of heaven may be compared to a king who wished to settle accounts with his servants. When he began to settle, one was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents. And since he could not pay, his master ordered him to be sold, with his wife and children and all that he had, and payment to be made. So the servant fell on his knees, imploring him, Have patience with me, and I will pay you everything. And out of pity for him, the master of that servant released him and forgave him the debt. But when that same servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii, and seizing him, he began to choke him, saying, Pay what you owe. So his fellow servant fell down and pleaded with him, Have patience with me, and I will pay you. He refused and went and put him in prison until he should pay the debt. When his fellow servants saw what had taken place, they were greatly distressed, and they went and reported to their master all that had taken place. Then his master summoned him and said to him, *You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you pleaded with me. And should not you have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?* And in anger his master delivered him to the jailers, until he should pay all his debt. So also my heavenly Father will do to every one of you, if you do not *forgive your brother from your heart.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%203%3A13&version=ESV][Colossians 3:13]]* - bearing with one another and, if one has a complaint against another, forgiving each other; as the Lord has forgiven you, so _you also must forgive._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But what about me with my situation regarding court? I don't know everything. Can I confess what I don't know? Sometimes I think we just have to deny self. I don't have an issue with that. But I do have an issue with what feels like injury my soul, and relentless ongoing spiritual attack after having sought to try to remain faithful to and obey Jesus regarding the situation. But it doesn't feel like freedom has been given to me on the other side of that, that I might live to my conviction, my decision, without what seems like satanic oppression/harassment/torment:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%204%3A17&version=ESV][James 4:17]]* - So whoever knows the right thing to do and fails to do it, for him it is sin. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But I continue walking in the light, in trusting obedience to Jesus, and Jesus' blood continues to cleanse me from all sin:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%201%3A7-9&version=ESV][I John 1:7-9]]* - But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin. If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess [[https://biblehub.com/greek/3670.htm][(G3670 homologeó)]] our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It is clear that following Jesus helps us to not sin, which means that the destructiveness of sin for us is still a reality if we are not following Jesus. We get on top of it by following Jesus and walking by His Spirit:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A14-16&version=ESV][Galatians 5:14-16]]* - For *the whole law is fulfilled in one word [[strongs:G3056][(G3056 logō)]]: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.* But if you bite and devour one another, watch out that you are not consumed by one another. But I say, *walk by the Spirit*, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Someone who has just been "born of God" is an infant in Christ and is counted as a child of God, but an infant. I mention this because an infant grows into maturity, into living in the Spirit the way that God does, into thinking and behaving as a mature child of God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%203%3A1&version=ESV][I Corinthians 3:1]]* - But I, brothers, could not address you as spiritual people, but as people of the flesh, as infants in Christ. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A14&version=ESV][Romans 8:14]]* - For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We've got to continue in Jesus' teachings/commandments:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20John%201%3A9-10&version=ESV][II John 1:9-10]]* - Everyone who goes on ahead and does not abide in the teaching of Christ, does not have God. Whoever abides in the teaching has both _the Father and the Son._ If anyone comes to you and does not bring this teaching, do not receive him into your house or give him any greeting, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Those who find a place for God's word in their heart, those who are of the truth, who receive God's word, they listen to what Jesus has said. They are not repulsed by Jesus' words, nor are they repulsed by Jesus' commandments. They are not repulsed by who Jesus is, and they are not repulsed by what Jesus has done as recorded in Scripture:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2018%3A37&version=ESV][John 18:37]]* - Then Pilate said to him, So you are a king? Jesus answered, You say that I am a king. For this purpose I was born and for this purpose I have come into the world—to bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth listens to my voice. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A37-47&version=ESV][John 8:37-47]]* - I know that you are offspring of Abraham; yet you seek to kill me because my word finds no place in you. I speak of what I have seen with my Father, and you do what you have heard from your father. They answered him, Abraham is our father. Jesus said to them, If you were Abraham's children, you would be doing what Abraham did, but now you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. This is not what Abraham did. You are doing what your father did. They said to him, We were not born of sexual immorality. We have one Father—even God. Jesus said to them, If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came from God and I am here. I came not of my own accord, but he sent me. *Why do you not understand what I say? It is because you cannot bear to hear my word. You are of your father the devil, and your will is to do your father's desires*. He was a murderer from the beginning, and has nothing to do with the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks out of his own character, for he is a liar and the father of lies. But because I tell the truth, you do not believe me. Which one of you convicts me of sin? *If I tell the truth, why do you not believe me? Whoever is of God hears the words of God. The reason why you do not hear them is that you are not of God*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%206%3A45&version=ESV][John 6:45]]* - It is written in the Prophets, And they will all be taught by God. *Everyone* who has heard *and learned* from the Father comes to me— (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus' commandments are rock-solid and they are eternal:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%207%3A24&version=ESV][Matthew 7:24]]* - Everyone then who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house on the rock. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2010%3A25&version=ESV][Proverbs 10:25]]* - When the tempest passes, the wicked is no more, but the righteous is established forever. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2024%3A35&version=ESV][Matthew 24:35]]* - Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We can trust Jesus' commandments as we trust Jesus Himself. If a person keeps them out of love for Jesus, with faith in Jesus, God can do some awesome stuff in and through that. Even the commandment to "give to the one who asks", for example, might be met with 'worldly' wisdom to deter someone from trusting God. Distrust for Jesus' commandments deters people from keeping them. But if we obey them out of faith and love for Jesus (and do so in a lawful way, not like a Robin-Hood way, for example), God absolutely sees our efforts in maintaining a good conscience keeping His commandments seeking to please God and not man. He can really use people who are keeping Jesus' commandments in faith:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%206%3A10&version=ESV][Hebrews 6:10]]* - For God is not so unjust as to overlook your work and the love that you showed for his sake in serving the saints, as you still do. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Thinking with faith in Jesus, maintaining a good conscience with God, believing He exist and that He rewards those who seek Him, trusting in God for the outcome, God is not so unjust that He'd punish us for acting in faith. If God works all things for good for those who love Him, and the one who keeps Jesus' commandments is the one that loves Him, and since suffering for righteousness-sake is a commendable thing in God's sight then we can trust God to use our obedient commandment-keeping (especially Jesus' commandments) towards our good or for the good of others.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A28&version=ESV][Romans 8:28]]* - And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2034%3A19&version=ESV][Psalms 34:19]]* - Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the LORD delivers him out of them all. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

One of Jesus' teachings we need to continue on in is to love those who hate us.

Be perfect as your heavenly Father is perfect - love also the ones who hate you:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A38-48&version=ESV][Matthew 5:38-48]]* - You have heard that it was said, An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth. But I say to you, *Do not resist the one who is evil*. But *if anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also*. And *if anyone would sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well*. And *if anyone forces you to go one mile, go with him two miles*. *Give to the one who begs from you, and do not refuse the one who would borrow from you*. You have heard that it was said, You shall love your neighbor and hate ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/3404.htm][3404. miseó, 3404 miséō – properly, to detest (on a comparative basis); hence, denounce; to love someone or something less than someone (something) else, i.e. to renounce one choice in favor of another.]]) your enemy. But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the just and on the unjust. For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same? And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing than others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same? You therefore must be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Keep in mind that what Jesus means by "perfect" is possible, because Jesus said the following, and this is how:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2019%3A21&version=ESV][Matthew 19:21]]* - Jesus said to him, If you would be perfect, go, sell what you possess and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%207%3A11&version=ESV][Hebrews 7:11]]* - Now if perfection had been attainable through the Levitical priesthood (for under it the people received the law), what further need would there have been for another priest to arise after the order of Melchizedek, rather than one named after the order of Aaron? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

In Christ, we must "be perfect" in the sense that Jesus means when He says "You, therefore, must be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect." In Christ, we must not hate one another. In Christ, we *must* agape love one another:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%203%3A13-14&version=ESV][Colossians 3:13-14]]* - Bear with one another and forgive any complaint you may have against someone else. Forgive as the Lord forgave you. And over all these virtues put on love (*[[https://biblehub.com/greek/agape_n_26.htm][26. agapé]]*), which is the bond of perfect unity. (engbsb2020eb)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A19-21&version=ESV][I John 4:19-21]]* - We love because he first loved us. If anyone says, I love God, and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen cannot love God whom he has not seen. And this commandment we have from him: *whoever loves God must also love his brother*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A10&version=ESV][I John 3:10]]* - By this it is evident who are the children of God, and who are the children of the devil: whoever does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is the one who does not love his brother. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A17&version=ESV][I John 4:17]]* - By this is love perfected with us, so that we may have confidence for the day of judgment, because as he is so also are we in this world. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A34-36&version=ESV][John 8:34-36]]* - Jesus answered them, Truly, truly, I say to you, everyone who commits sin is a slave to sin. The slave does not remain in the house forever; the son remains forever. So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

If you love Jesus, keep His commandments. The one who keeps Jesus' commandments is the one who loves Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15&version=ESV][John 14:15]]* - If you love me, you will keep my commandments. (ESV)

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A21&version=ESV][John 14:21]]* - Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves me. And he who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A2-4&version=ESV][I John 3:2-4]]* - Beloved, we are God's children now, and what we will be has not yet appeared; but we know that _when he appears we shall be like him, because we shall see him as he is._ And *everyone who thus hopes in him purifies himself as he is pure*. Everyone who makes a practice of sinning also practices lawlessness; sin is lawlessness. (ESV)

A person who is mature in Christ has faith in Christ, follows the teachings of Christ and the pattern of His life, and is spiritually minded, and thinks with Christ's wisdom, not worldly wisdom, and lives for the will of God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Colossians%201%3A28&version=ESV][Colossians 1:28]]* - Him we proclaim, warning everyone and teaching everyone with all wisdom, that we may present everyone mature in Christ. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must live in the spirit the way God does, not for human passions, but for the will of God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%204%3A1-6&version=ESV][I Peter 4:1-6]]* - *Since therefore Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves with the same way of thinking, for whoever has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin, so as to live for the rest of the time in the flesh no longer for human passions but for the will of God*. The time that is past suffices for doing what the Gentiles want to do, living in sensuality, passions, drunkenness, orgies, drinking parties, and lawless idolatry. With respect to this they are surprised when you do not join them in the same flood of debauchery, and they malign you; but they will give account to him who is ready to judge the living and the dead. For this is why the gospel was preached even to those who are dead, that though judged in the flesh the way people are, they might *live in the spirit the way God does.* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A1-17&version=ESV][Romans 8:1-17]]* - There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life has set you free in Christ Jesus from the law of sin and death. For God has done what the law, weakened by the flesh, could not do. By sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, he condemned sin in the flesh, in order that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the flesh but according to the Spirit. For those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, but those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit. To set the mind on the flesh [[strongs:G4561][(G4561 sarx)]] is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace. For the mind that is set on the flesh [[strongs:G4561][(G4561 sarx)]] is hostile to God, for it does not submit to God's law; indeed, it cannot. Those who are in the flesh cannot please God. You, however, are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if in fact the Spirit of God dwells in you. Anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him. But if Christ is in you, although the body is dead because of sin, the Spirit is life because of righteousness. If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you. So then, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh. For if you live according to the flesh you will die, but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live. For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God. For you did not receive the spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you have received the Spirit of adoption as sons, by whom we cry, Abba! Father! The Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God, and if children, then heirs—heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ, *provided we suffer with him in order that we may also be glorified with him*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Living by the Golden Rule (or better, the Royal Law) still comes after having been forgiven by Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%207%3A12&version=ESV][Matthew 7:12]]* - So whatever you wish that others would do to you, do also to them, for this is the Law and the Prophets. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I've heard it said Christians "do not need to follow the Golden Rule". But the Golden Rule is at the heart of Christ's law and even after being born-again and accepting forgiveness from God, we should walk in the light, following Christ's law.

Applying love to the Golden Rule, we have the second of the great commandments, the Royal Law, which is to: "Love your neighbour as yourself". It's actually very important.

We are supposed to fulfill the Royal Law, even after having received forgiveness:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A1&version=ESV][James 2:1]]* - My brothers, show no partiality *as you hold the faith* in our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Committing sin can still happen after having been forgiven. Committing sin happens when we do not fulfill the Royal Law, or when we are showing unfair bias as we do it. Therefore being led by the Spirit of Jesus, we should be abiding by the Royal law, and to be deliberately breaking the Royal law, a person could no longer say they are being led by the Spirit of Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A8-9&version=ESV][James 2:8-9]]* - If you really fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, You shall love your neighbor as yourself, you are doing well. But if you show partiality, you are committing sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But we must love like Christ loved us in the knowledge that He loved us first. We must forgive our family in Christ, as we have been forgiven:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Leviticus%2019%3A18&version=ESV][Leviticus 19:18]]* - *You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against the sons of your own people*, but *you shall love your neighbor as yourself*: I am the LORD. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%204%3A30-32&version=ESV][Ephesians 4:30-32]]* - And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption. Let all bitterness and wrath and anger and clamor and slander be put away from you, along with all malice. Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ forgave you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A23-24&version=ESV][Romans 8:23-24]]* - And not only the creation, but we ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies. For in this hope we were saved. Now hope that is seen is not hope. For who hopes for what he sees? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Also, I believe that abiding by Christ's law and loving your neighbour as yourself *does not cancel out* _the rest of the law of God_, but that a person must be *actually following Christ* by *obeying Christ's commandments* in order to not be "under the law" and to be "not guilty".

Following Jesus starts with believing in Him and believing He is the Son of God, and Anointed one, the Messiah, and following Jesus continues in getting to know Him through obedience to Him:

So by faith we believe we are children of God, and believing on the name of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, God gives us the right and the commandment to be sanctified in the Truth. An analogy I like is that that by believing on Jesus' name as Son of God and Christ, we are allowed to be placed into God's ambulance and brought to God. In other words, we continue in faith and obedience, as slaves of God to be cleaned up as we come to the knowledge of the Truth.
This imputed righteousness enables us to be sanctified by faith in Jesus with his blood:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A11-13&version=ESV][John 1:11-13]]* - He came to his own, and his own people did not receive him. But _to all who did receive him, who believed in his name_, he gave *the right to become children of God*, who were born, not of blood nor of the will of the flesh nor of the will of man, but of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A18&version=ESV][Acts 26:18]]* - to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, *that they may receive* forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are sanctified by faith in me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God continues to heal, sanctify, deliver us and help us to grow in knowledge of Him, as we obey Him:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%203%3A9-13&version=ESV][Philippians 3:9-13]]* - and *be found in him*, not having a righteousness of my own that comes from the law, but that which comes through _faith in Christ_, the righteousness from God that depends on faith— that I may *know him* and the power of his resurrection, and may *share his sufferings*, *becoming like him in his death*, that by any means possible I may attain the resurrection from the dead. _Not that I have already obtained this or am already perfect_, but I press on to make it my own, because Christ Jesus has made me his own. Brothers, I do not consider that I have made it my own. But one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So an important part of being led by the Spirit of Jesus and being not "under the law" is to continuing to forgive one another as we have been forgiven by Jesus, and walk in the light as He is in the light.

In Christ Jesus, as we are abiding in Jesus, getting to know Jesus through obedience to Him, getting to know Him in Spirit as we get really intimate with Jesus, walking as He walked, we have the peace of God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%204%3A7&version=ESV][Philippians 4:7]]* - And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, *will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Following Jesus includes your thought life:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%204%3A8&version=ESV][Philippians 4:8]]* - Finally, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is just, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is commendable, if there is any excellence, if there is anything worthy of praise, think about these things. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

All people should seek to follow the Royal Law which is to love one's neighbour as themself,
bearing their neighbours burdens and forgiving one another, but who has done that perfectly?

+ [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SDuXlGSV7l4][Quote by Tim Keller]] :: "I want you to meet the needs of other people with all of the strength, with all of the joy and all of the creativity and with all of the speed with which you meet your own needs. 12 hours, that's all - Golden Rule, just try it"

As Christians we were at one time disobedient, and were not able to do this perfectly, and we have been saved by Jesus, having been forgiven by Him,
and after we are grafted into Christ, we now have His righteousness and Almighty God as our Father, and Jesus is our Master and we seek to please our Master,
like the All Blacks try to please their coach, and we seek to follow the Royal Law, which is a part of being obedient to Jesus. We have His Spirit, and His Spirit helps us to do this.

Since Jesus is our Master then we should have the fear of God for Jesus who is God the Son of God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Malachi%201%3A6&version=ESV][Malachi 1:6]]* - A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If then I am a father, where is my honor? And if I am a master, where is my fear? says the LORD of hosts to you, O priests, who despise my name. But you say, How have we despised your name? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

For this reason, I think that Bible translations such as the ESV, correctly are reserved about printing the LORD's name inline throughout the whole Bible. The JW, as they consolidate their Bible translation (NWT) using the LORD's name, seems to me either like an effort to try to engineer God, or self-affirm their own understanding, which is self-exalting but may (especially by those in their congregation) be done in ignorance. I do not affirm the NWT translation, but I do affirm the doctrine of [[https://www.reformationbiblecollege.org/blog/the-five-solas][Sola Scriptura]].

As I was on my way driving to Elim church today, I was thinking "external holiness/cleanliness" is a good thing.
Jesus told some hypocritical Pharisees who were teachers of the Law but unclean within that they were like _whitewashed tombs.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A26-28&version=ESV][Matthew 23:26-28]]* - You blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and the plate, that the outside also may be clean. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but within are full of dead people's bones and all uncleanness. So you also outwardly appear righteous to others, but within you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The Pharisees were focusing on external cleanliness but ignoring their own hearts.

When we think of sin, it involves being enslaved to the practice of it, and it also involves the heart's desire of it.
Sinful thoughts should be quickly disposed of and not allowed to be sown in the heart.

If we focus on cleaning the heart through obedience to the Truth and the washing of the Word in our heart, then that's the most important thing. We can be justified by humbling ourselves before God.

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2018%3A11-14&version=ESV][Luke 18:11-14]]* - The Pharisee, standing by himself, prayed thus: God, I thank you that I am not like other men, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even like this tax collector. I fast twice a week; I give tithes of all that I get. But the tax collector, standing far off, would not even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, *God, be merciful to me, a sinner*! I tell you, this man went down to his house justified, rather than the other. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But our external circumstances may be making it difficult to meet the external appearance of obedient faith, such as "being employed and working money" which is important as to bear one's own load by working is a commandment from the Apostle Paul, but having paid employment in this world to earn your keep is no sure indication of actual obedient faith in the heart of the person.

- The mark of the beast seems to be specifically about trading/doing business/buying and selling - as in this mark would be required to partake in this system.
- I think that's inclusive of "employment", since it's selling your own services.
- It doesn't make sense to say that someone is being disobedient to Jesus when they want to work but are being prevented from working,
  otherwise you'd be making "employment" into an idol.
- The commandment says "willing to work", not "work." Some people say, if anyone doesn't work they don't eat, but that would be like agreeing that people should take the mark of the beast. It would mean there would be no freedom, for example, to go on strike if the only paid employment was immoral.

*** "Legalism"
#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A1&version=ESV][Galatians 5:1]]* - For freedom Christ has set us free; stand firm therefore, and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Any issue belonging to 'legalism' is always about the appearance of obedience, rather than inward obedience and good conscience with God.

Here, Jesus seems to show that saving human life, and doing good is obedient to God's law but that there is an unlawful way to keep the law of God, and as an example, an unlawful way to "keep the Sabbath":

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2012%3A12&version=ESV][Matthew 12:12]]* - Of how much more value is a man than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A9&version=ESV][Luke 6:9]]* - And Jesus said to them, I ask you, is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save life or to destroy it? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Legalism doesn't keep God's law lawfully.

Legalism would congratulate Robin Hood for giving to the poor because he always does it, though he stole from the metaphorical 'Caesar' in order to do so.
Legalism would condemn the poor person who can't work but has been obedient gives what they can when someone asks, as in the commandment.
Legalism would condemn the person who skipped going to church on Sunday in order to instead spend time showing love to someone who was thinking of killing themself.

There is absolutely one place I can think of where it is necessary to be ultra-strict, and that is in the testing of spirits to see if they are from God.
We are told to not trust a spirit which does not confess Jesus, and we are reassured that any spirit which confesses that Jesus Christ has come (from God, into the world) in the flesh is from God.
I wouldn't trust a person who refuses to confess openly to me that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God who has come in the flesh into the world from God.
It's important to be really strict with that.

Jesus has come from God into the world in the form of flesh (as in, the Word of God having *become* flesh) is the meaning of the Scripture means where it is written that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh. It's an important detail and distinction from Jesus being merely *in* an ordinary body of flesh. The word "incarnate" when used may incorrectly convey an idea that He was merely the Son of God as a spirit inside of ordinary flesh and His flesh holding no real significance. But His flesh was not ordinary flesh as His flesh is Word *become* flesh (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A1-14&version=ESV][John 1:1-14]]*), and for the propitiation of our sins He has suffered in His fleshly body, having been scourged in his flesh (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2010%3A5-14&version=ESV][Hebrews 10:5-14]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2053%3A5&version=ESV][Isaiah 53:5]]*), that is the flesh of the Son of God (it's Word of God flesh). And He had Father God and the Holy Spirit in Him (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A8-10&version=ESV][John 14:8-10]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%208%3A1-17&version=ESV][Romans 8:1-17]]*).

By this you know the Spirit of God: *every spirit that confesses [[https://biblehub.com/greek/3670.htm][(G3670 homologeó, confesses, acknowledges, agrees)]] that Jesus Christ has come in the [[strongs:G1722][(G1722 en; in [the form of])]] flesh is from God*, and every spirit that does not confess [[https://biblehub.com/greek/3670.htm][(G3670 homologeó, confess, acknowledge, agree with)]] Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist, which you heard was coming and now is in the world already. *** Honesty in pleasing God with works

Doing so-called 'good works' to justify yourself while denying Christ's atoning work on the cross, is actually self-righteousness and is very displeasing to God.

When we talk about 'merit' or 'credit', we were enabled to even be able to have merit in suffering for righteousness sake _because_ *Jesus bore our sins on the tree* that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. 'Live to righteousness' means walking in the light, walking in love and truth, practicing works that please God, making spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ. [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2013%3A1-8&version=ESV][I Corinthians 13:1-8]] says that without love (love that rejoices with the truth) we gain nothing. God loved us first and has chosen us to be a holy people for His possession, and we can now make spiritual sacrficies which God finds acceptable through Jesus Christ our Lord who we are holding faith in and who has loved us first, laying down His life for us first:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%202%3A15-25&version=ESV][I Peter 2:15-25]]* - For this is the will of God, that by doing good you should put to silence the ignorance of foolish people. *Live as people who are free, not using your freedom as a cover-up for evil, but living as servants of God.* _Honor everyone. *Love the brotherhood.* Fear God. Honor the emperor._ Servants, be subject to your masters with all respect, not only to the good and gentle but also to the unjust. For this is a gracious thing, when, mindful of God, one endures sorrows while suffering unjustly. For *what _credit_ is it if, when you sin and are beaten for it, you endure? But if when you do good and suffer for it you endure, this is a gracious thing in the sight of God*. For to this you have been called, because *Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you might follow in his steps*. He committed no sin, neither was deceit found in his mouth. When he was reviled, he did not revile in return; when he suffered, he did not threaten, but continued entrusting himself to him who judges justly. *He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we might die to sin and live to righteousness*. By his wounds you have been healed. For you were straying like sheep, but have now returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

*** Honesty in asking for help
I don't think it's right for a person (person A) to beg for help to help "them" if the intention is to pay off another's debt (person B),
especially if person B is not, say a dependent, such as a spouse or a child,
especially if the money was intended to be used to help person A, find employment.

It would be dishonest to be using the money differently while compromising on your 'obligations' to the person giving you money.
For example, if I was begging on the street asking for someone to help *'me'*,
it would be dishonest if in reality I was not using this money for the purpose of what I had asked specifically for,
i.e. get me on my feet, but instead simply forwarding it onto others to pay off other people's debt would be dishonest.

Just as an aside, for some issues such as having a criminal conviction, or having no reference, I don't think it's always possible to spend money
to solve the problem. How do I spend money to get past a criminal conviction or to get references? I can't think of any obvious legitimate way to go about doing that. So what would I do with excess funds but use to help other people get out of their problem?

If you say, please give me money so I can buy food, then the money should be for food.
If you say, please give me money because I need money to help me to find work, then the money should be to find work.
If you say, I need help and they ask, "What for?" and you say, "For food" and instead of spending on food you are paying off someone else's debt, then that is dishonesty.

OK, so what if you have a big debt yourself, like a student loan, and because of that
you feel like you have to become debt free before "giving to the one that asks"
and you have to walk past all the beggars, and you are forced to find employment to pay back that loan before you can help other people?

That's the dilemma I've found myself in.

Within the freedom of whatever the money loaning debt system has, I'm thinking of the welfare system,
I definitely believe there is flexibility in "receiving about the same amount as everyone else"
but living cheaply and donating excess to those in need.

+ [[https://youtube.com/watch?v=SUedSE78Mo0&t=5629][youtube.com: Bishop Barron @time: 1 hrs 33 min 49 sec]] :: Since the whole world belongs to God, ultimately, right? God makes the whole world from nothing, (it belongs to God; it doesn't belong to us) we are /stewards/ of it. So Leo said, "Everyone has a right to private ownership..." (i.e. private property, such as a house), but when it comes to the use of what we own, he said, "Once the requirements of necessity and propriety have been met in your own life, everything else you own belongs to the poor." That's Leo XIII.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%203%3A27&version=ESV][Proverbs 3:27]]* - Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in your power to do it. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But there are obligations that we are supposed to meet while on welfare that is given for a specific purpose.

Inward obedience to Christ comes first, of course, and we're individually keeping a good conscience with God over that and personally accountable to God over that.
I wouldn't want blood on my hands, for example, knowing I refused to feed or house someone and then found out they died overnight because they didn't get what they needed because I was being overly "legalistic".

It's starting to feel like witchcraft when you're being controlled by debt.

The reality is though, I think, that when God makes a person a new creation  [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g2537/kjv/tr/0-1/][(G2537 kainē; new)]] [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g2937/kjv/tr/0-1/][(G2937 ktisis; creation)]], their sin debt to God is cancelled.
Now people might start asking them to "cough up" on material debt all of a sudden.

So what's the next move? I think it's right to find employment to pay back Caesar, to pay my monetary debts.
Now if someone prevents me from finding employment, say with a criminal conviction, then that is very much like witchcraft,
trying to keep me under a satanic stranglehold.
In this world, everything seems to try to prevent me from following Jesus.

I think it's very true that in trying to resist sin, and maintain obedience to Christ's commandments,
it would naturally lead a person to rousing demons and to persecution so intense in the likeness of having your blood shed.
