So praying to God for mercy might be also a matter regarding justice. God's justice and His mercy are not mutually exclusive. In Jesus' parable the widow was crying out for justice and mercy at the some time:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2018%3A1-14&version=ESV][Luke 18:1-14]]* - And he told them a parable to the effect that they ought always to pray and not lose heart. He said, In a certain city there was a judge who neither feared God nor respected man. And there was a widow in that city who kept coming to him and saying, Give me justice against my adversary. For a while he refused, but afterward he said to himself, Though I neither fear God nor respect man, yet because this widow keeps bothering me, I will give her justice, so that she will not beat me down by her continual coming. And the Lord said, Hear what the unrighteous judge says. And will not God give justice to his elect, who cry to him day and night? , Will he delay long over them? I tell you, he will give justice to them speedily. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on earth? He also told this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and treated others with contempt: Two men went up into the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector. The Pharisee, standing by himself, prayed thus: God, I thank you that I am not like other men, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even like this tax collector. I fast twice a week; I give tithes of all that I get. But the tax collector, standing far off, would not even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, God, be merciful to me, a sinner! I tell you, this man went down to his house justified, rather than the other. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Thessalonians%201%3A5-8&version=ESV][II Thessalonians 1:5-8]]* - This is evidence of the righteous judgment of God, that you may be considered worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you are also suffering— since indeed God considers it just to repay with affliction those who afflict you, and to grant relief to you who are afflicted as well as to us, when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with his mighty angels in flaming fire, inflicting vengeance on those who do not know God and on those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus. ** 'Rebaptism' and baptism as an appeal to God for a good conscience

OK, so if a person has been baptised into Christ's death, if a person has the spirit of God living within them, then they have the ability to please God (Romans 8:8-9), and the power of God (Romans 15:19, Romans 15:19, Matthew 12:28, Colossians 1:29) works in and through them, and considering that baptism is an appeal for a good conscience through the resurrection of Jesus Christ (I Peter 3:21), but they're already going through the process (Romans 6:3) and the power of God is already working in them, then what it is is another appeal, but not another total death as they're already alive (Romans 8:10, John 11:26).

We are supposed to keep a good conscience with God (I Timothy 1:18-20) as we fight the good fight of faith. Yes, getting water baptised after being born-again of the spirit seems to be a "reality-transforming" experience, but so seems to be any confession or affirmation that we make after being made alive.

We are baptised into Christ ultimately, so while being baptised in water again may have some reality-shifting consequences, such as dramatic changes in a person's relationships with other people, there is an even higher reality of a singular overarching spiritual baptism into Christ's death John 11:26 as we live while maintaining their faith in Jesus Christ. We don't get grafted out of Christ with rebaptism, so long as we are maintaining a genuine faith in Jesus Christ (Romans 11:17-21) as affirming faith in Jesus Christ and endeavoring to maintain a good conscience with God are what we are supposed to continue doing as we fight the good fight of faith (I Timothy 1:18-20).

So, therefore, after rebaptising as an appeal for a good conscience through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, the resurrection which they're still going through (if they've already died with Christ), there'd probably be some dramatic shifts in a person's life regarding the people they interact with, but assuming that the person being baptised is affirm their faith in Christ, and maintaining their fear of God and self-humbling wanting God to be merciful to them and doing this as an appeal to God for a good conscience with God, I don't think getting baptised again is detrimental in any way, but could be seen as a public declaration of one's faith in Jesus Christ as they endeavour to maintain a good conscience (I Timothy 1:5) with God, which we have been called to do as we fight the good fight of faith (I Timothy 1:18-20).

Sure, it might be disruptive and perhaps some people might question whether or not that person even deserves another chance, a redo, but as far as a person's standing with God goes, it can only be a good thing. As Jesus mentioned that it is those who humble themselves who will be exalted (Luke 18:13-14).

Beating hand on chest and asking God for mercy, appealing to God for a good conscience through the resurrection of Jesus Christ can only be a good thing.

I affirm "one baptism" for the remission of sins, as in the Nicene creed, and there can only be one spiritual baptism, that is dying with Christ, no matter how many water baptisms (Romans 6:3).

That being said, I don't think multiple water baptism are ever needed, but I don't think I should be prohibited because it's an appeal to God for a good conscience through Christ's resurrection which the person may already be going through as they fight the good fight of faith.

But I definitely don't think it should be standard practice.

More appropriate than getting water baptised again would be public confession.

I believe that believer's baptism is correct practice and if a person's initial baptism was not them appealing to God for a good conscience through the resurrection of Jesus Christ then I believe they should be allowed to be baptised again.

+ [[https://www.earlychristianwritings.com/text/justinmartyr-resurrection.html][Saint Justin Martyr: Fragments of the Lost Work of Justin on the Resurrection {Roberts-Donaldson}]] :: The word of truth is free, and _carries its own authority, *disdaining to fall under any skilful argument, or to endure the logical scrutiny of its hearers*. But it would be *believed for its own nobility*, and for the confidence due to Him who sends it_. Now the word of truth is sent from God; wherefore the freedom claimed by the truth is /not arrogant/. For *being sent with authority, it were not fit that it should be required to produce proof of what is said*; since *neither is there any proof beyond itself, which is God*. For _every proof is more powerful and trustworthy than that which it proves; since what is disbelieved, until proof is produced, gets credit when such proof is produced_, and is recognised as being what it was stated to be. But *nothing is either more powerful or more trustworthy than the truth*; so that he who requires proof of this is like one who wishes it demonstrated why the things that appear to the senses do appear. For the test of those things which are received through the reason, is sense; but of sense itself there is no test beyond itself. As then we bring those things which reason hunts after, to sense, and by it judge what kind of things they are, whether the things spoken be true or false, and then sit in judgment no longer, giving full credit to its decision; so also we refer all that is said regarding men and the world to the truth, and by it judge whether it be worthless or no. But the utterances of truth we judge by no separate test, giving full credit to itself.

For that reason, I would have more confidence before God if I was serving Him, having put sin to death and trying to be holy and selfless and loving in faith towards Jesus, than if I believed precise theology but had no changed life / love for Jesus:

And the Word, being His Son, came to us, having put on flesh, revealing both Himself and the Father, giving to us in Himself resurrection from the dead, and eternal life afterwards. And this is Jesus Christ, our Saviour and Lord. He, therefore, is Himself both the faith and the proof of Himself and of all things. Wherefore *those who follow Him, and know Him, having faith in Him as their proof, shall rest in Him*. But since the adversary does not cease to resist many, and uses many and divers arts to ensnare them, that he may /seduce the faithful from their faith, and that he may prevent the faithless from believing/, *it seems to me necessary that we also, being armed with the invulnerable doctrines of the faith, do battle against him in behalf of the weak.*

Whoever truly believes Jesus trusts in and is obedient to Jesus. We must obey Jesus Christ, and that obedience means being a slave of righteousness, leading to sanctification, which leads to eternal life:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A36&version=ESV][John 3:36]]* - Whoever believes ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/pisteuo_n_4100.htm][G4100 pisteuōn]] - /is believing (verb)/) in the Son *has* eternal life; whoever does not obey ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/544.htm][544. apeitheó]]) the Son shall not *see* life, but _the wrath of God remains on him._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://biblehub.com/greek/pisteuo_n_4100.htm][G4100 πιστεύων (pisteuōn)]]: This is the present participle form of the verb "πιστεύω" ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/4100.htm][G4100 pisteuō]]), meaning "to believe" or "to have faith." In the participle form, it functions as a verbal adjective and can be translated as "believing."

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A10-13&version=ESV][I John 5:10-13]]* - Whoever believes ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/pisteuo_n_4100.htm][G4100 pisteuōn]] - /is believing (verb)/) in the Son of God has the testimony in himself. Whoever does not believe God has made him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony that God has borne concerning his Son. And this is the testimony, that God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life. I write these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God that you may know that you have eternal life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But we must not believe in vain. We must continue trusting Jesus. We must believe and hold fast to the gospel:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A1-2&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:1-2]]* - Now I would remind you, brothers, of the gospel I preached to you, which you received, in which you stand, and by which you are being saved, if you hold fast ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/2722.htm][2722. katechó]]) to the word I preached to you—unless you believed in vain. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://biblehub.com/greek/2722.htm][2722. katechó]] :: Usage: (a) I hold fast, bind, arrest, (b) I take possession of, lay hold of, (c) I hold back, detain, restrain, (d) I hold a ship, keep its head.

By faith we must continue obeying God, forsaking sin, that we may share in Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%203%3A12-19&version=ESV][Hebrews 3:12-19]]* - Take care, brothers, lest there be in any of you an *evil, unbelieving heart, leading you to fall away from the living God*. But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called today, that _none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin_. For *we share in Christ, if indeed we hold our original confidence firm to the end*. As it is said, Today, _if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion_. For who were those who heard and yet rebelled? Was it not all those who left Egypt led by Moses? And with whom was he provoked for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness? And *to whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest, but to those who were disobedient? So we see that they were unable to enter because of unbelief*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

While our faith may waver, Jesus remain faithful, but we must not turn away forever from Jesus:

The saying is trustworthy, for: If we have died with him, we will also live with him; if we endure, we will also reign with him; *if we deny him, he also will deny us*; if we are faithless, he remains faithful— for he cannot deny himself. And when you have turned again, strengthen your brothers. (ESV)

For God shows no partiality. (ESV)

+ [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EZIOPufv5_Y&t=204s][youtube.com: The BEST Explanation of the Trinity You Will EVER Hear | @shamounian {@ChristOverAll-1} @time: 3 min 24 sec]] :: But in creation, God said, “Let us make 
    Adam in Our image, after Our likeness.”
    But then it says Adam is them.
    “Let them have dominion over the world.”
    I’m summing up the passage.
    So here, He says, “I create 
    Adam—this Adam—in My image.”
    But then He says, “This Adam is them.”
    And [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%201%3A27&version=ESV][Genesis 1:27]] tells us 
    that Adam is male and female.
    The male and the female together are the one Adam.
    And in [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%205%3A2&version=ESV][Genesis 5:2]], it says:
    “In the day He created them, male and 
    female… He called them and named them Adam.”
    So, the male is called Adam.
    The female, his wife, is called Adam.
    And then in [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%202%3A24&version=ESV][Genesis 2:24]], it says:
    “For this reason, a man shall leave his 
    father and mother and cling to his wife,  
    and the two shall become one flesh.”
    Now here’s the problem.
    Eve, the female, has her own flesh body.
    She’s a distinct physical being.
    The male Adam, her husband, 
    has his own physical body.
    He’s a distinct physical being.
    But it says the two are one.
    So here, you can have two distinct physical 
    beings, physical persons, still being one.
    How much more God, who’s 
    not limited the way we are?
    Yep.

* The sheepfold

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2023%3A4&version=ESV][Psalms 23:4]]* - Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me; your rod and your staff, they comfort me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

When the person starts trusting Jesus they are justified.
But they must reach the end to be saved.

However, I believe that, so long as Jesus
knows that you're trusting in Him, he knows
you're His sheep.

The question is, when it is considered they have entered the door
and received eternal life and been saved?

Jesus says a person is saved when they enter the door.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2010%3A9&version=ESV][John 10:9]]* - I am the door. If anyone enters by me, _he will be saved_ and will go in and out and find pasture. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The following verse says they _will_ (when they have eternal life)
be unable to be snatched away from His hand, when they are saved.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2010%3A28&version=ESV][John 10:28]]* - I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, _and no one will snatch them out of my hand._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's possible to follow Jesus' voice even before having come to perfect
knowledge and obedience, but Jesus *knows* His sheep:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2010%3A26-29&version=ESV][John 10:26-29]]* - but you do not believe because you are not part of my flock. My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand. My Father, who has given them to me, is greater than all, and no one is able to snatch them out of the Father's hand. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Trust in God (Trusting in God involves trusting God and trusting God enough to do what He says):
- We should trust in God.
- We should have faith in God.
- We should have faith in Jesus.
- God justifies the one who puts their faith in Jesus, who trusts in Jesus.

Putting faith in Jesus means trusting in Jesus and trusting.

We don't love the Christmas presents more than our parents. Rather, we simply love our parents and they provide the Christmas presents.
Likewise, we trust in Jesus and we believe that God justifies the one who trusts in Jesus.

The true believers follow Jesus. They are Jesus' sheep, and they keep His teachings and trust in Him (enough to obey Him penitently):
- trust Jesus
  - [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wkd5ouw380E][youtube.com: I trust in God !]]
  - even for their justification
- hear Jesus' voice
- love Him
- follow Him (they're being obedient)
- Jesus knows them

I believe that what this says is that at the point Jesus knows you listen to His voice and obey His voice, He counts you as one of His sheep and He will not let you go.

** Sheep vs goats: Sheep inherit the kingdom of God, goats do not
I think that Jesus' sheep are goaded by Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A14&version=ESV][Acts 26:14]]* - And when we had all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ goad :: Drive (an animal) with a spiked stick. "the cowboys goaded their cattle across the meadows"

+ Notes on [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ycBgIaIp9BQ][youtube.com: The Unstoppable Gospel {@desiringGod}]] :: My 2 cents. JP at 19 mins mentions Acts 5:32 and makes a point about how people
    who were presently obedient had received (beforehand, I assume) the Holy Spirit
    but I still think that God gives His Holy Spirit to those who obey Him and
    that's still how I read the verse. After all, the call to faith is a call to
    obedience. We become bondservants of God, abiding in Christ's love, practicing
    His commandments. I'm convinced when it come to Jesus, obeying Him and trusting
    in Him are two sides of the same coin. And I think of the John 14
    love/obedience verses as goading us into abiding more deeply in Christ's love.
    I think there is a problem with thinking of obedience as 'works' since there
    are verses about obedience being in the heart, like faith and love are also
    based in the heart. Rather, I like to think of it as a believing, obedient,
    trusting, agape-loving heart. I think this is important because I only want to
    be goaded by Jesus into deeper love , deeper obedience to Jesus, deeper trust
    in Jesus, and I think these dual functions of both trusting in Jesus first and
    foremost and obeying Jesus first and foremost help us narrow down on doing the
    will of God, and being yoked to Christ alone.

#+BEGIN_SRC text -n :async :results verbatim code :lang text
    מוֹשִׁיעַ
    savior, deliverer, helper, saviour

But the Hebrew for helper in *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%202%3A18&version=ESV][Genesis 2:18]]* is not the 'saviour' but the assistant!:

#+BEGIN_SRC text -n :async :results verbatim code :lang text

  assistant, aide, helper, second

+ <2024-07-24 Wed> :: I forgive everyone. I've been under stress. I'm just seeking peace with God currently and sanctification, and no more spiritual attack / fiery trial / testing. I'm just trying to get to the finish line. I don't know everything. It's above my head. I just feel like a foot soldier in God's army, not the General. I hold no grudges towards anyone, and I'm confident that God will restore me in His own way.

I really think that the fruit of the Spirit is desirable in marriage and for choosing a marriage partner but what's essential is that the love has the characteristics of Christ's love. What I mean is, just because there is joy for the person wanting to propose, that's still not good enough because it's even more important that they are showing Christ's love. If the love produced as the fruit of the Spirit is truly Christ's love then that should comply with Christ's law. What I mean is, we have to bear our burdens and when it comes to spouses we need to be willing to bear theirs too.

We must love our wives as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her. We must love as Christ loved us:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%205%3A25-33&version=ESV][Ephesians 5:25-33]]* - *Husbands, love your wives, as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her, that he might sanctify her, having cleansed her by the washing of water with the word, so that he might present the church to himself in splendor, without spot or wrinkle or any such thing, that she might be holy and without blemish.* In the same way husbands should love their wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife loves himself. For no one ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it, just as Christ does the church, because we are members of his body. Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and hold fast to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh. This mystery is profound, and I am saying that it refers to Christ and the church. However, let each one of you love his wife as himself, and let the wife see that she respects her husband. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But choosing the right person to marry rightly *should* desirably mean exhibiting such things as the fruit of the Spirit, in my opinion because it's much easier to not sin when exhibiting the fruit of the Spirit:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A22-23&version=ESV][Galatians 5:22-23]]* - But the fruit of the Spirit is love (G26 *agape*), joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control; _against such things there is no law_. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But when choosing a wife, we must walk by the Spirit, and that includes bearing one another's burdens. This is also made plainly evident in *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%205%3A25-33&version=ESV][Ephesians 5:25-33]]*:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A15-17&version=ESV][Galatians 5:15-17]]* - But if you bite and devour one another, watch out that you are not consumed by one another. But I say, *walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.* For *the desires of the flesh are against the Spirit, and the desires of the Spirit are against the flesh,* for these are opposed to each other, to keep you from doing the things you want to do. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Regarding making a marriage proposal after getting born-again: The fruit of the Spirit, while lawful, are not enough to justify marrying a person. Also, only Jesus was perfect. Christ's law *must* be followed rather than using the fruit of the Spirit to as an excuse to self-justify; *Bearing your neighbours burdens*, and _awaiting God to provide_, because God is the justifier, not us. We can't force someone to marry us, but we must die to self and give ourself up for our wife:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%203%3A23&version=ESV][Romans 3:23]]* - for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Being _led by the spirit involves following Christ's law._ To be married to the right person makes it far easier to not sin. Yes, yielding the fruit of the Spirit, but also necessarily walking by the Spirit:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A13-16&version=ESV][Galatians 5:13-16]]* - For you were called to freedom, brothers. Only do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but _through love serve one another. For the whole law is fulfilled in one word [[strongs:G3056][(G3056 logō)]]: You shall love your neighbor as yourself._ But if you bite and devour one another, watch out that you are not consumed by one another. But I say, _walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

*If* we are led by the spirit (if we're serving Jesus Christ, seeking justification through faith in Jesus Christ) then we are not under the Mosaic law:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A18-21&version=ESV][Galatians 5:18-21]]* - But *if* you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law. Now the works of the flesh are evident: sexual immorality, impurity, sensuality, idolatry, sorcery, enmity, strife, jealousy, fits of anger, rivalries, dissensions, divisions, envy, drunkenness, orgies, and things like these. We have the right to take a believing wife, but that doesn't mean whoever we want. It doesn't mean we can't ask someone. I still think we have the right to propose. But we might not be allowed to marry them. That's the right way to understand it, I think.

This verbiage "take along" does sound like "lead about". So what Paul says he might be written more unambiguously as, "Are we not allowed to take around (bring) with us a wife who is a sister in Christ, as do the other apostles and the brothers of the Lord and Cephas?" If that's the way it was meant, then that still implicitly does carry with it the idea that they are allowed to have a wife. But the passage doesn't necessarily speak about merely "becoming married" (i.e. the right to 'become married') but does seem to entail that idea too because if someone has the right to bring along or spend time with their wife then that presupposes that a state of marriage is something someone has the right to be in:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%209%3A5&version=ESV][I Corinthians 9:5]]* - Do we not have the right [[strongs:G1849][(G1849 exousian: authority [N-AFS])]] to take along [[strongs:G4013][(G4013 periagein: to take about [V-PNA], to lead about with oneself)]] a believing [[strongs:G79][(G79 adelphēn: a sister [N-AFS]. i.e. a sister in Christ)]] wife, as do the other apostles and the brothers of the Lord and Cephas? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

See how it says that a person does not sin by taking a wife, even after they are called. But Paul says for those who marry after they are called there will be worldly troubles. And also, Paul points out that the present form of the world is passing away, so after we are called by God, we should really be anticipating the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%207%3A24-31&version=ESV][I Corinthians 7:24-31]]* - So, brothers, in whatever condition each was called, there let him remain with God. Now concerning the betrothed, I have no command from the Lord, but I give my judgment as one who by the Lord's mercy is trustworthy. I think that in view of the present distress it is good for a person to remain as he is. Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek to be free. Are you free from a wife? Do not seek a wife. But if you do marry, you have not sinned, and if a betrothed woman marries, she has not sinned. Yet those who marry will have worldly troubles, and I would spare you that. This is what I mean, brothers: *the appointed time has grown very short*. From now on, let those who have wives live as though they had none, and those who mourn as though they were not mourning, and those who rejoice as though they were not rejoicing, and those who buy as though they had no goods, and those who deal with the world as though they had no dealings with it. For the present form of this world is passing away. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://usccb.cld.bz/Catechism-of-the-Catholic-Church2/415/][usccb.cld.bz: Catechism of the Catholic Church - Page 415]] :: All the ordained ministers of the Latin Church, with the exception of permanent deacons, are normally chosen from among men of faith who live a celibate life and who intend to remain celibate "for the sake of the kingdom of heaven." Called to consecrate themselves with undivided heart to the Lord and to "the affairs of the Lord", they give themselves entirely to God and to men. Celibacy is a sign of this new life to the service of which the Church's minister is consecrated; accepted with a joyous heart celibacy radiantly proclaims the Reign of God. In the Eastern Churches a different discipline has been in force for many centuries: while bishops are chosen solely from among celibates, married men can be ordained as deacons and priests. This practice has long been considered legitimate; these priests exercise a fruitful ministry within their communities. Moreover, priestly celibacy is held in great honor in the Eastern Churches and many priests have freely chosen it for the sake of the Kingdom of God. In the East as in the West a man who has already received the sacrament of Holy Orders can no longer marry.

*** It's extremely important to respect the institution of marriage, and of marriage proposal
I believe that outlawing marriage proposal is very close to outlawing God.

I believe that it should be normalised that Christians should feel *comfortable* proposing or being betrothed without first needing to have a job or own a house.

What I mean by betrothed is being able to express commitment to the person who a person has decided they want to marry:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%207%3A37-38&version=ESV][I Corinthians 7:37-38]]* - But whoever is firmly established in his heart, being under no necessity but having his desire under control, and has determined this in his heart, to keep her as his betrothed, he will do well. So then he who marries his betrothed does well, and he who refrains from marriage will do even better. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

What I mean by this, is "having a job" or "owning a house" must never become a prerequisite to a Christian to being allowed to marry or at least to being "betrothed" (people should be allowed to propose and given a chance even if they have no assets, and no job).

Quickly, on the topic of agape love. God has done a thing for us freely, that is giving Jesus Christ. The sacrifice was made before the offer was received by us.
Therefore it was a completely unconditional act of love on God's part.

God has made the "first move":

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A8-10&version=ESV][I John 4:8-10]]* - Anyone who does not love does not know God, because God is love. In this the love of God was made manifest among us, that God sent his only Son into the world, so that we might live through him. In this is love, not that we have loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

In God's unconditional love He has paid the price for us to be saved from sin and death and hell. John 3:16 is not only saying that God has done what is needed for our sins to be forgiven, but is also saying that Jesus has come into the world as light so we can even turn away from darkness and towards light. Whoever stops following darkness and instead follows Jesus, whoever trusts in Jesus, whoever looks to Jesus and does what Jesus instructs, turns away from doing evil and in coming to faith in Jesus they will live. Jesus came into the darkness of the world as light so that we can turn to the light and in doing so, live. If Jesus didn't come then we could not receive the light of correction:

Back from the tangent.

Very sadly, after I made the marriage proposal in 2022 the devil really came at me to:
- Make me think I had to work for salvation after being born-again.
- Make me think I need to "pay" to marry her - which is like a spirit of prostitution or trafficking - the devil would happily attempt to turn marriage into an economy - the devil is like a pimp.

Trusting in Jesus shouldn't be just a means to the end of getting an idol:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%206%3A3-10&version=ESV][I Timothy 6:3-10]]* - If anyone teaches a different doctrine and does not agree with the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and the teaching that accords with godliness, he is puffed up with conceit and understands nothing. He has an unhealthy craving for controversy and for quarrels about words, which produce envy, dissension, slander, evil suspicions, and constant friction among *people who are depraved in mind and deprived of the truth, imagining that godliness is a means of gain*. Now *there is great gain in godliness with contentment, for we brought nothing into the world, and we cannot take anything out of the world*. But if we have food and clothing, with these we will be content. The testimony that God has borne concerning his Son ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A10&version=ESV][I John 5:10]]) is that God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A11&version=ESV][I John 5:11]]), and so we need to have the Son ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A12&version=ESV][I John 5:12]]) and if we are trusting in the name of the Son of God ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A13&version=ESV][I John 5:13]]) then we have confidence that we have eternal life.

I affirm the way I learned Christ was through trying hard to be faithful to Jesus in private - seeking glory from God who can see me, even when others can't.

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%204%3A18-20&version=ESV][Ephesians 4:18-20]]* - They are darkened in their understanding, alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance that is in them, due to their hardness of heart. They have become callous and have given themselves up to sensuality, greedy to practice every kind of impurity. But that is not the way you learned Christ!— (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But the yoke of the Lord Jesus has been extremely difficult.

*** Genuine belief results a dramatic decoupling with the world out of darkness and out from under the power of Satan
Going from darkness to light and arriving at a genuine understanding in the heart to agree with the truth coincides with a clash of beliefs between you (who has come into the light) and the world (which is still in darkness).

Agape-love can be misplaced. We go from agape-loving (treasuring, valuing) darkness to agape-loving (treasuring, valuing) light:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A16-20&version=ESV][John 3:16-20]]* - For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life. For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but in order that the world might be saved through him. Whoever believes in him is not condemned, but *whoever does not believe is condemned already*, because he has not believed in the name of the only Son of God. And this is the judgment: the light has come into the world, and people loved ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/25.htm][25. agapaó]]) the darkness rather than the light ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/5457.htm][5457. phós]]) because their deeds were evil. For everyone who does wicked things hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his deeds should be exposed. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Genuine agape loves the light. The Truth of God is light and is good and is not wicked:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2012%3A9&version=ESV][Romans 12:9]]* - Let love [[strongs:G26][(G26 agapé)]] be genuine [[strongs:G505][(G505 anupokritos)]]. Abhor what is evil; hold fast to what is good. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

In order to be faithful to God, you will start acting unpredictably to others who are still in darkness. Firstly, as happened to me, you may tell someone about Jesus for the first time. Also, you will be led amongst people in darkness and make confessions of the truth to combat lies in remaining faithful to God, and obey Jesus' commandments in situations where others in darkness or under the power of Satan may pressure you to not. And people may react in hostile ways. I just think that turning from darkness to light and the power of Satan to God naturally results in decoupling from the world:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2010%3A18-21&version=ESV][John 10:18-21]]* - No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of my own accord. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it up again. This charge I have received from my Father. There was again a division among the Jews because of these words. Many of them said, He has a demon, and is insane; why listen to him? Others said, These are not the words of one who is oppressed by a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A24-25&version=ESV][Acts 26:24-25]]* - And as he was saying these things in his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, you are out of your mind; your great learning is driving you out of your mind. But Paul said, I am not out of my mind, most excellent Festus, but I am speaking true and rational words. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

(ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

*** Holiness - J.C. Ryle
#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  Holiness:
  - The habit of being of one mind with God, according as we find His mind described in Scripture:
    - It is the habit of agreeing in God's judgment, hating what He hates, loving
      what He loves, and measuring everything in this world by the standard of
      His Word. He who most entirely agrees with God, he is the most holy man.
  - endeavor to shun every known sin and to keep every known commandment.
  - strive to be like our Lord Jesus Christ
  - follow after meekness, patience, gentleness, patience, kind tempers,
    government of his tongue. He will bear much, forbear much, overlook much and
    be slow to talk of standing on his rights
  - follow after temperance and self--denial. He will labor to mortify the
    desires of his body, to crucify his flesh with his affections and lusts, to
    curb his passions, to restrain his carnal inclinations
  - follow after charity and brotherly kindness
  - follow after a spirit of mercy and benevolence towards others
  - follow after purity of heart. He will dread all filthiness and uncleanness of
    spirit, and seek to avoid all things that might draw him into it
  - follow after the fear of God. I do not mean the fear of a slave, who only
    works because he is afraid of punishment and would be idle if he did not
    dread discovery
  - follow after humility. He will desire, in lowliness of mind, to esteem all
    others better than himself
  - follow after faithfulness in all the duties and relations in life. He will
    try, not merely to fill his place as well as others who take no thought for
    their souls, but even better, because he has higher motives and more help
    than they
  - follow after spiritual--mindedness. He will endeavor to set his affections
    entirely on things above and to hold things on earth with a very loose hand.
#+END_QUOTE

** I do not endorse gay 'marriage' - I consider it to be sin - grave sin, actually
I personally do not endorse gay 'marriage'. When I have in the past, I repent of that.

That is not to say it is not possible to endorse it yourself (and take the consequences of that) but a person is accountable to God for that act of annulling one of His commandments.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A19&version=ESV][Matthew 5:19]]* - Therefore whoever relaxes one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven, but whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
#+END_QUOTE

We are also supposed to speak up for the God's Truth. We should affirm sound Christian teaching when it comes to what is sinful. Just because we may not judge others when it comes to something sinful, that doesn't mean that God wont judge us for practicing and affirming something sinful.

I still think that we really do need to have the fear of God, actually, to be sound in our faith. Otherwise people will actually just say things like "God loves our sinfulness too and doesn't want us to be cleaned up but really just loves us as we are and wouldn't change a thing", and that is not true about God because God would change things about us. God's will is our sanctification (it's what He wants). God disciplines us and cleans us up as we trust and obey Jesus Christ. Also, the agape love we have for family in Christ is a "yoking" love which is not to be shared with those who are enemies of Jesus Christ. It's similar to the way in which a married man has certain duties to His wife that is not extended to other people.

Love is certainly to do with *duty* / *obligation* and our duties are described to us through God's word:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ecclesiastes%2012%3A13-14&version=ESV][Ecclesiastes 12:13-14]]* - The end of the matter; all has been heard. Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole duty of man. For God will bring every deed into judgment, with every secret thing, whether good or evil. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A Christian does not love all people with the same duty, actually, but rather loves all people in the way that God has commanded us to love them.
If we have different duties to different people, then we actually do love people differently, but so long as it's in accordance with sound teaching.

God's universal love for people is demonstrated in what He has done already in sending Jesus Christ. But God has also conditional love that does in fact depend on our heart posture towards God. But everyone is offered this conditional love but not everyone takes it. God offers all without partiality but with conditions His friendship and His eternal love, but by free choice some people reject God's offer by not meeting the conditions:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A8-13&version=ESV][James 2:8-13]]* - If you really fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, You shall love your neighbor as yourself, you are doing well. But if you show partiality, you are committing sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors. For whoever keeps the whole law but fails in one point has become accountable for all of it. For he who said, Do not commit adultery, also said, Do not murder. If you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law. So speak and so act as those who are to be judged under the law of liberty. For judgment is without mercy to one who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I heard this from somebody this morning, "God wants us to love everybody equally." Really? And what is meant by that?
God doesn't love everybody equally.

God *loved* all people in the same way, for sure, in sending Jesus Christ into the world. God has demonstrated His love for us in that while we were sinners, Christ died for us. That is true for everyone.
But God loves those who love Jesus in a different way altogether compared with how He loves those who have rejected Jesus.
God's friendship is for those who love Jesus and believe that He came from God.

I mean, on the surface saying that "God wants us to love everybody equally because God loves everybody equally" may sound nice to ears that are not trained to perceive the lie.
But God doesn't love everybody equally, and since Christians ought to be imitating God's love, then Christians shouldn't love everyone equally.
Father God's friendship is for those who love Jesus and believe that He came from God.
Jesus Christ's friendship is for those who have learned from Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A13-17&version=ESV][John 15:13-17]]*) and do what He says (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A9-14&version=ESV][John 15:9-14]]*).
Jesus Christ's agape love is for those who keep Jesus' commandments (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A10&version=ESV][John 15:10]]*).
It's right to say God has loved us. This is correct. It's also correct to say, God loves us in bearing with us in patience for us to repent and come to love Him back through faith in Jesus.
And it's right to say that to remain in God's love we must be keeping Jesus' commandments.
A person who rejects Jesus and continues on that path eventually receives the wrath of God.
The Christians' friendship should be for our family in Christ, and not for the world:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%204%3A4&version=ESV][James 4:4]]* - You adulterous people! Do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity with God? Therefore whoever wishes to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A Christian should not be "led" by evil people. And real love loves in the way prescribed by God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A2-3&version=ESV][I John 5:2-3]]*).

I think Mari would be better to have said, "By loving God and keeping His commandments, a person loves their neighbour, which is our duty as Christians." Sure, love everyone, even no-believres, but in the way that Jesus Christ loves them and that includes speaking the truth to them and bearing with them in patience that they will repent. But loving them doesn't mean affirming error or endorsing a sinful way of life:

+ [[https://youtube.com/watch?v=11z22HR1KHo&t=421][Quote from Mari Mari Emmanuel]] :: So fear nothing, love everyone, but be firm when it comes to speaking the truth. Truth cannot be compromised. ... The one who is all love, He was sharper than a sword; When it came to holding the Truth, fighting for the Truth, He stood firm, never gave way, never compromised. Now that is love. If you truly love someone, wouldn't you want them to be living in the Truth? If you truly love the person, you will tell them, "This is right... This is wrong..."

As Christians we must not "turn back" like Lot's wife did, and so we must not "love our former life", nor the world, etc., but rather take hold of what is truly life (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%206%3A17-19&version=ESV][I Timothy 6:17-19]]*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2017%3A32-37&version=ESV][Luke 17:32-37]]* - Remember Lot's wife. Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life will keep it. I tell you, in that night there will be two in one bed. One will be taken and the other left. There will be two women grinding together. One will be taken and the other left. And they said to him, Where, Lord? He said to them, Where the corpse is, there the vultures will gather. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%206%3A14-18&version=ESV][II Corinthians 6:14-18]],7:1* - Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership has righteousness with lawlessness? Or what fellowship has light with darkness? What accord has Christ with Belial? Or what portion does a believer share with an unbeliever? What agreement has the temple of God with idols? For we are the temple of the living God; as God said, I will make my dwelling among them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. Therefore go out from their midst, and be separate from them, says the Lord, and touch no unclean thing; then I will welcome you, and I will be a father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty. Since we have these promises, beloved, *let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of body and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
   *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A13-16&version=ESV][I John 3:13-16]]* - Do not be surprised, brothers, that the world hates you. _We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers._ Whoever does not love abides in death. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him. By this we know love, that he laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%208%3A35-36&version=ESV][Proverbs 8:35-36]]* - For whoever finds me finds life and obtains favor from the LORD, but he who fails to find me injures himself; all who hate me love death. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A12&version=ESV][I John 5:12]]* - Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%206%3A10&version=ESV][Galatians 6:10]]* - So then, as we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone, and especially to those who are of the household of faith. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We may love our enemies (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A43-48&version=ESV][Matthew 5:43-48]]*) but that doesn't involve lying to one another. Love agrees with God. So speaking the truth in love, etc. this is good. But speaking what is false about God is not love at all.

If someone hates us personally then there is certainly nothing wrong with loving that person. If someone is a hater of Jesus Christ, it's still not wrong to "do good" to them. It's not wrong to loving them in the way that God loves them. But the fact is, God's love for evil people generally is not one that is controlling or forcing them to love God back. And the fact is, we need to love God to live. Someone who remains a God-hater is someone who perishes in their way, even though they were loved by God, because they don't end up loving God back, they perish.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%203%3A18-21&version=ESV][Philippians 3:18-21]]* - For many, of whom I have often told you and now tell you even with tears, walk as enemies of the cross of Christ. Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and they glory in their shame, with minds set on earthly things. But our citizenship is in heaven, and from it we await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ, who will transform our lowly body to be like his glorious body, by the power that enables him even to subject all things to himself. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

In the manner in which I judge, I know I will be judged.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%207%3A1-2&version=ESV][Matthew 7:1-2]]* - “Do not judge so that you will not be judged. For in the way you judge, you will be judged; and by your standard of measure, it will be measured to you.
#+END_QUOTE

Self defence:

+ [[https://www.gotquestions.org/self-defense.html][gotquestions.org self-defense.html:  What does the Bible say about self - defense ? | GotQuestions . org]] :: *Exodus 22* gives some clues about God’s attitude toward self-defense: “If a thief is caught breaking in at night and is struck a fatal blow, the defender is not guilty of bloodshed; but if it happens after sunrise, the defender is guilty of bloodshed” (Exodus 22:2–3).

    Two basic principles taught in this text are the right to own private property and the right to defend that property. The full exercise of the right to self-defense, however, depended on the situation. No one should be too quick to use deadly force against another, even someone who means to do him harm. If someone was set upon by a thief in the middle of the night and, in the confusion of the moment the would-be thief was killed, the Law did not charge the homeowner with murder. But, if the thief was caught in the house during the day, when the homeowner was unlikely to be awoken from sleep, then the Law forbade the killing of the thief. Essentially, the Law said that homeowners shouldn’t be quick to kill or attack thieves in their home. Both situations could be considered self-defense, but deadly force was expected to be a last resort, used only in the event of a panicked “surprise attack” scenario where the homeowner is likely to be confused and disoriented. In the case of a nighttime attack, the Law granted the homeowner the benefit of the doubt that, apart from the darkness and confusion of the attack, he would not intentionally use lethal force against a thief. Even in the case of self-defense against a thief, a godly person was expected to try to restrain the assailant rather than immediately resort to killing him.

    Paul engaged in self-defense on occasion, although non-violently. When he was about to be flogged by the Romans in Jerusalem, Paul quietly informed the centurion with the scourge that he, Paul, was a Roman citizen. The authorities were immediately alarmed and began to treat Paul differently, knowing they had violated Roman law by even putting him in chains. Paul had used a similar defense in Philippi—after he was flogged—in order to secure an official apology from those who had violated his rights (Acts 16:37–39).

    The persistent widow in Jesus’ parable kept pounding on the judge’s door with the repeated plea, “Grant me justice against my adversary” ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2018%3A3&version=ESV][Luke 18:3]]). This widow was not about to give up and let her enemy take advantage of her; through the proper channels, she pursued self-defense.

    Jesus’ command to “turn the other cheek” ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A39&version=ESV][Matthew 5:39]]) has to do with our response to personal slights and offenses. Some situations may call for self-defense, but not retaliation in kind. The context of Jesus’ command is His teaching against the idea of “eye for eye, and tooth for tooth” (verse 38). Our self-defense is not a vengeful reaction to an offense. In fact, many offenses can simply be absorbed in forbearance and love.

    The Bible never forbids self-defense, and believers are allowed to defend themselves and their families. But the fact that we are permitted to defend ourselves does not necessarily mean we must do so in every situation. Knowing God’s heart through reading His Word and relying on “the wisdom that comes from heaven” ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%203%3A17&version=ESV][James 3:17]]) will help us know how to best respond in situations that might call for self-defense.

Think about appropriate penalties. Ideally, a thief would make full restitution rather than be executed. In the the situation of the thief breaking in at night, self-defence was involved because the thief breaking in at night posed a danger. The thief shouldn't have been there, and the other person defended the household, but the loss of life is not ideal:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Exodus%2022%3A2-3&version=ESV][Exodus 22:2-3]]* - If a thief is caught breaking in and is beaten to death, no one shall be guilty of bloodshed. But if it happens after sunrise, there is guilt for his bloodshed. A thief must make full restitution; if he has nothing, he himself shall be sold for his theft. (engbsb2020eb)
#+END_QUOTE

I believe the teachings about self-defence can help answer the question of "Should a nation ever go to war?"

Voting for the Republican Party or Democratic Party isn't what determines if a person is a Christian.

Every Christian no matter what shoes they find themselves in, whether a politician or a civilian, should _"If possible, *so far as it depends on them* (because sometimes it doesn't only depend on them), live peaceably with all"._

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2012%3A17-21&version=ESV][Romans 12:17-21]],13:1-10* - Repay no one evil for evil, but give thought to do what is honorable in the sight of all. *If possible, so far as it depends on you, live peaceably with all*. Beloved, never avenge yourselves, but leave it to the wrath of God, for it is written, Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord. To the contrary, if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him something to drink; for by so doing you will heap burning coals on his head. Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good. Let every person be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been instituted by God. Therefore whoever resists the authorities resists what God has appointed, and those who resist will incur judgment. For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Would you have no fear of the one who is in authority? Then do what is good, and you will receive his approval, for he is God's servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not bear the sword in vain. For he is the servant of God, an avenger who carries out God's wrath on the wrongdoer. Therefore one must be in subjection, not only to avoid God's wrath but also for the sake of conscience. For the same reason you also pay taxes, for the authorities are ministers of God, attending to this very thing. Pay to all what is owed to them: taxes to whom taxes are owed, revenue to whom revenue is owed, respect to whom respect is owed, honor to whom honor is owed. Owe no one anything, except to love each other, for the one who loves another has fulfilled the law. The commandments, You shall not commit adultery, You shall not murder, You shall not steal, You shall not covet, and any other commandment, are summed up in this word: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. Love does no wrong to a neighbor; therefore love is the fulfilling of the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We should never avenge ourselves, but leave it to the wrath of God.
But God has people in positions of authority who carry out His wrath on the evildoer.
We should be in subjection to the authority that has been placed in power over us, even if it's a situation like the Israelites in slavery in Egypt, and submit to them "in the Lord Jesus Christ" (i.e. while maintaining Jesus Christ's teachings) and endeavour to serve Christ as we do so, keeping Jesus' commandments.

Rulers should not be wicked. Their statutes should be just, not unjust:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2094%3A20&version=ESV][Psalms 94:20]]* - Can wicked rulers be allied with you, those who frame injustice by statute? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Lamentations%203%3A35-36&version=ESV][Lamentations 3:35-36]]* - to deny a man justice in the presence of the Most High, to subvert a man in his lawsuit, the Lord does not approve. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Jesus is still for the modern day. Justice is not belonging only to a past dispensation:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%2042%3A1-3&version=ESV][Isaiah 42:1-3]]* - Behold my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my Spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations. He will not cry aloud or lift up his voice, or make it heard in the street; a bruised reed he will not break, and a faintly burning wick he will not quench; he will faithfully bring forth justice. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Jeremiah%2023%3A5-6&version=ESV][Jeremiah 23:5-6]]* - Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, and he shall reign as king and deal wisely, and shall execute justice and righteousness in the land. In his days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell securely. And this is the name by which he will be called: The LORD is our righteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Christians should not "take the law into one's own hands" (i.e. they should not be judge, jury and executioner). Christians need to submit to the people who God has placed into authority. But, only *in the Lord*. We submit, but only "give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar". We must also give to God what belongs to God. God does put people into positions where they carry out justice (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2012%3A17-21&version=ESV][Romans 12:17-21]],13:1-10*) or carry out self-defence:

He looked this way and that, and seeing no one, he struck down the Egyptian and hid him in the sand. When he went out the next day, behold, two Hebrews were struggling together. And he said to the man in the wrong, Why do you strike your companion? He answered, Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Do you mean to kill me as you killed the Egyptian? Then Moses was afraid, and thought, Surely the thing is known. When Pharaoh heard of it, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from Pharaoh and stayed in the land of Midian. And he sat down by a well. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

And once more he bent down and wrote on the ground. But when they heard it, they went away one by one, beginning with the older ones, and Jesus was left alone with the woman standing before him. Jesus stood up and said to her, Woman, where are they? Has no one condemned you? She said, No one, Lord. And Jesus said, Neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on sin no more.]] (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

For this is the will of God, that by doing good you should put to silence the ignorance of foolish people. Live as people who are free, not using your freedom as a cover-up for evil, but living as servants of God. Honor everyone. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honor the emperor. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I think there is nothing wrong with *refusing* to kill another human being if a person is convicted by the fear of God that they must not kill people at all.
That is pacifism, and that person should do what they can to avoid being in a situation such as having a job as a "soldier" or perhaps a "police officer", or a "General" or a "Commander in Chief" such as the POTUS etc. because in such a position a person might be required and expected to carry out justice in the fear of God (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Samuel%2023%3A2-4&version=ESV][II Samuel 23:2-4]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Exodus%2018%3A21&version=ESV][Exodus 18:21]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2031%3A9&version=ESV][Proverbs 31:9]]*). If it doesn't fit with a person's faith, then they shouldn't be in that position. I'm a pacifist myself and accountable even right now for my beliefs. May God rescue me from every evil deed.

"Slaying/Killing" is not precisely the same thing as "murder" as concerns the Law of God. Slaying is the actions but actions come from what is in the heart. Murder happens when there is murderous hate or lack of love in the heart. But Christians who are looking to Jesus are supposed to _"seek peace" with all people (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2012%3A14&version=ESV][Hebrews 12:14]]*) as much as depends on oneself ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2012%3A18&version=ESV][Romans 12:18]])_ . When peace is taken away, men slay one-another (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%206%3A4&version=ESV][Revelation of John 6:4]]*).

Sin must be repented from:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%209%3A20-21&version=ESV][Revelation of John 9:20-21]]* - The rest of mankind, who were not killed by these plagues, did not repent of the works of their hands nor give up worshiping demons and idols of gold and silver and bronze and stone and wood, which cannot see or hear or walk, nor did they repent of their murders or their sorceries or their sexual immorality or their thefts. (ESV)

Real Christian pacifism would involve at the same time as refusing to murder, also be refusing to lie, and refusing to commit adultery in ones' heart, refusing to covet another's posessions, refusing to commit idolatry, refusing to blaspheme God, refusing to bear false witness, etc.
I think that pacifism (refusing to kill) is justified generally if it's done in righteousness, like in the following story:

+ [[https://renewaljournal.com/2017/11/29/the-true-story-behind-the-song-i-have-decided-to-follow-jesus/][renewaljournal.com:  The true story behind the song ' I have decided to follow Jesus ' - Renewal Journal]] :: About 150 years ago, there was a great revival in Wales. As a result of this, many missionaries came to north-east India to spread the Gospel. The region known as Assam was comprised of hundreds of tribes who were primitive and aggressive head-hunters

    Into these hostile and aggressive communities, came a group of missionaries from the American Baptist Missions spreading the message of love, peace and hope in Jesus Christ. Naturally, they were not welcomed. One missionary succeeded in converting a man, his wife, and two children. This man’s faith proved contagious and many villagers began to accept Christianity.

    Angry, the village chief summoned all the villagers. He then called the family who had first converted to renounce their faith in public or face execution. Moved by the Holy Spirit, the man said:

    “I have decided to follow Jesus.”

    Enraged at the refusal of the man, the chief ordered his archers to arrow down the two children. As both boys lay twitching on the floor, the chief asked, “Will you deny your faith? You have lost both your children. You will lose your wife too.”

    But the man replied:

    “Though no one joins me, still I will follow.”

    The chief was beside himself with fury and ordered his wife to be arrowed down. In a moment she joined her two children in death. Now he asked for the last time, “I will give you one more opportunity to deny your faith and live.”  In the face of death the man said the final memorable lines:

    “The cross before me, the world behind me. No turning back.”

    He was shot dead like the rest of his family. But with their deaths, a miracle took place. The chief who had ordered the killings was moved by the faith of the man. He wondered, “Why should this man, his wife and two children die for a Man who lived in a far-away land on another continent some 2,000 years ago? There must be some remarkable power behind the family’s faith, and I too want to taste that faith.”

    In a spontaneous confession of faith, he declared, “I too belong to Jesus Christ!” When the crowd heard this from the mouth of their chief, the whole village accepted Christ as their Lord and Saviour.

    The song is based on the last words of Nokseng, a man from Garo tribe of Assam (now Meghalaya and some in Assam), India. It is today the song of the Garo people.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Titus%201%3A7-9&version=ESV][Titus 1:7-9]]* - For an overseer, as God's steward, must be above reproach. He must not be arrogant or quick-tempered or a drunkard or violent or greedy for gain, but hospitable, a lover of good, self-controlled, upright, holy, and disciplined. He must hold firm to the trustworthy word as taught, so that he may be able to give instruction in sound doctrine and also to rebuke those who contradict it. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

There is more to "protecting" one's dependents than simply "not killing". In the story of the missionary to Assam, protecting His children also involved protecting their faith, and not denying Jesus.

In a different but related situation, righteous Lot *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Peter%202%3A1-22&version=ESV][II Peter 2:1-22]]* can be seen (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%2019%3A5-8&version=ESV][Genesis 19:5-8]]*) offering his own precious unmarried daughters to some wicked men to avoid the wicked people from the abominable sin of sodomy against two men who had come under the protection of his household. And so what I'm saying with that is that once again, in dealing with some situations, acting righteously involves the fear of God.

It's very important for a Christian to "not deny Jesus Christ".

God sees the thoughts and intentions of people's hearts etc. as they do anything.

The loss of life needs to be avoided if at all able to be avoided, and even to be avoided is the loss of life of a criminal or someone who is presently in the act of a crime because we are called to "Repay no one evil for evil, but give thought to do what is honorable in the sight of all. If possible, *so far as it depends on you*, live peaceably with all."

In the Mosaic Law it seems to show that where there is an intruding thief and the loss of his life owing
to someone defending the household from the intruder (probably in the protection of the members of the
household) where the circumstances (such as it being dark) had made it difficult to deal with the threat without risking force that may harm the intruder,
and where the intruder dies in that situation, the defender of the household is not guilty of murder.
But if there is visibility and precautions could be taken to avoid taking the intruder's life, then the use of excessive force resulting in the death of the intruder would come with guilt for his bloodshed:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Exodus%2022%3A2-3&version=ESV][Exodus 22:2-3]]* - If a thief is caught breaking in and is beaten to death, no one shall be guilty of bloodshed. But if it happens after sunrise, there is guilt for his bloodshed. A thief must make full restitution; if he has nothing, he himself shall be sold for his theft. (engbsb2020eb)
#+END_QUOTE

So the prevention of hateful harm and minimisation of harm (even to a criminal) is still important. And the "in the moment" situation of defending against someone who is presently attacking is also a very different issue to the issue of enforcing justice for someone having done something in the past.

It's not wrong to want to care even for the life of a criminal who is presently infringing and in striving to protect others from harm from them seek to minimise harm to the criminal *as is within one's power to do so*. See how the emphasis is on rescuing people from the wicked, rather than to destroying the wicked:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2082%3A3-4&version=ESV][Psalms 82:3-4]]* - Give justice to the weak and the fatherless; maintain the right of the afflicted and the destitute. Rescue the weak and the needy; deliver them from the hand of the wicked. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's not wrong to want to care even for the life of a criminal and seek to do no harm to them *as is within one's power to do so*, while striving to protect others from harm from them.

I think what matters is what's in the heart of a person when they are doing the defending against the present danger.

It's not wrong for someone to choose to mercy when they could seek justice. But it's also wrong to deny justice for someone who seeks justice:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Lamentations%203%3A35-36&version=ESV][Lamentations 3:35-36]]* - to deny a man justice in the presence of the Most High, to subvert a man in his lawsuit, the Lord does not approve. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%202%3A11-13&version=ESV][James 2:11-13]]* - For he who said, Do not commit adultery, also said, Do not murder. If you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law. So speak and so act as those who are to be judged under the law of liberty. For judgment is without mercy to one who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We need to be exercising the love of Father God. We should exercise "common grace" (God makes His sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the just and on the unjust), but without withholding justice (not necessarily enforcing justice, but not withholding it either) and we should do righteousness and be merciful and be faithful and truthful:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2033%3A5&version=ESV][Psalms 33:5]]* - He loves righteousness and justice; the earth is full of the steadfast love of the LORD. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A23&version=ESV][Matthew 23:23]]* - Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint and dill and cumin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faithfulness. These you ought to have done, without neglecting the others. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A38-48&version=ESV][Matthew 5:38-48]]* - You have heard that it was said, An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth. But I say to you, *Do not resist the one who is evil*. But *if anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also*. And *if anyone would sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well*. And *if anyone forces you to go one mile, go with him two miles*. *Give to the one who begs from you, and do not refuse the one who would borrow from you*. You have heard that it was said, You shall love your neighbor and hate ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/3404.htm][3404. miseó, 3404 miséō – properly, to detest (on a comparative basis); hence, denounce; to love someone or something less than someone (something) else, i.e. to renounce one choice in favor of another.]]) your enemy. But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the just and on the unjust. For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same? And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing than others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same? You therefore must be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So what is the metaphorical "rain" ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A38-48&version=ESV][Matthew 5:38-48]]*) in the situation of, say, how convicted criminals are dealt with? Well, it could be providing criminals with food and shelter, or it be giving them a life sentence instead of a capital punishment.

+ [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kdxLv3MKX3U][youtube.com:  Pope : Human dignity is not lost even after serious crimes are committed {@ VaticanNews }]] :: Furthermore, effective systems of detention can be and have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption. ... The common good can be safeguarded and the requirements of justice can be met without recourse to capital punishment.

We need to be keeping God's commandments, and seek peace and pursue it.

Jesus carried *his* cross first. Jesus didn't avoid his cross, and he didn't send his disciples forth to defend him against the Romans and the Sanhedrin, to avoid drinking the "cup" ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2022%3A42&version=ESV][Luke 22:42]]) of crucifixion which Father God had given him.
And what I mean by that is that we can give ourselves and our body away (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2013%3A1-8&version=ESV][I Corinthians 13:1-8]]*) in love. There's no greater love than to lay down one's own life for their friends (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A9-14&version=ESV][John 15:9-14]]*).

Wars are in a way inevitable in this world currently, and it's a consequence of there still being sin in the world. Not all people on earth are in Christ.
As Christians, we should ourselves endeavour to be blameless before God, we should be loving our family in Christ, and should be peacemakers with all people as much as it depends on oneself, while endeavouring to not commit sin, or partake in others' sin (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%205%3A22&version=ESV][I Timothy 5:22]]*), and while endeavouring to speak truth, while endeavouring to do good. That does involve Biblical separation. If in a position such as a judge, then seeking to do justice. If in a governmental position, then seeking to serve without corruption:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Chronicles%2016%3A9&version=ESV][II Chronicles 16:9]]* - For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to give strong support to those whose heart is blameless toward him. You have done foolishly in this, for from now on you will have wars. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2012%3A17&version=ESV][Romans 12:17]]* - Repay no one evil for evil, but give thought to do what is honorable in the sight of all. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%205%3A15&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 5:15]]* - See that no one repays anyone evil for evil, but always seek to do good to one another and to everyone. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%203%3A9-13&version=ESV][I Peter 3:9-13]]* - Do not repay evil for evil or reviling for reviling, but on the contrary, bless, for to this you were called, that you may obtain a blessing. For Whoever desires to love life and see good days, let him keep his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit; let him turn away from evil and do good; let him seek peace and pursue it. For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and his ears are open to their prayer. But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil. Now who is there to harm you if you are zealous for what is good? (ESV)

All things in heaven and earth are not united presently. But they're being united and there is still Biblical separation going on. I have heard people deny that Jesus is the Son of God. And how could all things presently be united in the truth if some people and spiritual forces are against the Truth? It's simply incorrect to say that all things are united, and we are all one etc. It's just not presently true. There is still a way in which we are to love people who are our neighbours or of different faiths etc. There is a proper, Biblical way to do it and that is by keeping God's commandments for us. There is no partnership between light and darkness. What happened to Jesus Christ when He was handed over to sinners to be executed, the same type of cross-carrying principle applies to Christians today:
