  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%2010%3A5-6&version=ESV][II Corinthians 10:5-6]]* - We destroy arguments and every lofty opinion raised against the knowledge of God, and take every thought captive to obey Christ, being ready to punish every disobedience, when your obedience is complete. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A3-6&version=ESV][I John 2:3-6]]* - And by this we know that we have come to know him, if we keep his commandments. Whoever says I know him but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, but whoever keeps his word, in him truly the love of God is perfected. By this we may be sure that we are in him: whoever says he abides in him ought to walk in the same way in which he walked. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A31-32&version=ESV][John 8:31-32]]* - So Jesus said to the Jews _who had believed ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/4100.htm][4100. pisteuó]], [[https://biblehub.com/greek/pepisteukotas_4100.htm][pepisteukotas]]) in him_, *If you abide in my word, you are truly my disciples*, _and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The word "end" here in Romans 10:4 doesn't mean abolishment. It means more like "ultimate" or "fulfillment" or in context I think it means "final say" or even "foundation" or "cornerstone".
So for those who have an agape-loving faith in Jesus Christ, a treasuring for the truth of the gospel, the free gift of righteousness that comes from God ultimately has the final say in judgement. In other words, the righteousness that is not of themselves but which is a free gift through faith in Christ based on His work alone has the ultimate say and also is the foundation for any other righteousness of a believer, such as persecution for the cross of Christ, and if all other righteousness fails, there is still no condemnation.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A4&version=ESV][Romans 10:4]]* - For Christ is the end [[strongs:G5056][(G5056 telos)]] of the law [[strongs:G3551][(G3551 nomos)]] for righteousness [[strongs:G1343][(G1343 dikaiosune)]] to everyone who believes [[strongs:G4100][(G4100 pisteuo, trusts)]]. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2010%3A11-15&version=ESV][Romans 10:11-15]]* - For the Scripture says, Everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame. For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek; the same Lord is Lord of all, bestowing his riches on all who call on him. For everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. But how are they to call on him in whom they have not believed? And how are they to believe in him of whom they have never heard? And how are they to hear without someone preaching? And how are they to preach unless they are sent? As it is written, How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the good news! (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A24&version=ESV][John 8:24]]* - I told you that you would die in your sins, for unless you believe that I am he you will die in your sins. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The true gospel which we should be preaching so as to not be accursed is the gospel the Apostle Paul preached where we are supposed to have faith in Christ, hold fast in that faith as we are being saved, serve Christ, obey Christ and be strengthened by Christ, Christ who's blood was shed for us, Christ who died for our sins on a tree and rose again from the dead. The true gospel is the one where there is a day where God judges our hearts through Jesus Christ and disciplines us in advance of final judgement so that we are not condemned along with the people of the world who fail to receive the love of the truth in hearts so as to be saved, the world who loves darkness rather than light because their deeds are evil.

How do we receive grace? How do we receive Jesus Christ? Just the way He's told us:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2010%3A40&version=ESV][Matthew 10:40]]* - Whoever receives you receives me, and whoever receives me receives him who sent me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2018%3A5&version=ESV][Matthew 18:5]]* - Whoever receives one such child in my name receives me, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%209%3A48&version=ESV][Luke 9:48]]* - and said to them, Whoever receives this child in my name receives me, and whoever receives me receives him who sent me. For he who is least among you all is the one who is great. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A12-13&version=ESV][John 1:12-13]]* - But to all who did receive him, who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God, who were born, not of blood nor of the will of the flesh nor of the will of man, but of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Timothy%202%3A8-9&version=ESV][II Timothy 2:8-9]]* - *Remember Jesus Christ*, risen from the dead, the offspring of David, as preached in my gospel, for which I am suffering, bound with chains as a criminal. But the word of God is not bound! (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

There are various means of grace by which we receive Jesus Christ through faith and obedience to Him. I believe that baptism, the eucharist (the Lord's supper / communion), doing as the good Samaritan did, keeping Christ's commandments are all means of grace.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%206%3A57&version=ESV][John 6:57]]* - As the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, so whoever feeds on me, he also will live because of me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Like the bedrock of a house strengthens the foundations of the house which strengthens the remainder of the house, the cornerstone (faith alone in Jesus Christ's blood, death and resurrection) strengthens the foundations (laid while practicing Jesus' commandments) which strengthens the rest of the house, the house that is the eternal dwelling that I believe God builds for those who practice Jesus' commandments. A person has a strong eternal dwelling built for them as they keep Jesus' commandments and the cornerstone is their faith in Jesus Christ and His blood.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2016%3A17-27&version=ESV][Romans 16:17-27]]* - I appeal to you, brothers, to watch out for those who cause divisions and create obstacles contrary to the doctrine that you have been taught; avoid them. For such persons do not serve our Lord Christ, but their own appetites, and by smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the naive. For your obedience is known to all, so that I rejoice over you, but I want you to be wise as to what is good and innocent as to what is evil. The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Timothy, my fellow worker, greets you; so do Lucius and Jason and Sosipater, my kinsmen. I Tertius, who wrote this letter, greet you in the Lord. Gaius, who is host to me and to the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the city treasurer, and our brother Quartus, greet you. _Now to him who is able to strengthen you according to *my gospel* and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery that was kept secret for long ages but has now been disclosed and through the prophetic writings has been made known to all nations, according to the command of the eternal God, to bring about the obedience of faith— to the only wise God be glory forevermore through Jesus Christ! Amen._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The devil works to stop us Christians from taking every though captive for obedience to Christ. Much of the spiritual attack comes from people to "stop striving to obey Jesus" and to 'rest'. Only the devil dissuade people from obeying Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%208%3A12&version=ESV][Luke 8:12]]* - The ones along the path are those who have heard. Then the devil comes and takes away the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2016%3A17-20&version=ESV][Romans 16:17-20]]* - I appeal to you, brothers, to watch out for those who cause divisions and create obstacles contrary to the doctrine that you have been taught; avoid them. For such persons do not serve our Lord Christ, but their own appetites, and by smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the naive. For your obedience is known to all, so that I rejoice over you, but I want you to be wise as to what is good and innocent as to what is evil. The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Those who keep Jesus' word, also keep the word of the direct Apostles of Jesus such as Peter, John and Paul:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2015%3A20&version=ESV][John 15:20]]* - Remember the word that I said to you: A servant is not greater than his master. If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you. If they kept my word, they will also keep yours. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's faith in God through faith in Jesus Christ, the same Jesus Christ who atoned for our sin. We go from serving sin to serving God through serving Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Thessalonians%201%3A9-10&version=ESV][I Thessalonians 1:9-10]]* - For they themselves report concerning us the kind of reception we had among you, and how you turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God, and to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, Jesus who delivers us from [[strongs:G1537][(G1537 ek; from, out of, by, away from)]] the wrath to come. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must keep ourselves in the love of God. We must not deny Jesus Christ by word or works:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%203%3A24&version=ESV][I John 3:24]]* - Whoever keeps his commandments abides in him, and he in them. And by this we know that he abides in us, by the Spirit whom he has given us. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20John%201%3A9&version=ESV][II John 1:9]]* - Everyone who goes on ahead and does not abide in the teaching of Christ, does not have God. Whoever abides in the teaching has both the Father and the Son. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Jude%201%3A20-21&version=ESV][Jude 1:20-21]]* - But you, beloved, build yourselves up in your most holy faith; pray in the Holy Spirit; keep yourselves in the love of God, waiting for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ that leads to eternal life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must gather with Jesus and agree with the Holy Spirit with hope of eternal life:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2012%3A30&version=ESV][Matthew 12:30]]* - Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters. (ESV)

(ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Having tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the age to come, and shared in the Holy Spirit, don't go back to sin:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%206%3A4-6&version=ESV][Hebrews 6:4-6]]* - For it is impossible to restore again to repentance those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, and have shared in the Holy Spirit, and have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the age to come, if they then fall away, since they are crucifying once again the Son of God to their own harm and holding him up to contempt. #+END_QUOTE

For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed to us. (ESV)

*** Anti-gospel
We must not pervert the grace of God. And we must not pervert the gospel of God into one which rejects God's authority over us:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Jude%201%3A4-19&version=ESV][Jude 1:4-19]]* - For certain people have crept in unnoticed who long ago were designated for this condemnation, *ungodly people, who pervert the grace of our God into sensuality and deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ*. Now I want to remind you, although you once fully knew it, that Jesus, _who saved a people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who did not believe_. And the angels who did not stay within their own position of authority, but left their proper dwelling, he has kept in eternal chains under gloomy darkness until the judgment of the great day— just as Sodom and Gomorrah and the surrounding cities, which likewise indulged in sexual immorality and pursued unnatural desire, serve as an example by undergoing a punishment of eternal fire. Yet in like manner these people also, relying on their dreams, defile the flesh, *reject authority*, and blaspheme the glorious ones. But when the archangel Michael, contending with the devil, was disputing about the body of Moses, he did not presume to pronounce a blasphemous judgment, but said, The Lord rebuke you. But these people blaspheme all that they do not understand, and they are destroyed by all that they, like unreasoning animals, understand instinctively. Woe to them! For they walked in the way of Cain and abandoned themselves for the sake of gain to Balaam's error and perished in Korah's rebellion. These are blemishes on your love feasts, as they feast with you without fear, looking after themselves; waterless clouds, swept along by winds; *fruitless trees in late autumn, twice dead, uprooted*; wild waves of the sea, casting up the foam of their own shame; wandering stars, for whom the gloom of utter darkness has been reserved forever. *It was also about these that Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied, saying, Behold, the Lord came with ten thousands of his holy ones, to execute judgment on all and to convict all the ungodly of all their deeds of ungodliness that they have committed in such an ungodly way, and of all the harsh things that ungodly sinners have spoken against him*. These are grumblers, malcontents, *following their own sinful desires*; they are loud-mouthed boasters, showing favoritism to gain advantage. But you must remember, beloved, the predictions of the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ. They said to you, In the last time there will be scoffers, following their own ungodly passions. It is *these who cause divisions, worldly people, devoid of the Spirit*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

*** Christ is a ransom to be offered to all
There is one God, one Mediator. We are called to take this message to the world. And we definitely should continue to do this:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%202%3A1-4&version=ESV][I Timothy 2:1-4]]* - First of all, then, I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all people, for kings and all who are in high positions, that we may lead a peaceful and quiet life, godly and dignified in every way. #+END_QUOTE

For this I was appointed a preacher and an apostle (I am telling the truth, I am not lying), a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

*** Journal entry <2025-07-12 Sat>
When I was born-again of the spirit on 2 April 2022, God gave me a new heart which feared Him and was able to receive correction from Him.
I didn't have all the answers.
I didn't have great theology.
But God would teach me.
In other words, He would write His laws on my heart,
and help me to abide in Christ's commandments.

I truly do despair of life as it is right now.
Against my understanding, I have been terrorised by demons - being punished and tormented without knowing why.
I've just been continually trying to understand why.
And of course, satan has huge numbers of accusations and reasons which he tries to make be believe.

If I'm in the kingdom of God then I feel like a package moving around a busy sorting facility, constantly being tested
and sorted, without end. I've felt constantly under constraint, deprived of sleep, woken up by demons - a messenger of Satan, I think.
And it feels like in my soul, the body of sin, the flesh, is trying to usurp and kill the new creation, and the people around me also placing such unreasonable pressure on me to obey the flesh and to not live in the spirit.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%207%3A16-17&version=ESV][Romans 7:16-17]]* - Now if I do what I do not want, I agree with the law, that it is good. So now it is no longer I who do it, but sin that dwells within me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

In other words, pressuring me to think like the world thinks, rather than to have the mind of Christ.

+ [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jvB8DvV5Ccs][youtube.com: I Need You More - Mark Barlow, REVERE {@REVERElive}]] :: 'Cause I never want to go back to my old life; I need You more; More than yesterday; I need You more; More than words can say; I need You more; Than ever before; I need You, Lord

And where is the promised testimony of the Holy Spirit as I seek to keep Christ's commandments and abide in His teachings? (Sorry if I sounded disgruntled as I wrote that.)

I feel like I'm dying sometimes, dying spiritually, losing the fight against the enemy who attacks my soul and attacks me through people around me.

I want to be set free, as Jesus Christ promised for those who He sets free.
I know Jesus bought me but sadly it seems He allowed me to be absolutely terrorised by demons.

Requiring employment/world's assets before marriage proposal is evil, as to require it puts man's kingdom above God's kingdom.
Because to do so would be saying that people have to have what the world says qualifies a person before they have the right to what God freely gave us.
It would be like telling a bird it's allowed to fly only if it can qualify as a human pilot.
It would be like telling a person they don't have a right to become a child of God through faith in Jesus Christ.
It would be like hating Jesus Christ, the Light of the world, so putting Him to death on a tree.
Denying what is given to us as a right is anti-God.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%204%3A1-3&version=ESV][I Timothy 4:1-3]]* - Now the Spirit expressly says that in later times some will depart from the faith by devoting themselves to deceitful spirits and teachings of demons, through the insincerity of liars whose consciences are seared, who *forbid marriage* and require abstinence from foods that God created to be *received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

After getting a conviction, it really does seem to me that I've still received intense demonic oppression to prevent me from marrying and working. I think that I've had excessive satanic resistance to getting married or getting a job. Meanwhile, the whole world is embracing this AI stuff which greedy people are trying to normalise. They're trying to normalise theft, misrepresentation, etc. and get people to think and live with it and run the economy on top of it, but this stuff is detached from reality. What's being done to exploit people and suppress the true knowledge of God is evil. I don't want anything to do with crypto assets or AI stuff because I don't want blood on my hands. I tried to help people see what was coming with AI stealing software and tried to warn people and when it rolled around I got given a criminal conviction and deplatformed for a marriage proposal and for what I think were unlawful bail breach accusations. Well, the world no doubt hates me like it hated Jesus because I testify that it's works are evil as Jesus did:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%204%3A1-5&version=ESV][I Timothy 4:1-5]]* - Now the Spirit expressly says that in later times some will depart from the faith by devoting themselves to deceitful spirits and teachings of demons, through the insincerity of liars whose consciences are seared, who forbid marriage and require abstinence from foods that God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth. For everything created by God is good, and nothing is to be rejected if it is received with thanksgiving, for it is made holy by the word of God and prayer. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%207%3A7&version=ESV][John 7:7]]* - The world cannot hate you, but it hates me because I testify about it that its works are evil. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Do I have the right to ask?

  AMEN!!

This person had said that they "believe in God." May God help them to change their ways and live pleasing to Him, pleasing to the Lord Jesus Christ.

Keep in mind that Paul advised a congregation of believers to put the sinful, evil person out of the congregation, hand them over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that their spirit would be saved. This person must have been unrepentant.

In sending them to jail or putting them outside the church, they might go through tribulation but perhaps they would repent, but Paul them doesn't want them to perish eternally by continuing to commit that sinful stuff they were doing.

We should be wishing for other people to be saved. And we should overcome evil with good, return good for evil.

I found out today about what Donald Trump recently said:

Regarding what Donald Trump said at the Memorial for Charlie Kirk:

+ Donald Trump said :: "In that private moment on his dying day, we find everything we need to know about who Charlie Kirk truly was. He was a missionary with a noble spirit and a great, great purpose. He did not hate his opponents. He wanted the best for them. That's where I disagreed with Charlie. I hate my opponent. And I don't want the best for them. I'm sorry. I am sorry, Erika. But now Erika can talk to me and the whole group and maybe they can convince me that that's not right. But I can't stand my opponent."

I think it might be OK that he said, "I can't stand my opponent" *if* it were meant in the sense of he's disgusted by his opponent if he is disgusted at them because they're evil, if they are evil. But being disgusted at our enemies shouldn't stop us from loving our enemies and doing good to them.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

(ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

So Paul here didn't "bear with" the evil person but still seemed to have their best interest in mind. So sending someone to prison for evil behaviour, or putting them out of the church is OK:

(ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But to say "I hate my opponent", I hope was only in that "loathing/disgusted by" sense and not in the "have no regard for the life of/does not see value in" sense, as agape love (which Christians are commanded to have for those who hate them) is a love which wishes for the other person to not perish eternally by being a slave to sin.

#+END_QUOTE

But now Erika can talk to me and the whole group and maybe they can convince me that that's not right. But I can't stand my opponent." Biblical love doesn't mean endorsing a person's works/behaviour and it's not against love, nor is it hateful to express your opinion on bad behaviour. The Bible makes it very clear here that a person can rebuke another person without hating them. Biblical love is not affirming of sin. But Biblical love does not hate one's neighbour in the heart. It's not wrong to call out evil behaviour, and it's not wrong to separate ourselves from the company of disbelievers. It's OK to hate sin. In fact, it's very important for Christians to hate sin:

You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the sons of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself; I am the LORD. (NASB)

Being '[[https://www.google.com/url?sa=t&source=web&rct=j&opi=89978449&url=http://biblehub.com/greek/5384.htm][philos with (friends with, allured by, attracted to)]]', money , self, pleasure, rather than ([[strongs:G3123][(G3123 mallon: rather [Adv])]]) being allured by God (wanting to be around God) is bad. In [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%20139%3A21&version=ESV][Psalms 139:21]], there are two words which are translated into the English word "hate" but they are different words with different meanings. [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%208%3A13&version=ESV][Proverbs 8:13]] shows that it's a good thing to hate evil. As [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%20139%3A21&version=ESV][Psalms 139:21]] shows, David loathed people who hate God but in the Greek it doesn't say that he hated them the same way that those people hated God because a different word was used. Sadly, the English translation here confuses this by using the same word in place of two different words.

#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://www.vatican.va/content/leo-xiii/en/encyclicals/documents/hf_l-xiii_enc_15051891_rerum-novarum.html][vatican.va rerum-novarum.html:  Rerum Novarum { May 15 , 1891 }]] :: *RERUM NOVARUM - ENCYCLICAL OF POPE LEO XIII - ON CAPITAL AND LABOR.*

    Given at St. Peter's in Rome, the fifteenth day of May, 1891, the fourteenth year of Our pontificate. LEO XIII

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *22.* Therefore, those whom fortune favors are warned that riches do not bring freedom from sorrow and are of no avail for
          eternal happiness, but rather are obstacles; /(9)/  that the rich should tremble at the threatenings of Jesus Christ -
          threatenings so unwonted in the mouth of our Lord /(10)/  - and that a most strict account must be given to the Supreme Judge
          for all we possess. The chief and most excellent rule for the right use of money is one the heathen philosophers hinted
          at, but which the Church has traced out clearly, and has not only made known to men's minds, but has impressed upon their
          lives. It rests on the principle that it is one thing to have a right to the possession of money and another to have a
          right to use money as one wills. Private ownership, as we have seen, is the natural right of man, and to exercise that
          right, especially as members of society, is not only lawful, but absolutely necessary. "It is lawful," says St. Thomas
          Aquinas, "for a man to hold private property; and it is also necessary for the carrying on of human existence."" But if
          the question be asked: How must one's possessions be used? - the Church replies without hesitation in the words of the
          same holy Doctor: "Man should not consider his material possessions as his own, but as common to all, so as to share them
          without hesitation when others are in need. Whence the Apostle with, ‘Command the rich of this world... to offer with no
          stint, to apportion largely.’" /(12)/  True, no one is commanded to distribute to others that which is required for his own
          needs and those of his household; nor even to give away what is reasonably required to keep up becomingly his condition
          in life, "for no one ought to live other than becomingly." /(13)/  But, when what necessity demands has been supplied, and
          one's standing fairly taken thought for, it becomes a duty to give to the indigent out of what remains over. "Of that
          which remaineth, give alms." /(14)/  It is a duty, not of justice (save in extreme cases), but of Christian charity - a duty
          not enforced by human law. But the laws and judgments of men must yield place to the laws and judgments of Christ the
          true God, who in many ways urges on His followers the practice of almsgiving - ‘It is more blessed to give than to
          receive"; /(15)/  and who will count a kindness done or refused to the poor as done or refused to Himself - "As long as you
          did it to one of My least brethren you did it to Me." /(16)/  To sum up, then, what has been said: Whoever has received from
          the divine bounty a large share of temporal blessings, whether they be external and material, or gifts of the mind, has
          received them for the purpose of using them for the perfecting of his own nature, and, at the same time, that he may
          employ them, as the steward of God's providence, for the benefit of others. "He that hath a talent," said St. Gregory the
          Great, "let him see that he hide it not; he that hath abundance, let him quicken himself to mercy and generosity; he that
          hath art and skill, let him do his best to share the use and the utility hereof with his neighbor." /(17)/ 
    #+END_QUOTE

    ...

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *35.* We have said that the State must not absorb the individual or the family; both should be allowed free and
      untrammelled action so far as is consistent with the common good and the interest of others. Rulers should, nevertheless,
      anxiously safeguard the community and all its members; the community, because the conservation thereof is so emphatically
      the business of the supreme power, that the safety of the commonwealth is not only the first law, but it is a
      government's whole reason of existence; and the members, because both philosophy and the Gospel concur in laying down
      that the object of the government of the State should be, not the advantage of the ruler, but the benefit of those over
      whom he is placed. As the power to rule comes from God, and is, as it were, a participation in His, the highest of all
      sovereignties, it should be exercised as the power of God is exercised - with a fatherly solicitude which not only guides
      the whole, but reaches also individuals.
    #+END_QUOTE

    ...

    #+BEGIN_QUOTE
      *42.* If we turn now to things external and material, the first thing of all to secure is to save unfortunate working
      people from the cruelty of men of greed, who use human beings as mere instruments for money-making. It is neither just
      nor human so to grind men down with excessive labor as to stupefy their minds and wear out their bodies. Man's powers,
      like his general nature, are limited, and beyond these limits he cannot go. His strength is developed and increased by
      use and exercise, but only on condition of due intermission and proper rest. Daily labor, therefore, should be so
      regulated as not to be protracted over longer hours than strength admits. How many and how long the intervals of rest
      should be must depend on the nature of the work, on circumstances of time and place, and on the health and strength of
      the workman. Those who work in mines and quarries, and extract coal, stone and metals from the bowels of the earth,
      should have shorter hours in proportion as their labor is more severe and trying to health. Then, again, the season of
      the year should be taken into account; for not unfrequently a kind of labor is easy at one time which at another is
      intolerable or exceedingly difficult. Finally, work which is quite suitable for a strong man cannot rightly be required
      from a woman or a child. And, in regard to children, great care should be taken not to place them in workshops and
      factories until their bodies and minds are sufficiently developed. For, just as very rough weather destroys the buds of
      spring, so does too early an experience of life's hard toil blight the young promise of a child's faculties, and render
      any true education impossible. Women, again, are not suited for certain occupations; a woman is by nature fitted for
      home-work, and it is that which is best adapted at once to preserve her modesty and to promote the good bringing up of
      children and the well-being of the family. As a general principle it may be laid down that a workman ought to have
      leisure and rest proportionate to the wear and tear of his strength, for waste of strength must be repaired by cessation
      from hard work.
  
      In all agreements between masters and work people there is always the condition expressed or understood that there should
      be allowed proper rest for soul and body. To agree in any other sense would be against what is right and just; for it can
      never be just or right to require on the one side, or to promise on the other, the giving up of those duties which a man
      owes to his God and to himself.
    #+END_QUOTE

*** Journal <2025-11-18 Tue>
Some thoughts I had this morning after getting a dream of me talking to someone from a Baptist church.
In this dream it was depicted of them that they asked me "is a person permanently saved forever if it was only for a moment that they believed". And in this dream I had said, "Yes." And they also asked, "Why?" And in this dream I quoted / paraphrased, rather, several scriptures.  Though now that I've awoken from that dream, I want to clarify my stance on this from Scripture, as I wasn't happy with the entire dream conversation. It seemed to have errors in it. So this is me clarifying my current position:

A person *can* fall away from the faith after first coming to believe.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%208%3A13&version=ESV][Luke 8:13]]* - And the ones on the rock are those who, when they hear the word, receive it with joy. But these have no root; they believe for a while, and in time of testing fall away. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%203%3A12-19&version=ESV][Hebrews 3:12-19]]* - Take care, brothers, lest there be in any of you an *evil, unbelieving heart, leading you to fall away from the living God*. But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called today, that _none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin_. For *we share in Christ, if indeed we hold our original confidence firm to the end*. As it is said, Today, _if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion_. For who were those who heard and yet rebelled? Was it not all those who left Egypt led by Moses? And with whom was he provoked for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness? And *to whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest, but to those who were disobedient? So we see that they were unable to enter because of unbelief*. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

A person *must* come to not only have faith in the truth but also *love* the truth:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A31-47&version=ESV][John 8:31-47]]* - So Jesus said to the Jews who had believed ([[strongs:G4100][G4100 pepisteukotas: having believed]] [[https://biblehub.com/grammar/v-rpa-amp.htm]['V-RPA-AMP past tense']]) in him, If you abide in my word, you are truly my disciples, and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free. They answered him, We are offspring of Abraham and have never been enslaved to anyone. How is it that you say, You will become free? Jesus answered them, Truly, truly, I say to you, everyone who commits sin is a slave to sin. The slave does not remain in the house forever; the son remains forever. So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed. I know that you are offspring of Abraham; yet you seek to kill me because my word finds no place in you. I speak of what I have seen with my Father, and you do what you have heard from your father. They answered him, Abraham is our father. Jesus said to them, If you were Abraham's children, you would be doing what Abraham did, but now you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. This is not what Abraham did. You are doing what your father did. They said to him, We were not born of sexual immorality. We have one Father—even God. Jesus said to them, If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came from God and I am here. I came not of my own accord, but he sent me. Why do you not understand what I say? It is because you cannot bear to hear my word. You are of your father the devil, and your will is to do your father's desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, and has nothing to do with the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks out of his own character, for he is a liar and the father of lies. But because I tell the truth, you do not believe me. Which one of you convicts me of sin? If I tell the truth, why do you not believe me? Whoever is of God hears the words of God. The reason why you do not hear them is that you are not of God. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

As *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2018%3A20-32&version=ESV][Ezekiel 18:20-32]]* clearly shows and as Jesus also says, a person is able to repent. A person is able to come into agreement with God and love the truth and forsake sin.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2013%3A3&version=ESV][Luke 13:3]]* - No, I tell you; but unless you repent ([[https://biblehub.com/greek/3340.htm][3340. metanoeó]]), you will all likewise perish. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We have to abide in Jesus Christ's commandments through faith and obedience, and with perseverance.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%203%3A12-19&version=ESV][Hebrews 3:12-19]]* - Take care, brothers, lest there be in any of you an *evil, unbelieving heart, leading you to fall away from the living God*. But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called today, that _none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin_. For *we share in Christ, if indeed we hold our original confidence firm to the end*. As it is said, Today, _if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion_. For who were those who heard and yet rebelled? Was it not all those who left Egypt led by Moses? And with whom was he provoked for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness? And *to whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest, but to those who were disobedient? So we see that they were unable to enter because of unbelief*. (ESV)

In obedience we must abide in Jesus Christ's love, actually exercising it ourselves from our heart. We must not only hold our faith in Jesus Christ, but we must love Him and be keeping His commandments. We must be presently trusting and loving Jesus Christ, and continuing to abide in Jesus' commandments.

#+END_QUOTE

Now to bring up John 11. This says whoever is "believing..." [[strongs:G4100][(G4100 pisteuōn, is believing, is trusting)]]. So a person has to have died while trusting in Jesus Christ (see in John 11) and then continue going on trusting in Jesus Christ, continuing to trust Jesus Christ, in order to "by no means" die. So we *must* be abiding presently in Jesus Christ's commandments. We must be trusting before and after and during this "death" that we die.

And it's God's role to give eternal life.

I don't want to overspecify things to the point where it seems like I'm the one saying who is saved.
I don't want to lean on my own understanding.

+ Disclaimer :: Also, I need God to for the love of Jesus Christ deliver me from the satanic intrusive dreams and other demonic harassment, and clean up my soul from all the defilement which I'm blaming on being put under demonic oppression after I was born-again for a very extended amount of time. And I'd like God to please give me the promised testimony from Holy Spirit so that I know when to trust a dream or a vision, etc. I just want to clarify that because God needs to make the first move so that I can be led. Everything is on the backburner until God fulfills His promises which He has promised.
    I'm continually sacrificing good things while Jesus lets the devil rob me and lets the 'locusts' ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Joel%202%3A25&version=ESV][Joel 2:25]]) attack me continually, all because I'm waiting on Jesus Christ to fulfill His promises and can't make particular moves without Jesus' faithfulness in particular things.
    What's not done in faith is sin after all, so there are things I need to wait for Jesus to do before I have confidence to speak about or confidence to do because I don't want to be in the driver's seat. I want to be led by Jesus, not feeling like I'm being 'played' by the devil continually.

OK, disclaimer given.

So if a person is not continuing to trust in Jesus Christ or love Him by abiding in His commandments then they are presently a disbeliever and presently condemned. A saved person can be described by attributes. One of them is preferring God to evil. A person who is saved loves the truth and prefers God to evil.

I do not think is correct to say that *every* person who has "belief" no matter how well sown the word is (i.e. disregarding Jesus' parable about the sower) can't "fall away" from the faith. Clearly there are examples of people from Jesus' parable who lost their faith.

Even the Apostle Paul shows it's important to hold one's faith and a good conscience because some people have made a shipwreck of their faith by rejecting this advice. In other words, if a person's faith were likened to a ship, that ship crashed and was *very severely damaged* and ruined and the Apostle Paul thought it necessary for them to learn not to blaspheme by being handed over to satan. And blasphemy is when a person is bringing dishonour to God's name, to God's reputation by committing sin.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *I Timothy 1:18-20* - This charge I entrust to you, Timothy, my child, in accordance with the prophecies previously made about you, that by them you may wage the good warfare, holding faith and a good conscience. By rejecting this, some have made shipwreck of their faith, among whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have handed over to Satan that they may learn not to blaspheme. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

The fact is, if a person has disbelieved, they still have opportunity to repent (change their mind), so long as they are not dead and in Hades with an unbelieving heart.
And Jesus conquered death by the way.
Jesus went down there into the place of the dead ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%203%3A18-20&version=ESV][I Peter 3:18-20]]) and if someone who is dead hears His voice with a believing heart then they live but I'm quite sure the idea is that we need to have that faith in Jesus Christ so that when we do die (and I'm confident that refers to the spiritual baptism) we are raised to life with Him. A person may go through this death to life, perhaps in baptism, or just suddenly when God does it (it happened to me on 2 April 2022).

People who had that believing heart who had died before Jesus was crucified would have then heard and accepted Jesus' voice when He went into death, and those people would live.

A person needs a faith that is accompanied with agape love for the truth that treasures that truth and is so deeply rooted in the heart that it can't be removed. We need a law-abiding faith.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

*** Journal <2025-11-22 Sat>
I have close to no freedom.
I have very little joy.
I feel crushed to a pulp both by the world and by the church.
I've been made to endure testing, and harassment while having my joy stolen from me, while I have been trusting and obeying Jesus Christ, which *should* lead to peace that cannot be taken away and to rest.

But how does anyone weather such trials without joy?
How does anyone find motivation to do anything when joy has been taken way.
And how easy it is to do things when full of joy.

This is the pattern:
- 1. I find joy in something or someone (e.g. in God's commandments, or in getting born-again or in another person)
- 2. The devil comes along to try to steal that joy from me by undermining it in some way

The hope of the righteous brings joy (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Proverbs%2010%3A28&version=ESV][Proverbs 10:28]]*).
And love rejoices with the truth (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2013%3A6&version=ESV][I Corinthians 13:6]]*).

I mean, there's nothing like feeling washed clean and given a brand new heart and spirit.
Nothing quite like it.
It's better than buying a new computer, that's for sure.
And practicing righteousness, acting in truth and not lies, is joyous.
And practicing righteousness, acting in charity and mercy, is joyous.

I do not think I am a greedy person at all, and that's a really good thing to not covet or agape-love money.
But that means that I'm not motivated by earning lots of money.
I love to give to other people.
So, not being motivated by money, yet being compelled to work very hard in order to just get by, it is painfully difficult to do that when I do not have my own wife or family. Why? Because there is very close to no motivating reason to be working so, so much.

In 2020 there was someone else who I was interested and I'm using her as an example, because even before I was born-again and regenerated, in doing stuff for her, I had so much joy. With joy acting in truth out of love, there's no desire to want to sin. Like even though I was not in a relationship with this person, not a 2-way relationship anyway, if I gave her flowers (which she never accepted, which is fine. I think it's an important detail), or a birthday present or whatever it was, I'd easily just empty my wallet or all of my time to make something for her or give her something and when I actually followed through and did it I had so much joy that I could work endless hours, and I could resist sinful habits and not do them. There might be the thought "if there was ever to be a relationship between me and this person then they wouldn't want me to be watching porn", for example, so I wouldn't, and there was also no desire to do so because I was just happy while living authentically. My thoughts were actually more along the lines of, "I just feel so much better when acting out of integrity rather than lies. It gave me joy to do things for this person." That was not reciprocal but I felt like I no longer had a fractured heart. God doesn't want our hearts to be corrupt and a heart that doesn't desire to do good is the problem. I mean, when I had started acting out of my convictions to overcome anxiety, anxiety bought on by these social "rules" (which were not God's rules, that's for sure), and when I stopped listening to liars and started acting on "what felt right, correct" (I'm not advocating "feelings"-alone as a guiding principle of course, but Biblically good feelings are good feelings and not bad ones. We are supposed to have good motivations and not evil ones. The good person out of his good treasure brings forth good, and the evil person out of his evil treasure brings forth evil - [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2012%3A35&version=ESV][Matthew 12:35]]) then I had joy - lots of joy. But, she didn't feel the same way and that's OK. But after that I was not going to go back to living out of lies or out of guile. But overcoming the "fear of man" led to the next part of my journey. Christians are not supposed to fear man, but we are supposed to fear God!

But the point I try to make is:
- When I have no joy, it's like trying to make bricks without straw.
- When I have no joy, my concentration gets severely compromised, and distractions and false-substitutes are then used to fill the time. The devil knows this, so the devil tries to cut off sources of joy from my life, and undermine my good conscience with God, in order to tempt me into sin (to take the temporary edge off of my pain). But sin, I am now dead to (being regenerate), and are divinely empowered to stop practicing it. But that doesn't mean that the temptations cease with getting regenerated.
- I can complete huge amounts of work (or study, or 'labours of love') when I have *joy*.

Then in 2021 soon after I had properly given up with the last person, I met someone else. It was very unexpected. I wasn't looking or thinking about anyone else. But they just turned up.

And I had so much joy. And it felt like there was none of the former problems at all.
I can't tell you how happy I was.

There's a memory I have of looking at her like face to face from across a room and there were several seconds before I even registered that it happened. I was like a cat looking at a car's headlights no longer able to do anything. It was like that.
That was before I met her.

But then years later I meet here really unexpectedly and everything feels good.

I had so much *joy* and *hope*. And we were talking and then (I'm claiming family interference) I was not able to talk to her anymore. Conversation with her was terminated by my own free will out of their interests.

I had been talking to her about Pen.el, coming up with the name "Pen of Imagination", when I had just started working on it and getting ideas on it. That year I spent so, so much time pouring into this project because I was prevented from talking to her, she who I ended up proposing to later, and that the Pen.el project was one of the last things we had talked about and I wanted to make something for her out of it.

I can complete *huge* amounts of work when I have *joy*.

Towards the end of 2021, I begin turning to God, and seeking Him, because I could see what was coming with AI LLMs etc. and my joy was constantly being hacked at and everything seemed futile because no amount of work could ever "get on top" of AI or ever be enough to "find a wife". It just seemed like everything was impossible because of evil.
I kept going because I had faith that I would see her again. That is what was motivating me.
I had to keep having faith in seeing her again in order to keep going on.

And then I began seeking God much more diligently because of the AI stuff on the horizon.

I began falling in love with God's commandments.
I had begun actually trying to follow the 10 commandments from the heart.
I would wear a necklace with 10 1s on it (an identity matrix) which represented to me following the 10 commandments from the heart.

And then I get born-again on 2 April while wearing it and I became so full of joy and wonder over God.

I feel huge amounts of joy over Jesus Christ and over the grace of God which I received in a new spirit.

Out of wanting to honor Jesus after receiving the grace of God, I immediately put down a lot of bad sinful habits like watching porn which was a very dirty, depraved, habit. At least where previously it was the joy I had in those two girls/women which helped me to not engage in sinful stuff. But now, I felt like I didn't need that sinful stuff anymore.

God fixed me. God washed me. My room was extremely messy. But God fixed me. I was made new.

After getting born-again, it becomes very important to be a light to other people. It's important to not receive the grace of God in vain. It's important to not squander the grace but to share it with others.

After 1 month of pouring myself into telling people about me getting born-again, as I wanted to give God my *first fruits*, the pain of being cut off from talking to the person who I had met 1 year before started to become too great again. One month after being born-again of the spirit I became depressed. The only way I was able to continue is by reassuring myself that I'd see her again. That's kind of how faith works.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A1&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:1]]* - Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But it's faith based on what? It was faith based on believing that it was good/pure.
I wouldn't say it was faith based on a word from God.

Up to 2 April 2022 I was building Pen.el like Noah built an ark (Hebrews 11:7), but I wasn't warned by God regarding the AI stuff.
Up to 2 April 2022 I was also building Pen.el fully sure that I'd see her again (Hebrews 11:1).
Up to 2 April 2022 I was walking by faith for absolute sure, but faith in what?
I had faith, joy and hope.

Before I was born-again, building Pen.el when it was AI software, I was exercising faith but it was faith in one day being able to talk to her again.

After I was born-again, I have been writing my Bible and "walking by faith" but I needed a lot of correction and I was learning to trust God's Word. It has been very difficult sometimes:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Titus%202%3A11-13&version=ESV][Titus 2:11-13]]* - For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation for all people, training us to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live self-controlled, upright, and godly lives in the present age, waiting for our blessed hope, the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A36-40&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:36-40]]* - Others suffered mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment. They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were killed with the sword. They went about in skins of sheep and goats, destitute, afflicted, mistreated— of whom the world was not worthy—wandering about in deserts and mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth. And all these, though commended through their faith, did not receive what was promised, since God had provided something better for us, that apart from us they should not be made perfect. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Where there is hope there can be joy.

Being born-again and regenerate my joy must be grounded on having a good conscience with God. If I don't have a good conscience with God, I wont have joy.
So that's a real force for giving up idols, that is striving to maintain a good conscience with God.

But when I was born-again it became important to be putting my faith in God.

I think that right now I would have a lot of joy if:
- I felt clean and not harassed so that I could have hope and the joy of my salvation returned
- I was spoken to clearly and trustworthily by God with the testimony that Jesus Christ has come into the world from God in the flesh.

How joy has been taken away from me. So joy which I had regarding being born-again has been after a while taken away:
  - I have been made to *feel* like I have committed eternal sin because of an out of body meeting with someone claiming to be Holy Spirit on 3 May 2022, and then me, maybe gullible me, unsure, claiming that it was Holy Spirit but later realising that it didn't carry with it the testimony of Jesus Christ that the Apostle John says means that spirit is from God. So the spirit did not tell me that "Jesus Christ has come [from God, into the world,] in the flesh (i.e. flesh and blood)". That doesn't mean it *wasn't* the Holy Spirit, I don't think, anyway. But because it didn't give me the testimony, I can't say for sure that it was. Now, initially, I had just assumed that good things were happening. But after a couple of years I have been forced to question whether it was Holy Spirit or not, and having made claims.
  - But in my defense, on 3 May 2022, I spoke to the spirit and said, "My God is the God of Truth, Jesus has saved me from lies and Holy Spirit is my comforter. Are you the Holy Spirit?" And the spirit responded with, "Yes. I'll take a look at you."
    - No matter what that spirit said to me, I testified of Jesus. I testified of the God of Truth. I don't think I said anything wrong there. I was set free from *sin* through baptism into Jesus Christ's death ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%206%3A7&version=ESV][Romans 6:7]]). So I *was* set free from lies.
  - But, later on, I have come see the spirit's response with a big question mark because of what Jesus says in [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A37&version=ESV][Matthew 5:37]]. It's a little bit ambiguous because the response *was* simply a yes, followed by another separate sentence. I cannot be conclusive about it. In my view because there was not the "I John 4:2" testimony of Jesus Christ then I cannot trust it completely.
    - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A37&version=ESV][Matthew 5:37]]* - but let your word be, Yes, Yes, No, No, and that which is more than these is of the evil. (YLT)

Here is the pattern again. The pattern is that the devil targets my joy. The devil tries to kill steal the hope and the joy from me, and to be honest has been largely successful, but I'm trusting Jesus that that is temporary. I will have joy that the devil will not be able to steal:
- 1. On 3rd of May 2022, something happens. Now I thought at the time that this date was providence.
  - For a long time leading up to this, I have been unable to "get a Christian girlfriend". Forming romantic relationships has been impossible. They've been denied. I've been prevented from marrying. I've been prevented from having intimacy, from having a partner who acts on good will and on good faith and unconditional love. If it's a relationship then it has had to be unequally yoked in order for me to have it. So when I meet someone where it seemed like there were none of those types of problems about a year before I was born-again, I just had *joy* over it. It was pure joy for me. The only obstacle seemed to be "what other people thought" as far as I could tell.
- 2. And on 3rd of May 2022, I thought that having that "meeting" with someone who claimed to be Holy Spirit was providence because of the date that it happened. One year later, on 3 May 2023, I'm in a court of law being told by a judge that I must have
e been baptised at midnight.

I feel like my joy of being born-again and the feeling of being right and clean with God, and the feeling of having someone who I thought God made for me has all been taken from me, and I've been left feeling abandoned by God after pouring myself into trying to please Him.

This is what it has been like for me.

The attacks just kept going, and going, and going.

I made a marriage proposal to the person who I wanted to marry and I started getting spiritually attacked a lot after that.

My outwards appearance was messy.
My room was messy.
My room is currently messy, actually.
But I loved God and I loved that girl.
God gave me a new heart and a spirit and then I proposed to someone.

I proposed to them despite having been warned to not communicate with them.
I got a warning letter from the police after that.
It was like the terminator appearing on my doorstep.
You decide if this is good or evil.
Is it good or evil to deny marriage, but who exactly has been denying it?
Is it people or is it demons.
I don't blame the police officer, although if it were me, I would have used more discernment I would hope.
I don't even really blame the other side of court.
I think the problem is demons, and I think this problem has been a problem for longer than I know.

Was it good or evil that I decided to propose to her?
Was it wrong for me to ignore the warning and do it?

If someone told you to not inhale air while in the same room as them, then as a Christian are you obligated to hold your breath and suffocate and die because it might offend someone - because you have to "love them"? If an evil person told a Christian to renounce their faith in Jesus because they are offended by it, a Christian should surely not do as the evil person has said. That is because a Christian is not supposed to act fraudulently or deny the truth, and a Christian is not supposed to obey unrighteousness but honor God in their body. A Christian must love in the truth.

The question is, if someone said, "You're not allowed to speak to someone", but you couldn't bare not being able to talk to them every again, feeling like you'd want to kill yourself if you couldn't and then intended to propose to them, is it wrong to propose to them? And if it is wrong, is it the type of thing that needs to be punished so cruelly? I think that making it impossible to propose marriage is not OK. Actually the Bible says that in the last days people will forbid marriage (I Timothy 4:3).

Did God plan out this living nightmare in advance for me?

I think that Jesus should have spoken clearly to me about what has happened before it got to this point. I think that He should have answered one of my prayer requests a long time ago. By being in this situation without God's very specific guidance, I feel a little bit wronged by God. God sees the heart, so he saw what was in my heart. He must've seen the good. And yet, I feel like the good has been treated as if it was sin.

Imagine this, a person goes through life looking for someone to do life with. After spending their 20s and early 30s and to be honest teenage years too denied the right type of Christian relationship, and without Christian discipleship either, unable to marry and working extremely hard for hardly any money, finally meeting someone and out of peace, joy, agape love, rest, wanting to propose to them, but someone has made it impossible, and also, you've just been born-again of the spirit.

Not only would I not cover up being born-again of the spirit ([[https://web.archive.org/web/20220402091720/https://mullikine.github.io/posts/astral-projection/][I blogged about it the day it happened]]), but why would I also want to suffocate and kill a love. God doesn't want me to cover up His gospel, or good deeds. Would God want me to experience love that wants to marry someone and then suffocate it and never let it see the light of day? Is that what God wants? To first let a person experience what it's like to love someone and then destroy out of duty? I think Jesus Himself needs to give me the answer to that one. And He also needs to fix me.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A16&version=ESV][Matthew 5:16]]* - In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in heaven. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

If I am not made totally clean again and restored and spoken to, then I believe God has wronged me. What I've been through is a living hell that has left me feeling defiled and forsaken by God. It's really not OK. The adversity has gone way too far.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A2-3&version=ESV][I John 5:2-3]]* - By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and obey his commandments. For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments. And his commandments are not burdensome. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

So this is the basic pattern.
- 1. I'm washed clean. God gives me a new heart that fears Him and a new spirit, with a good, clean conscience and joy. I learn to reject lies and rejoice with the truth
- 2. The devil then tries to attack the joy of being washed clean or the joy in the truth. I am attacked by demons, almost every single day waking up to lewd, antichrist, lying, dreams and visions and other attacks against my soul. And when I cave in to temptation it feels like I become a bit more unclean.

I need to be clean and have a good conscience to have joy:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Jude%201%3A24-25&version=ESV][Jude 1:24-25]]* - Now to him who is able to keep you from stumbling and to *present you blameless* before the presence of his glory *with great joy*, to the only God, our Savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory, majesty, dominion, and authority, before all time and now and forever. Amen. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

How am I supposed to function properly if I'm not allowed to have joy? Why would I have *any* interest in being here on the earth when I've got nothing to hope in and nothing to have joy about?

Now I am only hoping in being released from this world so I can go to a place where righteousness dwells, rather than darkness, because this world is darkness, and it's giving me no love.

I hope to be saved and raptured. Even that hope of rapture has been attacked.
Even the hope of being caught up with Jesus Christ in the air at the end of the ages and going to heaven has been attacked.
Yes, even that. It could be this one. It's correct to be encouraged by that hope.

Rapture is biblically correct, and judgement at the *close* of the age is biblically correct, and a total renewal of the cosmos (heavens and earth) is biblically correct. Sure, the earth has had many ages and earth might even go on for many more ages, but only the Father knows when the very end is. But at the end of the age there is the separation of the wheat and the tares.

Then there is the resurrection of the body. It's normal for a born-again Christian to also die an earthly death but this is not the death of the spirit. The person's consciousness continues after bodily death. And the physical body is resurrected also to life:

#+END_QUOTE

When people the righteous rise from the dead with their resurrection body, they are like angels - imperishable, never to die anymore. There is certainly no reincarnation for them. While I believe there are "many" ages of the Earth, I do not believe in an earthly reincarnation. After one go in this Earth, I believe the righteous go to heaven. And heaven is a place without corruption. That's my beliefs:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2012%3A25&version=ESV][Mark 12:25]]* -  For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven. (ESV)

*** Journal <2025-11-24 Mon>
The good Samaritan didn't stalk the innkeeper
to find out how they used the money which he gave to support the neighbour he made.

It's not our duty to avenge wrongdoing.
It's our duty to keep God's commandments for us.

So that means when we give we do it out of mercy, faith and obedience to Jesus (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%205%3A42&version=ESV][Matthew 5:42]]*).
That's our duty.

We do our duty in that moment of charity, but that doesn't mean our duty ends in that moment.
The good Samaritan was so committed to the welfare of the neighbour he met, that he made a commitment to pay anything further that the innkeeper may require in caring for his neighbour when next he visits.

The only person who can make this commitment with a guarantee is God since God owns the cosmos (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2050%3A11-12&version=ESV][Psalms 50:11-12]]*) and God always fulfills His promises at the right time (*Hebrews 11:39*) for those who through faith and patience inherit His promises (*Hebrews 6:11-12*):

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%206%3A11-12&version=ESV][Hebrews 6:11-12]]* - And we desire each one of you to show the same earnestness to have the full assurance of hope until the end, so that you may not be sluggish, but imitators of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A17-19&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:17-19]]* - By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac, and he who had received the promises was in the act of offering up his only son, of whom it was said, Through Isaac shall your offspring be named. He considered that God was able even to raise him from the dead, from which, figuratively speaking, he did receive him back. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We should still love like the good Samaritan, but recognise that despite our best efforts, we will always fall short of the glory of God, and need God's grace so are justified by our faith in Jesus Christ, not works, but in faith we obey Jesus and in faith we love God and our neighbour and hope in God:

The Innkeeper has a duty. I believe we need to continue to seek commendation from God even after having received mercy:

#+END_QUOTE

I believe that justification is a state of righteousness which we don't commend ourselves for (God commends people for their faith), Jesus talks about those who humble themselves. The tax collector here remained in a place of knowing they *still* need mercy from God.

I believe we need to continue seeking to please God and to forsake sin and to keep Jesus' commandments. Humility continues to endeavour to be commended by God. So that is what we should do. I think it's OK to think of a servant of Jesus as the Innkeeper in Jesus parable, Jesus being the ultimate Good Samaritan, and then Jesus' servants exercising this same type of love in the way that Jesus commands us to love. Jesus is our Redeemer. So I think we can think of the Innkeeper as having been redeemed in order to exercise the love of God. God draws people to Jesus, Jesus entrusts His servants with the care of people along with the means to do so. In the parable, the good Samaritan gave the Innkeeper a person and the means to care for them, and a commandment to do so, and the Innkeeper has to go on in faith. It might get difficult, the good Samaritan promised that he would pay anything extra when he returns. So sometimes things might look quite tight financially but we are commanded to have faith and do our duty:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

I fast twice a week; I give tithes of all that I get. But the tax collector, standing far off, would not even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, God, be merciful to me, a sinner! I tell you, this man went down to his house justified, rather than the other. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Saving for own future while at the same time neglecting the duty that we have for our neighbour and family in Christ is lacking in faith.
Saving is OK but it's not good if it means willful disobedience to Jesus.

Who saves fire extinguishers for their own house when their neighbour's or nearby relative's house is burning down?
Likewise, our earthly possessions should be thought of as belonging to Jesus, and should be used as a means to take care of one another.

How could it be said there was faith in the obedience if you only had confidence if you are assured by natural means such as sight
how the money is going to be used?
That would be very "works"-based as well, rather than "faith-based".

We walk by faith and not by sight.

Now, if you "did" see the money being misused, that makes things more complicated (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2010%3A28-29&version=ESV][I Corinthians 10:28-29]]*).

But we're not supposed to be actively ensuring that everyone is definitely going to use the money for this specific purpose.
Sinful people do make mistakes and sometimes fall into temptation and misuse money that's been given to them in charity or for charity.
But God sent Jesus while were yet sinners.
God gave us the benefit of the doubt.
And that's how God continues to deal with us.
If we repent, God gives more mercy.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

Like the master in Jesus's parable, we give people the "benefit of the doubt" when it comes to giving:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2025%3A19-21&version=ESV][Matthew 25:19-21]]* - Now after a long time the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them. #+END_QUOTE

If there was no "benefit of the doubt" then there'd be no freedom in it,
there'd be no opportunity for the person to will the good, rather than out of compulsion.

It would be eliminating God's work in the situation and to not have faith that God is working in the situation if one were to think they needed to be constantly enforcing how the money is used.

If the innkeeper in the parable of the "good Samaritan" thought he may need to spend some money on medicine, food or something for the comfort (*Proverbs 31:6-7*), or to give money to the person in need for travels, say or whatever may arise as a need in the care of the person, then they have freedom to use that money in that way and God sees everything.

Rather than following people around to see how they use goods given to them in charity, we could give to one person, and entrust the situation to God, and immediately are ready for doing something else.

The Holy Spirit *must* make this confession (speak the same thing as God) that Jesus Christ has come (from God, into the world) in the flesh (as flesh and blood) for us to know that the spirit is from God. So if we are to *know* for sure that the spirit is from God then it must confess this fact, that Jesus Christ has come (proceeded forth) [from God, into the world] in the flesh [i.e. as flesh and blood]. If you don't know that the spirit affirms this fact then we can't know that it's the Holy Spirit:

I think [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2011%3A13&version=ESV][Matthew 11:13]] reads in the Greek more like, "All the prophets and the law until John prophesied."
The way the ESV reads, it seems to make it [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2011%3A13&version=ESV][Matt 11:13]] out to say there were only prophets up until John, and so by implication excludes Jesus Christ Himself, who is also the Son of God, from being a 'prophet'.
And it also seems to read like the Law itself was only until John.
But I do not believe that [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2011%3A13&version=ESV][Matthew 11:13]] actually reads like that the Greek. I believe that the way the Greek reads is more like this: "all the prophets and the Law up to John prophesied".
Consider that Jesus Christ is the telos of the Law and Jesus also gave commandments (Christ's Law), it also makes sense that He is the "telos of the prophets". Jesus is the Son of God, but that doesn't mean He is not also regarded as a prophet.
Jesus also made prophets Himself.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%204%3A11-13&version=ESV][Ephesians 4:11-13]]* - And it was He who gave some to be apostles, some to be prophets, some to be evangelists, and some to be pastors and teachers, to equip the saints for works of ministry and to build up the body of Christ, until we all reach unity in the faith and in the knowledge of the Son of God, as we mature to the full measure of the stature of Christ. (engbsb2020eb)
#+END_QUOTE

If we are "in the Spirit" then what other people confess or refuse to confess identifies whether or not the spirit working through them is from God. The principle can and should be used to test dreams, visions, angels, demons and human beings to see if we can trust them. I would never trust someone completely who refuses to give me the testimony that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh, as the Apostle John speaks of in [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A2-3&version=ESV][I John 4:2-3]].

[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A2-3&version=ESV][I John 4:2-3]] doesn't say that if a spirit speaks the name "Jesus" then it's from God. It doesn't say that at all. Rather, this word confess [[https://biblehub.com/greek/3670.htm][(G3670 homologeó)]] surely means that "confess Jesus" is agreeing with, agreeing with Jesus. The spirit must agree that Jesus has come in the flesh and the spirit must agree with Jesus. Now if a spirit does say to me that "Jesus Christ has come from God into the world in the flesh", then that gives me confidence that the message is from God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A2-3&version=ESV][I John 4:2-3]]* - By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the [[strongs:G1722][(G1722 en; in [the form of])]] flesh is from God, and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist, which you heard was coming and now is in the world already. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE
