#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%204%3A7-10&version=ESV][James 4:7-10]]* - Submit (*[[https://biblehub.com/greek/5293.htm][G5293 Hypotagēte]]*) yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded. Be wretched and mourn and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning and your joy to gloom. Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://biblehub.com/greek/5293.htm][G5293 Hypotagēte]] :: hupotassó: To subject, to subordinate, to submit, to be under obedience. From hupo and tasso; to subordinate; reflexively, to obey -- be under obedience (obedient), put under, subdue unto, (be, make) subject (to, unto), be (put) in subjection (to, under), submit self unto.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Titus%202%3A11-14&version=ESV][Titus 2:11-14]]* - For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation for all people, training us to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live self-controlled, upright, and godly lives in the present age, waiting for our blessed hope, the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ, who gave himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for himself a people for his own possession who are zealous for good works. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2019%3A2-5&version=ESV][Acts 19:2-5]]* - And he said to them, Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed? And they said, No, we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit. And he said, Into what then were you baptized? They said, Into John's baptism. And Paul said, John baptized with the baptism of repentance, telling the people to believe in the one who was to come after him, that is, Jesus. On hearing this, they were baptized in the name (G3686 onoma) of the Lord Jesus. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://biblehub.com/greek/3686.htm][G3686 ónoma]] :: name; (figuratively) the manifestation or revelation of someone's character, i.e. as distinguishing them from all others. Thus "praying in the name of Christ" means to pray as directed (authorized) by Him, bringing revelation that flows out of being in His presence. "Praying in Jesus' name" therefore is not a "religious formula" just to end prayers (or get what we want)!

So typically, we come to faith, get baptised into Jesus' name (G3686 onoma. i.e. into the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit is still Jesus's onoma name), are forgiven and we should straight away endeavour to be doing all the will of God for us (all of what God wants us to do) and continue learning and understanding what God's will is for us and put into practice what God's will is for us (i.e. sanctification, faith in Jesus, trusting and obeying Jesus, love in the truth, etc.).
Peter advises us to arm ourself with the way of thinking that is to be doing the will of God even in face of the suffering that comes from the active resistance to doing the will of God. I.e. we should submit to God in obedience, resist rendering evil for evil, stop letting sin reign, stop obeying sin, and instead obey Jesus and practice good works done in faith.
Since Jesus suffered in the flesh because He was practicing perfect rightetousness while sinful men killed Him, we arm ourselves with this same way of thinking, that is to cease from issin and live for the rest of the time in the flesh no longer for human passions but for the will of God.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%204%3A1-9&version=ESV][I Peter 4:1-9]]* - Since therefore Christ suffered in the flesh, *arm yourselves with the same way of thinking*, for whoever has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin, so as to live for the rest of the time in the flesh no longer for human passions but for the will of God. The time that is past suffices for doing what the Gentiles want to do, living in sensuality, passions, drunkenness, orgies, drinking parties, and lawless idolatry. With respect to this they are surprised when you do not join them in the same flood of debauchery, and they malign you; but they will give account to him who is ready to judge the living and the dead. The end of all things is at hand; therefore be self-controlled and sober-minded for the sake of your prayers. Above all, keep loving one another earnestly, since love covers a multitude of sins. Show hospitality to one another without grumbling. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%207%3A21&version=ESV][Matthew 7:21]]* - Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

If we're really loving in the truth then we will speak the truth about what God's word says. We don't want to lie in order to get out of punishment. We want to choose the path of love even if it means we might be punished for it. It would be wrong to plea guilty to a lesser charge if you knew you were not guilty of the charge in order to get out of taking a greater charge carrying a greater sentence but where the charge is true. Because love doesn't fear punishment. We're not supposed to fear what mankind might do to us, or fear prison time because if we are doing what pleases God, we have a good conscience. We're supposed to fear God and do what pleases God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2018%3A7-8&version=ESV][Matthew 18:7-8]]* - Woe to the world for temptations to sin! For it is necessary that temptations come, but woe to the one by whom the temptation comes! And if your hand or your foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life crippled or lame than with two hands or two feet to be thrown into the eternal fire. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

I am despairing right now because the fight against sin and error has been so difficult and I keep caving into temptation.

I get spiritually attacked fairly frequently through other people sometimes.

This week someone just blurted out to me "fiery arrows" like "you have a long way to go", after I tell them that Jesus is the way the truth and the life and there's no way to Father God except through Him and that we need to focus on Jesus by trusting and obeying Him and that if someone keeps Jesus commandments then the Holy Spirit will come to them and Jesus will manifest to them. Jesus is the reality, the truth. I said this to the person and they just said "you have a long way to go". And this in the moment was a fiery dart. I did respond to the person with "salvation is not just a thing we hope for but is a here and now thing." And I mentioned Romans 10:8-10.

(that is, to bring Christ down) or Who will descend into the abyss? (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead). But what does it say? The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart (that is, the word of faith that we proclaim); because, if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. but I believe we must also continue on in Christ's teaching. I'm a believer in God's word which includes what's written in Romans 11.

=@acsberean4092=: I would suggest saying "Whoever keeps Jesus Christ's commandments PROVES they abide in Him."

=@ShaneMulligan-n7h=: =@acsberean4092=, that's true also. Both verses in [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15&version=ESV][John 14:15]],21 are true. My way of wording it would go as following: The person born of God trusts and loves God, and keeps His commandments and abides in Him and does good by default. Jesus commanded us to have faith in Him ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A1&version=ESV][John 14:1]]), so it is an entrypoint, as in if we are doing this (trusting in Him) then we abide in Him. But a person must continue to abide in His teaching ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20John%201%3A9&version=ESV][2 John 1:9]]), so in hearing more commandments such as to love our family in Christ, it is essential that we do so. After all, to deny that we need to love our family in Christ would be to not trust His words. So we have to be correctable by Jesus and His teachings. But the new creation person born-of God does really love their family in Christ but while we are lugging around the sinful flesh sometimes we make mistakes (as in sin) but they're the mistake and not a part of the new identity but like the prodigal son returning to his father, we confess and turn from sins if we make them. By default a child of God does the will of God and from the good treasure (love of God) in their heart they produce good. We identify as the new child of God, the one who loves God and trusts Him, and we don't identify as the sinful flesh. [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A15&version=ESV][John 14:15]],21 at first seemed like a bit of a chicken-and-egg problem, where which comes first: "If you love Jesus, you will keep Jesus' commandments." or "The one who keeps Jesus' commandments is the one who loves Jesus." But a miracle happens where God circumcises the heart so we love Him and live. And God will help us to love Him with our whole heart. God will sanctify us.

*** Journal <2026-01-03 Sat>
The principle behind being a "doer" rather than merely a "hearer" of God's word still applies:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A13&version=ESV][Romans 2:13]]* - For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but the doers of the law who will be justified. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%201%3A22&version=ESV][James 1:22]]* - But be doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Those who actually trust God's word, even given through Moses, would trust Jesus' word:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A46&version=ESV][John 5:46]]* - If you believed Moses, you would believe me; for he wrote of me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2016%3A29-31&version=ESV][Luke 16:29-31]]* - But Abraham said, They have Moses and the Prophets; let them hear them. And he said, No, father Abraham, but if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent. He said to him, If they do not hear Moses and the Prophets, neither will they be convinced if someone should rise from the dead. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We must be those who receive Jesus Christ's word and do it:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%208%3A37&version=ESV][John 8:37]]* - I know that you are offspring of Abraham; yet you seek to kill me because my word finds no place in you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

It's certainly not about boasting that we've done the law. But about actually doing it. And a person's praise is from God:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%207%3A19&version=ESV][John 7:19]]* - Has not Moses given you the law? Yet none of you keeps the law. Why do you seek to kill me? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God wants us to listen and obey His Word, and His Word appeared in the flesh. Jesus came into the world in the flesh:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Kings%2018%3A11-12&version=ESV][II Kings 18:11-12]]* - The king of Assyria carried the Israelites away to Assyria and put them in Halah, and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes, because they did not obey the voice of the LORD their God but transgressed his covenant, even all that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded. They neither listened nor obeyed. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

We have to be "doers" of Jesus' word. We have to trust and obey Jesus:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%204%3A3&version=ESV][Romans 4:3]]* - For what does the Scripture say? Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2011%3A28&version=ESV][Luke 11:28]]* - But he said, Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and keep it! (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A37-42&version=ESV][John 5:37-42]]* - And the Father who sent me has himself borne witness about me. His voice you have never heard, his form you have never seen, and you do not have his word abiding in you, for you do not believe the one whom he has sent. You search the Scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that bear witness about me, yet you refuse to come to me that you may have life. I do not receive glory from people. But I know that you do not have the love of God within you. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A24-25&version=ESV][John 5:24-25]]* - Truly, truly, I say to you, whoever hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life. He does not come into judgment, but has passed from death to life. Truly, truly, I say to you, an hour is coming, and is now here, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%205%3A28-29&version=ESV][John 5:28-29]]* - Do not marvel at this, for an hour is coming when all who are in the tombs will hear his voice and come out, those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment. *** Journal <2026-01-05 Mon>
We must be led by the spirit, not by the flesh. If a person is not led by the
spirit (i.e. if they are lawless and disobedient, ungodly sinners, unholy and
profane, etc.), then they're under the law and will get "hit by the book".
Being led by the spirit, a person should not be led by anyone who does not
confess or agree with Jesus Christ and are not themselves led by the spirit. So
even when Jesus was going to people's houses, etc. Jesus was ultimately was not
led at all by them but rather by Father God as Jesus mantained His obedience and faithfulness to Father
God. So whatever we do as Christians should be bridled by a faithfulness and
obedience to God as well. Because whatever is not done in faith is sin:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%201%3A8-9&version=ESV][I Timothy 1:8-9]]* - Now we know that the law is good, if one uses it lawfully, understanding this, that the law is not laid down for the just but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for those who strike their fathers and mothers, for murderers, (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But if you bite and devour one another, watch out that you are not consumed by one another. But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh. For the desires of the flesh are against the Spirit, and the desires of the Spirit are against the flesh, for these are opposed to each other, to keep you from doing the things you want to do. #+END_QUOTE

I do not think [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A19&version=ESV][I John 5:19]] passage is saying that the kosmos is controlled/run by Satan. It would be a misreading to think that the planet is controlled by Satan. Rather, I think it's saying that it's laden or it lays with evil and that the people who are still in darkness are under the power of Satan, and that makes sense to me, because as we know there exists spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A19&version=ESV][I John 5:19]]* - We know that we are from God, and the whole world (G2889 kosmos; world) lies in the power of the evil one. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ [[https://biblehub.com/interlinear/1_john/5-19.htm][I John 5:19 (Interlinear)]] :: We know that of God we are and the world [[strongs:G2889][(G2889 kosmos)]] whole [[strongs:G3650][(G3650 holos)]] in [[strongs:G1722][(G1722 en)]] the [[strongs:G3588][(G3588 tō)]] evil/evil [one] [[strongs:G4190][(G4190 ponērō)]] lies [[strongs:G2749][(G2749 keitai; laid, appointed, set, standing, destined)]]

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%2026%3A18&version=ESV][Acts 26:18]]* - to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, *that they may receive* forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are sanctified by faith in me. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Taking a look at other parts of Scripture helps to understand better, the situation. Those who are "of the world" rather than "of God" are in darkness (they don't walk according to the truth, they don't love God, they don't love the truth). But God sent Jesus Christ as light so that whoever is trusting in Him, hearing His word and trusting His word, may not remain in darkness. So the whole world / kosmos being laid in evil, or laying in the power of the evil one (another interpretation), is really saying that Satan has the people who are "of the world" deceived and walking in darkness, and also reiterating that there are forces of evil in the kosmos, in the world in the heavenly places:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2012%3A44-48&version=ESV][John 12:44-48]]* - And Jesus cried out and said, Whoever believes in me, believes not in me but in him who sent me. And whoever sees me sees him who sent me. *I have come into the world as light, so that whoever believes in me may not remain in darkness*. If anyone hears my words and does not keep them, I do not judge [[strongs:G2919][(G2919 krinō: do judge)]] him; for I did not come to judge the world [[strongs:G2919][(G2919 krinō: I might judge)]] but to save the world. The one who rejects me and does not receive my words has a judge; the word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

(ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

But it's truly God who is ultimately in control of the world. Satan is a defeated foe and his destiny is hell. But Satan tries to bring people down with him:

*** Journal <2026-02-11 Wed>

I went into the city today and I met with various people and God encouraged me through those interactions.
I have faith that God is still working and will deliver me from all defilement etc.
And I'll still be meditating on God's word and trying to put it into practice (be a doer of His word).

God uses law enforcement and as a believer in Jesus, it's very important to be endeavouring to maintain a good conscience and to be a "doer" of love when participating in a court of law:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2013%3A1-10&version=ESV][Romans 13:1-10]]* - Let every person be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been instituted by God. Therefore whoever resists the authorities resists what God has appointed, and those who resist will incur judgment. For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Would you have no fear of the one who is in authority? Then do what is good, and you will receive his approval, for he is God's servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not bear the sword in vain. For he is the servant of God, an avenger who carries out God's wrath on the wrongdoer. Therefore one must be in subjection, not only to avoid God's wrath but also for the sake of conscience. For the same reason you also pay taxes, for the authorities are ministers of God, attending to this very thing. Pay to all what is owed to them: taxes to whom taxes are owed, revenue to whom revenue is owed, respect to whom respect is owed, honor to whom honor is owed. Owe no one anything, except to love each other, for the one who loves another has fulfilled the law. The commandments, You shall not commit adultery, You shall not murder, You shall not steal, You shall not covet, and any other commandment, are summed up in this word: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. Love does no wrong to a neighbor; therefore love is the fulfilling of the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%2013%3A9-11&version=ESV][Mark 13:9-11]]* - But be on your guard. And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all nations. And when they bring you to trial and deliver you over, do not be anxious beforehand what you are to say, but say whatever is given you in that hour, for it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Behold, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison, that you may be tested, and for ten days you will have tribulation. Be faithful unto death, and I will give you the crown of life. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Peter%201%3A6-7&version=ESV][I Peter 1:6-7]]* - In this you rejoice, though now for a little while, if necessary, you have been grieved by various trials, so that the tested genuineness of your faith—more precious than gold that perishes though it is tested by fire—may be found to result in praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

(ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Love is not afraid of punishment. Love does not intend to do harm to our neighbour. Love abhors evil and rejoices with the truth. We should not be afraid of punishment if we are doing good, but should at all times endeavour to be speaking the truth, maintain a good conscience before God who knows everything, walking by faith and loving one another. We need to be doers of good, having been forgiven by God through faith in Jesus, loving Jesus rather than evil:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%204%3A17-21&version=ESV][I John 4:17-21]]* - By this is love perfected with us, so that we may have confidence for the day of judgment, because as he is so also are we in this world. There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear. For fear has to do with punishment, and whoever fears has not been perfected in love. We love because he first loved us. If anyone says, I love God, and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen cannot love God whom he has not seen. And this commandment we have from him: whoever loves God must also love his brother. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

And for the record, when I went through court, I was not offered the option of "no plea" to my memory.
I do have a problem with that, because sometimes the right thing to do is stay silent.
I was asked to plead guilty or not guilty.
And I was pushed into the situation where I had to do that by what felt like witchcraft.
It felt like a total stitchup.
If a person does not know if they are guilty or not guilty then it would be wrong to plead guilty or not guilty especially when there is not full agreement of the facts which have been filed into court which are given to the judge.
But my intentions with pleading guilty was to minimise harm to the other party while acknowledging that I wasn't without fault.
And I would advise others who end up in court to do whatever is the most loving thing, endeavouring to maintain a good conscience with God.
I still have unresolved issues because of a continuing defilement of spirit or flesh which I never used to have which I blame on seemingly unending demonic harassment.
I have been continually asking God to provide for me the promised testimony of Jesus Christ from Holy Spirit and to heal me and deliver me from evil.

*** Journal <2026-02-16 Mon>

I think that key to walking in victory over the "sin in the flesh" is to fill one's mind and heart with thoughts, feelings and intentions that are of the Spirit of God. So when the sin in the flesh is fighting against my mind to try to make me do things that are defiling, the way to disempower it is to fill my mind and heart with thoughts, feelings and intentions that are of the Spirit. This morning I put that into practice and it worked, but there was a battle. I think that walking by the Spirit includes such things as believing the Truth, being obedient to Jesus, willing to love not only in thought but in deed because walking by the Spirit needs to be walking in the Truth.

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Galatians%205%3A17-18&version=ESV][Galatians 5:17-18]]* - For the desires of the flesh are against the Spirit, and the desires of the Spirit are against the flesh, for these are opposed to each other, to keep you from doing the things you want to do. But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Fear of God and faith in God go hand in hand. Love for God and hatred of evil go hand in hand. Abraham did not cheat. He was a doer in reality.

I pray for old friends I have known since before I was born-again.
I get pictures of them in my mind in dreams quite frequently - almost on a daily basis, even if the dreams to not seem "true".
Even if the dreams seems often also to bring up or refer to mistakes I have made in the past.
Even if the dreams seems often to encourage debauchery and sin.
If I get pictures of old friends from before I was born-again, and of family members "of the flesh" (i.e. from natural birth), I still pray to God to save them.
Of course, I want them all to be saved and to have a genuine faith in Jesus Christ.
And I'm trying my best to fight the spiritual battles.

Also, since God wants me to not have desires for evil things, then perhaps God is simply giving me opportunities to say no to various temptations.
A major part of the spiritual attacks, I believe are opportunities for me to choose the good, to choose holiness and godliness over lewdness and sinful passion.

I'm so tired of battling, though.

*** Journal <2026-08-30 Sun 19:47>
I have fond memories of my former life, and thankful to God for a relatively decent previous life, but I'm not agape loving it.
But certainly those people I remember, I hope and pray do come to or continue in the knowledge of God through faith in Jesus Christ.
But that previous life of mine died, and I am now looking forwards, endeavouring to walk in newness of life, living for the will of God.
I don't agape love my previous life.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Philippians%203%3A8&version=ESV][Philippians 3:8]]* - Indeed, I count everything as loss because of the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. For his sake I have suffered the loss of all things and count them as rubbish, in order that I may gain Christ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

My former parents are of my previous life. My previous life is dead.
My former genaeology is not my present genaeology.
Those who I formerly regarded as "uncle" and "aunty", "nana", "grandad" and "grandpa" and "grandma" and "brother" and "sister"
I no longer regard as having those titles. But if any of them are in Christ then they would be brother and sister to me.

I reject calling my former parents (from my former life) who I am still in close physical proximity to as "my parents".

I haven't said they are not believers, and neither have I said they are believers. I have simply said they are not my parents.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2014%3A26&version=ESV][Luke 14:26]]* - If anyone comes to me and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, yes, and even his own life, he cannot be my disciple. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Now since these people who appear as my previous parents, are truly no longer my parents in reality,
then in understanding Jesus' teaching that anyone who comes to Him and does not hate their mother and father
cannot be His disciple, it's correct to say that there is no need for me to hate these people anymore
if I am to come to Jesus Christ some more because they are not my parents.
Jesus is talking about hating parents and these people are not my parents.

But that doesn't mean that I have /never/ hated people who I considered at some point to be my parents (i.e. those who formerly I had regarded as being my parents)
and crucially *when* they actually were my parents.
But if the people I hated are no longer my parents then I don't have to hate them in order to come to Jesus.

Now I hate my previous life.

It is no more the reality that these people are my parents, as I died an actual death when I was born-again, and all things became new,
and so those people from my previous life have died along with my previous life.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%205%3A14-15&version=ESV][II Corinthians 5:14-15]]* - For the love of Christ controls us, because we have concluded this: that one has died for all, therefore all have died; and he died for all, that _those who live *might no longer* live for themselves but for him who for their sake died and was raised._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2011%3A25-27&version=ESV][John 11:25-27]]* - Jesus said to her, I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live, and everyone who lives and believes in me shall never [[strongs:G3756][(G3756 οὐ)]] [[strongs:G3361][(G3361 μή)]] die. Do you believe this? She said to him, Yes, Lord; I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who is coming into the world. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I hate my old life. And even this new life now has felt rather spoiled and contaminated in part to what has felt like extreme resistance to walking in newness of life,
and a Satanic snare which seems to have been an attempmt to trap me into walking according the flesh by peer pressure.
I simply can't affirm that those people I formerly regarded as my parents are my parents anymore if I am to love them in reality how I'm commanded to love them.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1-2&version=ESV][I John 5:1-2]]* - Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the Father loves whoever has been born of him. _By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God *and* obey his commandments._ (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

I have a new family now, my family in Christ. God has made all thing new.

I would love those who I formerly regarded as family to come to know God through faith in Jesus Christ,
walking by the Spirit, abiding in Jesus Christ's commandments in reality.
But reflecting on who I pray for, I actually pray for them just about as frequently for them as I do for other people, that they come into the knowledge of God / come into greater knowledge of God through faith in Jesus Christ.

There is a way I love those who are surely family in Christ which is that of true agape love for my true family who are in Christ,

OK, so Abraham was rich, but He was also a servant of God. God delights in the welfare of His servant (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2035%3A27&version=ESV][Psalms 35:27]]*). So if a person is a good steward of God's belongings (and the whole earth belongs to God), then God delights in their welfare, for that person is like the innkeeper in the story of the "good Samaritan". It's clear that Abraham did not receive the King of Sodom's gifts because he wanted God to get all the glory (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis%2014%3A21-23&version=ESV][Genesis 14:21-23]]*). And Abraham did not covet the gifts of God (including his only begotten son Isaac) more than God Himself, and Abraham even tithed. It's clear that Abraham was a servant of God, and also prosperous. So if a person is actually maintaining their faith in God in reality and opportunistically choosing to keep Jesus Christ's teachings including "giving to the one who begs from you", for example, then they can be trusted with prosperity/welfare (not necessarily money).   - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%207%3A24&version=ESV][John 7:24]]* - Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment. (ESV)

    - *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%206%3A45&version=ESV][Luke 6:45]]* - The good person out of the good treasure of his heart produces good, and the evil person out of his evil treasure produces evil, for out of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaks. (ESV)

So long as people are being like the Bereans, testing everything,
and abiding in Jesus' commandments (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A2&version=ESV][I John 5:2]]*), "misuse" isn't an issue.
I still try to avoid using the AI/AGI stuff until I am assured that they have not been built from theft.
If the data which has gone into training(building) the LLMs / MoE models has been willingly put forward/donated by the people who own it, then there isn't a theft issue as far as I see.
So, for example, if a bunch of artists got together and decided they wanted to have an AI art generator trained on their own collections, then that is OK.
But it would be wrong to take two different artists/producers, such as downloading Lord of the Rings and the Narnia series stuff and then producing and distributing and selling AI generated books and movies that are an interpolation of those works, when the copyright holders did not consent to a collaboration.

I have mentioned this also on John Piper's video ([[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CIMZH7DEPPQ&lc=UgwXjwaeOp6gzd9rueV4AaABAg][youtube.com:  John Piper Asked ChatGPT to Write a Prayer {@ thegospelcoalition }]]):

At 1:45, JP mentioned as recorded on this video from May 3 2025 that "Computers do words better than you. Seriously, better than me."

It crossed my mind today (April 18 2026) that, "Real speech comes from the heart, so AI can still be called a speechless idol, even if it produces the imitation of speech or writing".

4 words from the heart of a human being saying "Jesus Christ is Lord" or 7 words from the heart of a human being saying "Jesus Christ is the Son of God" to me, even if it sounded wrongly articulated to my ears, but God heard it in the spirit, is worth more than infinite words generated by AI.

The person "doing the will of Father God" is the person who "believes" and is the person who "does in reality" and is the person who "goes to work in the vineyard". A person might therefore have said the wrong thing but ended up doing the right thing. Man looks at the outwards appearance. God looks at the heart. God wants us to be the one who goes out in reality. This parable doesn't mention the quality of any potential work done. But it's saying we must be those who go out in reality to do God's will for us:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2021%3A24-32&version=ESV][Matthew 21:24-32]]* - Jesus answered them, I also will ask you one question, and if you tell me the answer, then I also will tell you by what authority I do these things. The baptism of John, from where did it come? From heaven or from man? And they discussed it among themselves, saying, If we say, From heaven, he will say to us, Why then did you not believe him?     Jesus instructed to call no man on earth their father ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A1&version=ESV][Matthew 23:1]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2023%3A9&version=ESV][Matthew 23:9]]), then they would be referring
    to God as their father, and God is certainly not dead. Jesus responds to the man, "Follow me, and leave the dead
    to bury their own dead." (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%208%3A21-22&version=ESV][Matthew 8:21-22]])
    
    I avoid AI stuff such as ChatGPT for various reasons. It seems to me like some combination of golden calf and tower of Babel. It's built on theft. People have been hoping in it instead of Jesus.
    
    - [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A24-29&version=ESV][I John 2:24-29]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%203%3A21&version=ESV][John 3:21]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2016%3A25&version=ESV][Matthew 16:25]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%206%3A1&version=ESV][II Corinthians 6:1]],6:16-18,7:1, [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2011%3A1&version=ESV][I Corinthians 11:1]]
    
    The way to imitate Jesus is from faith in Jesus to actually believe what He's saying and do it:
    
    - [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A12&version=ESV][John 14:12]]
    
    Putting a stop to calling the person father who was previously my father I've been resisted like the cocoon trying to stop the butterfly from leaving.
    But the born-again person is a new creation who is supposed to be walking like Jesus walked.
    
    The "doing" of "faith", is the "doing" of the love and trust and confidence and obedience in Jesus. A deed is done in "faith" or without faith. We can "do" faith. So we hold faith in Jesus, and then when we do deeds, they'd be done in "faith". So it's not relying on our "works". But God sees the person's heart and commends them for their faith in Jesus. We don't self commend. Whoever loves Jesus will keep His commandments. Whoever believes in Jesus will do the works that He did - good deeds from good faith.

*** Journal <2026-05-30>
Since getting born-again of the spirit, the enemy the devil has clearly been trying to get me "unequally yoked with unbelievers" and has been bombarding me with these lies that I'm "of the night", even using this label of being of the "night watch".

After I was regenerated, born-again of the spirit, I was subsequently attacked by satan to hold me in a prison of circumstance, and I was slandered in public, forced out of church assemblies and prevented from getting employment and meeting other people who are believers, etc. It feels like I was buried in demonic harassment.
I've had to fight and defend against the fiery darts (the lies and various other spiritual attacks) from the enemy.

Now, I do not want to be unequally yoked with unbelievers. To be unequally yoked would be to allow myself to be in a situation where the circumstances are hindering me from serving Christ:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%206%3A14-18&version=ESV][II Corinthians 6:14-18]]* - Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership has righteousness with lawlessness? Or what fellowship has light with darkness? What accord has Christ with Belial? Or what portion does a believer share with an unbeliever? What agreement has the temple of God with idols? For we are the temple of the living God; as God said, I will make my dwelling among them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. Therefore go out from their midst, and be separate from them, says the Lord, and touch no unclean thing; then I will welcome you, and I will be a father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

Sadly, I've been ostracised and ghosted and not helped in time of need by those who I thought were "believers", even those who profess to be believers.
And in wanting to not hurt my former parents through arguments I have sought to leave this household of my former parents.
But no actively professing Christians have offered to help me get out of the situation, but rather have put pressure on me to "appologise to my dad" and "stay with my parents" as they have said mistakingly referring to my former father as my dad, to my pain.

And the only person who has asked if I want to go flatting has been with extreme frequency referring to my former parents as my "mum and dad".
It's a very bizarre situation I have found myself in.

But I was thinking today about "unqual yoking" and have decided after thinking about the application of Scripture today
that going flatting with somoeone of unknown or ambivalent belief/disbelief
though is far less that ideal, isn't in itself "unequal yoking", though does seem to be obviously from my perspective not a clean severance
from whatever has been trying to keep me "bound in the flesh".

then I'd take it as an opportunity to serve Christ:

  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ephesians%206%3A5-8&version=ESV][Ephesians 6:5-8]]* - Slaves, obey your earthly masters with fear and trembling, with a sincere heart, as you would Christ, not by the way of eye-service, as people-pleasers, but as servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart, rendering service with a good will as to the Lord and not to man, knowing that whatever good anyone does, this he will receive back from the Lord, whether he is a slave or free. The word [[strongs:G2086][(G2086 heterozygéō)]] that is translated into "unequally yoked" would be better translated as "yoking two different types together", rather than "sharing equal load" which is what I had thought it meant this morning.

+ [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g2086/kjv/tr/0-1/][blueletterbible.org:  G2086 - heterozygeo - Thayer's Greek Lexicon { KJV }]] :: ἑτεροζυγέω, ἑτεροζύγῳ; (ἑτερόζυγος yoked with a different yoke; used in
  Leviticus 19:19 of the union of beasts of different kinds, e. g. an ox and an
  ass), to come under an unequal or different yoke (Beza,impari jugo copulor),
  to be unequally yoked: τίνι (on the dative see Winers Grammar, § 31, 10 N. 4;
  Buttmann, § 133, 8), tropically, to have fellowship with one who is not an
  equal: 2 Corinthians 6:14, where the apostle is forbidding Christians to have contact with idolaters.

I think that Thayer's Greek Lexicon says this too strongly. Saying that all "contact" is bad is not what is conveyed in the Scripture, to my understanding.
Rather, the issue is to be "yoked" to unbelievers. Imagine, for example, if when Jesus Christ was doing His ministry in His 30 or so years in the flesh, He were to be led away from His task.

#+END_QUOTE

And in this dream I put up my hand and explained:
- Managing to execute an external action component of a deed is not what makes love to be in the truth most fundamentally.
  And this is why the Scripture doesn't say, "love in truth by having deeds" but rather the Scripture is saying that we can have confidence that we are "in the truth", confidence that comes from doing deeds that are done out of real love for the truth, from our heart.
  We knows that God can see our heart and it gives us confidence when we are deeding from the heart. But even if our heart condemns us, we know that God is greater than our heart.
  So the heart attitude when doing the deed is what counts (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A4&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:4]]*),
  but even if we doubt our own faith we know that God is greater than our heart.
  So we have a conscience and we should be acting on good conscience for confidence (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%201%3A5&version=ESV][I Timothy 1:5]]*). But God is greater than our conscience.
  God is greater than our own ability to judge our own faith. But God sees our heart and what is in our heart better than we know ourselves.
  For love to be done in "reality" there has to be real love in the heart and then when a deed is done that deed is done in love in reality.
  If a person is deeding with love for the truth in their heart then that deed is done in love in reality rather than in false pretense (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2081%3A15&version=ESV][Psalms 81:15]]*).
  True love is independent, technically, (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2013%3A1-8&version=ESV][I Corinthians 13:1-8]]*) from the external actions and can still exist without the external actions.
  True love for Jesus Christ and keeping His commandments is not contingent on one's ability to "make it to 'church'" so to speak, for example.
  The heart attitude comes first, and the fellowship is a promise given to the person who has the heart attitude of a loving faith in Jesus Christ in their heart.

I commented on [[https://www.youtube.com/post/Ugkxl30UHevAEi_JSWjMxdko-ahwIknoH9s5][youtube.com:  Quiz from Towards Jesus]]:

Yeah, Jesus gives the rest though.
Jesus says whoever learns from the Father comes to Him.
So we learn from God and come to Jesus.
Jesus says we will find it if we come to Him, but it's still up to Jesus to actually give the rest.

We are required to rest in a 'sense', but Jesus gives us the rest, and we strive to enter that rest. We don't
simply take the rest. Jesus gives it to us. We strive in faith and obedience to Jesus, to keep His commandments,
and Jesus gives the rest. So, like with the Israelites leaving Egypt, God was leading them to the promised land
and the Israelites had to keep faith in God and continue to keep His commandments, and not regress back into
idolatry. And this is they way in which we are also supposed to enter into God's rest, by faith obeying Jesus
Christ:

- [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Timothy%204%3A7-10&version=ESV][I Timothy 4:7-10]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2011%3A28-30&version=ESV][Matthew 11:28-30]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Ezekiel%2037%3A12-14&version=ESV][Ezekiel 37:12-14]]

I think entering into God's rest is not an act of disobedience, and it's not an act of distrst. The starting point
of entering into God's rest might be thought of as the point of repentance from dead works and turning to faith in
God:

- [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%206%3A1-2&version=ESV][Hebrews 6:1-2]]

We "do" the will of God to enter into God's rest. After all, how can someone rest if they are being tormented
because they did not pass forward forgiveness?

- [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%2018%3A32-35&version=ESV][Matthew 18:32-35]]

We entering into God's rest through "faith and obedience" to Jesus Christ and to His gospel:

- [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%204%3A1-14&version=ESV][Hebrews 4:1-14]]

Christ:

*** Journal <2026-07-22 Wed 16:53>

If a person is going around telling people, "I'm a Christian," that doesn't mean that they really are a Christian, so to guage whether or not a person is a Christian wouldn't be to ask, "Are you a Christian?"
If a person is going around telling people, "Jesus (or Yeshua) is the Son of God," then there is evidence that they are a Christian.
If a person is going around telling people that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, then there is evidence that they are a Christian.
If a person is going around telling people the truth about God then there is evidence that they are a Christian.
If a person appears to be doing what Christ commanded then there is evidence that they are a Christian.
I mean, God knows if they truly are, because God sees the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
God sees the person's faith (i.e. sees what's really going on in their heart). But a person's confessions of faith and their deeds are still a witness to others to guage whether or not they are a true follower of Jesus.
I mean, would it be right to trust that someone is presently a Christian if once some time ago you heard them make a profession of faith, but now
they appear to be rejecting Jesus and His words, or that they became devoted to idols/demons, following after false gods?
I'd see no reason to trust that person is presently a Christian if their present witness that they are making is not to the truth.
Real faith must continue. And we're all still accountable to God for our deeds (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%205%3A9-12&version=ESV][II Corinthians 5:9-12]]*).

A person's testimony to others is not given merely by their words.
A person's deeds are also a witness to others. Jesus Christ's deeds did bear witness that God His Father was working through Him (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2010%3A37-38&version=ESV][John 10:37-38]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A12&version=ESV][John 14:12]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Titus%201%3A16&version=ESV][Titus 1:16]]*).

So to guage whether or not a person is really a Christian, a much more reliable way than asking them, "Are you a Christian?" would be to ask them what they believe about Jesus Christ,
(i.e. Find out if they really believe that Jesus really is the Son of God, and is the Christ, and died on a tree and rose from the dead, for example).
Asking someone if they are a Christian is not a reliable way to find out if they are a Christian.

If a person is confessing that God has loved us first in sending Jesus into the world to die for our sins ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A3&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:3]]), then there is good reason to believe that person is a Christian, because it's the truth of Scripture.
It has to be genuine faith that loves the truth, and also must continue ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A2&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:2]]), though, for a person to be a Christian in reality, though, and God knows.
But as far as guaging who the Christians are, if somebody wants some evidence towards if another person is a Christian, there are indicators.

Genuine love loves in the way God has commanded. And the true Christian loves.
Someone who says they are a Christian might actually not be a Christian.
The true Christians have a genuine faith in Jesus Christ in their heart, and those who have faith in Jesus will do the deeds He did.
So you might guage whether a person is a Christian or not by their witness to the truth from their confession to the truth, or from the way they appear to conduct themselves.
There's nothing wrong with testifying to God that someone else you saw appeared to testify to the truth at a certain point of time.
But God sees the heart. God knows for sure whether or not someone has faith in Him, and whether or not they continue in faith in Him.
God sees our faith and our deeds with total clarity. There's no deceiving God at all.

+ [[https://www.earlychristianwritings.com/text/polycarp-lightfoot.html][Polycarp 4:3]] :: Our widows must be sober-minded as touching the faith of the Lord,
    making intercession without ceasing for all men, abstaining from all
    calumny, evil speaking, false witness, love of money, and every evil
    thing, knowing that they are God's altar, and that all sacrifices are
    carefully inspected, and nothing escapeth Him either of their thoughts or intents or any of the secret things of the heart.

A person witnesses to others about what they believe in what others can see about them.
So if a person sees another person confessing that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, for instance, then this is a good indication that they are a believer.
Do they witness to the truth about God? Does it appear like Jesus Christ is working through them to produce the deeds of Jesus, as in walk like Jesus walked ([[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2010%3A37-38&version=ESV][John 10:37-38]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A12&version=ESV][John 14:12]], [[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A3-6&version=ESV][I John 2:3-6]])?

    If a person is going around telling people, "I'm a Christian," that doesn't mean that they really are a Christian, so to guage whether or not a person is a Christian wouldn't be to ask, "Are you a Christian?" If a person is going around telling people, "Jesus (or Yeshua) is the Son of God," then there is evidence that they are a Christian. If a person is going around telling people that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, then there is evidence that they are a Christian. If a person is going around telling people the truth about God then there is evidence that they are a Christian. If a person appears to be doing what Christ commanded then there is evidence that they are a Christian. I mean, God knows if they truly are, because God sees the thoughts and intentions of the heart. God sees the person's faith (i.e. sees what's really going on in their heart). But a person's confessions of faith and their deeds are still a witness to others to guage whether or not they are a true follower of Jesus. I mean, would it be right to trust that someone is presently a Christian if once some time ago you heard them make a profession of faith, but now they appear to be rejecting Jesus and His words, or that they became devoted to idols/demons, following after false gods? I'd see no reason to trust that person is presently a Christian if their present witness that they are making is not to the truth. Real faith must continue. And we're all still accountable to God for our deeds (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%205%3A9-12&version=ESV][II Corinthians 5:9-12]]*).
    
    A person's testimony to others is not given merely by their words. A person's deeds are also a witness to others. Jesus Christ's deeds did bear witness that God His Father was working through Him (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2010%3A37-38&version=ESV][John 10:37-38]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A12&version=ESV][John 14:12]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Titus%201%3A16&version=ESV][Titus 1:16]]*).
    
    So to guage whether or not a person is really a Christian, a much more reliable way than asking them, "Are you a Christian?" would be to ask them what they believe about Jesus Christ, (i.e. Find out if they really believe that Jesus really is the Son of God, and is the Christ, and died on a tree and rose from the dead, for example). Asking someone if they are a Christian is not a reliable way to find out if they are a Christian.
    
    If a person is confessing that God has loved us first in sending Jesus into the world to die for our sins (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A3&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:3]]*), then there is good reason to believe that person is a Christian, because it's the truth of Scripture. It has to be genuine faith that loves the truth, and also must continue (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Corinthians%2015%3A2&version=ESV][I Corinthians 15:2]]*), though, for a person to be a Christian in reality, though, and God knows. But as far as guaging who the Christians are, if somebody wants some evidence towards if another person is a Christian, there are indicators.
    
    Genuine love loves in the way God has commanded. And the true Christian loves. Someone who says they are a Christian might actually not be a Christian. The true Christians have a genuine faith in Jesus Christ in their heart, and those who have faith in Jesus will do the deeds He did. So you might guage whether a person is a Christian or not by their witness to the truth from their confession to the truth, or from the way they appear to conduct themselves. There's nothing wrong with testifying to God that someone else you saw appeared to testify to the truth at a certain point of time. But God sees the heart. God knows for sure whether or not someone has faith in Him, and whether or not they continue in faith in Him. God sees our faith and our deeds with total clarity. There's no deceiving God at all.
    
    A person witnesses to others about what they believe in what others can see about them. So if a person sees another person confessing that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, for instance, then this is a good indication that they are a believer. Do they witness to the truth about God? Does it appear like Jesus Christ is working through them to produce the deeds of Jesus, as in walk like Jesus walked (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2010%3A37-38&version=ESV][John 10:37-38]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A12&version=ESV][John 14:12]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%202%3A3-6&version=ESV][I John 2:3-6]]*)?

But God is the righteous judge:

When God judges the world, the saints (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%2014%3A12&version=ESV][Revelation of John 14:12]]*) are involved. But surely they do not practice those sinful things that they do not approve of (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Matthew%207%3A2&version=ESV][Matthew 7:2]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%202%3A1-13&version=ESV][Romans 2:1-13]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%204%3A12&version=ESV][James 4:12]]*), but they rather keep God's commandments for them (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%2014%3A12&version=ESV][Revelation of John 14:12]]*):

+ *enjoin* :: Defintion: Giving an order or direction authoritatively and urgently and often with admonition or solicitude.

+ [[https://www.earlychristianwritings.com/text/polycarp-lightfoot.html][Polycarp 11:2]] :: 
    But he who cannot govern himself in these things, how doth he enjoin

    be defiled by idolatry, and shall be judged as one of the Gentiles
    who know not the judgment of the Lord, Nay, know we not, that the
    saints shall judge the world, as Paul teacheth?

Saints should not "directly" judge their neighbours (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=James%204%3A12&version=ESV][James 4:12]]*). Admonishing and reproving your neigbour, calling out wickedness, we *should* do (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%208%3A22&version=ESV][Acts 8:22]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Leviticus%2019%3A17-18&version=ESV][Leviticus 19:17-18]]*). It would be fine to say, I disapprove of this or that, and it's OK to affirm and even speak to others the truth of Scripture, for example that "all who are presently believing in Jesus Christ are presently not condemned and that all who are disbelieving in Jesus Christ are presently condemned", because it's the truth of Scripture, but it's not OK to turn to your neighbour and say with certainty to them that God has judged them because in the end it's God who judges, and also because in imitation of Christ who came to save the world, rather than judge, we should be speaking the truth of Scripture to others (warning people of coming judgement) but leaving that judgement to God. *** Journal <2026-08-02 Sun 02:58>
So I have just had a couple of interesting dreams. It still bothers me that there was no explicit testimony of Jesus Christ from Holy Spirit to me.
But I will quote relevant Scripture. Trust God's word through Scripture, rather than rely on dreams (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Jude%201%3A8&version=ESV][Jude 1:8]]*).
It also bothers me that yesterday there was a greater than average experience of this defilement and demonic dreams etc.
It's been a real spiritual battle. I've been feeling sick because of the ongoing spiritual warfare.
May Yahweh (Father, Son and Holy Spirit), deliver me completely from it (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Corinthians%207%3A1&version=ESV][II Corinthians 7:1]]*) and from this world (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%202%3A40&version=ESV][Acts 2:40]]*) in Jesus Christ's name.

+ First dream :: 
    The first one was of me walking through a restaurant or conference with dining tables and people seated at them
    and someone called out to me loudly so that everyone had his attention stating that I have the answer to why Jesus said,
    "Call no man on earth your father for you have one father who is in heaven."
    And so everyone seemed to pay close attention as I began speaking.
    
    I said, "Firstly, nowhere in the New Testament..."
    Then I paused as I thought that these people may not be aware of the New Testament
    because they may be people who are living in the period before the New Testament was written.
    But I continued, "Nowhere is it recorded as Jesus having called anybody on earth 'father' other than God."
    Then all of a sudden, strangely, people lost interest dramatically and just returned to conversing with each other at their tables,
    even speaking over me in commotion as I continued speaking.
    
    I continued while nobody was listening to me, "Secondly, when Jesus said, 'You have one father who is in heaven, He was saying that,'"
    and everyone was speaking so loudly with one another ignoring me that it was difficult to speak or think.
    "He was saying that a person has only one...."  (and I was thinking of what to say, 'dad' or 'parent')
     He was saying that whoever has been begotten of God, they have a new..." (and I was thinking of what to say, 'dad' or 'parent')
    But everyone was speaking to loudly over top of me it was difficult to think.

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1&version=ESV][I John 5:1]]* - Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the Father loves whoever has been born of him. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

+ Second dream :: 
    In this second dream I was in some kind of backyard where there was what appeared to be a vintage carnival going on.
    In this carnival there might have been themes of "bad theology".
    At least one other person was standing over what appeared to be a attraction comprised of a silverware tray with some teacups on it at one end of a bench,
    and at the other end of the bench was tree stump that was horizontally oriented to work like a pile-driver.
    Something triggered the tree stump to whack the silverware tray and send the tray moving down the bench.
    So I tried to explain to a lady (if I recall correctly) how it worked.
    
    Then I found myself inside and someone was asking me about Jesus.
    So I said to them, "About a year after I was born-again, perhaps a little less then a year, I began to get clued up
    on discerning sound theology.
    In this dream, I said, "Jesus said whoever learns from him, comes to him. So we have to actually be learning from Jesus."
    And then the lady said, "And do what he says."
    And I said, "Yes, and do what he says."
    And then she sounded, "Huh," as if something clicked for her.
    
    Then I woke up.
    
    I immediately reflected on this dream.
    It did bother me initially that in the dream I had said in this dream, "Jesus said 'whoever learns from him, comes to him'."
    because Jesus actually said that whoever has heard and learned from the Father comes to him.
    Yet Jesus also said that the Father who sent him has told him what to speak,
    and he said that the Son can do nothing apart from what he sees the Father doing.
    So, really, if someone is learning from Jesus who is the Son of God then they are still learning from Father God and as such are coming to Jesus.

    As for the "doing" is concerned, the promise is that those who have faith will do the works of Jesus.
    If a person has the right faith then the promise to them is that they will do good deeds.
    We don't try to contrive the deeds. Rather we walk by faith and the deeds follow (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Revelation%2014%3A13&version=ESV][Revelation of John 14:13]]*).
    Obedience depends on love for the truth (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms%2081%3A15&version=ESV][Psalms 81:15]]*).

God sets up the deeds for those who are walking in the light, but we should be obedient and ready to do them as they are given to us. So we don't contrive the deeds by forcing our way into "helping" widows and orphans, as if to check off some list and self-commend to tell Jesus when we served Him! No, God gives us the deeds. What does not proceed from faith is sin. We should be obedient, *ready* for every good deed:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Titus%203%3A1&version=ESV][Titus 3:1]]* - Remind them to be submissive to rulers and authorities, to be *obedient, to be ready for every good work,* (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2012%3A44-50&version=ESV][John 12:44-50]]* - And Jesus cried out and said, Whoever believes in me, believes not in me but in him who sent me. And whoever sees me sees him who sent me. I have come into the world as light, so that whoever believes in me may not remain in darkness. If anyone hears my words and does not keep them, I do not judge him; for I did not come to judge the world but to save the world. The one who rejects me and does not receive my words has a judge; the word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day. For I have not spoken on my own authority, but *the Father who sent me has himself given me a commandment—what to say and what to speak. And I know that his commandment is eternal life. What I say, therefore, I say as the Father has told me.* (ESV)

#+END_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

#+END_QUOTE

I also want to say that ever since being born-again, yes there has been a lot of correction going on, but I've had the fear of God since I was newly born-again, and I've had a love for God and for people and desire to do the will of God right from the very beginning.
But who am I to self-commend or to say, I love God and my neighbour in the way that God requires? But I'm still called to not hide my light under a bush. Newly born-again, I'm called to tell other people about Jesus.

But the subsequent and prolonged war of attrition against me from chronic demonic/satanic oppression,
the sleep interruptions, being opposed with extreme high frequency in even basic daily tasks,
as I endeavour to walk in the truth, and the lack of hearing the testimony of Jesus Christ from Holy Spirit ongoingly, has had me continually seeking guidance from Scripture, and praying for deliverance several times daily for years.
And even going back before I was born-again, I would ask God to deliver me.

In the month after getting born-again I was writing about keeping the 10 commandments from the heart, and I was also writing about how a person's beliefs in their heart should be
in agreement with the truth about God.
No-one in these years has taken time to critique my writings and respond to me.
I have not been told how much of the theologising I was doing was correct or incorrect, even at the early stages. I certainly wouldn't throw it all out.

I had written about following God's commandments from the heart. But God is the one who circumcises the heart. The elect have soft hearts.

The elect have soft hearts:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2011%3A7-10&version=ESV][Romans 11:7-10]]* - What then? Israel failed to obtain what it was seeking. The *elect* obtained it, but *the rest were hardened*, as it is written, God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that would not see and ears that would not hear, down to this very day.  And David says, Let their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution for them; let their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see, and bend their backs forever.
#+END_QUOTE

A soft heart is needed to perceive and understand:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Mark%208%3A17&version=ESV][Mark 8:17]]* - And Jesus, aware of this, said to them, Why are you discussing the fact that you have no bread? Do you not yet perceive or understand? Are your hearts hardened? (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

God can harden or soften hearts, but so can people harden and soften their own heart:

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2%20Chronicles%2036%3A12-13&version=ESV][II Chronicles 36:12-13]]* - He did what was evil in the sight of the Lord his God. He did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke from the mouth of the Lord. He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God. He stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against turning to the Lord, the God of Israel. (ESV)
#+END_QUOTE

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
  *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%203%3A8&version=ESV][Hebrews 3:8]]* - do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion, on the day of testing in the wilderness,
#+END_QUOTE

When God gives a person a new heart of flesh, He gives a person a new heart that is soft.
A heart of stone can't receive correction. God doesn't remove a heart of flesh to put in a heart of stone.
God removes the heart of stone and puts in a heart of flesh that is responsive to correction and then He writes His laws on it.

Just because God circumcises our heart, doesn't mean the new heart of flesh didn't have any love in it.
On the contrary, I felt healed when I was made new. But God continued to work on me.
In some ways I feel as though "religious theologising" has put heavy burdens on me who felt so free when I was born-again,
but at the same time, I think that it has been prudent and absolutely necessary to receive correction from the Scripture.
By learning from Scripture, I have been saved from endorsing some very demonic doctrines.

I haven't been so self-sure as to ignore guidance from my peers too but I've also wisened up to the fact that there is absolutely atrocious theology circulating, and it just seems to me as though
even amongst the "churches" what is being preached is so compromised, and distracts and actively deters people from actually coming into agreement with Jesus Christ's words
and actually doing as He says.

Generally-speaking (but not in all cases), people I interact with seem to be actively hostile to, or impatient when talking about theology, or stubbornly resistant to what the Scripture is actually saying.
And all the while I've been getting such intense spiritual attacks, and strange dreams.
I've felt opposed in every direction.

May God deliver me from this evil which has continued to come against me.
The spirtual warfare has been so intense. It's not easy to think sometimes because of the attacks that come against my mind.
I'm still waiting for God to testify of Jesus Christ by the Holy Spirit as a direct word to my heart, but in due time I'm sure He will (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Hebrews%2011%3A6&version=ESV][Hebrews 11:6]]*, *[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Luke%2011%3A2-13&version=ESV][Luke 11:2-13]]*).

Father God is the Truth ([[https://www.earlychristianwritings.com/text/justinmartyr-resurrection.html][Saint Justin Martyr]]).
Jesus Christ the Son of God is the Truth (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%2014%3A6&version=ESV][John 14:6]]*).
Holy Spirit is the Truth (*[[https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20John%205%3A1-6&version=ESV][I John 5:1-6]]*)
God is the Truth.

The truth is reality [[https://www.blueletterbible.org/lexicon/g225/kjv/tr/0-1/][(G225 aletheia)]].
I refuse to imbibe on this delusional AI chatbot theft rubbish.
